Purpose
With
--moe-backend humming
and expert parallelism, Humming runs DeepSeek-V4.1's MXFP4 experts on its grouped GEMM. On Hopper the indexed GEMM is much faster for this model. This PR makes
get_humming_moe_gemm_type()
return
indexed
when all of these hold:
the experts are MXFP4 with DeepSeek V4 routing;
model_type
is
deepseek_v41
or
deepseek_v41_text
;
the device is CUDA SM90;
there are no all2all kernels, or the backend is
allgather_reducescatter
.
Without EP, Humming already picks indexed, so nothing changes there.
VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE
still overrides the choice. Since
#56997
, Humming is the default MXFP4 MoE backend on SM90, so V4.1 with EP on Hopper otherwise runs the grouped GEMM by default; this PR moves that default path to indexed too. The rule applies with BF16 activations and with per-token FP8 activations (
--quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
).
The MXFP4 MoE method (DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi-K3, plain mxfp4) now runs
quantization_config.moe.activation
:
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
Humming takes the named format as a fixed input schema, with its input-schema fallback off.
Other explicit backends must run the named format, and
auto
keeps only the backends that do. Before, these models ignored the name on every backend. Now a backend that does not run it stops vLLM, on every platform (CUDA, ROCm, XPU, CPU). The DeepSeek V4 MegaMoE backends (
deep_gemm_mega_moe
,
aiter_mega_moe
) build their own experts and do not read the name. On ROCm, the Kimi-K3 AITER path, which skips the backend selector, now refuses a named activation instead of ignoring it. For example,
fp8_per_token
with
flashinfer_trtllm
now stops vLLM instead of running MXFP8. A draft model with its own
speculative_config.moe_backend
inherits the target's
quantization_config
, so the same rule applies to it.
The startup log prints the format Humming runs:
Humming MoE activations: fp8_per_token (group size 0, scale dtype float32)
. The line appears for every Humming MoE model, gpt-oss included.
On SM90 Humming,
mxfp8
and
fp8_per_block_dynamic
stop vLLM at startup, before the weights load. Humming has no e8m0 input scales on WGMMA, and humming 0.1.16 rejects fp32 group scales with MXFP4 weights (
[Bug][Humming] MXFP4 weight + block-FP8 activation is listed as supported on Hopper, but humming-kernels 0.1.16 rejects it
#60600
). Group-wise scales are also 1.2x to 24x slower than per-token in the SM90 Humming GEMM at M >= 256 (numbers in the review reply).
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG
still works as on main, with no early check: a format Humming cannot run fails while the weights convert, as before. With
--moe-backend humming
, setting it together with
moe.activation
is an error.
gpt-oss is unchanged. With no name, nothing changes.
Test Plan
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k
"
named_activation or activation_on_sm90 or humming or indexed
"
pytest tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py \
    tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py \
    tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_gfx942_int4.py
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k unsupported_reasons
test_humming_deepseek_v41_hopper_uses_indexed_gemm_with_ep
calls
get_humming_moe_gemm_type
and checks that V4.1 with EP gets indexed, with and without
allgather_reducescatter
, and that DeepEP, SM100 and DeepSeek V4 keep the grouped GEMM. It does not need the humming package.
test_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_backend_must_run_named_activation
checks on any GPU that
auto
and
flashinfer_trtllm
refuse
fp8_per_token
, and that
humming
refuses the env JSON plus a name ("not both").
test_humming_deepseek_v4_activation_on_sm90
checks that SM90 Humming accepts
fp8_per_token
and refuses
mxfp8
. It skips on other GPUs, so in CI it runs only in the optional H100 FP8 MoE kernels job;
kernels-moe-test
runs on L4. The Kimi-K3 AITER refusal has no unit test: it is a short guard, and a test would have to mock the whole K3 path.
user_moe_activation_override()
(was
_user_moe_activation_override()
) is now public because
quantization/mxfp4.py
imports it; the existing monkeypatches in
test_b12x.py
,
test_ocp_mx_moe.py
and
test_gfx950_moe.py
use the new name.
Startup check:
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 8 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend humming
on 8x H200, with these additions:
A:
--quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
and DSpark speculative decoding (
--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":1}'
; V4.1 has no classic MTP draft), then one completion request.
B:
--quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8
.
C:
--quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_block_dynamic
.
D:
--quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
with
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"float8e4m3"}'
.
E: only
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"float8e4m3"}'
, then one completion request.
auto
: no
--moe-backend
and no activation name, then one completion request.
Throughput: offline
LLM
runs of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x H200, TP8+EP,
--moe-backend humming
, 2 repeats. Prefill is 16 random 8192-token prompts with 1 output token. Decode is 64 random 512-token prompts with 256 output tokens. The GEMM type was set with
VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE
.
Test Result
Unit tests on one H200: the
test_moe.py
selection above, 41 passed (the SM90 test runs there, not skipped). The other selector and config tests: 1741 passed, 17 skipped.
test_gfx942_int4.py
: 7 passed. The
test_ocp_mx_moe.py
test that patches the renamed function: 1 passed. pre-commit is clean.

(no

[fused_humming_moe.py:146] Using indexed gemm for humming moe
[mxfp4.py:808] Using 'HUMMING' Mxfp4 MoE backend.
[moe.py:633] Humming MoE activations: bf16 (group size 0, scale dtype None)

fp8_per_block_dynamic
): stops at model init. On this head the check is the same; the message is now:
ValueError: Humming MoE cannot run activation=fp8_per_block_dynamic: No compatible Humming input schema for HummingInputSchema(... input_scale_group_size=128, input_scale_dtype=float32 ...) with weight schema HummingWeightSchema(b_dtype=float4e2m1, bs_dtype=float8e8m0, weight_scale_group_size=32 ...) on SM90 (allow_fallback=False)

E (env JSON only): ready after 430 s, completion
" Paris."
, and the log shows
Humming MoE activations: fp8_per_token (group size 0, scale dtype float32)

I think it is interesting to support this, but I am a bit skeptical about how safe it is to make it the default, i.e., assume per-token FP8 quantization has no accuracy impact over BF16/grouped-FP8.
Notably, on Blackwell where FP8 activations are already the default, we use MXFP8 (group-32 e8m0 scales), or block-FP8 (group-128); both much finer-grained than one scale per token row. I suspect per-token FP8 is too coarse, and GSM8K is simply not a rigorous enough eval to study real accuracy impact.
I would either make the per-token FP8 path opt-in for now, or evaluate this more exhaustively before making it default, e.g. on agentic evals.

Thanks, agreed. The latest push makes the activation format an explicit, named choice. It uses the existing typed field instead of a new env string, because those names are documented, validated at parse time, and shared with gpt-oss:
--moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
The names come from
QUANT_KEY_NAMES
(
fp8_per_token
,
fp8_per_block_dynamic
,
mxfp8
). Each name is one scale layout on every arch. A named format turns Humming's input-schema fallback off, so it runs as named or vLLM stops.
It applies to the MXFP4 MoE method: DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi-K3 and plain mxfp4 checkpoints. A backend that cannot run the name stops vLLM at startup, also on SM100f. For example,
fp8_per_token
with
flashinfer_trtllm
or
auto
no longer runs MXFP8 silently.
On SM90 Humming,
mxfp8
and
fp8_per_block_dynamic
stop vLLM at startup, before the weights load.
mxfp8
needs e8m0 input scales, which Humming's WGMMA path does not have. humming 0.1.16 rejects
fp8_per_block_dynamic
(fp32 group-128 scales) with MXFP4 weights, although vLLM's supported-pairs table lists it for Hopper. I opened
[Bug][Humming] MXFP4 weight + block-FP8 activation is listed as supported on Hopper, but humming-kernels 0.1.16 rejects it
#60600
for that mismatch.
The startup log prints the resolved format, for example
Humming MoE activations: fp8_per_token (group size 0, scale dtype float32)
. It also does so for the old
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG
path, which still works. Setting both the env JSON and the name is an error.
With no name nothing changes: Marlin with BF16 stays the default for V4.1 on Hopper.
gpt-oss is unchanged: its selector still drops Humming when an activation is named.
Why SM90 gets only per-token: I ran a dense-GEMM microbenchmark of the Humming MXFP4 GEMM on H200 (not the MoE path). Group scales rescale the WGMMA accumulators once per group:

On a synthetic outlier test, the relative error against a BF16-input reference was 0.022-0.024 for per-token, 0.015-0.020 for g128 and g32 with fp32 scales, and 0.025-0.027 for MXFP8 numerics (e8m0 scales). That is not a model eval.

[Perf][DeepSeek V4.1] Humming indexed MoE GEMM with EP on Hopper, and…
…
47e6dff
… a named MoE activation format

Humming indexed GEMM with EP on Hopper: for DeepSeek V4.1 (model_type
deepseek_v41 / deepseek_v41_text) MXFP4 experts on SM90, Humming now
picks the indexed GEMM also under expert parallelism, when there is no
all2all or the all2all is allgather_reducescatter. Other EP setups still
use grouped_contiguous. Humming is already the default MXFP4 MoE
backend on SM90 (
vllm-project#56997
), so this also changes the default path. On
TP8+EP, indexed is 47% faster at prefill and 63% faster at decode with
BF16 activations, and 24% and 36% faster with per-token FP8.
VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE still overrides the choice.

Named MoE activation format: the DeepSeek V4 MXFP4 MoE selector now
honors --quantization-config.moe.activation, so per-token FP8 on Humming
is an explicit choice:

  --moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token

- With --moe-backend humming, the format is checked before the weights
  load and then passed to the Humming conversion with schema fallback
  off. On SM90, mxfp8 is refused because WGMMA has no e8m0 input scales.
  Setting VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG as well is an error. The env
  JSON alone works as on main.
- Another explicit backend that does not run the format fails, and auto
  keeps only the backends that run it. For example, fp8_per_token with
  flashinfer_trtllm no longer runs MXFP8 without saying so.
- The Kimi-K3 SiTU AITER path skips the selector and runs BF16 only, so
  it refuses a named format.
- The Humming MoE conversion logs the activation format it runs.
- user_moe_activation_override() is public and returns None when no
  vLLM config is set.

Without moe.activation, backend and activation selection are unchanged.

H100 multi-node data point for the EP default (Hopper, TP8+EP, latency-bound agentic workload)
Setup: 2 nodes x 4 H100-64GB, vLLM nightly
0.32.0rc1.dev122+g23fbc2ec2
(not this PR's head), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,

Metric: P90 request interactivity (1/TPOT, tok/s).

Grouped vs Marlin was an interleaved 3A+3B comparison on fresh servers: +32.8%, and every Marlin run was above every grouped run.
Indexed and its Marlin reference (113.95) ran in the same allocation, on consecutive fresh servers.
The grouped runs came from other allocations. Against their mean, indexed is +26.8%; that comparison crosses allocations, and run-to-run spread between allocations was about 5%.
A torch profile of the grouped path shows the w13/w2 GEMMs at 54/33 us per MoE layer on all 8 ranks, independent of routing. That matches visiting all 16 local experts while only about 4 receive tokens at these batch sizes.
Conclusion: in this low-batch Hopper EP setup, switching to indexed recovers most of the gap to Marlin, and Marlin stays about 7% ahead. Not covered here:

🐛 Describe the bug
HummingExpertsBase._supports_quant_scheme()
lists MXFP4 weights with block-FP8 activations (group 128, float32 scales) as a supported MoE pair. The comment says it works on Hopper (
fused_humming_moe.py#L325-L328
):
# MXFP4 weight (group-32 e8m0) with block-FP8 activation
# (group-128 float32). Runs via WGMMA software dequant, so it
# works on Hopper (SM90/H200) as well as Blackwell.
(
kMxfp4Static
,
kFp8Dynamic128Sym
),
tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py
(from
#51332
) asserts that this pair is allowed.
humming-kernels 0.1.16 refuses the pair.
is_humming_schema_compatible()
in
humming/schema/humming.py
(lines 499 and 501) requires group-wise input scales to be e8m0 or e4m3 when the weights are FP4 with group scales:
if
input_group_size
>
0
and
as_dtype
not
in
[
dtypes
.
float8e8m0
,
dtypes
.
float8e4m3
]:
return
False
if
input_group_size
>
0
and
weight_group_size
>
0
and
as_dtype
!=
bs_dtype
:
return
False
The rule does not depend on the GPU. So vLLM's backend selection accepts
kFp8Dynamic128Sym
with MXFP4 weights, and the run then fails at weight load in
check_and_fallback_input_schema()
. With
allow_fallback=True
the input silently becomes per-token FP8 instead.
Minimal check on an H200:

# ValueError: No compatible Humming input schema for HummingInputSchema(...,
#   input_scale_group_size=128, input_scale_dtype=float32, ...) with weight schema
#   HummingWeightSchema(b_dtype=float4e2m1, bs_dtype=float8e8m0, weight_scale_group_size=32, ...)
#   on SM90 (allow_fallback=False)
The kernel itself can run this layout. When the compatibility check is bypassed, a dense MXFP4 GEMM with group-128 float32 input scales runs on H200 and its output matches the reference (kernel error 0.0017-0.0032, the same level as per-token FP8). So the mismatch is between vLLM's supported-pairs table and humming's schema rule, not a missing kernel.
A related limit on SM90: MXFP8 inputs (group 32, e8m0 scales) pass
is_humming_schema_compatible()
but have no SM90 kernel.
humming/tune/candidate.py:287
rejects every WGMMA candidate with "WGMMA input scales must use float32 storage, got float8e8m0", and
humming/tune/sm90_policies.py:256
then raises "no legal grouped-scale SM90 schedule".
For context, the dense-GEMM probe on H200 (N=2048, K=4096, MXFP4 weights) also showed that group-wise input scales are much slower than per-token on WGMMA at M=4096: 535.7 us for group 128 and 1720 us for group 32 (fp32 scales), against 72.2 us for per-token FP8 and 110.9 us for BF16.
Questions
Should humming accept float32 group scales with MXFP4 weights on SM90 (the kernel runs), or should vLLM drop
(kMxfp4Static, kFp8Dynamic128Sym)
on SM90 and fix the comment and the test?
Is e8m0 input-scale support on WGMMA planned? Without it, MXFP8 activations cannot run on Hopper.
PR
#59488
makes
--quantization-config.moe.activation
select the Humming MoE activation format for MXFP4 checkpoints. Until this is settled, it refuses
fp8_per_block_dynamic
and
mxfp8
on SM90 Humming at startup.

Overview
Proof of concept: on Hopper with expert parallel, run DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 MXFP4 experts on Humming with block FP8 (group 128) activations by default instead of BF16. Related to
#59488
(opt-in
--quantization-config.moe.activation
for the same method), which this would rebase onto.
Claims
DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 + EP on H200: +25% decode output throughput (TPOT 25.2 -> 20.0 ms) and +6% prefill-heavy throughput, with GSM8K unchanged.
Scope:
Mxfp4MoEMethod
with the HUMMING backend, DeepSeek V4 routing (V4 and V4.1), expert parallel, SM90. Everything else keeps the current BF16 default, and
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG
still overrides.
Validation
DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 4x H200, Humming MoE backend (the SM90 default). Baseline is
main
(BF16 activations). The FP8 column was measured with
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"a_dtype": "float8e4m3", "input_scale_group_size": 128}'
. That override resolves to the same Humming layer config as this PR's
kFp8Dynamic128Sym
(group 128,
DynamicGroup
, float32 scales on SM90).

Tests:
pytest tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py
passes (11). The new test fails without the source change.
Details
DeepSeek V4 MXFP4 experts go through
Mxfp4MoEMethod
, which passes no activation key. On SM90 the Humming backend then builds its input schema from
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG
and defaults to BF16. This PR sets
activation_key = kFp8Dynamic128Sym
in that case.
#59815
already plumbs the key into Humming's input schema with fallback disabled. The DeepSeek V4 checkpoint declares block FP8 GS128 with UE8M0 scales for its FP8 layers, so block FP8 matches what the model was built for.
Why only with EP: under EP each rank runs full-size experts (hidden 4096, intermediate 2048), where Humming's FP8 x MXFP4 kernels are faster. Under TP4 the intermediate is split to 512 per rank, and dynamic activation quantization costs more than it saves. Gating on DeepSeek V4 routing keeps other MXFP4 models (Kimi K3, plain mxfp4) unchanged.
Limitations:
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash was not run; it shares the routing and method, so it gets the same default.
[Perf][DeepSeek V4.1] Humming indexed MoE GEMM with EP on Hopper, and a named MoE activation format
#59488
reports the indexed GEMM is faster for V4.1 with EP on Hopper, and the FP8 gain should be re-measured on that path.
Measured on H200 with the default all2all backend. DeepEP v2 and H100/H20 were not measured.
The FP8 column was measured with the equivalent env override. I could not rerun end to end on this exact build because the shared machine's GPUs were taken.
Not a duplicate:
[Perf][DeepSeek V4.1] Humming indexed MoE GEMM with EP on Hopper, and a named MoE activation format
#59488
adds an opt-in activation format for the same method, and this PR changes the default for one configuration.

#53184
fuses SwiGLU with per-token FP8 quantization for W2.
[Model][Quant] DeepSeek-V4: opt-in lossless MXFP4->block-FP8 expert dequant (Hopper prefill speedup)
#53709
dequantizes experts to block FP8 instead.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Tune fused mHC post + pre-norm for SM90 at up to 8 tokens by ShuoleiWang · Pull Request #61461 · vllm-project/vllm · GitHub
body:
Conversation
ShuoleiWang
commented
Oct 13, 2026
•
edited

.
Copy link
Copy Markdown
Contributor
Overview
The fused mHC post + pre-norm kernel runs twice per decoder layer in DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 and GLM-5.3-Flash. Its split configs were tuned on GB300 (
#56633
). This PR gives SM90 its own config for 1–8 tokens:
(tile_n, n_splits, n_thr) = (12, hidden / 512, 256)
. Other architectures and token counts are unchanged.
Claims
On H20 at 1–8 tokens, the op gets faster:
DeepSeek-V4-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash (hidden 4096): 4.4–16.3%.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (hidden 5120): 9.1–14.1%.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro (hidden 7168): 2.1–22.8%.
The band includes DSpark k=5 decode at C1, which runs 6 tokens per step.
Residual streams are bit-identical. The mixing coefficients, and through them the layer inputs, differ only in FP32 summation order.
Startup warmup compiles the new variant. Off SM90, the set of compiled kernels is unchanged.
Validation
Microbenchmark.
H20,
hc_mult = 4
, FlashInfer CUPTI with a CUDA graph and a cold L2, median of 3 runs of 200 replays. Outputs are checked before timing.
The 4096 and 7168 columns time
mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang
, which DeepSeek-V4 and GLM-5.3-Flash call.
The 5120 column times
mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_tilelang
, which DeepSeek-V4.1 calls.
All columns come from one run of this PR's
tilelang_kernels.py
. Each cell is main → this PR, in µs.

The minimum tensor traffic is 1.7–3.9 MB per op, corresponding to an effective bandwidth of 152–308 GB/s.
From 9 to 32 tokens, main and this PR pick the same config, and their times agree within ±1.1%.
At 5120, the new config had the lowest total time over 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 tokens in a sweep of 63 configs. It was within 4.6% of the best config at each of those token counts.
Tests.
pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_jit_warmup.py tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py
passes on H20, with one exception:
test_mhc_fused_post_pre[4-7168-128]
. That case runs 128 tokens, outside the band, and fails the same way without this change.
A 1-hour TP8 serving run built no TileLang kernels after warmup. CI runs
kernels/mhc
on B200 only, so this H20 run is the only coverage for the SM90 cases.
E2E sanity check.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8×H20 with TP8, 1K in / 1K out. It ran on main
240ee8d
(2026-10-07) with this change applied;
kernels/mhc/
has not changed since.
DSpark k=5 at a synthetic acceptance length of 3.51.
One run per server, in the order main, PR, PR, main.
At C1, both PR runs beat both main runs: output throughput +0.9%, TPOT p50 −1.0%. At C64, which is outside the band, both PR runs fall between main's two runs in throughput and TPOT p50.
Accuracy.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on the same build, GSM8K, 5-shot, with real DSpark verification:
Correct answers: 1274 / 1319 on main, 1276 / 1319 with this PR.
Acceptance length: 3.863 and 3.868.
GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4 were checked at the op level only.
Details
Why it is faster.
Every (token, tile, k-slice) block recomputes the post mapping.
main's
(2, 8, 128)
runs 12 tiles, and each thread makes 4–7 serial memory round trips.
The new config runs 2 tiles with 2 round trips each.
Band.
A separate candidate config,
(12, 8, 128)
, improved latency at 9–18 tokens on H20. Those gains may depend on H20's 78-SM grid scheduling and have not been validated on H100/H200, so this PR leaves that band unchanged.
H100/H200.
These GPUs are not measured. Both grids should fit in one wave on 132 SMs, so the gain is expected to carry over. The 6–7-token dip at 7168 looks like a wave spill on H20 and is not expected there.

body:
Conversation
mengziheng
commented
Sep 29, 2026
Copy link
Copy Markdown
Purpose
Package the SM90 mHC prenorm GEMM register-lifetime fix from
deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#448
, authored by jason (leevan). In a multi-stage K loop, the next iteration can overwrite register A operands before the previous asynchronous WGMMA has finished. Repeated calls with identical inputs can therefore produce different outputs. The upstream fix waits immediately after committing the WGMMA batch.
This integrates that existing fix into vLLM's packaged JIT header until the pinned DeepGEMM dependency contains it; it is not a new kernel implementation. DeepGEMM
#448
is currently open. Remove the temporary integration once the dependency pin includes the fix.
This correctness change was split out of
vLLM #58986
, which now contains only the H20 block-FP8 MoE tuning. This branch starts from main
07f1ba2ec66776650a490630ddfa9e3c92713c33
and does not depend on that performance PR. The corresponding v0.30 backport remains
mengziheng/vllm#3
. There is no throughput improvement claim for this correctness repair.
Changes
Generate a patched header during CMake configuration and install it without modifying a supplied
DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR
. Exclude the original header from the directory install to prevent a same-timestamp overwrite.
Use the same helper in the standalone DeepGEMM installer. Recognized patched input is idempotent; unrecognized source fails without overwriting the destination.
Extend the existing mHC suite with six SM90 regressions: 256/512/1024 tokens, different split-K counts, default and side streams, independent FP32 references and exact repeatability. Skip when DeepGEMM is unavailable.
Validation
The following GPU results were recorded on H20/v0.30 before this PR split. The main test path is
tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py
; the v0.30 suite used
tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py
.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k
'
sm90_mhc_prenorm_preserves_register_operands or test_mhc_fused_post_pre
'
-v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k sm90_mhc_prenorm_preserves_register_operands -v
The pinned original header fails the new regression; the fixed header passes all six cases. The final test including its DeepGEMM availability guard returned
6 passed, 212 deselected
.
The broader selection returned
17 passed, 9 skipped, 1 failed
. The existing H=7168/M=128 BF16 reference case fails with both original and repaired headers. No tolerance was loosened; this is not a full-suite pass.
A fresh-process audit of the complete mHC operation covers 12 shape/seed groups with five repeats each. Repaired results are exactly repeatable; the original produces inconsistent results at 256/512 tokens. This does not establish whole-model token determinism.
An installation fixture using the actual CMake integration verified installed bytes equal the upstream fix, repeated configure/install preserves it, and supplied source content remains unchanged. Standalone idempotence and rejection of unknown input without destination overwrite also passed. A full wheel build was not performed.
Fresh local checks for this split:
pre-commit run --from-ref 07f1ba2ec66776650a490630ddfa9e3c92713c33 --to-ref HEAD
git diff --check 07f1ba2ec66776650a490630ddfa9e3c92713c33 HEAD
All applicable pre-commit checks pass. The three integration/helper files are byte-identical to the previously tested implementation, and the new regression's AST is identical. A local helper check again passed original-to-fixed conversion, idempotence, source preservation and unknown-input rejection. The generated header SHA256 is
b90beeaed11e279d3451ad3d438b8a64a41fd003c4b7f4d5e0a8fb79a20ad80b
. GPU tests were not rerun on this latest-main branch; these checks establish split equivalence, not a full main-wheel or full-model validation.
Model evaluation
Historical validation uses the same GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint on 4×H20, TP4, FP8 weights/BF16 activations and MTP3, with v0.30 native extensions and the patched JIT header. The corrected control without the MoE tuning and the corrected candidate with the tuning each score
121/128
on a GSM8K first-128, five-shot raw-completion diagnostic (greedy, concurrency 8, output cap 768). Each has 128 successful requests and no truncation. Only 39/128 output texts match exactly; each arm uniquely answers three questions correctly. This subset is not an accuracy-improvement claim or proof of full-model equivalence.
The corrected control completed
1,152/1,152
measured serving requests successfully; all three recorded control/candidate blocks completed
3,456/3,456
in total. The corrected candidate also passed six context-retrieval checks at 511/2047/2048/2049/4097/8193 tokens. Full serving settings, paired measurements and limitations remain in
#58986
. Those performance differences belong to the MoE tuning, with this fix present in both arms.
B200, production traffic, long soak tests and full-model serving on latest main were not validated.
Related work
The open-PR duplicate search was refreshed before splitting.
#50645
and
#53055
address missing-DeepGEMM fallbacks,
#52165
changes detection,
#48619
ports the SM100 kernel to CuTeDSL, and
#41834
/
#42856
concern SM12x support.
#55184
repairs sparse MLA on SM8x;
#54955
is an opt-in batch-invariant execution preview using explicit mHC operations. Neither addresses packaging this register-lifetime fix in the default SM90 path. No duplicate integration was found. The same code has been removed from
#58986
so the two community PRs do not duplicate it. No second DeepGEMM fix PR is proposed.
AI assistance was used for investigation, integration, tests and this description. Human review has not been asserted.

Overview
Draft: add an experimental, explicit opt-in for DeepSeek-V4.1 mHC coefficient overlap on Hopper (SM90), reusing the stream path introduced by

. Hopper remains disabled by default; GPU validation is pending.
Claims
KernelConfig.enable_mhc_overlap=None
preserves SM100 automatic selection;
True
additionally permits SM90, and
False

Existing DeepGEMM, shape, ubatching, FULL CUDA graph and small-batch restrictions remain. SM90 uses the ordinary TP collective and cannot select the SM100-only fused all-reduce.
No speedup, numerical equivalence, model quality or production-readiness claim is made in this draft.
Validation
CPU only, using this branch's Python source on Linux, Python 3.12.3 and pytest 9.1.1, in an isolated container with no GPU devices (2 CPU cores / 4 GiB). Installed dependencies were inherited from a vLLM v0.28.0 image; this was not a fresh main wheel build.

All applicable hooks pass, including mypy, config validation and Buildkite test tethering. The new dispatch tests are in the existing mHC suite. The replay test now permits SM90 but

The existing eligibility gate excludes SM90. This change makes Hopper experimental and opt-in via

title: [WIP][Kernel][DSv4.1] Add compensated BF16 mHC prenorm for SM90 by xijiaat · Pull Request #60777 · vllm-project/vllm · GitHub
body:
Conversation
xijiaat
commented
Oct 9, 2026
Copy link
Copy Markdown
Contributor
Purpose
Draft a compensated BF16 mHC prenorm primitive for Hopper, adapted from SGLang's
hc_mix_stats_bf16x3
in
sgl-project/sglang#39664
and
sgl-project/sglang#41251
. It splits the FP32 mixing weight into three BF16 components, accumulates their projections separately in FP32, and computes the input squared norm in the same pass.
This initial draft contains a kernel, correctness tests and a comparison benchmark.
Serving dispatch is intentionally not wired yet. No kernel or end-to-end speedup, numerical equivalence, or production-readiness claim is made.
Integration and default selection depend on real SM90 measurements against the current fused mHC path, not only against a standalone GEMM.
Implementation
Accept caller-owned prepared weights and output buffers; no allocation or CPU/GPU synchronization in the projection wrapper.
Write
[splits, tokens, mix]
projection and
[splits, tokens]
squared-norm partials, compatible with the existing prenorm epilogue layout.
Support split counts 1/4/16, token tiles 32/64/128, empty batches, masked tails, and contiguous offset views. These are tuning candidates, not validated performance defaults.
Reuse the existing mHC correctness suite. Add FP64 reference, cancellation/weight-reconstruction, output-boundary and changed-input/weight CUDA graph tests.
Add a CUPTI benchmark that checks correctness before timing and sweeps both DeepGEMM and candidate configurations with CUDA graphs and cold L2. Weight preparation, allocations and the common epilogue are excluded from the reported prenorm timing.
The prepared weights occupy 6 bytes per original FP32 element, in addition to any retained original weight. The caller must rebuild them after weight updates. Different accumulation orders can change outputs; batch invariance is not promised. SGLang's bundled serving gains are not an estimate for this isolated kernel or for vLLM.
Duplicate check and provenance
Checked
#57448
and public open/closed PR searches for
mHC
,
compensated
,
bf16x3
,
SM90
, and Hopper on 2026-10-09. No open PR implementing this compensated mHC projection was found.

Overview
vLLM has no MegaMoE that runs on Hopper today:
the DeepGEMM MegaMoE (
deep_gemm_mega_moe
) requires SM100;
the FlashInfer MoE-EP megakernels (
flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl
,
flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm
) require SM100
This PR runs block-FP8 MoE checkpoints on Hopper with FlashInfer's SM90 FP8 MegaMoE, which ships in FlashInfer 0.7.2. The kernel fuses dispatch, both expert GEMMs and combine. It goes through the existing
--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl
path with no model code, so any block-FP8 MoE can use it.

Details
Kernel.
FlashInfer
Sm90PullFp8MegaMoeConfig
, with FP32 128x128 weight scales and a SwiGLU clamp.
FlashInfer's push-style SM90 backend has no SwiGLU clamp, so it cannot serve
swiglu_limit
models.
Weights.
The kernel wants FC1 rows interleaved as
[pair, {gate, up}, 8]
under one 128x128 scale. Each scale block therefore covers rows from two checkpoint blocks, and both use
max(s_gate, s_up)
.
This is exact for power-of-two scales, which GLM-5.3-Flash has. Other checkpoints get one extra E4M3 rounding on half of the FC1 rows.
Workspaces.
The kernel always processes its whole token buffer, with a launch geometry picked for that size. With a single buffer sized at
max_num_batched_tokens
, decode is slower than the baseline.
The adapter therefore adds 64-, 256- and 1024-token workspaces. Each call uses the smallest one that fits the largest batch across DP ranks. Without DP-wide token counts it uses the default workspace, because every rank must pick the same buffer.
Loaders.
The fp8, compressed-tensors, online FP8 and Quark FP8 MoE methods now call the experts'
process_weights_after_loading
. It is a no-op for other experts.
The SM90 path is chosen from the quant config, not the weight dtype. FP8 weights keep their dtype, so a rebuild from preprocessed weights picks the same path.
Idle ranks.
With pass-through stages, the experts own the EP collective. A rank without tokens therefore still enters them. The change is identical to the one in
[Beam] Enable CuTeDSL NVFP4 MegaMoE
#62073
.
Limitations.
The backend needs expert parallelism and
nvshmem4py
.
It rejects DBO, runtime weight transfer and
apply_router_weight_on_input
.
Shared experts are not fused.
FlashInfer's SM90 input staging is torch-composed, about 1.2 ms per step at C128.

Code Quality and Style:
Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
Pull Request Contents:
Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

suggestion
: Placing
ptx::warpgroup_wait<0>()
after
warpgroup_commit_batch()
is the correct minimal fix: it keeps the single-buffered register operands
a[...]
live until the async WGMMA has consumed them. Consequence is that every K stage now fully drains its WGMMA before the next A load, so WGMMA and the next stage's A-load/reduction cannot overlap. This is not a regression versus the buggy code (which already waited each iteration) and correctness must come first, but it is worth a short follow-up note: if the kernel is compute bound, double-buffering
a
and using
warpgroup_wait<1>()
would restore overlap while still protecting the register source.

The MR fixes a real SM90 register-source WGMMA race in sm90_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm. Previously the kernel loaded the FP32 A fragment into single-buffered
a[...]
registers BEFORE waiting for the previous stage's asynchronous WGMMA to complete, so the in-flight WGMMA could read A registers that had already been overwritten. The fix moves

empty_barriers[(s-1)]->arrive()
ordering remains safe because the previous stage's WGMMA has now been drained. 📌 Description
Follow-up to
#6343
(SM90 FP4 MegaMoE):
Cleanup fix:
with
single_active_dispatch_warp
, the inactive dispatch warp cleaned the workspace with empty expert counts and left pool blocks ≥ 32 of hot experts stale, so the next launch failed (H20, 97–128 tokens per rank, e.g. CUDA-graph capture); it now fetches the counts first (outputs bitwise unchanged, timing within noise).
H200 push dispatch:
add measured H200 EP8 buckets that enable push for M ≤ 32 on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiMo-V2.5-Pro, and M ≤ 64 on DeepSeek-V4-Pro (rotated pool at M 33–64), saving about 10 µs per call (1.03–1.16x kernel time, bitwise-identical outputs; H20 and EP4 plans unchanged).
Other models:
accept any expert count that divides across ranks, keep the selected plans compilable for untuned geometries (H20 buckets match the full geometry, the
BLOCK_M=8
stage count follows the shared-memory budget, unsupported shapes raise
ValueError
), and allow push only on validated plans, so Kimi-K2, DeepSeek-V3, GLM-4.x and Qwen3 shapes now run correctly while plans of the three tuned geometries are unchanged.
Usage docs:
the weight-preparation docs now state what callers must convert before
transform_{nvfp4,mxfp4}_weights_for_mega_moe
: Marlin byte order (checkpoints are usually low-nibble-first), scales inside the decoder range (NVFP4
6 * scale <= 448
; MXFP4
2^-5
–
2^6
for groups with nonzero codes, otherwise outputs silently saturate or flush), and the excess moved into per-expert global scales passed at run time; the module example shows the full flow.
How to use:
FlashInfer only provides the kernels and the layout transforms; frameworks convert checkpoint tensors to the format above at load time (the SGLang integration does this for
nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4
, where about 51% of blocks would saturate without rebalancing).

Single-dispatch-warp plans fetch the per-expert counts only in warp 0, but
cleanup_workspace() runs on every dispatch warp and derives pool block offsets
from each warp's cached counts. Warp 1 used offset 0, so blocks 32+ of every
local expert except expert 0 kept stale L1 arrival counts / L2 masks and the
next launch failed (H20, M 97..128, one expert > 32 BM24 blocks, e.g. CUDA graph
capture). Let inactive dispatch warps fetch the final counts before cleanup.

Adds test_hot_expert_workspace_cleanup (hot routing, M=97/128, repeated calls and
CUDA graph replay): fails before the fix on 8xH20, passes after (41 passed).

Counter dispatch:
- Allow push / rotated pool only on the validated small-M plans (M <= 64,
  BLOCK_M <= 24) and when the push row copy supports the hidden size
  (hidden % 1024 == 0); force_* overrides outside that range fall back to the
  barrier path (forced push at BM64 could produce run-to-run differences).
- Geometries without measured buckets push (without the rotated pool) up to
  M = 32 on H20 and H200.

Untuned geometries (e.g. DeepSeek-V3 H7168/E256/K8, Kimi-K2 H7168/E384/K8):
- The H20 tile buckets assume the RS arm of the three tuned geometries; match
  them on (hidden, experts, top-k) instead of hidden alone. Before, any other
  geometry with the same hidden got 6 stages without RS and failed to compile
  ("Unexpected SM90 pipeline depth", shared-memory capacity).
- Replace the Pro-only BLOCK_M=8 stage clamp with the shared-memory budget the
  4-stage layout leaves for the expert-count table and dispatch send rows;
  H7168/E384 (Kimi-K2) and H >= 7680 no longer overflow at M <= 16.
- Reject shapes the kernel cannot compile (hidden alignment, intermediate not a
  multiple of 128 or larger than hidden / 2) with a ValueError.

Plans of the three tuned geometries are unchanged on H20/H200, EP4/EP8,
M 1..256. 198 distinct fused/split plans of six untuned geometries compile;
Kimi-K2 and DeepSeek-V3 shapes pass the reference check on 8xH200 (fused
M 1..128 random/hot routing, split M 384/1024).

Summary
Batch-invariant mHC mixing statistics for DeepSeek-V4.1's hyper-connection layers, in
mhc.py
:
hc_mix_stats
computes the per-row mixing projections and sum of squares over a fixed number of K slices with
tf32x3
dots, so a row's result is bitwise identical whether computed alone or in a batch;
hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn
fuses the slice reduction with the sinkhorn normalisation that
hc_split_sinkhorn
performs.
Two compensated variants of the same projection for large batches, keeping the fp32 weight exact on the tensor cores:
hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_bf16x3
(Triton, three bf16 weight components, one activation read) and
hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_deepgemm
(tf32 high part plus fp32 residual through DeepGEMM), with
split_bf16_hc_weight
/
split_tf32_hc_weight
preparing the weight parts. Both accumulate over
_HC_MIX_COMPENSATED_SLICES
and share the sinkhorn reduce kernel; sizes come from the input shapes and
hc_mult
.
hc_split_sinkhorn
answers an empty batch directly instead of launching a zero-sized grid, which the TileLang backend rejects.
Changes to existing kernels
hc_split_sinkhorn
: the empty-batch return only. Its existing caller already returns before reaching it with no tokens, so results on existing models are unchanged; the guard is for callers that do not pre-check.
Verification
Sinkhorn arithmetic (eps placement, iteration count, RMS scaling order) matches the existing Triton
hc_split_sinkhorn
port and the reference implementation.
The two compensated variants produce bitwise identical outputs to their previous standalone-module versions for M in {4096, 5000, 8192} (bf16x3) and {128, 1000, 4096} (DeepGEMM) at K = 20480.
test_mhc_kernels.py
and
test_hc_combine.py
cover the untouched kernels of the module.

Motivation
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Hopper spends substantial decode time in group32 dense GEMMs, capacity-sized indexer work, mHC statistics, and padded Marlin MoE projections. This PR tunes those paths. On Blackwell, flattened prefill selection also launches separate mask, sort, slot-map and raw-offset operations; the added integer kernel combines them.
Changes
Tune Hopper group32 GEMMs and reuse exact BF16 expansions of eligible FP8 weights, preserving activation quantization boundaries and the original fallbacks.
Use live paged indexer lengths and variable-length top-k; fuse masking, sorting and slot mapping.
Enable guarded Hopper mHC combine/norm and compensated BF16 projection paths, with decode statistics overlap.
Preserve intermediate activation rounding in fused clipped SwiGLU; defer MXFP4 padding until Marlin repacking.
On SM100-family CUDA GPUs, fuse flattened prefill selection into one integer kernel. Keep the changing visible slot count as a non-specialized runtime argument, so new context lengths do not create new JIT variants. Hopper retains its existing Torch selection path.
Pinned validation

GB300 accuracy uses2048 prefill budgets, because upstream main's FlashMLA scheduling metadata exceeds its48KB shared-memory implementation limit on a GSM8K batch at the default16K budget. Performance comparisons use the same16K budget on every arm and are kept separate. AIME24 candidate versus ordinary PR changes by−0.625 percentage points; truncations40→42,14 correct→wrong and11 wrong→correct. There is also one additional wrong nontruncated answer. The higher-cap paired run still has AIME24 −0.625 percentage points (456→453 correct; truncations22→24;7 correct→wrong,4 reverse), and GSM8K −0.1516 percentage points (1279→1277; neither arm truncated). These scores do not prove identical generation or statistical accuracy equivalence.
Correctness coverage
Existing H200 focused regression:582 passed,60 skipped,16 subtests passed on the rebased runtime.
New integer selection/CUDA Graph/cache-reuse cases:34 passed on real GB300 SM100 dispatch, and34 passed on H200 with the SM100 entry mocked to exercise the integer helper.
Full GB300 indexer test file:133 passed,2 skipped.
Real-model8K/32K prefill audit at concurrency1/16:1908 calls across four ranks, with both page and raw indices exactly equal to the original Torch operations. Rows1–16384, visible slots1–48900. This is integer-mapping evidence, not a substitute for generation-quality evaluation.
A second actual-model audit dispatches fusion before any reference GPU work:1908 calls,477 per rank, with exact page/raw index agreement. Padding is separately covered by the unit tests.
Actual model GPU traces contain40
_finish_flat_indexer_topk_kernel
events per rank; all four original trace files are retained with source hashes.
Pinned pre-commit and diff whitespace checks passed. CI is not fully green: the existing AMD raw-draft-metadata test still needs alignment with main's deferred metadata API; no ROCm validation is claimed.
Memory and weight updates
The Hopper derived caches trade GPU memory for throughput. In the original weight-load measurement, memory increased72.71→75.43GB/GPU and max_total_num_tokens fell16,012,800→14,223,104 at the same static memory fraction. These are the original configuration's measurements, not newly measured final-commit memory numbers.
Online weight updates require disabling both derived caches with
SGLANG_OPT_HOPPER_BLOCK_FP8_BF16=0
and
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0
; otherwise updates fail before writing weights. Other TP/EP layouts are not covered by the reported serving comparisons.

def _get_priority_backends() -> list[Mxfp4MoeBackend]:
    """Get available backends in priority order. SM100+ prefers DeepGEMM FP4 /
    TRTLLM MXFP8; SM90 falls through to Triton_unfused or Marlin (the
    backend-level ``is_supported_config`` check filters by device capability).
    """
    if current_platform.is_rocm():
        return [
            Mxfp4MoeBackend.AITER_MXFP4_BF16,
            Mxfp4MoeBackend.EMULATION,
        ]
    if current_platform.is_xpu():
        return [Mxfp4MoeBackend.XPU]
    if current_platform.is_cpu():
        return [Mxfp4MoeBackend.CPU]
    _AVAILABLE_BACKENDS = [
        Mxfp4MoeBackend.FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8,
        Mxfp4MoeBackend.DEEPGEMM_MXFP4,
        # TRITON_UNFUSED has bug with MTP support
        # TODO re-enable after kernel is fixed
        # TRITON_UNFUSED
        Mxfp4MoeBackend.MARLIN,
        Mxfp4MoeBackend.BATCHED_MARLIN,
    ]
    return _AVAILABLE_BACKENDS

FILE vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang_kernels.py:58-98; SHA256 61a384a091344d8207a04b2b7c74d30a81626eec4c068cf1dd034699cbfc34b5
# every (tile_n, n_thr) pair is one more kernel to compile. Tuned on GB300
# (hc_mult 4, hidden_size 5120 and 7168) against the separate post + split-k
# GEMM it replaces; the bands are coarse because the loss against a per-shape
# optimum is ~1-2%, while one fixed config gives up to 18% at the top of the
# range.
_FUSED_POST_PRE_N_THR = 128
_FUSED_POST_PRE_MAX_TOKENS = 32


def mhc_fused_post_pre_split_config(
    num_tokens: int, hidden_size: int, hc_mult: int
) -> tuple[int, int, int] | None:
    """Pick ``(tile_n, n_splits, n_thr)`` for the fused post + pre-norm GEMM.

    Returns None when a separate post kernel followed by a split-k GEMM is the
    better choice, or when the hidden size does not divide evenly across the
    fused kernel's block. One source of truth for the dispatch decision, the
    compile key and the launch, which must agree.
    """
    if num_tokens > _FUSED_POST_PRE_MAX_TOKENS:
        return None
    n_thr = _FUSED_POST_PRE_N_THR
    if hidden_size % n_thr:
        return None
    # The projection tiles supply the parallelism a small token count cannot,
    # so the tile grows with the batch: 1.3x at one token and 1.03x at 32
    # against a split-k GEMM given the split its own estimator computes.
    if num_tokens < 16:
        tile_n, n_splits = 2, 8
    else:
        tile_n, n_splits = 6, 8
    # The kernel drops projection tiles and k-slices it cannot fill evenly.
    mix_size = hc_mult * (hc_mult + 2)
    while tile_n > 1 and mix_size % tile_n:
        tile_n -= 1
    while n_splits > 1 and hidden_size % (n_splits * n_thr):
        n_splits //= 2
    return tile_n, n_splits, n_thr

# The fused all-reduce + mHC kernel of the overlap path, built once by
# init_mhc_all_reduce.
_all_reduce_mhc: "AllReduceMHC | None" = None


def supports_mhc_overlap(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> bool:
    """Check kernel requirements and safety of sharing the coefficient stream."""
    config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
    # DeepGEMM's prenorm kernel requires K % 64 == 0, N % 8 == 0, and N <= 32.
    mix_size = config.hc_mult * (config.hc_mult + 2)
    return (
        current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
        and is_deep_gemm_supported()
        and config.hidden_size % 64 == 0
        and 0 < mix_size <= 32
        and mix_size % 8 == 0
        and not vllm_config.parallel_config.use_ubatching
    )


def supports_mhc_all_reduce(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> bool:
    parallel = vllm_config.parallel_config
    config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
    if (
        parallel.tensor_parallel_size != 4
        or parallel.enable_expert_parallel
        or config.hidden_size != 5120
        or config.hc_mult != 4
    ):

    # The custom all-reduce's MNNVL buffers succeed exactly when NVLink
    # multicast does, which the fused kernel's own mailbox needs too.
    comm = cast("CudaCommunicator", get_tp_group().device_communicator).ca_comm
    return comm is not None and bool(comm.mnnvl_lamport_ag_multicast_ptr)

title: [NVIDIA][AgentX] GB300 GLM-5.2 NVFP4 Dynamo+SGLang: PP4-prefill disagg and TP4/TP8 agg points / GB300 GLM-5.2 NVFP4 Dynamo+SGLang：PP4 prefill 分离式与 TP4/TP8 聚合配置点
body:
Moves both GB300 GLM-5.2 NVFP4 Dynamo + SGLang AgentX keys to `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261016-a93f16f0` (multi-arch digest pinned). The aggregated key runs the ai-dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261015` bundled in the image (`dynamo.install: false`). The disaggregated key installs the ai-dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261016` wheel. The disaggregated points move to one PP4 prefill worker per node (sgl-project/sglang#39378).

| Config key | Topology | Conc | Nodes | Key settings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `glm5.2-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-agg` | TP4 | 1 | 1 | MTP 4 steps, fp8 KV cache, cutedsl BF16 GEMM, 8 running requests and decode graphs, HiCache 100 GB/rank |
| | TP8 | 1 | 2 | MTP 5 steps, 2 running requests and decode graphs, HiCache 100 GB/rank |
| `glm5.2-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-disagg` | 1x PP4 prefill + 5x TP4 decode | 30 | 6 | prefill HiCache 100 GB/rank, decode radix cache, 24 requests per decode worker |
| | 1x PP4 prefill + 3x TP4 decode | 40 | 4 | as c30 |
| | 1x PP4 prefill + 1x DEP8 decode | 56 | 3 | 8k prefill chunks, prefill mem-fraction 0.75, 32 requests per decode rank |
| | 3x PP4 prefill + 1x DEP8 decode | 216 | 5 | prefill layer split 20,20,20,18, 32 requests per decode rank |
| | 3x PP4 prefill + 1x DEP8 decode | 264 | 5 | as c216 with 8k prefill chunks, prefill mem-fraction 0.88, HiCache 185 GB/rank, decode mem-fraction 0.94 |
| | 4x PP4 prefill + 1x DEP16 decode | 256 | 8 | 32 requests per decode rank |

- Every point uses EAGLE MTP on the checkpoint's built-in NextN head with HiCache write_back DRAM KV offload. Prefill and decode use the same MTP settings (5 steps, top-k 1, 6 draft tokens; TP4 agg uses 4 steps and 5 draft tokens).
- Synthetic acceptance follows the golden GLM-5.2 thinking-on AL: 3.33 at 4 MTP steps and 3.61 at 5. No recipe sets `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` or `SGLANG_NVFP4_CKPT_FP8_NEXTN_MOE`.
- KV transfer uses NIXL; no recipe sets `UCX_*` variables. DEP decode workers set `expert-parallel-size` explicitly to match the master config's `ep`.
- Prefill workers advertise a 3600 s session-affinity TTL to the prefill router; decode workers advertise an active-request weight of 8192 to the decode router, so decode routing balances request counts.
- `dram-utilization` is raised to 0.85 for the disaggregated key so c264's 185 GB/rank prefill HiCache plus the DSA-indexer host pool fit; the aggregated key stays at 0.80.
- Tachometer and the Dynamo OTel collector are disabled.
- Removes the aggregated TP8 c2/c4 points, the DEP4-prefill 1P2D/1P4D/1P6D points, the DEP8/DEP16 2P1D c192 point, and `disagg-2p1d-p-dep8-d-dep16-c192-mtp.yaml`, which only that point used.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

- `glm5.2-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-agg`：
  - TP4 c1（1 个节点）：MTP 4 步，fp8 KV cache，cutedsl BF16 GEMM，8 个运行请求与 decode graph，HiCache 每 rank 100 GB。
  - TP8 c1（2 个节点）：MTP 5 步，2 个运行请求与 decode graph，HiCache 每 rank 100 GB。
- `glm5.2-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-disagg`：
  - 1P5D c30（1 个 PP4 prefill + 5 个 TP4 decode，6 个节点）与 1P3D c40（4 个节点）：prefill HiCache 每 rank 100 GB，decode 启用 radix cache，每个 decode worker 24 个请求。
  - 1P1D c56（1 个 PP4 prefill + 1 个 DEP8 decode，3 个节点）：prefill chunk 8k，prefill mem-fraction 0.75。
  - 3P1D c216（3 个 PP4 prefill + 1 个 DEP8 decode，5 个节点）：prefill 层划分 20,20,20,18。
  - 3P1D c264（5 个节点）：同 c216，另使用 8k prefill chunk、prefill mem-fraction 0.88、HiCache 每 rank 185 GB、decode mem-fraction 0.94。
  - 4P1D c256（4 个 PP4 prefill + 1 个 DEP16 decode，8 个节点）。
  - DEP decode 每个 rank 32 个请求。
- 所有配置点均使用基于 checkpoint 内置 NextN head 的 EAGLE MTP，并启用 HiCache write_back DRAM KV offload。prefill 与 decode 使用相同的 MTP 设置（5 步、top-k 1、6 个 draft token；TP4 聚合为 4 步、5 个 draft token）。
- 模拟接受长度采用 GLM-5.2 thinking-on 的 golden AL：MTP 4 步为 3.33，5 步为 3.61。recipe 中未设置 `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` 或 `SGLANG_NVFP4_CKPT_FP8_NEXTN_MOE`。
- KV 传输使用 NIXL，recipe 中未设置任何 `UCX_*` 变量。DEP decode worker 显式设置 `expert-parallel-size`，与 master config 的 `ep` 一致。
- prefill worker 向 prefill router 声明 3600 秒 session affinity TTL；decode worker 向 decode router 声明 active-request 权重 8192，使 decode 路由按请求数均衡。
- 分离式 key 的 `dram-utilization` 提高到 0.85，以容纳 c264 每 rank 185 GB 的 prefill HiCache 与 DSA indexer 主机内存池；聚合 key 保持 0.80。
- 关闭 Tachometer 与 Dynamo OTel collector。
- 移除聚合 TP8 c2/c4、DEP4 prefill 的 1P2D/1P4D/1P6D、DEP8/DEP16 2P1D c192 配置点，以及仅被 2P1D 使用的 `disagg-2p1d-p-dep8-d-dep16-c192-mtp.yaml`。

title: perf(dsv4): repin MI355X vLLM AgentX to the 2026-09-20 ROCm nightly / 将 MI355X vLLM AgentX 重新固定至 2026-09-20 ROCm nightly
body:
## Description

Repin the DSV4 MI355X vLLM AgentX recipe (`dsv4-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp`) to the newest published ROCm nightly, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-d05da62e9ccdf8e342b15bf6785d83224cc165af` (digest `sha256:461e9c79…`, Docker Hub pushed `2026-09-20T06:32:10Z`, tag commit vllm-project/vllm@d05da62e), up from `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-eed1f3d0c6043bd494424a22443ee198dd56f657` on `main` (pinned in #3071).

The original revision of this PR pinned the 2026-09-15 build `nightly-rocm100-cd10ed6f…`. That tag is now five nightlies old, so the pin moved forward to the current one. `main` has also been merged into the branch, which moved this PR's `perf-changelog.yaml` entry to the physical end of the file; `main`'s changelog bytes are preserved byte-for-byte.

### What the new nightly adds

`d05da62e` is 294 upstream commits ahead of `cd10ed6f` and 352 ahead of the CSA merge commit. Besides [vllm-project/vllm#51794](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51794), which enables CSA (Compressed Sparse Attention) multi-stream overlap for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm so the two compressor `wkv_gate` GEMMs run on aux HIP streams instead of serially on the main stream during decode, the range brings in:

| Upstream PR | Change |
| --- | --- |
| [#57132](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57132) | Reverts the DeepSeek-V4 accuracy breakdown on ROCm (accuracy-relevant for the eval leg) |
| [#57465](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57465) | Fixes fused MoE expert distribution for DeepSeek V4 |
| [#56853](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56853) | Enables HCA dual-stream overlap for DeepSeek-V4 |
| [#50455](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50455) | Fixes the sparse-indexer logits collapse on gfx950/gfx942 |
| [#56743](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56743), [#57434](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57434) | gfx950 decode top-k optimization and ragged-metadata reuse across layers |
| [#55934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55934) | triton + triton_kernels 3.8 MXFP4 MoE support for DeepSeek-V4 |
| [#56885](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56885) | Bumps AITER to v0.1.22.post1 |

No recipe fields other than `image` change. The search space, concurrency lists (`1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64` without DP attention and `64, 128, 192` with DP attention plus `vllm-router` 0.1.14), `dram-utilization: 0.60`, and the `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` workaround from #3071 are untouched. `benchmarks/single_node/agentic/dsv4_fp4_mi355x_vllm_mtp.sh` reads the image from `amd-master.yaml` and is unmodified.

Note for the reviewer: this range contains several AITER and MXFP4 MoE fixes ([#57426](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57426), [#57204](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57204), [#56568](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56568)) that touch the shared-expert fusion path the `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` workaround guards against. The workaround is deliberately left in place here because nothing in this PR establishes that it is safe to drop; re-testing it is a separate change.

## AI model disclosure

- Model/version: `claude-opus-5-thinking-high` as exposed by the Cursor runtime. The exact upstream build string is not exposed, so it could not be verified beyond this identifier.
- Role: Queried Docker Hub for the newest published `nightly-rocm100` tag and its digest, verified upstream commit ancestry via the GitHub API, updated `configs/amd-master.yaml` and the `perf-changelog.yaml` entry, merged `main` and resolved the changelog conflict with `infx.workflows.prepare_perf_changelog_merge`, ran the local validation below, and wrote this description. No work was delegated to other agents or models.
- Earlier revisions of this PR were prepared with a model the current runtime cannot identify; that disclosure could not be verified retroactively.

## Type of Change

- [x] Configuration change

## Validation

Local, on head commit `10adbcd93`:

- `python3 -m infx.workflows.validate_perf_changelog --base-ref origin/main --head-ref HEAD` → `Validated perf-changelog.yaml: final newline present and matrix generated`.
- `infx.matrix.generate test-config --config-keys dsv4-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp` emits 12 rows, and every row's `image` is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-d05da62e9ccdf8e342b15bf6785d83224cc165af`. Inspected fields are unchanged versus the pre-bump generation: `tp: 8`, `pp: 1`, `ep: 1`, `dcp-size: 1`, `pcp-size: 1`, `spec-decoding: mtp`, `scenario-type: agentic-coding`, `kv-offloading: none`, `run-eval: false`, concurrency `1/4/8/16/32/40/48/56/64` at `dp-attn: false` and `64/128/192` at `dp-attn: true` with `router: {vllm-router, 0.1.14}`.
- `pytest utils/test_process_changelog.py utils/changelog_gate_tests/` → 139 passed.
- YAML parse of `configs/amd-master.yaml`, `configs/runners.yaml`, and `perf-changelog.yaml`; `git diff --check`; `bash -n benchmarks/single_node/agentic/dsv4_fp4_mi355x_vllm_mtp.sh`.

## Description

Add `dsv41flash-fp4-b300-vllm-dspark`: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash fixed-sequence serving on two B300 GPUs (TP2), 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, concurrency 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. Existing TP2/TP4 AgentX configs are unchanged. Updated from TP1 at the user's request; the TP1 sweep was cancelled.

- Pin `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-ddd6fbca148a867aad1fcab7ec72f582b9977db4`; the Docker Hub tag exists for amd64.
- Explicit Engram CPU offload. Expert weights and FP8 KV stay on GPU; the TP1 recipe's 60 GiB expert-weight offload is removed.
- Use native five-token DSpark with probabilistic drafting and real block verification. No synthetic acceptance, engine patches, draft-weight changes, or draft-specific precision overrides.
- Route vLLM through the shared fixed-sequence client and forward `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41` to the pinned image's native tokenizer adapter. The checkpoint has no HF chat template, so generic AutoTokenizer chat rendering is insufficient.
- Canary-gated `full-sweep-fail-fast` scope is this new fixed-sequence key only. Default eval selection covers c64 and c128. No merge requested.

Upstream reference: [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.yaml). This B300 TP2 fixed-sequence recipe remains unverified until its replacement sweep and evals pass.

- Upstream SRT `validate_config_file`: all variants pass.
- InferenceX native selector: exactly one recipe per concurrency, two serving GPUs; fixed-sequence dispatch retains real verification.
- Focused tests: 77 passed across fixed-sequence client routing, native SRT binding/launchers, and benchmark client/tokenizer behavior.
- `ruff check infx`, `ruff format --check infx`, Bash syntax, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local test environment note: the existing H100 launcher test requires `RUNNER_NAME`; the initial run failed on that missing input. With `RUNNER_NAME=local-validation`, all 77 focused tests pass. No H100 code or fixture was changed.

title: [AMD][MI355X] Kimi-K3 vLLM AgentX FP8 per-channel linear quantization-config / [AMD][MI355X] Kimi-K3 vLLM AgentX 新增 FP8 per-channel linear quantization-config
body:
## Summary
- Add `--quantization-config '{"linear":"fp8_per_channel","ignore":["*kv_b_proj","*vision_tower*","*mm_projector*"]}'` to the base `agg` args of the Kimi-K3 MI355X vLLM AgentX recipe (`benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/kimik3/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`), so every point of `kimik3-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp` (added in #3561) inherits it.
- vLLM online-quantizes the target's linear layers to FP8 per-channel at load: 489 layers per rank (attention in/out projections, `q_b_proj`, `fused_qkv_a_proj`, `g_proj`, `f_b_proj`, shared-expert and dense MLPs). `kv_b_proj` stays BF16, and the routed experts stay MXFP4 from the checkpoint.
- Image (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-36768d1bfd39094681cdbc8cb37d4b31c0729c89`), concurrencies, KV offload and all other flags are unchanged.
- Append the `perf-changelog.yaml` entry.

## Measurements
One MI355X node, clean image above (no patch, no aiter config override), `server.sh`-style TP8, DSpark k=7 with synthetic acceptance 3.84, `max-num-seqs` 2, `vllm bench serve` random 8k/1k:

| Concurrency | Output tok/s (without → with) | Mean TPOT ms | Mean TTFT ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 282.93 → 289.90 (+2.5%) | 6.51 → 6.32 | 7085 → 6953 |
| 8 | 294.17 → 303.27 (+3.1%) | 6.41 → 6.20 | 19130 → 18583 |

## Draft model precision

The load log lists only target layers as quantized.

title: Add opt-in borrowed receive storage for compact BF16 dispatch
body:
`dispatch(..., borrow_recv=True)` skips the activation copy of the dispatch epilogue: the epilogue writes only metadata plus a row map and returns a `DispatchRecvView` (`slab`, `row_indices`) over the communication buffer, which an indexed consumer such as a gathered GEMM reads directly. The view holds an exclusive lease: `release(*streams)` orders the next communication after the consumers, and dispatch/combine/LB calls/`destroy()` reject an active view. Supported: fresh compact BF16 dispatch within one NVLink domain with CPU counts and `defer_epilogue=False`; everything else is rejected up front. Default behavior is unchanged.

8×H200, deterministic, hidden 3072, top-8, 16 local experts, dispatch plus the same indexed consumer: −13.1% at 8192 tokens/rank and −13.5% at 16384, but +15.9% at 1024, hence opt-in. Fixed-route serial forward only; no overlap or training-throughput claim. Combined with DeepGEMM #463 in a live EP8 + gate/up GEMM + SwiGLU step: −17%. Raw cycles and the reproducer: [gist](https://gist.github.com/yuweih205/d3fd1e4c3fcb97364f36ec8fda996cfe).

Test: `python tests/ep/test_recv_view.py --num-processes 8` (bitwise payload/metadata against the gathered inputs, replay/combine after release, delayed cross-stream readers, invalid-mode rejection).

Re-validated 2026-10-16 at 71157be (100350f differs only in documentation; native code byte-identical to the measured build) on 8×H200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132: `test_recv_view.py` 16/16 cases under both `EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM` policies; the EP8 functional suite passes with CPU counts for direct and deferred epilogues. With `--do-cpu-sync 0` the unmodified suite stops at its full-capacity `recv_x_twice` comparison on this branch exactly as on upstream main; with the valid-prefix comparison from #786 it passes on both.

DeepEP V2.5 introduces dedicated communication buffers for EP, PP, Engram, and bucket collectives, together with new primitives for redundant-expert load balancing. GPU kernels are now compiled through DeepJIT, while installation builds the host C++ extension.
This release also fully removes V1 and its NVSHMEM dependency.
New Features
Dedicated buffer APIs
@LyricZhao
Split ElasticBuffer into EPBuffer, EngramBuffer, PPBuffer, and BucketBuffer, sharing the BufferBase lifecycle.
Add BufferAllocator for planning symmetric tensor allocations before buffer construction.
Expert load balancing
@cqzhangyu
@LyricZhao
Add EPBuffer.lb_prefetch_weights to transfer expert weights and quantization scales to redundant expert slots over NVLink.
Add EPBuffer.lb_reduce_grads to accumulate redundant experts’ FP32 gradients into the original experts.
These primitives support the dynamic expert-replication approach explored by MoonEP and UltraEP. Replication planning and token rerouting are supplied by the integrating framework.
Bucket collectives for CP and DP
@jason-huang03
@bucket-xv
@cqzhangyu
@dromniscience
@sphish
Batched all-gather, reduce-scatter, and all-reduce across NVLink, RDMA, and hybrid domains.
Sessions for communicating ordinary PyTorch tensors through temporary bucket storage.
EP improvements
@LyricZhao
Deferred dispatch/combine epilogues for communication-computation overlap.
Cached expanded layouts and zero padding between experts.
Engram
@tianr22
@sphish
Multi-layer storage on GPU or CPU, with one completion hook per layer.
Build and runtime
@LyricZhao
Move GPU kernel compilation to DeepJIT.
Remove installation-time NVCC compilation and GPU architecture selection.
Notes
Migrate from ElasticBuffer to the dedicated buffer APIs.
V1 APIs, legacy documentation, and NVSHMEM support have been removed.
Bucket collectives, Engram, and PP remain experimental.
Requires NVIDIA Hopper or newer GPUs, CUDA 13.1+, NCCL 2.32.3+, PyTorch 2.10+ with CUDA support, Python 3.10+, and a C++20 compiler.

title: perf: skip unused source-order sorts for expanded deterministic dispatch
body:
Fresh expanded deterministic dispatch runs its own stable expert/source sort, and cached expanded dispatch writes into the saved sorted slots, so the compact source-order sort computed before them is never consumed. `deterministic_sort` now returns early for cached expanded dispatch and only builds the compact sort inside the compact branch.

| Deterministic layout | Sorts before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh expanded | 2 | 1 |
| Cached expanded | 1 | 0 |
| Compact | 1 | 1 |

Two repeated-dispatch checks in `tests/ep/test_ep.py` now compare only the valid receive prefix: unused sync-free capacity is undefined even without expert-alignment padding.

8×H200 (PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132): the EP8 functional suite passes (72 direct + 36 deferred configurations, 12,288 rank-dispatch checks across both record-stream policies, BF16/FP8, CPU/GPU counts, fresh/cached); fresh expanded dispatch at 1024 tokens/rank, hidden 3072, top-8 is 4.7–5.8% faster (12/12 process repeats on each of two nodes, A/A spread 0.81%). Per-process data: [gist](https://gist.github.com/yuweih205/1696535356c2654b255f28617f9fa96f).

title: [RFC] Benchmark valid-prefix sorting and count prefetch for compact dispatch
body:
Add a standalone experimental benchmark that separates valid-prefix deterministic sorting from early receive-count copies for compact BF16 dispatch. It compares four factorial arms with both native sync-free and native deferred materialization, using the same independent GEMM work and synchronized end-to-end readiness timing.

This is a **draft experiment/benchmark PR**, with no production API or default change. On eight H200 GPUs, all eight measured scenarios remain slower than native deferred. Valid-prefix sorting helps relative to the matching full-capacity sort, while early count copies do not provide a consistent additional benefit. The documentation retains all six arms, all cases and all three fresh-process summaries.

The existing GPU study covers 1920 correctness/smoke rank/cases plus 1152 full-performance preflight rank/cases: independent dispatch-reference equality, counts, combine, cached replay, saved-view backward, both allocation streams, both record-stream policies, and uneven/duplicate/skewed/masked routes. The published execution code matches the measured script; only its docstring and historical-source log label changed. Local compilation, AST equivalence, evidence-count checks and `git diff --check` passed before publication.

See `tests/ep/prefix_sort_experiment.md` for reproduction, complete results and scope. This is a one-NVLink-domain compact BF16 experiment; it does not establish full-training gains or cover FP8/expanded/hybrid dispatch.

title: Document and test ordinary sync-free receive tensor lifetimes
body:
## Summary

Document and exercise the lifetime contract of **ordinary independently allocated receive outputs** from compact `dispatch(do_cpu_sync=False)`.

- Add a README paragraph explaining valid receive prefixes, output ownership versus stream readiness, the explicit ready-event/`record_stream` handoff, and why a prefix view retains the full capacity allocation.
- Add a 166-line standalone native regression for saved-view backward after later dispatches and delayed cross-stream consumers under allocator pressure.

No production Python/C++/CUDA implementation, default, or API changes. The internal dispatch copy epilogue still runs. This is not borrowed communication-buffer storage or a zero-copy dispatch implementation.

## Regression coverage

The new `tests/ep/test_recv_lifetime.py` uses the independent NCCL dispatch reference and requires bitwise equality of payloads, local expert indices, routing weights, source-token metadata, and the saved-activation weight gradient.

Each process run covers:

- Deterministic dispatch off/on; output allocation on the compute/communication stream.
- Uneven inputs, balanced routes, masked routes, and highly skewed routing with empty receivers.
- Two selected experts on the same destination rank, distinguishing unique receive rows from token/expert assignments.
- A prefix saved with `ctx.save_for_backward`, followed by three additional dispatches through the same buffer before backward.
- A delayed reader on another stream, dropping the original receive allocation references and allocating/filling four same-capacity tensors on the allocation stream. The copy destination and allocator warm-up are prepared before the delay. Pressure writes must finish while a **pre-read** event is still pending; a pending post-copy event alone is insufficient.

Scheduling can miss the pressure window. All ranks agree on numerical correctness and window validity, then retry in collective lockstep with a longer delay (at most three attempts). Actual corruption fails immediately; an inconclusive window is never silently reported as coverage.

The consumer handoff uses a CUDA event captured **after the first dispatch-event wait**, including its deterministic-sort hook. It does not depend on repeated waits on the original `EventOverlap`; that is separate from this lifetime coverage.

## Validation

### Current polished revision

Head: `97fa6d18ff717df99acbdbb862325bda3d4a0d46`, based on public main `b5a33eefda39485f438dc764695b71ba7b9249b6`.

The current 166-line test passed on H200 with PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, CUDA 13.2 and NCCL 2.32.3. Each native lifetime policy was run once with eight ranks: 24 distributed saved-prefix/backward cases in total, with 24 valid delayed-consumer allocator-pressure windows. This is positive coverage of the current reorganized test; the historical negative and scheduling controls below were not rerun against this revision.

```bash
EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=0 python tests/ep/test_recv_lifetime.py --num-processes 8 --num-tokens 64 --hidden 512
EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=1 python tests/ep/test_recv_lifetime.py --num-processes 8 --num-tokens 64 --hidden 512
```

### Historical validation of the earlier test version

Tested commit: `01c31d0d75f155ca00ba933a6b9ab7a01459169e`, based on upstream `93eb6eb238127e96c6d7a4a625a6dad158348509`. The results in this subsection belong to that earlier test version, not to a rerun of the current 166-line test.

One node, eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs in a single NVLink domain; PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, CUDA runtime 13.2, loaded NCCL 2.32.3. The unchanged upstream native extension and the tested source archive/test-file hashes were verified. No borrowed-view implementation or event-wrapper patch was included.

Both native lifetime policies were run in fresh processes, three repeats each, using the same two command lines above.

Validation controls: `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`, `EP_REUSE_NCCL_COMM=0`, `EP_BUFFER_DEBUG=0`, `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none`, `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8`. Seed 42; deterministic PyTorch algorithms enabled with uninitialized-memory filling disabled.

| Native record-stream policy | Fresh repeats per arm | Positive rank/cases | Exact saved-view gradients | Deleted-record rejections | Forced-retry passes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=0` | 3 | 288/288 | 288/288 | 96/96 | 96/96 |
| `EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=1` | 3 | 288/288 | 288/288 | 96/96 | 96/96 |

Two additional controls were run outside the PR using that exact earlier public test source, without changing DeepEP's implementation:

- **Negative control:** AST-remove exactly the consumer-side `prefix.record_stream(reader)` expression from `cross_stream_pressure`. For balanced nonempty receives, run both deterministic modes and both allocation streams. All 24 distributed cases were rejected by the specific `CROSS_STREAM_RECEIVE_MISMATCH` assertion; actual local data corruption was observed in all 192 rank/cases. Other assertions or an ineffective window do not count as detection.
- **Scheduling control:** synchronize only rank 0 immediately before its first `pending_before` query. All ranks must retry attempt 0 together and pass on a later effective attempt. All 24 distributed cases / 192 rank/cases passed.

An earlier draft's post-copy-event stress missed the deleted-record mutation. That draft is not the sensitivity evidence above; the pre-read/completed-pressure ordering and destination preallocation were added before rerunning all historical arms.

All eighteen historical fresh launches exited successfully. Source/input hashes, exact per-rank coverage, control mutation identities and completion/exit sentinels were audited from downloaded logs. Archive SHA256: `834a31fa761e439678244ae49cdaf98491ead5fb23b4724500ba038366eac777`.

Local checks for that earlier revision: Python compilation, Ruff 0.6.5, YAPF 0.40.2 (no diff), and `git diff --check` passed.

## Scope

This establishes component lifetime/gradient correctness for ordinary compact BF16 receives in one physical NVLink domain. It does not establish full-model convergence, training throughput gains, borrowed-storage safety, FP8/expanded layouts, or multi-node hybrid routing. Capacity-retention assertions deliberately distinguish logical tensor bytes from retained storage bytes.

Inspired by the SM90 FP8×FP8 MegaMoE implementation introduced in
deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#383
and the SM90 FP8×NVFP4 work in
AichenF/DeepGEMM@megamoe_nvfp4_dev_m
, this PR adds an optimized FP8×MXFP4 MegaMoE backend for SM90 GPUs. Keeping routed-expert weights in MXFP4 enables native reuse of Hugging Face MXFP4 MoE checkpoints, while substantially reducing GPU memory pressure by avoiding a persistent FP8 weight expansion.
Summary
Unified SM90 persistent execution.
Unlike
[SM90] Add FP8 MegaMoE support
#383
, this implementation fuses dispatch, routed/shared L1 and L2, and combine into one persistent kernel. It adapts the SM100 ring-buffer and wave-interleaved scheduler to a cluster-free Hopper design using register-resident WGMMA, one CTA per task, and two resident CTAs per SM.
Humming-inspired MXFP4×FP8 compute path.
Routed weights remain packed MXFP4 in global memory. Model-load preprocessing rebases the K32 UE8M0 exponents into bounded relative scales plus one FP32 secondary scale per expert, following the fused MXFP4×FP8 approach used by Humming. During execution, packed E2M1 tiles are loaded into compact shared-memory staging, decoded and expanded on the fly into E4M3 FP8 tiles, and then consumed by Hopper WGMMA. This avoids materializing a persistent FP8 copy of the routed weights.

做运行时下界裁剪。因此 num_ranks>1 且 num_tokens≤32 时，若某 expert 收到超过 kMaxSwapABTokens 个 token（如 8 rank × M=8 × topk6 随机路由并不罕见），超出部分不写 L2 acts/SF，combine 结果静默错误。现有测试覆盖不到：production.flash_m8/16/32 用 forced ring-wrap 轮转路由（每 expert ≤2 token），随机路由场景均为 hidden=512（swap-AB 关闭）。建议：桶按 min(num_tokens*num_ranks, 64) 选取，或 valid_m>kMaxSwapABTokens 时回退常规路径，至少加 DG_TRAP_ONLY_DEVICE_ASSERT(valid_m<=kMaxSwapABTokens) 并补多 rank 热点路由测试。
