title: [Kernel] Fuse DeepEP-v2 decode globalize+align into one launch
body:
Fuses the DeepEP-v2 INDEXED cudagraph-decode metadata chain (`_globalize_recv_topk_idx` + `moe_align_block_size` + `count_and_sort_expert_tokens`) into a single CUDA launch for the Humming path.

`recv_topk_idx` holds **local** expert ids; the kernel bins by local id (align/sort) while writing back the global id, and reads `num_recv` on-device from `psum[-1]` so it is CUDA-graph safe. Sizing by local (not global) experts shrinks the sentinel/`expert_ids` region by ~`ep_size` under EP. The fused kernel also produces the optional scatter index used by Humming for larger EP batches.

The fused path is selected for CUDA Humming INDEXED experts when DeepEP-v2 defers globalization during CUDA-graph decode. Other paths keep the standalone globalization and alignment behavior.

## Numbers

H200, EP32, INDEXED decode — fused vs the 3-kernel chain, measured before the October 6 rebase:

| tokens | speedup |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1.23x |
| 8 | 1.14x |
| 32 | 1.16x |
| 64 | 1.36x |
| 128 | 1.67x |
| 256 (n=8192) | 2.01x |

## Testing

After the October 12 rebase onto upstream commit `c599b5971`: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed on the six changed Python files; Apple `clang-format` 21 `--dry-run --Werror` passed on the changed CUDA/C++ files; `git diff --check` passed. `git range-diff` confirmed that the functional patch is unchanged apart from adapting paths to upstream's new `csrc/moe` layout. CI then found a stale `libtorch_stable/torch_utils.h` include in the moved CUDA source; commit `52d7e1c15` changes it to `torch_utils.h`, matching the other MoE CUDA files. The corrected include and formatting were checked locally, but the CUDA build needs to rerun in CI. The pinned `clang-format` and mypy hooks passed on the prior October 7 base but were not rerun here. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_globalize_align_block_size.py -v` could not run on the macOS rebase host. The test includes correctness cases for the optional scatter index.

Pending on CUDA hardware: `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` rebuild, the pytest run, and a model evaluation (for example gsm8k) with the fused path active. The kernel originated from a validated standalone prototype; the measurements above have not been repeated on the rebased code.

## Notes

- Not a duplicate — no open PR fused this chain when the PR was created (`gh pr list --search "globalize align"`).
- AI assistance (Claude Code and OpenAI Codex) was used. Human review of the rebase resolution and GPU validation are pending.

Issue body actions
Describe the bug
estimate_local_valid_shape_m()
in
python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/humming.py
returns
topk_ids.nelement()
when no
expected_m
is given (~line 204, carries
# TODO: update for EP and DP
, introduced in
#23754
).
Under EP this counts the global routed elements.
local_expert_mapping
keeps the tensor shape unchanged and writes -1 for non-local experts, so
nelement()
= M_global x top_k, while each rank's GEMM only touches ~1/ep_size of those rows.
The value only drives kernel config selection: the Python block-size ladder in
_prepare_indexed_gemm_kwargs
and the humming launcher's variant lookup (
find_kernel_launch_data
in launcher.cpp). Correctness is unaffected, the launcher validates against real tensor shapes. So under EP every humming MoE GEMM picks its config for a workload ~4x larger than what the rank actually computes (EP4).
We tried the obvious fix, a graph-safe host estimate
max(1, M * top_k / ep_size)
(exact counting needs a D2H sync, illegal under CUDA graph capture). It moves every working point to the true local shape and passes unit tests, but serving regressed:
arm
decode tok/s/req
vs parent
parent (current code)
52.2
-
EP-aware estimate
49.5
-5.1% (perm p=0.003, n=10/arm)
EP-aware + ladder bands recalibrated from per-point kernel microbench
-
-4.0% e2e (C48 median, 3-arm check)
Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (384 routed experts, top_k 6, MXFP4 experts), TP4/EP4, 4x H200-class GPUs, DSPark speculative decoding, random workload at 32-48 concurrency, unique-seed A/B protocol with flush_cache between rounds, cross-session reproducible.
Per-cubin enumeration against the deployed heuristic ladder explains why. The ladder bands were calibrated against the global-element scale, and the two gemm types disagree about what the input even means:
indexed, routed rows ~750-2100: the local-rows input picks kernels 22-26% faster than the global-scale input
grouped, same points: opposite direction, the global-scale input wins by 8-12%
small decode CUDA-graph tiers (<200 rows): both land in the same band, zero effect
re-mapping ladder bands empirically flipped kernel rankings once real routing skew and CUDA-graph replay entered the picture
A single scalar cannot carry both total routed rows and per-expert density once num_local_experts != num_experts. For reference, the masked/DeepEP-LL path already uses
expected_m * num_local_experts
, and DeepEP-normal dispatch carries exact host-side
num_recv_tokens_per_expert
.
Reproduction
Any EP>1 run with
--moe-runner-backend humming
(default gemm type indexed). The wrong value is observable without serving, it is just
topk_ids.nelement()
under EP:
# decode bs=48, top_k=6, EP4: topk_ids (48, 6).nelement() = 288 passed as
# valid_shape_m while the rank's GEMM only handles ~72 rows.
# See estimate_local_valid_shape_m in
# python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/humming.py
Serving A/B protocol:
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 384 --max-concurrency 48
, unique seed per round, /flush_cache between rounds, drop first warmup round, median of 4.
Environment
Python: 3.12.3, PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA: 13.0 (driver 580.105.08)
GPU 0-3: NVIDIA L20X (SM90)
sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+g20518d851, sglang-kernel: 0.4.7
flashinfer: 0.6.18, triton: 3.7.1, transformers: 5.12.1
Possible fixes (for discussion)
(a) Document
valid_shape_m
as a hint defined on the global routed-element scale and leave the estimator as-is (what we reverted to; zero risk).
(b) Make ladder generation convention-aware per gemm_type and re-tune per device.
(c) Extend the launcher/config-selection API to take (rows, local expert count) or tokens-per-expert as a second key.

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] moe: Add a fused CUTLASS MXFP4A8 backend for SM90.
body:
## Motivation This PR adds an SGLang-native CUTLASS **MXFP4A8 fused MoE backend for SM90/Hopper**, targeting MXFP4-expert models such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The implementation keeps expert weights in MXFP4 (E2M1 with block-32 E8M0 scales), dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 E4M3, and executes both expert GEMMs on Hopper FP8 tensor cores. The current scope is deliberately limited to **TP deployments with EP=1**. `EP>1` is not supported by this PR and is rejected explicitly during weight initialization. ## Summary - Add an MXFP4-to-FP8 mixed-input CUTLASS path for SM90. - Add load-time Humming-compatible MXFP4 weight preprocessing. - Add an EP1 fused runtime covering routing metadata preparation, input permutation and quantization, GEMM1, SwiGLU, requantization, GEMM2, output permutation, router weighting, and top-k reduction. - Add shape-specialized SM90 schedulers for serving-time token buckets. - Preserve the existing INT4A8 path unchanged. - Add numerical tests for MXFP4 conversion, scale layouts, grouped GEMM, and cross-backend consistency against FlashInfer. The backend is selected with: ```bash --moe-runner-backend cutlass ``` ### Execution flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant X as BF16 input participant R as Top-k routing participant S as SGLang fused path participant F as FlashInfer participant W as MXFP4 weights participant Y as MoE output X->>R: tokens and topk=6 W-->>S: Humming-compatible view W-->>F: Humming view par SGLang EP1 path R->>S: GPU-built routing metadata S->>S: reorder + per-token FP8 quant S->>S: grouped GEMM1 S->>S: SwiGLU + FP8 requant S->>S: grouped GEMM2 S-->>Y: reorder + router-weight reduction and FlashInfer R->>F: topk IDs + router weights F->>F: bucketed tactic lookup F->>F: fused MoE body F-->>Y: fused finalize end Note over S,F: Same logical MXFP4 weights and routing inputs
Different runtime orchestration and scheduling ``` ## Implementation ### MXFP4A8 tensor-core path Weights remain in checkpoint-native MXFP4. Activations are quantized per token to FP8 E4M3. The E2M1 values `{0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6}` are exactly representable in E4M3, so the E2M1-to-E4M3 conversion uses a lossless signed-nibble lookup. The mixed-input mainloop derives the scale group from `TileK / PackedScalesNum`, allowing the existing INT4A8 group-128 path and the new MXFP4A8 group-32 path to share the same mainloop without changing INT4 behavior. ### Load-time weight preprocessing The EP1 path prepares one runtime representation after checkpoint loading: - interleaved MXFP4 weights; - folded E8M0 offsets; - one residual scale per expert. The representation follows the SM90 Humming preprocessing semantics. Runtime execution is implemented by SGLang AOT kernels. Only the fused representation is retained for EP1 to avoid storing two complete weight layouts on H20. ### Fused EP1 execution `cutlass_mxfp4a8_fused_moe_core` performs: 1. expert-offset, problem-size, and permutation preparation; 2. routed-input reorder and per-token FP8 quantization; 3. grouped GEMM1; 4. fused SwiGLU, optional clamp, and FP8 requantization; 5. grouped GEMM2; 6. output reorder, FP32 router-weight multiplication, `routed_scaling_factor`, and top-k reduction. For `M <= 64`, metadata preparation and shuffled input quantization use a bounded fused CUDA path. Larger batches use the AOT metadata and quantization kernels without host synchronization. Intermediate tensors are retained in reusable workspaces. ### SM90 scheduling The implementation includes: - a persistent single-warpgroup ping-pong kernel for tiny and arbitrary serving-time shapes; - a precomputed grouped scheduler with prebuilt TMA descriptors for validated large-M buckets; - a packed warp-shuffle GEMM2 epilogue. | Tokens | GEMM1 config | GEMM2 config | |---:|---:|---:| | `M <= 64` | 100 | 100 | | `M = 2048` | 313 | 313 | | `M = 4096` | 320 | 334 | | `M >= 8192` | 322 | 334 | | Other shapes | 101 | 101 | ## Validation ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash end-to-end A/B Hardware and runtime: - 8x NVIDIA H20; - native DeepSeek-V4-Flash checkpoint; - TP8 / EP1; - FP8 KV cache and DSV4 attention; - separate fresh containers for the two backends; - identical package versions except for the locally built `sglang-kernel` wheel; - FlashInfer 0.6.18 W4A8 as the upstream baseline. Serving workload: - exact paired token-ID prompts; - 128 requests; - concurrency 32; - output length 1536; - repeat 1. | Input -> output | CUTLASS output tok/s | FlashInfer output tok/s | Throughput | Mean TTFT | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8192 -> 1536 | 1399.19 | 1247.18 | **+12.19%** | **-17.26%** | | 16384 -> 1536 | 933.52 | 814.49 | **+14.61%** | **-16.95%** | | 32768 -> 1536 | 541.48 | 466.34 | **+16.11%** | **-16.18%** | All 384 requests completed successfully. Neither server log contained a CUDA error, OOM, or traceback. ### GSM8K The complete 1319-question GSM8K set was evaluated with five fixed shots, temperature 0, 32 threads, and repeat 1. | Backend | Correct | Accuracy | |---|---:|---:| | CUTLASS MXFP4A8 | 1252 / 1319 | 94.9204% | | FlashInfer | 1246 / 1319 | 94.4655% | The paired discordance was 16 CUTLASS-only correct versus 10 Humming-only correct (exact McNemar `p=0.3269`). This run does not establish a statistically significant accuracy difference. ### Kernel and operator tests | Test suite | Result | |---|---:| | CUTLASS MXFP4 grouped GEMM | 11 passed | | CUTLASS vs FlashInfer fused MoE | 3 passed | | Existing INT4 grouped GEMM | 605 passed | | Focused DSV4 norm/RoPE | 16 passed | The cross-backend test generates one logical MXFP4 weight set and uses the same BF16 input, top-k IDs, and router weights for both implementations. It covers `M=1`, `M=16`, and `M=65` with DeepSeek-V4-Flash `topk=6`, and requires: - normalized L2 error `< 2.5%`; - cosine similarity `> 0.9995`. ## Limitations - Supported hardware: SM90/Hopper. - Supported expert-parallel configuration: **EP=1 only**. - `EP>1` is explicitly rejected; this PR does not claim a legacy or DeepEP fallback. - Hidden size must be divisible by 128; intermediate size must be divisible by 32 and may be padded for validated GEMM shapes. - The load-time representation reuses FlashInfer's SM90 preprocessing semantics; runtime execution uses SGLang AOT kernels. - The reported performance results are specific to DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 8x H20 with the configuration above. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Validate MXFP4, INT4, and DSV4 regressions. - [x] Provide complete GSM8K accuracy results. - [x] Provide paired end-to-end performance results against current upstream FlashInfer. - [ ] Add user-facing documentation if maintainers request it. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #39389973536](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39389973536) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39389973468](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39389973468) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39389973442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39389973442)

Motivation
SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang
#24816
on top of FlashInfer
#3084
. FlashInfer
#3738
adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion.
This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in:
--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8
The existing
default
and
bf16
behavior is unchanged.
Related work:
SGLang
Add FlashInfer SM90 cutlass MXFP4 MoE backend (W4A16) for GPT-OSS + DeepSeek-V4
#24816
FlashInfer
perf: optimize MXFP4xBF16 & INT4xFP8 and add MXFP4xFP8 CUTLASS MoE backend for SM90
flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3738
FlashInfer version requirement
This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer
#4431
, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape
[num_local_experts]
. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP.
The original
#3738
ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by
#4411
. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI.
The new option therefore requires both:
flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18
preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming
SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting
fp8
fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change.
GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit
8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264
, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer
#4431
.
Modifications
Runtime selection and compatibility
Add
fp8
to
--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision
.
Select the new path only for
flashinfer_mxfp4
on SM90.
Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior.
Reject the SM90-specific
fp8
option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths.
Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI.
Pass
use_wfp4afp8_humming=True
only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility.
Weight preprocessing
Use
preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming
for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing.
Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer.
Store
residual * 64
as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2.
Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules.
Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range.
Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path.
Kernel invocation
Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API:
FC1 folded weight block scales
FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed
2^6
compensation
Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale
FC2 folded weight block scales
FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed
2^6
compensation
The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale.
Tests and benchmark
Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with:
GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper
five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison
aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions
padding invariance for per-expert residual scales
EP rank with global expert IDs
DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing
fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18
Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare:
SGLang Marlin W4A16
FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16
FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8
Update the server-argument documentation.
Accuracy Tests
The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed:
python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v
18 passed, 1 skipped
The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with:
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
  --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \
  --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000
DeepSeek-V4 accuracy was evaluated using the same 200-example GSM8K setup as SGLang
#24816
. Both runs used the same TP=4 configuration, dataset, sampling parameters, and server options; only
--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision
changed between
bf16
and
fp8
.
PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang_dev/python \
python -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --port 30000 \
  --eval-name gsm8k \
  --num-examples 200 \
  --api chat \
  --max-tokens 1024 \
  --num-threads 32 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --gsm8k-data-path /tmp/gsm8k-test.jsonl
MoE precision
GSM8K score
Total latency
Output throughput
W4A16 (
bf16
)
0.985
37.301 s
611.809 token/s
W4A8 (
fp8
)
0.985
32.952 s
683.574 token/s
W4A8 preserved the W4A16 GSM8K score while reducing evaluation latency by 11.7% and increasing output throughput by 11.7%. The score also matches the 0.985 W4A16 result reported in SGLang
#24816
.
Speed Tests and Profiling
The downstream benchmark uses the GPT-OSS-like shape from SGLang
#24816
: hidden size 4096, intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, and top-k 6. Each FlashInfer path was fully autotuned, followed by 5 warmup iterations and 30 timed iterations. The remaining token shapes were run in parallel with one independent shape per H20 GPU; each W4A16/W4A8 pair ran on the same GPU.
The benchmark can be reproduced with FlashInfer 0.6.18+:
PYTHONPATH=python:/path/to/flashinfer \
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py
Results on NVIDIA H20-3e:

FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 was faster at every measured token count, with speedups ranging from 1.63x to 2.08x. The gain reaches approximately 2.0x for token counts of 2048 and above. The GSM8K latency and throughput numbers above provide an end-to-end serving sanity check, but the kernel benchmark is the more controlled performance comparison because generated output lengths are not fixed.
Scope and Limitations
The implementation is SM90-only.
It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path.
A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update is required before production enablement.
Checklist
Format the code with pre-commit.
Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions.
Update server-argument documentation.
Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18.
Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result.
Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change.

FusedMoE rounds hidden_size up (GPT-OSS 2880 -> 3072) BEFORE
create_weights whenever the flashinfer_mxfp4 backend is selected -- the
same gate that later selects _fi_kernel = "cutlass_sm90". The SM90
post-load processor therefore sees K_un = 3072 = K_pad, so the
preserve_expert_range fill guarded an empty region, while scale columns
[2880, 3072) INSIDE K_un keep the _UE8M0_ONE (127 = 2^0) buffer fill

Humming derives each expert's residual from its min/max E8M0 exponents.
The stale 127s sit far above any real per-expert max, so they inflate
the range, shift the residual, and perturb the REAL weights on repack.
Same story on w2's K rows.

Fix: FusedMoE records hidden_size_unpadded before the round-up,
create_weights stores it as _unpadded_hidden, and the w13/w2 scale
copies stop at the checkpoint's K (ceil'd to the 32-wide group boundary)
so the never-written tail is covered by the existing per-expert fill.
The tail's weight bytes are zeros (never written), so whatever scale
sits there multiplies zero -- numerically inert in the GEMM. The trim is
gated on preserve_expert_range, so the W4A16 path stays byte-identical.
The SM120 helper needs no change: it has no per-expert range statistic,
and its stale scales multiply zero weights.

Add test_humming_range_ignores_prerounded_hidden_tail, which builds the
production shape (buffers at 3072, checkpoint data to 2880, real scales
well below 127) and asserts the per-expert residual is invariant to the
tail content. The existing tests missed this twice over: they construct
the method at 2880 directly (never seeing FusedMoE's pre-round), and
their random scales span 125..130, which straddles 127.

title: [Feature] Integrate Cake kernels via FlashInfer: model-by-model tracker
body:
**End-to-end validation and issue reporting:** Our shape coverage and correctness have not yet been validated end to end in model serving. If you encounter (1) end-to-end accuracy degradation, (2) unsuitable API requirements, such as unnecessarily requiring contiguous inputs, or (3) faster kernel benchmarks but worse end-to-end performance because the shapes optimized by the kernel do not cover the actual model-serving workload, please open an issue and tag @yyihuang with the affected kernel, the missing or problematic shape(s), and relevant model/serving details or a reproducer. We will resolve reported issues within **6 hours**.

## Motivation

Track integration of Cake kernels already delivered through FlashInfer into SGLang, grouped by the models that requested them. The upstream inventory is [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254); model requirements below come from its subissues and the linked implementation PRs.

The proposed integration is through FlashInfer's public/prepared APIs. Each task should connect the relevant model operator, weight/cache layout, and execution mode to an eligible kernel, then measure the complete serving path. Upstream kernel benchmarks are useful starting points, not claims of SGLang end-to-end speedup.

**Snapshot: 2026-10-03 (UTC; October 2 in US Pacific); FlashInfer main [46340689a5ab](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/46340689a5ab5665ab39f6281dac4d021d7ae94b).** “Merged” below means available in upstream FlashInfer, not necessarily in a released wheel or integrated here. Open follow-ups are explicitly marked and are not included in the merged coverage. Most listed kernels target SM100/SM103; exact architecture, SM-count, dtype, layout, and shape admission remain API-specific. Let the serving adapter retain its existing backend for configurations outside those contracts.

Notation: `T/M` = token rows, `B` = requests, `Q` = query tokens per request, `S` = KV length. MoE tuples are **(hidden size, expert intermediate size, number of experts, top-k)**; an intermediate size marked “local” is after TP sharding. Enumerated benchmark shapes are evidence points, not an assertion that every combination is supported.

## Integration and acceptance

- [ ] Pin a FlashInfer revision/release containing the required merged APIs and register backend selection at the existing operator boundary.
- [ ] Check the selected release branch separately: [#5978](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5978) is merged into `release-v0.7.1` only and reverts the BF16 head-dim-256 small-M speculative-decode route because of an intermittent B200 hang. This is a separate route from the E4M3/page-64 DCP entries below; a merge on the release branch does not establish a fix on main.
- [ ] Prepare weights, plans, output buffers, and workspaces before graph capture; account for changing request lengths, routing, state indices, and graph buckets.
- [ ] Validate each listed model/checkpoint, quantization recipe, TP/EP/CP configuration, and state/cache layout. Cover prefill, decode, speculative verification, ragged batches, and prefix-cache reuse where relevant.
- [ ] Compare against the current engine backend on model quality, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, and memory. Record the actual selected route and unsupported configurations before changing defaults.

SGLang already has model/operator boundaries for these families. Existing integration work is linked below so this tracker can be completed by extending or landing those changes.

## 1. Kimi-K3 / Kimi-K3-NVFP4 / Kimi-K3 vision

Requirements: [NVFP4 end-to-end #4568](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4568), [TP12 #4542](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4542), [ragged MLA/DCP #4658](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4658), [NVFP4 MLA #4644](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4644), [W4A8 SiTU #5156](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5156).

Start from [`kimi_k3.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py) for KDA/MLA/LatentMoE and [`kimi_k3_vl.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3_vl.py) for the vision tower. Preserve the model's layer ordering, TP reductions, state-cache semantics, and ModelOpt checkpoint preparation.

| Integration task | Covered shape / contract | FlashInfer delivery / upstream status |
|---|---|---|
| KDA prefill and fused decode | D=128. Fused one-token decode includes H=8 for TP12, plus H=12/24/32/48/96; BF16/FP32 indexed recurrent states and width-4 convolution. Prefill consumes strided q/k/v views of packed `[T,3*H*128]` projection output without densification. Prefill checkpoint outputs are BF16; FP32 checkpoints and `checkpoint_state_indices` are not admitted by the Cake prefill route. Recurrent T=1 decode with explicit `cu_seqlens` is outside the explicit Cake contract; `auto` now respects that guard. | **Merged:** `recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` and `fused_kda_decode(..., backend="cake")`; [#5551](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5551), [#5846](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5846); selector/binding updates [#5901](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5901) and [#5919](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5919) preserve the public API and served shape contracts; explicit-`cu_seqlens` auto-dispatch fix [#5760](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5760); [API](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/kda.py). |
| Dense FP8 MLA and ragged/DCP MLA | Kimi latent=512, RoPE=64, E4M3 query/cache, page=64; registered H=12/96 decode and Q<=8 MTP paths. The separate var-Q DCP API accepts BF16 or FP8 query/cache, H<=128, registered pages 32/64/128, compact cumulative query lengths and rank-local KV metadata; returns BF16 output + FP32 natural-log LSE. Caller performs the cross-rank merge. | **Merged:** `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(..., backend="cake")`, [#5552](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5552), [#5627](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5627); `cake_mla_varq_dcp_decode`, [#5577](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5577). |
| FP8 dense projections | BF16 activations and ModelOpt E4M3 weights with 128x128 block scales. 22 TP1/TP8 projection families, evaluated at M={1,8,64,256,4096,16384}; hidden=7168, representative global K→N: 7168→49152 fused QKVG, 7168→1536 Q-A, 1536→18432 Q-B, 7168→576 KV-A, 512→24576 KV-B, 12288→7168 O. Prepare/repack weights once; preserve padding and valid output columns. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.gemm.kimi_k3_fp8_projection`, [API/shape guide](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/kimi_k3_fp8_projection/README.md), merged [#5642](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5642). |
| Fused router + expert-aligned route plan | FP32 logits `[M,896]`, top-16, sigmoid + selection bias, normalization of unbiased selected weights, deterministic lower-ID ties; block_m=8/16. **Current M admission is powers of two from 1 through 8192**, not arbitrary batches. | **Merged:** `kimi_k3_fused_router` / `prepare_kimi_k3_fused_router`; [#5531](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5531), [#5621](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5621), [contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/kimi_k3_fused_router/README.md). |
| LatentMoE front and tail, TP1/TP8 | BF16 input `[T,7168]` → router logits `[T,896]`, latent `[T,3584]`, shared SiTU `[T,6144/TP]`; tail reduces supplied routed partials, normalizes, projects to 7168 and combines shared output. T=1..128 decode, prefill validated through 16384. **148-SM devices only in this package**, TP1/8, no EP; final all-reduce remains caller-owned. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.kimi_k3_latent_moe` prepared front/tail APIs; merged [#5734](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5734), [contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/kimi_k3_latent_moe/README.md). |
| TP12 distributed LatentMoE tail | Routed latent `[M,3584]`, shared partial `[M,7168]`, reduce + norm + up-projection + shared reduction. Twelve GB200/GB300 NVL72 ranks in one NVLink domain; evaluated M=1..4096. Separate API/workspace from TP1/8; each rank must agree on M and workspace capacity. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.kimi_k3_tp12_tail`; [#5603](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5603), [#5668](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5668). |
| NVFP4 SiTU experts | TP8-local (3584, **384 local**, 896, 16), T=1..16384, BF16 in/out, SiTU gate beta=4 and linear limit=25. Uses TRT-LLM shuffled block-16 NVFP4 weights and caller-owned workspace; output still needs the engine's communication. | **Merged:** `cutlass_fused_moe(..., backend="cake")`, `cake_fused_moe_prepare_workspace`; [#5183](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5183), [#5710](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5710), [tutorial](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/docs/tutorials/cake_kimi_k3_situ.rst). |
| Small-token NVFP4 warp-decode | Separate full expert geometry (3584, **3072**, 896, 16), every integer T=1..32, SiTU beta=4 / linear limit=25. Do not substitute the TP8-local I=384 geometry. | **Merged:** `CakeWarpDecodeConfig` / `CakeWarpDecodeRunner`; [#5134](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5134), [#5593](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5593). |
| AttnRes fusion | BF16 hidden=7168, residual-block count 0..8; residual update, snapshot, softmax mixing, output norm. Main evaluation M=1..16384 powers of two with block counts {0,1,4,8}; additional odd-M and all-block-count correctness rows. Current package requires 148 SMs. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.kimi_k3_attn_res.prepare_kimi_k3_attn_res`; [#5853](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5853) plus schedule-selection refresh [#5916](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5916) (47 registered programs; API and precision unchanged), [contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/cake_kimi_k3_attn_res/README.md). |
| MoonViT-3D + PatchMergerV2 vision tower | 27 layers; normalized BF16 patches `[T,3,14,14]`, host grids (t,h,w), 1<=t<=4, positive even h/w<=512. T=sum(t*h*w), output `[sum((h/2)*(w/2)),7168]`. Prepare per grid layout and replan when grids change; the resolved plan must have a registered kernel key. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.kimi_k3_vision` prepared tower/weights; [#5746](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5746), [contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/kimi_k3_vision_tower/README.md). |

- [ ] Integrate and qualify the eligible KDA, MLA, projection, router, LatentMoE, SiTU, AttnRes, and vision paths separately.
- [ ] Keep the outstanding precision paths explicit: Kimi's 512+64 **NVFP4 MLA** remains a separate request (#4644). For **W4A8 MXFP4 SiTU**, the previous implementation was reverted by [#5681](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5681), and replacement [#5783](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5783) is still open at this snapshot.

## 2. Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 MoE

Requirements: [FP8 grouped GEMM #3712](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3712) and [Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4-V2 ragged decode #4832](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4832). Use the Qwen3.5 model's GDN and MoE boundaries. Existing [SGLang #40656](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40656) is an open **draft** integration PR for FlashInfer MTP verification; complete/extend that work before creating a competing implementation.

### NVFP4 small-token MoE

Merged [#5134](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5134) and [#5593](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5593) cover **every T=1..32 on SM100/SM103**, through `CakeWarpDecodeConfig` / `CakeWarpDecodeRunner`, for these checkpoint/operator geometries:

| Model | (H, I, E, top-k) |
|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | (2048,768,128,8) |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B | (4096,1536,128,8) |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | (2048,512,256,8) |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B | (4096,1024,512,10) |

- [ ] Connect the NVFP4 expert path for matching layouts/geometries. A matching model name alone does not admit an FP8 checkpoint or a different TP-local intermediate size.

### Qwen3.5 GDN, FP8 experts, and ragged attention

| Integration task | Covered shape / contract | Delivery / upstream status |
|---|---|---|
| Gated Delta Net prefill, including CP | `chunk_gated_delta_rule(..., backend="cake_gdn", use_cp=True/False)`; SM100/SM103, BF16/FP16 activations, supported state dtypes, packed/ragged and indexed-state contracts. Use the registered prefill routes rather than a blanket model-wide dispatch. Include the public-wrapper fix for imbalanced CP batches when `max_seqlen` is omitted; callers that know the exact maximum can keep supplying it. | **Merged:** [#5320](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5320), [#5243](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5243); CP sequence-length-bound fix [#5661](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5661); [guide](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/csrc/gdn/cake/README.md). |
| Seven-token speculative verification | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B TP2: B=1..8, T=7, H=8/HV=16, K=V=128, BF16 state/checkpoint cache; registered B=1/T=8 and TP1 B=1/T=7 H=16/HV=32 cases also exist. Preserve `disable_state_update=True` and accepted-token state semantics. | **Merged:** [#5378](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5378). |
| Contiguous grouped FP8 GEMM | **SM100 only.** E4M3 A[M,K], B[G,N,K], FP32 activation and 128x128 weight scales; sorted int32 expert indices, BF16 output. | BGMV MoE LoRA shrink + expand | SM90/SM100/SM103; BF16/FP16 X[T,H], one LoRA slice, H positive and divisible by 8, rank={8,16,32,64}, LoRA-B output width H, FP32 accumulated output. Arbitrary routed-pair order, including expert-sorted dispatch. H=2688/3072, rank32, T<=2048 keeps specialized programs; other admitted shapes use generic bundles. Prepare pointer-stable buffers before graph use; current validation requires contiguous inputs. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.fused_moe.prepare_bgmv_moe(..., backend="cake", fallback=True)`, [#5850](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5850), portable fallback/current-stream fix [#5809](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5809); [API contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/fused_moe/bgmv_moe.py). Inspect `plan.backend_used` / `fallback_reason`; unsupported valid inputs can use the portable path, `fallback=False` rejects unsupported Cake shapes, and invalid inputs still raise. |
| Grouped MXFP8 quantization / fused SwiGLU quantization | BF16/FP16 input, grouped/ragged quantization and the GEMM consumer's scale layout; use forward-only activation paths for inference. | **Merged:** [#4820](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4820), [#4638](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4638). |
| Softmax and fused top-k→top-p→sampling | FP32 probabilities [B,V], top-k 1..1024, `top_k_first` semantics; representative B=1..128, V={32768,128256,151936,262144}. Round-8 runtime evidence on SM90/SM100/SM103/SM107; capability-specific dispatch. Preserve per-request k/p and RNG semantics; deterministic replay within this backend does not imply identical token streams to every other sampler. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.cake_sampling`, [#5439](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5439), [#5731](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5731), round 7 [#5847](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5847) and latest round 8 [#5950](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5950) (same correctness/RNG contract); existing `flashinfer.sampling.softmax` dispatch, [#4282](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4282). For standard-library sampler comparisons/fallbacks, include [#5745](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5745): batch-length seed/offset tensors now apply per output row, including gathered/repeated input rows. |
| Block-sparse/VSA and Sage attention | VSA wrapper backend for supported sparse metadata; separate SM90 and SM100-family paths. Sage FP8 block-sparse on SM100/103 supports its documented ragged/GQA and scale contracts; SM120 INT8 is another portfolio. | **Merged:** [SM90 VSA #5687](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5687), [SM100 VSA #4593](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4593), [Sage FP8 #5442](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5442), [SM120 #5127](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5127). |
| Thor XQA, where a serving deployment requires it | Exact SM110 experimental D512 route, FP16/E4M3, contiguous or page128 KV, GQA ratios 2/4/8/16. Qualify against the dedicated API/toolchain; this is not blanket SM110 coverage for the kernels above. | **Merged:** [#5674](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5674). |
| Experimental MXFP8 MegaMoE EP16 evaluation | SM103, 16 ranks, E=512/top8/H=3072/I=5120, T={16,32,64} per rank, NVSHMEM. Current prepared session has bounded routing capacity and no CUDA Graph support; it needs additional work for general dynamic serving. | [package contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16/README.md), [multi-capacity request #4727](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4727). |

- [ ] Add shared adapters and eligibility checks, then record per-model qualification in the sections above.

title: [Refactor] kernels: Regroup operators by computation and dissolve ops/muse_spark
body:
## Motivation

`python/sglang/kernels/README.md` says to classify kernels by the computation they perform, not by the model that first used them, and never to add a model bundle as a top-level group. An audit of current main found that this had drifted:

- `ops/muse_spark/` (#44665) was a model-named top-level group. It contained 22 files mixing norms, routing, GEMMs, collectives and reductions, with no KernelSpecs and no kernel tests. It had been added to `_GROUPS`, which is the only thing the guard test checked, so the test did not catch it.
- `attention/dsv4/` and `attention/dsa/` had collected quantization kernels, KV-cache stores and copies, a split-K GEMV, collective attention-residual kernels, runtime controllers and config predicates, and test oracles.
- Elsewhere, ops sat in the wrong group: GEMMs in `quantization`, RMSNorms in `elementwise`, attention metadata in `kvcache`, a forwarding shim in `attention/utils.py`, and the same computation implemented in two or three groups.

This PR fixes all of it in one pass. It writes the classification rules into the README and the `kernel-organization` skill, and makes the guard test enforce the README.

## Classification rules (README + skill)

- RoPE, including standalone RoPE and position ids, stays in `attention`.
- **Producer + output quantization belongs to the producer's group:**
  - norm + quant → `layernorm`
  - activation + quant → `activation`
  - a GEMM with a quant epilogue → `gemm`
  - MoE dispatch + quant → `moe`
  - `quantization` holds only pure format conversion: quant, dequant, scale layout, repack.
- **Any kernel that performs a cross-rank collective, or reads or writes peer memory, → `communication`**, whatever compute it fuses. Workspaces, symmetric buffers and process groups stay in `srt/layers/communication/`.
- **`kvcache` owns ops that read or write KV-cache contents:** store, gather, copy, quantize-into-cache, clear rows.
- **`attention` owns the index, shape and schedule tables attention kernels consume:** page tables, cu_seqlens, kv_indices, schedule metadata.
- A fused compute+store op stays with its compute group.
- `kda_kernels/` and `cake_kernels/` are documented as the agent-generated kernel backends. They are deliberately left in place, and new agent kernels keep landing there.

**Guard test** (`test_kernels_namespace.py`):
- The README group list must equal `_GROUPS`.
- The README Layout must list exactly the packages under `sglang/kernels/`.

Both checks fail on main.

## Modifications

All relocations are `git mv` plus import updates. Every moved function, class and constant was checked to be byte-identical apart from import paths, either by AST comparison or by a normalized diff. Relocation commits are kept apart from semantic commits. No forwarding shims remain: 94 old module paths have zero references anywhere.

### `ops/muse_spark` dissolved
- **layernorm:** `muse_spark_norm_gate{,_jit,_helion}`, `muse_spark_norm_residual{,_jit}`, `muse_spark_rmsnorm_nvfp4_quant{,_helion}`, `_muse_spark_tuning`.
- **attention:** `muse_spark_qk_norm_rope_store{,_helion}`.
- **moe:** `muse_spark_routing{,_jit}`, `muse_spark_post_expert_finalize_triton`.
- **communication:**
  - `muse_spark_all_gather`, `muse_spark_all_gather_norm_residual`
  - `muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce{,_cutedsl,_helion}`
  - SP `cutlass_all_gather_gemm`, `cutlass_gemm_reduce_scatter`, `sp_collective_gemm` (moved from `gemm`)
- **elementwise:** `row_sum`. **gemm:** `muse_spark_router_gemm`. It is kept but still unused; the model only reads its `MAX_TOKENS` threshold.
- **Helion runtime:** → `kernels/jit/utils/helion_runtime.py`.
- **Runtime state → `srt/layers/communication/`:** the GEMM+all-gather composition and projection workspace, `FinalizePushWorkspace`, and the SP collective-GEMM symmetric-memory workspace. The SP kernels now take the workspace as an argument.
- **The model calls the all-gather+norm op directly.** The removed `forward_with_ag` used to route it, and the norm op no longer imports srt model classes.
- **New coverage:** KernelSpecs for every entry point, plus 6 kernel test files (fused vs native). `triton_sum` → `sglang.test.kernels`, used as the `row_sum` bitwise reference.

### DeepSeek V4 / DSA
- **To `quantization`:**
  - `act_quant` (Triton and TileLang)
  - `fp8_group_major_quant_ue8m0` (was `dsv4/fp8_wo_a`)
  - `fp4_fake_quant` (was `dsv4/torch_quant`)
  - `quantize_fp4_indexer_tensor`
  - `dsa_quant_k_cache` (returns new tensors; it never writes the cache)
- **To `kvcache`:**
  - request-window row copy, c128 draft-state cleanup
  - V4 main-KV and DSA index-K accessors
  - unified-KV scatter
  - FP4 index-K store and gather (CUDA and HIP)
  - the DSA fused index-K store
- **To `gemm`:** `dsv4_indexer_head_weights_hip`, a split-K GEMV.
- **To `communication`:** `attn_res_collective` (NVLS pull reduce-scatter, multicast all-gather).
- **Runtime code → srt:** `OnlineC128MTPController`, the unified-KV config gate, `Gfx950FusedIndexer`.
- **Launchers into the kernel modules:** the sparse-prefill and CP-interleave launchers now live there, so srt no longer imports private `@triton.jit` kernels.
- **Folder fixes:**
  - DSA-only files at the attention top level → `dsa/`
  - V4-only files → `dsv4/`; `nsa_triton_decode/` → `dsv4/triton_sparse_decode/`
  - `dsv4/elementwise.py` → `dsv4/norm_rope.py`
  - the V3.2-only Q indexer → `dsa/indexer_q.py`
- **Renames:**
  - same-named dequant functions → `*_dsa` / `*_dsv4`
  - kpool metadata functions → `*_kpool`
  - `_kv_splits_for_stream` → `kv_splits_for_stream` (public)
- **Test oracles → `sglang.test.kernels`.** The dead `triton_create_paged_compress_data` is deleted.

### kvcache ↔ attention, attention subpackages
- **To `attention`:** `kv_indices`, `trtllm_mha_page_table`, `trtllm_mha_graph_metadata`, `aiter_unified_page_table`, `fused_qk_rope_reshape_and_cache`, and the MLA Q/K prep from `cache_ops` (→ `mla_qk_prep.py`).
- **`attention/utils.py` forwarding re-exports removed.** 21 importers now import from the defining modules. The shuffle-5D store and gather → `kvcache/shuffle_5d_cache.py`. Two duplicate inventory specs dropped.
- **SGLang-written files moved out of the vendored `attention/fla/`:** 7 files → `attention/linear/`, and `kda_prefill_graph_track` → `mamba/`. `BailingLinearKernel` → its srt backend.
- **FA4 MLA SM100:** test and benchmark code moved out of the production module (`flash_fwd_mla_sm100.py`) into `test/manual/`.
- **MiniMax sparse:** the Gluon prefill moved from `srt/layers/attention/minimax_sparse_ops` → `kernels/ops/attention/minimax_sparse/`. Its `tests/` folder had never been collected and had stale imports; it is now in `test/registered`, with the slow autotune test nightly. The unused `naive/` references are deleted.
- **Lazy KernelSpecs** for unregistered public entry points: Helion/CuTeDSL/PTX KDA and GDN, FP8 FA SM120, vattn asm, minimax sparse and CP indexer, and others.

### Other groups
- **GEMMs out of `quantization` → `gemm`:** `nvfp4_gemm_swiglu_nvfp4_quant`, the gfx950 MXFP8 GEMV/GEMM (with its tuning JSON), `mxfp8_flydsl`, `mxfp8_aiter`, and the MXFP8 blockscaled linears.
- **By rule 3:**
  - `rmsnorm_fake_quant_amd_gfx95` → `layernorm`
  - SwiGLU/SiLU+MXFP8 → `activation`
  - `minimax_quant_ue8m0` → `moe`
  - `upscale` (dequant) → `quantization`
  - MXFP8 epilogue helpers → `quantization`
  - `quant_store_kv_mxfp8` and the interleaved SF → `kvcache`
  - diffusion modulate+MXFP8 → `diffusion/modulate`
- **`elementwise`:** RMSNorms → `layernorm`; `gelu_and_mul_triton` and `bias_gelu` → `activation`.
- **Other moves:**
  - `hc_mix` split-K → `gemm`; `router_gate_matvec` → `gemm`
  - `silu_and_mul_clamp` / `silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant` → `activation`; these also serve dense MLPs.
  - `ngram_embedding` → `embeddings`
  - `softcap_row_argmax` → `sampling`
  - `bmm_fp8`'s implementation moved out of srt into `gemm/flashinfer_bmm_fp8.py`
  - `communication/mp.py` → `srt/distributed`
- **Duplicates:**
  - `moe/triton_sigmoid_gate_mul` merged into `elementwise.fused_sigmoid_mul`: bit-exact over 92 cases on sm_90/sm_100/sm_120.
  - Kept, each with a one-line comment saying why, because they are not bit-exact with their twin: `mla_output_gate` (rounds the gate to bf16 first), the `hc_mix` split-K vs persistent kernels, `swiglu_oai_mxfp8`, DSpark `SoftmaxTemp`, `act_quant`, the V4 Triton RoPE, the grok/gfx1250 RMSNorms, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU.
- **Housekeeping:**
  - hipcc build helpers → `kernels/jit/utils/hipcc.py`
  - `_jit_*` module prefixes removed
  - KernelSpecs added for `kv_canary` / `lplb`
  - `mhc.hc_combine` → `mhc_combine` (it clashed with `elementwise.hc_combine`)
  - test helpers `fp8_cvt` and `scatter_req_token_ids` reference → `sglang.test.kernels`
  - the unused `mxfp4_marlin_repack` deleted
  - CODEOWNERS kept in sync for moved files

## Bugs fixed along the way
- **CuTeDSL GDN/KDA prefill was selected on SM120 and crashed.** `_is_blackwell()` returned `major >= 10`, but the kernels need tcgen05. The first extend failed with an NVVM `unsupported operation` on sm_120a. They are now gated to SM10x, and SM120 falls back to Triton; B200 still selects CuTeDSL.
- **Muse Spark RMSNorm+NVFP4 quant had no native reference.** `forward_native` raised `NotImplementedError`, which BaseFusedOp does not allow. It is now implemented and checked against the JIT kernel.
- **MiniMax sparse attention tests never ran:** they sat inside the srt package with stale imports. They are fixed and registered.
- **FlashInfer KDA comments wrongly said "SM100-only".** SM120 runs the generic CuTeDSL path, verified on an RTX PRO 6000. Comment fix only.

## Coordination
**#44667 and #44668** (Fridge003) touch `ops/muse_spark/`. New locations:

| old `ops/muse_spark/…` | new |
|---|---|
| `fused_muse_spark_routing.py` | `moe/muse_spark_routing.py` |
| `fused_norm_gate.py` | `layernorm/muse_spark_norm_gate.py` |
| `fused_norm_residual.py` | `layernorm/muse_spark_norm_residual.py` |
| `fused_op_tuning.py` | `layernorm/_muse_spark_tuning.py` (configs in `layernorm/configs/muse_spark/`) |
| `fused_qk_norm.py` / `helion_qk_norm.py` | `attention/muse_spark_qk_norm_rope_store{,_helion}.py` |
| `helion_runtime.py` | `kernels/jit/utils/helion_runtime.py` |
| `fi_trtllm_moe_finalize_with_rmsnorm_cutedsl.py` | `communication/muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce_cutedsl.py` |

Notes for the rebase:
- `FusedPostNormResidualPreNorm` now takes `post_norm_is_input_scale` and `use_residual_gate`, and `forward_with_ag` is gone. Call `communication.muse_spark_all_gather_norm_residual(..., **op.jit_kernel_kwargs())`.
- `FinalizePushWorkspace` now lives in `srt/layers/communication/muse_spark_finalize_workspace.py`.
- #44668's `helion_megakernels/` and its tests need a logical group; the guard test rejects `ops/muse_spark` and `test/registered/kernels/ops/muse_spark`.

## Validation

- **Static checks:**
  - pre-commit is clean on every changed file.
  - Every relocation is byte-identical apart from import paths (AST or normalized diff, per move).
  - The 94 old module paths have 0 remaining references.
  - A static resolver over every `sglang.*` import and every KernelSpec target finds 0 new unresolved names vs main.
- **Collection and imports:**
  - `pytest --collect-only` over `test/registered`, the diffusion unit tests and the AOT tests shows no new collection errors on H200 or B200. 340 more tests are collected: the new tests plus the MiniMax tests that could not be collected before.
  - The import walk over `sglang.kernels`, `multimodal_gen` and `srt.{layers,models,speculative,mem_cache,disaggregation}` fails on exactly the same modules as main. These are only the optional helion/aiter/flydsl dependencies, now under their new paths.
- **GPU sweep on H200 (sm_90) and B200 (sm_100):** 676 test files, covering every changed test and every test that imports a changed module.
  - Each failure was re-run on main and compared by FAILED test id. **No new failures.**
  - The two files that failed only in the parallel sweep hit port collisions (`EADDRINUSE`) and pass when run alone.
  - The split MXFP8-swizzled tests reproduce main's 29 H200 failures exactly. They are registered on B200 only.
- **Multi-GPU (4×B200, through each test's torchrun launcher):** `test_collectives` (covers the moved attn_res collectives and the gemm all-gather), `test_ar_fusion`, `test_tp_qknorm`, `test_symm_mem_all_gather` and `test_deterministic_reduce_scatter` all pass on both main and this PR.
- **Moved ops vs main:** bitwise identical, old path vs new path, for 17 ops on H200 and B200, and for `indexed_scale_shift_mxfp8_` both directly and through the diffusion facade. The `sigmoid_gate_mul` merge is bit-exact over 92 cases on sm_90, sm_100 and sm_120.
- **New Muse Spark kernel tests (fused vs native)** pass on sm_90, sm_100 and sm_120.
- **Helion backends:** the four moved Helion kernel files are line-identical to main apart from imports, and they import under Helion 1.4.0. Helion is not in the CI image, and its pinned configs cover only production shapes.
- **sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000):** the GDN/KDA CuTeDSL gate fix was checked before and after; FlashInfer GDN/KDA was probed against Triton; the Muse Spark op tests pass.
- **Final head with latest main merged:** main's new tests and the namespace test (85 passed) pass on H200 and B200.
- **Not validated at runtime:**
  - ROCm/HIP, NPU and XPU paths, which got static checks plus imports of the CUDA-importable modules.
  - Muse Spark's multi-GPU paths (all-gather, fused-AR finalize, SP collective GEMMs). They have no unit tests; only `test_muse_spark_12_b300_pd.py` covers them.
  - The 8-GPU variants.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Motivation
The SM90 FP4 decode/target-verify indexer uses a capacity-sized CUDA Graph grid while visible lengths change on device between replays. For a short live context, masking K loads still leaves FP4 dequantization and dot products running on entirely invisible tiles. For example, a row with 8,192 visible positions can reserve 1,048,896 output columns.
This change skips scoring for fully invisible tiles and writes
-inf
directly, reducing unnecessary work while preserving the dense logits interface.
Modifications
Add a tile-uniform branch using the current device-side visible length. Invisible tiles write
-inf
on every replay, including when previously visible tiles become invisible.
Preserve the original arithmetic, BF16 rounding points and masks for visible and partially visible tiles. The launch grid, output shape, cache layout and candidate-selection behavior remain unchanged.
Add focused decode correctness and CUDA Graph replay tests to the existing FP4 indexer test file.
The change adds no host-side length read, synchronization, extra kernel launch, dependency or configuration flag. The PR changes only the kernel and its test file.
Accuracy Tests
Validation hardware/software: NVIDIA H20-3e, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, Triton 3.6.0.
Existing FP4 indexer suite with the added tests:
23 passed, 36 skipped
. The skipped cases target Blackwell vectorized prefill.
11 added decode cases
cover empty/partial/full tiles; zero, negative and over-capacity lengths; heads 32/64; page sizes 64/128; strided inputs; padded page strides; and invalid inactive slot IDs.
An independent Torch FP64 reference checks FP4 decoding and the prescribed BF16 rounding points using controlled dyadic inputs. CUDA Graph replays grow/shrink visibility, change queries and slot mappings, and poison output buffers to detect unwritten tails.

11 cases, zero errors
, with the reference calculation moved to CPU in the validation harness.

Description
hit-zhengbao

on Jul 13, 2026
Issue body actions
We are evaluating an MXFP4 x MXFP8 W4A8 GEMM on NVIDIA H100.
The fused-E8M0 Humming kernel is numerically correct, but with group-32
MXFP8 activation scales it is significantly slower than both:
Humming's generic group-scale path
A QDQ baseline that dequantizes both operands and then runs a BF16 GEMM
We would like to ask whether group-32 MXFP8 input scaling is an intended
performance target and whether there are plans to optimize this case on Hopper.
Quantization format
The operands use the following format:
Activation payload: FP8 E4M3
Activation scale: per-token, per-K-group power-of-two scale
Activation group size: 32
Weight payload: MXFP4 E2M1
Weight scale: E8M0
Weight group size: 32
Output dtype: BF16
This is an MXFP8-style activation representation: each 32-element K group
contains an E4M3 payload and one power-of-two scale.
Humming receives the decoded real FP32 activation scales through
input_scale
. The original activation scales are exactly representable
as E8M0 powers of two.
This differs from the DeepEP grouped-FP8 case added by
#37
:
PR
fix: support grouped FP8 MXFP4
#37
activation group size: 128
This case activation group size: 32
Both cases use MXFP4 weights with E8M0 group size 32
Environment
GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
Humming commit tested:
79c1cef
/
#35
Output dtype: BF16
Warmup: 20 iterations
Measurement: 200 iterations
Timing: CUDA events and CUDA Graph replay
GEMM operation count:
2 * M * N * K
PR
#37
was merged after the tested commit. Based on its diff, it adds the
group-128 integration and fixes non-fused scale tail decoding, but does
not appear to change fused WGMMA accumulator scheduling or the H100
heuristics. We can confirm the measurements on the latest main if needed.
Humming configuration
The fused kernel is configured approximately as follows:

The following implementations were compared against an FP32 reference:
Fused-E8M0 Humming

QDQ baseline
The QDQ latency includes activation dequantization, weight dequantization,

For large-M shapes, the fused kernel reaches only approximately
20-22 effective TFLOPS.
Suspected bottleneck
Our current understanding is:
For FP8,
kPartMmaShapeK
is 32.
With
input_scale_group_size=32
, every WGMMA step reaches an activation
scale boundary.
scale_d
is therefore false at every K=32 step.
The current path performs
wgmma_commit()
followed by
wgmma_wait<0>()
, register fencing, and accumulator scaling for every
K=32 group.
The fused H100 heuristic selects a relatively large
128x128x128
base tile, which may increase the cost of processing the accumulator
at each group boundary.
With the group-128 input scales used by PR
#37
, four K=32 WGMMA operations
can accumulate before applying the activation scale. The synchronization
and accumulator-processing overhead can therefore be better amortized.
This is only our interpretation of the current implementation; please
correct us if we are missing another bottleneck.
Comparison with an experimental Gluon implementation
For reference, an experimental Gluon implementation reaches approximately
580-665 effective TFLOPS for the same large-M shapes.
That implementation performs one-time offline preprocessing of the static
MXFP4 weight into a cached FP8 weight tensor and therefore consumes an
additional
N * K
bytes of device memory. It is not a direct memory-footprint
comparison with Humming's packed-MXFP4 kernel, but it suggests that the
group-32 activation scaling itself does not necessarily prevent high
throughput if preprocessing extra static weight storage is acceptable.
We do not expect the packed-MXFP4 Humming kernel to match this result
without considering that memory tradeoff.
Questions
Is MXFP8 activation group size 32 an intended performance target for
Humming's fused-E8M0 W4A8 kernel?
Is the current implementation primarily optimized for group-128 input
scales such as the DeepEP format in PR
fix: support grouped FP8 MXFP4
#37
?
Are there plans to optimize the group-32 case on Hopper?
Would you recommend a different block/warp shape or disabling stream-K
for this workload?
Could an accumulator ring, delayed retirement, or another scheduling
strategy reduce the per-group
wgmma_wait<0>
overhead?
Would it be useful for us to provide the complete benchmark script,
Nsight Compute reports, or results from additional shapes?
Thank you.

This is because the combination of mixed‑precision quantization with group‑wise input quantization has a relatively low performance ceiling, it won't be much better than using BF16 activations.

Hi，the attachment contains the source code.
Core Kernels
1. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_accs_kernel
Processes one 32-element K group at a time:
WGMMA(A_fp8, W_fp8) -> FP32 partial
partial *= input_e8m0_scale
master += partial
This is the key to preserving numerical accuracy: the activation scale is applied to the FP32 partial accumulator, avoiding an additional rounding step from dequantizing and casting the activation back to FP8.
2. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_accs_batched_kernel
Loads multiple 32-element K groups in each TMA stage, typically using LOAD_K=128 or LOAD_K=256. This reduces TMA transactions, barrier overhead, and main-loop scheduling costs. It is the default high-performance path for large M.
3. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_splitk_kernel
Used for small M. It increases parallelism by distributing the K dimension across multiple CTAs. Each CTA accumulates into an FP32 temporary output using atomic additions, after which the result is converted to the requested output dtype.
4. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_prmt_kernel
A fallback path used when the WPREQ exactness guard fails. It uses prmt.b32 to fuse the decoding of packed MXFP4 weights with their weight scales into FP8 values. This path requires an offline T2 weight repacking step.
5. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_kernel
The most general but slower fallback path. It explicitly performs MXFP4 decoding, E8M0 scale application, and FP8 conversion inside the main loop.

Thank you. I manually performed some temporary local tuning and achieved only 500+ TFLOPs, which is lower than gluon. This is mainly because Humming's current implementation is not friendly to groupwise input scaling; a major optimization would require reimplementing a separate WGMMA path.
Additionally, I noticed a few issues with your code:
For the kernels under small batch sizes, you dequantize the input, multiply by the scale, and then quantize back to FP8. This is likely to cause serious precision problems, especially when the actual FP16 input values are very small (e.g., on the order of 0.001).
For the benchmarking script, you use CUDA Graphs. This may inflate the performance numbers for small batch sizes because the L2 cache is not flushed. I suggest using DeepGEMM's testing script instead.
https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1f6f3f378920ccb5cc036ef43eb3f5972e921713/deep_gemm/testing/bench.py#L79-L146

title: Whistle and Wrong Lyrics: Synthetic Queries Are Not Enough for Real-World Query-by-Melody
body: People look up a song by humming it, but also by whistling it or singing it with the wrong words. Published query-by-humming systems and benchmarks focus on hums and sung queries, and no public dataset pairs whistles or wrong-lyrics singing with song recordings. We study both query types with a melody-only retrieval system: a key-normalized pitch track embedded by a 5.2M-parameter contour encoder, with a spectral-peak tracker for whistles. First, a physics-grounded generator renders synthetic whistles and nonsense-syllable singing from the vocal melodies of 11,083 songs. Training on them raises top-1 retrieval of held-out synthetic queries against an 11,050-song gallery from 0.180 to 0.251 for whistles and from 0.193 to 0.264 for wrong-lyrics singing, but the gain does not transfer: on the MLEnd test performers the best synthetic-only model gets 210 of 339 real whistles right at top-1, against 214 for the baseline. Second, a closed-set fine-tune on real MLEnd whistles with performer-disjoint splits raises whistle-to-hum top-1 from 0.631 (95% CI 0.581-0.681) to 0.673 (0.622-0.723), on known songs only. Third, two further generations of synthetic queries also fail to transfer: melody-conditioned whistles and la-la singing from a commercial neural music model leave real-whistle top-1 at 0.631, and an open-source pipeline (YingMusic-Singer-Plus singing with partly wrong, mumbled or nonsense lyrics, a DDSP whistle synthesizer, and a melody-error model fitted on real performers) gives at best 0.619 (paired difference -0.012, 95% CI -0.038 to +0.015). Across physics-based, commercial neural and open-source neural synthetic data, nothing transferred to real whistles, which points to collecting real queries as the missing step. Code is public; models and data will be released.

title: An approach to hummed-tune and song sequences matching
body:
Melody stuck in your head, also known as "earworm", is tough to get rid of,
unless you listen to it again or sing it out loud. But what if you can not find
the name of that song? It must be an intolerable feeling. Recognizing a song
name base on humming sound is not an easy task for a human being and should be
done by machines. However, there is no research paper published about hum tune
recognition. Adapting from Hum2Song Zalo AI Challenge 2021 - a competition
about querying the name of a song by user's giving humming tune, which is
similar to Google's Hum to Search. This paper covers details about the
pre-processed data from the original type (mp3) to usable form for training and
inference. In training an embedding model for the feature extraction phase, we
ran experiments with some states of the art, such as ResNet, VGG, AlexNet,
MobileNetV2. And for the inference phase, we use the Faiss module to
effectively search for a song that matched the sequence of humming sound. The
result comes at nearly 94\% in MRR@10 metric on the public test set, along with
the top 1 result on the public leaderboard.

title: NeuPIMs: NPU-PIM Heterogeneous Acceleration for Batched LLM Inferencing
body:
Modern transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) are constructed with a
series of decoder blocks. Each block comprises three key components: (1) QKV
generation, (2) multi-head attention, and (3) feed-forward networks. In batched
processing, QKV generation and feed-forward networks involve compute-intensive
matrix-matrix multiplications (GEMM), while multi-head attention requires
bandwidth-heavy matrix-vector multiplications (GEMV). Machine learning
accelerators like TPUs or NPUs are proficient in handling GEMM but are less
efficient for GEMV computations. Conversely, Processing-in-Memory (PIM)
technology is tailored for efficient GEMV computation, while it lacks the
computational power to handle GEMM effectively. Inspired by this insight, we
propose NeuPIMs, a heterogeneous acceleration system that jointly exploits a
conventional GEMM-focused NPU and GEMV-optimized PIM devices. The main
challenge in efficiently integrating NPU and PIM lies in enabling concurrent
operations on both platforms, each addressing a specific kernel type. First,
existing PIMs typically operate in a "blocked" mode, allowing only either NPU
or PIM to be active at any given time. Second, the inherent dependencies
between GEMM and GEMV in LLMs restrict their parallel processing. To tackle
these challenges, NeuPIMs is equipped with dual row buffers in each bank,
facilitating the simultaneous management of memory read/write operations and
PIM commands. Further, NeuPIMs employs a runtime sub-batch interleaving
technique to maximize concurrent execution, leveraging batch parallelism to
allow two independent sub-batches to be pipelined within a single NeuPIMs
device. Our evaluation demonstrates that compared to GPU-only, NPU-only, and a
na\"ive NPU+PIM integrated acceleration approaches, NeuPIMs achieves 3times,
2.4times and 1.6times throughput improvement, respectively.

title: [AMD][MI355X] Kimi-K3 vLLM AgentX FP8 per-channel linear quantization-config / [AMD][MI355X] Kimi-K3 vLLM AgentX 新增 FP8 per-channel linear quantization-config
body:
## Summary
- Add `--quantization-config '{"linear":"fp8_per_channel","ignore":["*kv_b_proj","*vision_tower*","*mm_projector*","*in_proj_qkvgfab","*f_b_proj","*fused_qkv_a_proj","*self_attn.g_proj","*.layers.0.mlp.down_proj"]}'` to the base `agg` args of the Kimi-K3 MI355X vLLM AgentX recipe (`benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/kimik3/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`), so every point of `kimik3-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp` (added in #3561; supersedes #3626) inherits it.
- vLLM online-quantizes the target's linear layers to FP8 W8A8 (per-channel weights, dynamic per-token activations) at load: 302 layers per rank (`o_proj`, MLA `q_b_proj`, shared-expert `gate_up_proj`/`down_proj`, dense layer-0 `gate_up_proj`). The routed experts stay MXFP4 from the checkpoint.
- These stay BF16:
  - `kv_b_proj`.
  - KDA `in_proj_qkvgfab` (N=6288) and MLA `fused_qkv_a_proj` (N=2112): no tuned AITER FP8 shape on this image, so they would fall back to `torch._scaled_mm`.
  - KDA `f_b_proj`, MLA `g_proj` and the dense `down_proj`: no gain from FP8 at decode once the per-token activation quant kernel is counted.
- The benchmark numbers below were measured before the ignore list was extended, with all 489 layers in FP8.
- Image (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-36768d1bfd39094681cdbc8cb37d4b31c0729c89`), KV offload and all other flags are unchanged.
- Concurrency sweep (`configs/amd-master.yaml`): the dcp1 DRAM-offload arm moves from 8/10/12/14 to 10/12/14/16, and the dcp8 arm adds 75 (44/48/70/75). The kvnone c1/c4 arm is unchanged.
- New recipe variants for the new points, copied from their neighbours and not yet measured:
  - `override_tp8_c16_simple`: as c14, with `max-num-seqs` 32, FULL CUDA graphs captured at 2-128, DSpark k=3 and DRAM offload.
  - `override_tp8_c75_dcp8_simple`: as c70, with `max-num-seqs` 150 and captures at 1-150 plus 256-8192.
  - `override_tp8_c8_simple` stays in the recipe but is no longer swept.
- Append the `perf-changelog.yaml` entry, covering the flag and the concurrency change.

## Measurements
One MI355X node, clean image above (no patch, no aiter config override), `server.sh`-style TP8, DSpark k=7 with synthetic acceptance 3.84, `max-num-seqs` 2, `vllm bench serve` random 8k/1k:

| Concurrency | Output tok/s (without → with) | Mean TPOT ms | Mean TTFT ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 282.93 → 289.90 (+2.5%) | 6.51 → 6.32 | 7085 → 6953 |
| 8 | 294.17 → 303.27 (+3.1%) | 6.41 → 6.20 | 19130 → 18583 |
| 16 | 293.48 → 303.09 (+3.3%) | 6.43 → 6.22 | 44217 → 42858 |

## Draft model precision
No change to the DSpark draft (`Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`). Its `ModelConfig` is built from the speculative config's own `quantization` (unset) and never receives `quantization_config`, and the K3 draft's `get_draft_quant_config()` returns `None`, so it keeps its BF16 checkpoint weights. The load log lists only target layers as quantized.

## Validation
- `python -m infx.workflows.validate_perf_changelog --base-ref origin/main --head-ref HEAD`: passed, matrix generated.
- Recipe parses as YAML, and each of the 10 matrix points (c1, c4, c10-c16, c44, c48, c70, c75) matches exactly one variant by CONC and KV_OFFLOADING.
- Not yet run: GSM8K accuracy with the flag, the full AgentX sweep (this PR), including the new c16 and c75 variants.

<details><summary>中文</summary>

## 概要
- 在 Kimi-K3 MI355X vLLM AgentX recipe（`benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/kimik3/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`）的 base `agg` 参数中新增 `--quantization-config '{"linear":"fp8_per_channel","ignore":["*kv_b_proj","*vision_tower*","*mm_projector*","*in_proj_qkvgfab","*f_b_proj","*fused_qkv_a_proj","*self_attn.g_proj","*.layers.0.mlp.down_proj"]}'`，`kimik3-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp`（#3561 新增；取代 #3626）的所有点都会继承该参数。

DSpark 草稿模型（`Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`）不变。其 `ModelConfig` 使用 speculative config 自身的 `quantization`（未设置），不会接收 `quantization_config`，且 K3 草稿的 `get_draft_quant_config()` 返回 `None`，因此保持检查点中的 BF16 权重。加载日志中被量化的只有目标模型的层。

- `validate_perf_changelog` 通过，matrix 生成成功。
- recipe 可正常解析，10 个 matrix 点（c1、c4、c10-c16、c44、c48、c70、c75）按 CONC 与 KV_OFFLOADING 各自恰好匹配一个变体。

</details>

title: [Klaud Cold] Add MiMo-V2.6-Flash B200 SGLang and vLLM AgentX recipes / [Klaud Cold] 新增 MiMo-V2.6-Flash B200 SGLang 与 vLLM AgentX 配方
body:
## Summary

Adds AgentX coverage for [XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL](https://huggingface.co/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL), a 309B-total / 15B-active MiMoV2 model, on B200 with upstream SGLang and upstream vLLM. Neither key uses speculative decoding yet.

**What runs:** two new keys, 24 points in total. Every point keeps the KV cache on the GPU (no CPU offload).

| Key | Image | Points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mimov2.6flash-fp4-b200-sglang-agentic` | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130` | TP4 at conc 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64; TP2 at 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 |
| `mimov2.6flash-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic` | `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` | TP8 at conc 1, 4; TP4 at 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64; TP2 at 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 |

Both images are pinned by digest. Admission is 2× concurrency for subagent fan-out, and decode CUDA graphs cover the concurrency.

**Precision (`fp4`), checked against the checkpoint's safetensors headers:**
- Routed experts, about 98% of the parameters, are packed MXFP4 (E2M1 with an E8M0 scale per 32 values).
- Dense MLP, fused QKV and MTP layers are FP8 E4M3 with 128×128 block scales.
- `o_proj`, router, embeddings and `lm_head` are BF16.
- On B200 both engines run the routed experts natively as MXFP4 weights × MXFP8 activations (FlashInfer TRT-LLM), and the FP8 layers as block-scaled FP8. This is the same mixed layout as `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, which this repo labels `fp4`.

**SGLang settings** (from the [SGLang MiMo-V2.5 cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Xiaomi/MiMo-V2.5); V2.6-Flash uses the same `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` architecture and size class):
- `moe-runner-backend: flashinfer_mxfp4`. v0.5.21's MiMo default picks the FP8 TRT-LLM runner on SM100 for any `quant_method: fp8` checkpoint, which cannot read packed MXFP4 experts. The upstream fix (sgl-project/sglang#41668) landed after v0.5.21.
- `attention-backend: fa4`, because the default `trtllm_mha` rejects MiMoV2's asymmetric K/V head dims on Blackwell.
- No `language-model-only`: v0.5.21 rejects it for `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` (the first canary failed at startup on it). The vision and audio encoders (~2 GB) therefore load, with `mm-attention-backend: fa4` for the ViT; text-only AgentX requests never run them.
- `chunked-prefill-size 16384`, `mem-fraction-static 0.85`, `mimo` reasoning and tool-call parsers.
- No TP8: the fused QKV weights are interleaved for 4-way TP (`num_key_value_heads = 4`), and SGLang requires the attention TP size to divide 4.

**vLLM settings** (from [vLLM's MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL.yaml), which names v0.31.0 as the first release that loads this checkpoint):
- `gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`, `max-model-len auto` (the largest context the KV pool holds, for the uncapped AgentX corpus), `max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, `mimo` parsers.
- TP8 is valid here: vLLM regroups the fused QKV per rank and replicates KV heads.
- vLLM's `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` is text-only, so no `language-model-only` flag is needed.
- KV cache stays BF16: the MiMo FP8 KV fix (vllm-project/vllm#58128) landed after v0.31.0.

Thinking stays on for both engines, which is the chat template's default.

**Known gaps:**
- **No speculative decoding yet.** `infx/golden_al_distribution/` has no MiMo curve, so a speculative run would fail at launch. #4331 adds a vLLM collector for the checkpoint's DFlash drafter; DFlash arms follow once that curve is committed.
- **Weights are not pre-staged on `b200-nscale`.** `runners.yaml` has no entry for this model, so `hf:XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL` is served from the shared HF hub cache, the same way as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on this cluster. The repo is not gated. The first job downloads the checkpoint.
- **Checkpoint choice.** Xiaomi has since released `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD` (same architecture and format), which fixes the RL release's tool-call repetition. This PR stays on the RL checkpoint; MOPD can be added separately.
- **Not in the engine-mapping table.** This PR adds only the MODELS.md support-matrix row; maintainers decide the model-to-engine mapping.
- **Not yet run end to end on GPUs.** The first canary failed at server startup on `language-model-only` (fixed above); the `full-sweep-fail-fast` sweep reruns on the latest commit.
