**运行内容：** 新增两个配置键，共 24 个点。所有点的 KV 缓存都保留在 GPU 上（不做 CPU 卸载）。

| 配置键 | 镜像 | 测试点 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mimov2.6flash-fp4-b200-sglang-agentic` | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130` | TP4，并发 1、4、8、16、32、64；TP2，并发 1、4、8、16、32 |
| `mimov2.6flash-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic` | `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` | TP8，并发 1、4；TP4，并发 1、4、8、16、32、64；TP2，并发 1、4、8、16、32 |

两个镜像均按 digest 固定。准入上限为并发的 2 倍，以容纳子 agent 扇出；decode CUDA graph 覆盖到并发数。

**精度（`fp4`），已对照检查点的 safetensors 头信息核实：**
- 路由专家约占参数量的 98%，以打包的 MXFP4 存储（E2M1，每 32 个值一个 E8M0 缩放因子）。
- 稠密 MLP、融合 QKV 与 MTP 层为 FP8 E4M3，采用 128×128 分块缩放。
- `o_proj`、路由器、词嵌入和 `lm_head` 为 BF16。
- 在 B200 上，两个引擎都以原生 MXFP4 权重 × MXFP8 激活（FlashInfer TRT-LLM）运行路由专家，FP8 层按分块缩放 FP8 运行。这与 `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` 的混合布局相同，本仓库将其标记为 `fp4`。

**SGLang 设置**（参照 [SGLang MiMo-V2.5 cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Xiaomi/MiMo-V2.5)；V2.6-Flash 与 V2.5 采用相同的 `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` 架构，规模也相同）：
- `moe-runner-backend: flashinfer_mxfp4`。v0.5.21 的 MiMo 默认配置会在 SM100 上为任何 `quant_method: fp8` 的检查点选择 FP8 TRT-LLM runner，而它无法读取打包的 MXFP4 专家。上游修复（sgl-project/sglang#41668）在 v0.5.21 之后才合入。
- `attention-backend: fa4`：在 Blackwell 上，默认的 `trtllm_mha` 不支持 MiMoV2 的非对称 K/V head 维度。
- 不使用 `language-model-only`：v0.5.21 对 `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` 会拒绝该参数（首次 canary 因此在启动时失败）。因此会加载视觉与音频编码器（约 2 GB），ViT 使用 `mm-attention-backend: fa4`；纯文本的 AgentX 请求不会调用它们。
- `chunked-prefill-size 16384`、`mem-fraction-static 0.85`、`mimo` 推理与工具调用解析器。
- 无 TP8：融合 QKV 权重按 4 路 TP 交错存储（`num_key_value_heads = 4`），SGLang 要求注意力 TP 大小能整除 4。

**vLLM 设置**（参照 [vLLM 的 MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL 配方](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL.yaml)，其中指出 v0.31.0 是首个能加载该检查点的版本）：
- `gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`、`max-model-len auto`（KV 池能容纳的最大上下文，适配不截断的 AgentX 轨迹）、`max-num-batched-tokens 16384`、`mimo` 解析器。
- vLLM 可以跑 TP8：它会按 rank 重新组织融合 QKV，并复制 KV head。
- vLLM 的 `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` 只含文本部分，因此无需 `language-model-only`。
- KV 缓存保持 BF16：MiMo 的 FP8 KV 修复（vllm-project/vllm#58128）在 v0.31.0 之后才合入。

两个引擎都保持开启思考模式，这是 chat template 的默认行为。

**已知缺口：**
- **暂未启用投机解码。** `infx/golden_al_distribution/` 中还没有 MiMo 曲线，投机解码运行会在启动时失败。#4331 新增针对检查点 DFlash 草稿模型的 vLLM 采集脚本；曲线提交后再加入 DFlash 配置。
- **`b200-nscale` 上未预置权重。** `runners.yaml` 中没有该模型的条目，因此 `hf:XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL` 从共享 HF hub 缓存加载，与 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 在该集群上的做法相同。该仓库不需要申请访问权限，首个任务会下载检查点。
- **检查点选择。** 小米随后发布了 `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD`（架构与格式相同），修复了 RL 版本的工具调用重复问题。本 PR 仍使用 RL 检查点，MOPD 可另行添加。
- **未加入引擎映射表。** 本 PR 只在 MODELS.md 支持矩阵中新增一行，模型与引擎的映射由维护者决定。
- **尚未在 GPU 上完整跑通。** 首次 canary 因 `language-model-only` 在服务启动时失败（已在上文修复）；`full-sweep-fail-fast` sweep 会在最新提交上重新运行。

Summary
This PR pipelines direct NVLink dispatch using three shared-memory TMA buffers per dispatch warp.
Previously, a dispatch warp prepared tokens sequentially around remote S2G stores. With this change, the next token's hidden data, scale factors, metadata, and routing information are prefetched while previous remote stores remain in flight.
At steady state, the three buffers are used for:
A previous token whose remote S2G store may still be in flight.
The current token being sent to remote ranks.
The next token being prefetched from global memory.
Before recycling the oldest buffer,
tma_store_wait<1>()
reduces the number of outstanding store groups to one. This keeps buffer reuse safe without fully draining all remote stores between tokens.
The shared-memory calculation now accounts for all three staging buffers, and direct NVLink dispatch is limited to at most 14 dispatch warps. The non-NVLink path remains single-buffered.

🤖 ds-review-bot Code Review
v6
The multi-buffer TMA scheduling and matching shared-memory sizing appear consistent across NVLink and non-NVLink paths, with outstanding stores flushed before buffer reuse.
v4
The dispatch kernel switches from single per-warp staging (drained fully per token) to three round-robin staging TMA buffers per dispatch warp. While the current token's remote S2G/NVLink/RDMA store stays in flight, the next token's hidden/SF/metadata/routing is prefetched into the buffer whose previous use is the oldest outstanding store group (deterministically token_iter - 2 of 3, or none on a warm-up iteration); tma_store_wait<1>() retires that group before the buffer is overwritten, and the final barrier drains the last in-flight store. The host sizes per-warp smem by 3x (RDMA: 1x) and caps NVLink dispatch warps at 14, with the RDMA path remaining single-buffered and full-drained (unchanged behavior). Edge cases (first iteration, last token skipped, warps with no tokens, per-token global slot/counter writes) are all safe and unchanged. Measured on 8xH100 dispatch goes 250->280 GB/s, combine unchanged. Overall the change correctly and faithfully implements the PR as a pure pipelining/perf optimization on the previously single-buffered path.
v3
This PR pipelines direct NVLink dispatch by switching from double- to triple-buffered TMA staging (kNumDirectNVLinkTmaBuffers 2->3, kNumTmaBuffers 2->3 for the NVLink path), and refactoring the per-token body into a
prepare_token
lambda so the next token's hidden/SF/metadata/routing can be prefetched while the current token's remote S2G stores are in flight. The phase tracking was generalized from two scalars (phase_0/phase_1) to a
phases[kNumTmaBuffers]
array, and buffer indexing changed from bitmask (
& (kNumTmaBuffers-1)
) to modulo (
% kNumTmaBuffers
) to support 3 (non-power-of-two) buffers. The host-side shared-memory computation already multiplies by num_tma_buffers and caps direct NVLink dispatch at 14 warps.
Correctness analysis (all verified sound):
Buffer-reuse safety: In steady state, entering iteration N up to 2 store groups (iters N-2, N-1) are outstanding.
tma_store_wait<1>()
retires iter N-2's store (which read buffer (N-2)%3 == (N+1)%3) before prepare_token(N+1) writes into that same buffer. This correctly matches the recycled buffer to the just-retired store group, so triple buffering is safe.
Per-buffer mbarrier phases persist across reuse (buffer b used at iters b, b+3, ...), and
phases[]
is zero-initialized; flip semantics are preserved.
The buffer indexing change to
% kNumTmaBuffers
is applied consistently in both prepare_token and the main loop and is required because 3 is not a power of two.
The NVLink prefetch (prepare_token for the next token) is issued before awaiting the current buffer's load arrival, correctly overlapping the next token's G2S load with the current token's remote S2G store; it targets a distinct buffer with an independent mbarrier so there is no cross-buffer hazard.
Non-NVLink path stays single-buffered (kNumTmaBuffers=1) and keeps a full
tma_store_wait()
drain before recycling; behavior is unchanged. Startup/drain edges (num_tokens <= 1, first iteration with no outstanding stores) are handled by the
next_token_idx < num_tokens
guards.
Host/device consistency: the smem divisor in dispatch.hpp accounts for num_tma_buffers=3 and matches the device-side kNumTmaBuffers.
Overall the change is internally consistent and the pipelining logic is sound. The two comments below are minor maintainability suggestions, not correctness issues.

title: Fix cross-stream waits after deferred epilogues
body:
## Summary

Retain a completion event after a successfully executed `EventOverlap` hook, so
later waits on other CUDA streams also depend on the work enqueued by that hook.

The event returned by the communication operation precedes its deferred epilogue.
The first wait runs the hook on its current stream and clears the hook; another
stream currently waits only for the original communication event. It can then
read tensors before the epilogue's GPU work is complete. The same issue applies
to deterministic sorting registered as an after-wait hook.

The fix keeps the original event and its retained tensors alive, records a
separate native `EventHandle` after the hook succeeds, and includes it in later
waits. Explicit `release_handle=True` releases both event handles. Hooks still
run once and only the first wait returns their result. A failing hook remains
retryable. The ordinary no-hook path records no additional CUDA event. No
host/device synchronization is added.

## Regression coverage

The current diff includes a standalone two-function CUDA regression in
`tests/utils/test_event.py`:

- A deliberately delayed hook writer and a second-stream reader, with a raw
  original-event negative control, repeated waits, single-hook execution and
  explicit event-handle release. The test requires the delayed write to still
  be pending when the negative control completes; an ineffective window fails.
- A no-hook wait and context-manager release, checking that no extra epilogue
  event is recorded.

Run it in an installed/built checkout:

```bash
python tests/utils/test_event.py
```

### Historical extended harness

The earlier standalone CUDA regression harness, retained in the tested commit
[`e15813d`](https://github.com/yuweih205/DeepEP/blob/e15813df91be6a4288b280b8cb26a5e84b96c0e0/tests/utils/test_event.py), checks:

- Two subsequent reader streams after a deliberately delayed writer hook,
  with and without explicit release.
- Context-manager waits after a prior hook on a different stream.
- Multi-stream CUDA Graph capture and three replays.
- No extra event capture when no hook is registered.
- Hook failure/retry and first-wait return semantics.

Its eager race tests require the delayed write to still be pending before the
reader is queued. Otherwise they fail as an ineffective race test. They drain
both streams even if an assertion fails. This historical five-method harness
is not the current two-function regression.

## Validation

### Current polished revision

Head: `ebaaab5f4b58d3fd96ccbc9ba66481ba41cd1703`, based on public main
`b5a33eefda39485f438dc764695b71ba7b9249b6`.

Both current CUDA regression functions passed on H200 with PyTorch
`2.13.0+cu132`, CUDA 13.2 and NCCL 2.32.3. This run covers the current
two-function regression, not a rerun of the extended historical harness or
its CUDA Graph cases. The production wrapper's Python AST matches the
previously published fixed implementation.

### Historical extended validation

Validated on eight H200 141GB GPUs, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132, CUDA 13.2 and NCCL
2.32.3. Base: public main `93eb6eb238127e96c6d7a4a625a6dad158348509`; pinned
DeepJIT `cba802df081985141eeee36803685775c183a047`. The `_C` extension was built
from those unmodified native sources. Only the Python event wrapper differs
between the original/fixed regression arms.

- Original wrapper: all 24 suites (three per GPU) reproduce stale reads in
  both explicit-reader release cases and the context-manager case. The CUDA
  Graph case also reproduces stale reads in all 24 suites.
- Fixed wrapper: all 24 suites pass all five methods (120 method runs), with
  no skipped tests. Each Graph test verifies three replays.
- Upstream EP8 functional suite, deterministic, CPU counts enabled: all 36
  deferred-epilogue configurations and all 72 non-deferred configurations pass.
  This covers fresh/cached, compact/expanded, BF16/FP8 dispatch and combine,
  bias variants, previous-event and allocation-stream settings, and repeated
  deterministic dispatch checks.

These results belong to the earlier extended harness and functional-suite
validation. That larger harness is not included in the current diff; the
two-function CUDA regression above is included.

Re-run the upstream EP8 functional suite in an installed/built checkout:

```bash
for deferred in 1 0; do
    python tests/ep/test_ep.py --num-processes 8 --num-tokens 128 --hidden 512 \
        --num-topk 2 --num-experts 16 --num-sms 8 --skip-perf-test \
        --deterministic --defer-epilogue "$deferred"
done
```

The first historical build attempt stopped before tests because the image
lacked the DeepJIT dependency `elfutils/libdwfl.h`. Reusing the available
libdw/libelf development headers allowed the frozen source/test payload to
build and pass.

This is a stream-ordering correctness change, not a performance claim or a
full-model/training/backward validation.

title: [Bug] SM90 `fp8_einsum("bhr,hdr->bhd", a, b, d, c)` silently drops `c` and returns `a @ b.T`
body:
## Description

On SM90, `deep_gemm.fp8_einsum("bhr,hdr->bhd", a, b, d, c=c)` returns $d = a \cdot b^\top$ instead of $d = c + a \cdot b^\top$. No error is raised, and the output looks like a normal result. The same happens when `d` and `c` are the same tensor (in-place accumulation). On SM100 the result is correct.

[The README's convention](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/README.md?plain=1#L63) is `D = C + A @ B` ("`fp8_gemm_nt` will do a `D = C + A @ B.T`"), and `fp8_einsum` accepts `c` on every architecture. `"bhr,hdr->bhd"` is the only `fp8_einsum` expression that runs on SM90, so any caller that accumulates through it on Hopper gets a wrong result.

## Environment

- H100 80GB HBM3 (sm_90), driver 580.126.09, CUDA 13.0 (nvcc V13.0.88), torch 2.9.1+cu130.
- DeepGEMM `main` 1fc9c66, CUTLASS f3fde58, built with `./develop.sh`.

## Root Cause

The host prepares `d` for an accumulating kernel, but on SM90 it launches a kernel that only stores:

1. `fp8_einsum` passes `c` to `fp8_bmm` ([einsum.hpp L276](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/apis/einsum.hpp#L276)), which calls `gemm::early_return` ([L230](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/apis/einsum.hpp#L230)). It copies `c` into `d`, expecting the kernel to add into `d` ([gemm.hpp L49–L51](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/apis/gemm.hpp#L49-L51)):

   ```cpp
   // With accumulation, do copy before GEMM (assuming the GEMM kernel does not support different C/D)
   if (c.has_value() and not is_cd_same)
       d.copy_(c.value());
   ```

2. On SM90, `fp8_bmm` calls `sm90_fp8_bmm` ([einsum.hpp L247](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/apis/einsum.hpp#L247)), which launches `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d_impl`. It sets `with_accumulation = c.has_value()` in the `GemmDesc` ([sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp L300](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp#L300)), but the flag is not a template argument of the kernel ([L36–L61](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp#L36-L61)), and the kernel writes `D` with a plain TMA store ([sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.cuh L434](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.cuh#L434)):

   ```cpp
   if constexpr (kGemmType == GemmType::Batched) {
       cute::SM90_TMA_STORE_3D::copy(&tensor_map_d, smem_ptr,
                                     n_idx, m_idx, scheduler.current_group_idx);
   ```

   This overwrites the `c` that step 1 copied into `d`. For comparison, `sm90_bf16_gemm` passes `with_accumulation` to its kernel as `kWithAccumulation` and switches the store to a reduce-add.

3. The other launcher of the same kernel, `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d` (used by `fp8_gemm_nt`), rejects `c` ([sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp L81](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp#L81)):

   ```cpp
   DG_HOST_ASSERT(not c.has_value() and d.scalar_type() == torch::kBFloat16);
   ```

   `sm90_fp8_bmm` has no such check.

`tests/test_einsum.py` passes `c` to `fp8_einsum` only on SM100 ([L183](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/tests/test_einsum.py#L183)), so the SM90 path with `c` is untested.

## Reproduction

`repro.py`:

```python
import torch
import deep_gemm
from deep_gemm.utils.math import per_block_cast_to_fp8, per_token_cast_to_fp8

torch.manual_seed(0)
b, h, r, d = 128, 8, 4096, 1024
x = torch.randn(b, h, r, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
y = torch.randn(h, d, r, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
x_fp8, x_sf = per_token_cast_to_fp8(x.view(-1, r), use_ue8m0=False)
y_fp8, y_sf = zip(*(per_block_cast_to_fp8(y[i], use_ue8m0=False) for i in range(h)))
a_ = (x_fp8.view(b, h, r), x_sf.view(b, h, r // 128))
b_ = (torch.stack(y_fp8), torch.stack(y_sf))

ab = torch.einsum('bhr,hdr->bhd', x.float(), y.float())
# as large as a @ b.T, in the layout fp8_einsum requires for C: [h, b, d] viewed as [b, h, d]
c = (ab.std() * torch.randn(h, b, d, device='cuda')).bfloat16().permute(1, 0, 2)
d_out = torch.empty_like(c)
deep_gemm.fp8_einsum('bhr,hdr->bhd', a_, b_, d_out, c=c)

rel_err = lambda ref: ((d_out.float() - ref).norm() / ref.norm()).item()
print(f'relative error vs c + a @ b.T: {rel_err(c.float() + ab):.3f}')   # expected: small
print(f'relative error vs a @ b.T:     {rel_err(ab):.3f}')               # actual: small
```

## Expected vs Actual

Expected: `d_out` ≈ `c + a @ b.T`, with a relative error at the FP8 level. If SM90 does not support `c` here, a host assertion is expected, as in `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d`.

Actual (`python repro.py` on the H100 above): `d_out` is `a @ b.T` up to the FP8 error, and `c` is missing.

```
relative error vs c + a @ b.T: 0.707
relative error vs a @ b.T:     0.037
```

## Suggested Fix

Either of the following removes the silent wrong result. Which one fits the intended SM90 support?

1. **Reject `c` in `sm90_fp8_bmm`**, as `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d` does:

   ```diff
   @@ -287,7 +287,7 @@ static void sm90_fp8_bmm(const torch::Tensor& a, const torch::Tensor& sfa,
                             const std::string& compiled_dims) {
   -    DG_HOST_ASSERT(d.scalar_type() == torch::kBFloat16);
   +    DG_HOST_ASSERT(not c.has_value() and d.scalar_type() == torch::kBFloat16);
        DG_HOST_ASSERT(major_a == cute::UMMA::Major::K and major_b == cute::UMMA::Major::K);
   ```

   With this change, `repro.py` raises `RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp:290): not c.has_value() and d.scalar_type() == torch::kBFloat16` on the same H100. As in `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d`, the check runs after `early_return` has copied `c` into `d`.

2. **Support `c` on SM90**: add an accumulation flag to `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d_impl` that writes `D` with a TMA reduce-add, as `sm90_bf16_gemm` does with `kWithAccumulation`, and pass `with_accumulation` to it from `sm90_fp8_bmm`.

I can open a PR for either option.

title: [Feat]Add native FP8 Tensor Core GEMM support for SM89 (Ada Lovelace)
body:
**Title**  
Add native FP8 Tensor Core GEMM support for SM89 (Ada Lovelace)

**Body**

## Summary

This change adds a native FP8 Tensor Core GEMM for SM89 (Ada Lovelace). SM89 is the first architecture below Hopper that has FP8 Tensor Cores.

Previously, SM80 and SM89 used the same path. The path required SM90 or higher for FP8. This was correct for SM80 because Ampere has no FP8 Tensor Cores. It was wrong for SM89. SM89 implements the instruction `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k32.row.col.f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32` (`QMMA.16832.F32.E4M3.E4M3`). The change separates the two architectures and gives SM89 a real kernel.

## Why

- SM89 has FP8 Tensor Cores. It does not have the SM90 features (no TMA, no `mbarrier.try_wait.parity`, no WGMMA, no clusters). It could not reuse the SM90 or SM100 kernels. It fell back to BF16 through cuBLASLt.
- FP8 users on Ada had to dequantize and run BF16. They lost about 2× of Tensor Core throughput.
- The shared SM80/SM89 path also gave wrong error messages. An SM89 user saw a message that did not apply to their GPU.

## Design

SM89 has no TMA and no asynchronous barriers. The kernel uses the pre-Hopper primitives.

- It uses `mma.sync` (wrapped in `deep_gemm/mma/sm89.cuh`, with A/B/C fragment layouts documented) and `ldmatrix.x4` for operand staging.
- It uses a multi-stage `cp.async` pipeline with a 128-byte XOR swizzle.
- It uses a persistent block scheduler (one CTA per SM). Tiles walk in a loop.
- It uses direct global stores because SM89 has no TMA store. It has an alignment-safe scalar tail. An MMA lane owns a pair of adjacent columns. For odd N the element offset of a row can be odd. A 2-element vector store is then illegal. This caused the original misaligned address failure.
- Block K is fixed at 128 because of the per-128-channel scaling granularity. Pipeline depth and tile shapes come from a new cost model in `csrc/jit_kernels/heuristics/sm89.hpp`. The warp split uses one shared function `get_mma_sync_warps_n()`. Host heuristics and device code both call it so they cannot disagree.

Both SM90 SF recipes are supported:  
`(1, 1, 128)` (per-token A and B scales) and  
`(1, 128, 128)` (per-token A, one B scale per 128-column N block).  
The second recipe is the default when FP32 scales are used. SM89 uses the same FP32 SF layouts as SM90. The function `transform_sf_into_required_layout` was extended. It was not duplicated.

## Scope

Supported features:  
dense FP8 GEMM, K-major (NT) operands only, FP32 and BF16 outputs, `D = C + A @ B`, ragged M/N, `k % 16 == 0`, both aliases (`fp8_fp4_gemm_nt`, `fp8_gemm_nt`, `fp4_gemm_nt`), and shape specialization.

Still rejected (with an explicit message that names the requirement):  
grouped and K-grouped FP8, MN-major FP8 operands, FP4, custom epilogues, `alpha` scaling, PDL, and MQA/attention.  
BF16 keeps its cuBLASLt fallback.

## Incidental fixes

- `set_pdl()` now panics below SM90. It no longer sets a flag that `griddepcontrol` cannot honour.  
  `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()` is wrapped in a no-op below `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900` so the SF-layout kernels compile for SM89.
- `call_cublaslt_api` used `CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32` for non-FP32 operands. That mode only down-casts FP32 inputs to TF32. BF16/FP8 operands ran at TF32 precision by mistake. Now only FP32 inputs use that mode.
- A new `DG_PANIC` macro throws always and carries a message.

## Bug found during validation

The persistent loop primed its `cp.async` pipeline only in the prologue before the tile loop. It relied on a cross-tile tail load to prime the next tile. A tile’s tail can only reach the stages that are already free of the current tile — prologue stages `p ∈ [0, kNumStages-2-num_k_blocks]`. The next tile’s K loop consumes `p = 0..num_k_blocks-1`. When `num_k_blocks < kNumStages-1` (example: `k=512`, 4 blocks, 8 stages) the high stages were never reloaded. The next tile read the previous tile’s shared memory. Symptom: non-deterministic `nan` and values near 1e30. The problem appeared only for small M spread over many N tiles.

The fix extracts the prologue into `prime_pipeline()` and re-primes unconditionally after the epilogue. The re-prime is guarded by `cp_async_wait<0>()` and a `__syncthreads()`. `cp.async` completion is per-thread, so both are required before the stages can be reused. The change removes a prologue/epilogue overlap that was never correct. Measured cost is about 0–3.5 % (4096³: 2518 µs vs 2507 µs, within noise; 4096×4096×512: 420 µs vs 405 µs).

`tests/test_sm89.py` added the shapes `(1, 4096, 512)`, `(64, 4096, 512)` and `(128, 4096, 128)`. Reverting the fix makes these tests fail (34 failures). They are real regression tests.

## Testing

Hardware: RTX 4060 Laptop (SM89, 24 SMs, 7.6 GiB), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

- `tests/test_sm89.py` — 17 tests, OK from a cold JIT cache (~130 s).  
  Covers both recipes × both output dtypes × accumulate × 12 shapes, explicit `recipe=(1,128,128)`, `recipe_a`/`recipe_b` pairs, entry-point aliases, compiled-dim specialization, bitwise determinism across repeats, accumulation-versus-zero-C equivalence, BF16 GEMM and all its layouts, cuBLASLt FP8/BF16, SF layout kernels, and one rejection case per unsupported feature.
- `tests/test_layout.py` — OK.
- Upstream `tests/test_fp8_fp4.py::test_gemm` — OK.  
  The upstream shape grid reaches m=129280 / n=7168 and OOMs on a 7.6 GiB card. Shapes were clamped to m≤4096, n≤4096, k≤1280 by monkey-patching `enumerate_normal` in a throw-away driver. The test body, recipes and assertions were not changed.
- Upstream `tests/test_bf16.py::test_gemm` — correctness OK, same clamping.  
  The perf-print block was stubbed because `bench_kineto` matches on the kernel name `bf16_gemm`, which does not exist on SM89 (BF16 goes through the cuBLASLt fallback). All `diff < 1e-5` assertions ran without change.
- Other suites fail only for environmental reasons and are unchanged by this PR:  
  `test_einsum` raises the intended “Unsupported architecture”,  
  `test_lazy_init` and `test_locality_domain` need multiple GPUs,  
  `test_bf16` / `test_legacy` OOM at upstream shapes.

Throughput, single GPU, FP8 in / BF16 out:

| m    | n    | k    | time      | TFLOPS |
|------|------|------|-----------|--------|
| 1    | 4096 | 4096 | 33.6 µs   | 1.0    |
| 128  | 4096 | 4096 | 168.4 µs  | 25.5   |
| 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 2517.8 µs | 54.6   |
| 4096 | 4096 | 512  | 419.7 µs  | 40.9   |

Summary
Replace
fmaxf(x, 0)
with
x + fabsf(x)
in the SM90 FP8 MQA logits epilogue, recovering the 2× throughput gap between FMNMX (half-rate) and FADD (full-rate) on Hopper. The factor-of-2 introduced by the identity is resolved by folding
0.5f
into the existing
scale_kv
multiply — zero extra instructions, bit-exact numerics.
Background
On SM90,
fmaxf(x, 0)
compiles to a single FMNMX, which issues at 64 ops/clk/SM — half the rate of FADD/FFMA (128 ops/clk/SM). Meanwhile
x + |x|
compiles to a single FADD with the absolute-value operand modifier, which is a free encoding bit in the instruction word:
FADD R3, R3, |R3|    ; one instruction, full rate (cuobjdump, sm_90a)
The relu executes once per
(token, head, kv)
score element in the MQA logits epilogue, so at 64 vs 128 ops/clk/SM the FMNMX form doubles the FP32 pipe time spent on relu alone.
Since
x + |x| = 2 · relu(x)
holds exactly for all finite IEEE-754 floats (
+0
for x ≤ 0), the doubled sum is simply halved by folding
* 0.5f
into the already-existing
scale_kv
multiplication (an exponent decrement, also exact):

x + |x| == 2*relu(x)

scale_kv * 0.5f

Placement of the

/

fmaxf(x, 0)
ReLU in the SM90 FP8 MQA logits epilogue with a full-rate FADD using the free absolute-value operand modifier (
x + |x|

* 0.5f

scale_kv

x + |x| == 2*relu(x)

x + x == 2x
exactly for x > 0); (2) the factor-of-2 is uniform across the per-term weight multiply and across both the intra-thread and inter-thread (shuffle-xor) reductions, so it factors out exactly; (3)
scale_kv * 0.5f

fl((2*sum) * (scale/2)) == fl(sum * scale)

fmaxf
path. The change is local (3 lines in one file: line 286 transform plus the two
* 0.5f

fabsf
+
/2

fmaxf(NaN, 0) == 0
while
x + |x|
propagates NaN and
x == -inf
gives
NaN

scale_kv

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash stores each KV token as 528B: 512B of FP8 E4M3 covering
the full 512-wide K (rope lanes quantized, no BF16 rope segment) plus a 16B
footer of 16 UE8M0 scales over 32-wide groups (the
deepseek-ai/FlashMLA#221
layout, SM100-only there). Add ModelType::DSV4_1 on top of the ScaleSpec
groundwork: GLM53_NOPE-style geometry (D_ROPE=0) composed with a 32-wide
UE8M0 footer.

Kernel side the format is simpler than DSV4 (one 512B bulk per row, a single
unified block-scaled FP8 QK pass, no rope MMA paths). The two new mechanics:

- the 16B footer row generalizes the scale gather from one uint64_t to a
  width-selected load (uint4) in both the prefill IO helper and the decode
  kernel's staged gather;
- the 32-wide groups constrain the XV W-fold (one scale group per W buffer),
  so an 8-warp XV split would floor NT_PER_WARP_XV to 0: decode runs a
  4-math-warp tile at BI=64 (the DOTS3_SWA halving precedent) and prefill is
  SG-only on the BI=32 producer/consumer tile. The ComputeTraits/SmemLayout
  aliases now take the XV warp count so the NT_PER_WARP_XV assert evaluates at
  the warp count the XV MMA actually runs at.

title: [SM90] Add packed selected-KV sparse decode by xyz2606 · Pull Request #200 · deepseek-ai/FlashMLA · GitHub
body:
Conversation
xyz2606
commented
Jul 26, 2026
•
edited
Loading

Copy link
Copy Markdown
Summary
This PR adds an opt-in, two-stage packed selected-KV sparse decode path for the
GLM-5.2 / V3.2 FP8 MLA format on SM90:
pack_selected_kv
gathers selected records from the paged KV cache into an
opaque tile-major workspace.
flash_mla_with_packed_kvcache
consumes that workspace with a packed
sparse-decode specialization that avoids sparse index and page translation
on the attention critical path.
The existing native sparse-decode API and dispatch remain unchanged. The new
path is explicitly restricted to SM90 and is not enabled automatically.
Note
Alternative host-offload path (not part of this pr):
The packed interface also enables a separate offload path in which gathering and packing are performed on the host, followed by transferring only the packed selected-KV workspace to the device. In this case, the full KV caches of the shared layers no longer need to remain resident in HBM. This can substantially expand KV-cache capacity.
Since this implementation introduces a compile-time packed-KV specialization in the existing SM90 sparse decode kernel, I’d appreciate maintainers’ guidance on whether you prefer the current shared-kernel approach, a policy/loader-based abstraction, or a separate packed-kernel implementation; I’m happy to restructure it in a follow-up revision based on your feedback.
Motivation
GLM-5.2 can share selected physical indices across multiple MLA layers. When
those indices are available before the layer that consumes them, the runtime
can move sparse address resolution and KV gathering into an earlier overlap
window.
The attention kernel can then read a contiguous packed workspace instead of
repeatedly:
loading and validating physical indices;
translating indices into page and in-page coordinates;
constructing unrelated global addresses; and
gathering NoPE, scale, and RoPE components from the paged cache.
Packing and attention are intentionally separate operations so a runtime can
overlap packing with preceding work such as MoE communication.
What changed
SM90 packing kernel
pack_selected_kv
copies each selected 656-byte V3.2 record byte-for-byte:
512-byte FP8 E4M3 NoPE data;
16-byte FP32 scales; and
128-byte BF16 RoPE data.
The packer writes an opaque 64-token tile-major workspace. It supports a valid
selected-index prefix described by
topk_length
and zero-fills invalid suffix
records.
Callers may provide reusable contiguous
uint8
storage using
get_packed_kv_workspace_size
.
Packed attention specialization
The packed H=64 and H=128 instantiations reuse FlashMLA's existing:
WGMMA and dequantization pipeline;
online softmax;
DSM clustering for H=128;
split accumulation;
epilogue; and
combine kernel.
The specialization replaces the sparse index/page/gather loader with direct
tile-major loads and preserves partial-tail masking.
Scheduler policy
H=128 uses the same scheduler as native sparse decode.
H=64 uses the compact request-local scheduler selected by the L20X
experiments. For the measured full-prefix
topk=2048
, 132-SM
B*S_q=16
regime, it falls back to the faster native scheduler.
This scheduler is used only by the opt-in packed helper and does not change
native sparse decode. The benchmark includes an identical-scheduler control to
isolate the packed-load kernel gain.
Python API
This PR adds:
get_packed_kv_workspace_size
get_packed_mla_metadata
pack_selected_kv
flash_mla_with_packed_kvcache
Supported scope
The initial path is intentionally limited to:
SM90;
V3.2 FP8 sparse KV records;
d_qk=576
;
d_v=512
;
H in {64, 128}
;
MQA KV; and
top-k capacity divisible by 64.
The API fails closed for unsupported architectures and shapes. SM100 is not
enabled because this implementation has only been evaluated on SM90.
L20X results
The repository-local benchmark was run on an NVIDIA L20X with 132 SMs using:
CUDA 13.0;
PyTorch 2.13.0;
topk=2048
;
B={1,2,4,7,8}
;
S_q={1,2,3,4,8,16}
;
H={64,128}
;
request-disjoint physical KV ranges;
a 512 MiB L2 flush before each measured path;
10 warmups and 200 timed repetitions; and
60 total cases.
Comparison
Geometric-mean speedup
Wins
Packed attention, identical scheduler
1.098x
60/60
Integrated packed attention stage
1.115x
60/60
Integrated H=64 cohort
1.131x
30/30
H=128 cohort, native scheduler
1.100x
30/30
Pack + attention without overlap
0.740x
0/60
Packing is excluded from the attention-stage comparisons.
The unhidden result is included deliberately: this path is useful only when
the runtime can move most packing work outside the attention critical path.
This PR does not add automatic dispatch or change the default native path.
The H=64 hybrid policy selected the tuned scheduler in 26 cases and the native
fallback in four cases. The four fallback cases improved by approximately
6.5% to 7.4% compared with using the tuned scheduler unconditionally.
Correctness and benchmark coverage
python tests/test_flash_mla_packed_sparse_decoding.py
python benchmark/bench_flash_mla_packed_sparse_decode.py \
  --output packed_sparse_decode_latency.csv
The correctness test passes five cases covering:
a single full boundary tile;
H=64 partial tails and heterogeneous active lengths;
the H=64 native-scheduler fallback;
full production top-k with H=128; and
H=128 heterogeneous partial tails.
The tests compare both output and LSE with native sparse decode and verify the
packed workspace layout.
Observed result:
passed 5 packed sparse-decode cases
The new CUDA kernels compiled for SM90 without register spills. The packer
used 18 registers, and both packed-attention instantiations used 168 registers.
Runtime follow-up
This PR contains the two FlashMLA kernels needed for the packed path, but
intentionally does not include current-token runtime orchestration.
A future vLLM integration can:
pack historical records early into caller-managed storage;
overwrite any selected current-token record after its KV becomes available,
for example with a scatter operation;
synchronize the packing/update stream with attention; and
select native fallback when the expected overlap is insufficient.
Workspace pooling, CUDA stream placement, current-token updates, overlap
eligibility, and end-to-end TPOT measurements belong to that runtime
integration.
For
topk=2048
, the workspace requires approximately 1.281 MiB per query row,
so runtime dispatch should also enforce a workspace budget.
Non-goals
This PR does not:
replace or modify the behavior of native sparse decode;
enable the packed path by default;
add SM100 support;
claim an end-to-end speedup without concurrent runtime integration; or
include current-token patch orchestration.
setup.py
is changed only to register the three new CUDA source files.

title: [SM90] Support dynamic top-k for V3.2 sparse decode by Livinfly · Pull Request #216 · deepseek-ai/FlashMLA · GitHub
body:
Conversation

Copy link
Copy Markdown
Summary
This PR adds optional per-request
topk_length
support to the SM90
DeepSeek-V3.2 FP8 sparse decode kernel (
d_qk=576
). SM90 V3.2 can now use
dynamic top-k instead of always processing the full allocated top-k capacity.
When
topk_length
is provided, the kernel:
loads the valid length for each batch row;
schedules only
max(ceil_div(topk_length, TOPK_BLOCK_SIZE), 1)
blocks;
masks a partial tail before its indices can be used for KV addressing; and
includes the absolute top-k position in the softmax validity predicate.
When
topk_length == nullptr
, the existing fixed top-k behavior is preserved.
There is no public API change, and MODEL1 and SM100 behavior are unchanged.
Why
template<bool DYNAMIC_TOPK, ...>
I also tested a single-device-kernel implementation that checks
params.topk_length != nullptr
at runtime. The condition is grid-uniform, but
the compiler cannot remove the length load, tail predicates, extra control
flow, or their value lifetimes from the fixed path.
template<bool DYNAMIC_TOPK>
moves the choice to host launch dispatch:
false
: the dynamic-length logic is compiled out, preserving the fixed path;
true
: per-row block counts and partial-tail safety checks are enabled.
The comparison implementation is available at
7b7c831
on
test/sm90-v32-dynamic-topk-runtime-device
. It regresses the representative
B64-B128 fixed cases by 8.4%-9.4%, while the specialized implementation stays
within 0.5% of the baseline. Both builds report 168 registers, 12 barriers,
and no spills, so the generated hot-path instructions—not an occupancy

title: feat(moe_ep): per-token FC1 activation scale for the SM100 CuTeDSL NVFP4 MegaMoE
body:
## 📌 Description

Adds an optional **per-token FC1 activation scale** to the SM100 CuTeDSL NVFP4 MegaMoE path (`sm100_nvfp4_nvfp4_bf16_cutedsl`).

**Why.** NVFP4 activations carry only an e4m3 block scale (3 mantissa bits per 16-element block), so a caller that wants to keep a per-token dynamic range (e.g. quantize `x_t / s_t` instead of `x_t`) has nowhere to put `s_t` on the input side: `fc1_alpha` is per-expert, and `topk_weights` is applied *after* the activation. The scale must be re-applied to the dequantized FC1 output **before** the clamp / SwiGLU nonlinearity, i.e. inside the FC1 epilogue. This PR ports that feature from the kernel team's MR (`cutedsl_megamoe!1`, "support static runtime per-token global scale") into the vendored drop and plumbs it through the shim, the FI backend, and `MoEEpTensors`.

**Math.** With `s_t` the per-token scale and `q(·)` the host NVFP4 quantizer:

```
kernel input:   q(x_t / s_t)
FC1:            acc1_t = W1 · q(x_t / s_t)             ≈ (W1 x_t) / s_t
FC1 epilogue:   real   = fc1_alpha_e · s_t · acc1_t  → clamp → gated act (→ × topk) → NVFP4 quant
FC2 / combine:  unchanged
```

**What changes**

- Kernel drop (`kernel_src/sm100/cutedsl_megamoe/src/`, recorded as a pending-upstream diff in `VENDOR.md`):
  - `kernel_fc12.py` / `megamoe_kernel.py`: new constructor switch `enable_fc1_activation_per_token_scale` (enters `name()`), new optional runtime arg `fc1_activation_per_token_scale: (T,) fp32`, new pool-ordered local workspace region `l1_fc1_activation_per_token_scale_buffer`. Off by default: `name()`, the workspace layout and the compile ABI are byte-identical to today when disabled.
  - `token_comm.py`: the dispatch warps peer-pull the source token's scale (lane 0, one `ldg.f32` next to the existing topk-weight load) and write it to the pool slot, so the user tensor lives on the symmetric heap exactly like `topk_weights`.
  - `custom_ext.py`: `get_gmem_tensor("fc1_activation_per_token_scale")` = data-token `domain_offset`, same as `"topk"`.
  - `epilogue_refactor.py`: `alpha_swiglu_clamp` folds `alpha · s_t` into the dequant multiply. Tokens 32..63 are activated after the register transpose (one token per lane → one scale per lane); tokens 0..31 are activated *before* the transpose, where register `i` of lane `L` holds token `2i + (L//2)%2`, so the scale is fetched with `shfl.idx` from lane `2i + parity` (16 SHFL per lane per subtile). This keeps the existing 3-transpose schedule instead of adding a 4th transpose.
- Shim (`shim/nvfp4.py`): `MegaMoENvfp4Config.enable_fc1_activation_per_token_scale`, `MegaMoENvfp4Inputs.fc1_activation_per_token_scale`, `MegaMoESymmBuffer.fc1_activation_per_token_scale` (symmetric-heap `(num_max_tokens,)` fp32, allocated only when enabled, initialised to 1.0), `get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe(..., enable_fc1_activation_per_token_scale=)`, `create_dummy_inputs(...)`; validation (present iff enabled, `(T,)` fp32 CUDA), compile-key / launch-key / slicing plumbing.
- FI backend: `Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig.enable_fc1_activation_per_token_scale`, `MoEEpTensors.fc1_activation_per_token_scale` (staged into the workspace each forward, validated in `validate_forward`), workspace pool key.
- Docs: `VENDOR.md` pending-diff entry, `docs/design_docs/moe_ep_architecture.md` field table.

**Not ported from the MR (on purpose).** The MR also made the FC1 quantization norm-const a compile-time constant (dividing it back in the FC2 epilogue) and added a `quick_geglu` activation. FlashInfer already has a runtime per-expert `fc1_norm_const` tensor (callers fold `1/norm_const` into `fc2_alpha` on the host; for a power-of-two norm like 16 this is bit-identical) and already covers quick-GeGLU through `swiglu_alpha=1.702` / `swiglu_beta`, so both are left out to keep the public API unchanged.

**Usage**

```python
cfg = Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig(
    intermediate_size=..., top_k=..., enable_fc1_activation_per_token_scale=True)
layer = MoEEpLayer(..., backend=MegaConfig(megakernel=cfg, quantize_input=False))
y = layer.forward(MoEEpTensors(
    hidden_states=x_nvfp4_packed, scales=x_sf, topk_ids=..., topk_weights=...,
    fc1_activation_per_token_scale=s_t))   # (num_tokens,) fp32
```

## 🔍 Related Issues

Kernel-team MR: `qiangf/cutedsl_megamoe!1` (branch `feature/nvfp4-static-per-token-scale`, head `71a70c7`, base `9d004cc`).

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

New / extended tests (all on 4× B300, `lmsysorg/sglang:dev`: torch 2.13.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.2, nvshmem 3.4.5):

- `tests/moe_ep/test_nvfp4_cutedsl_kernel_vs_reference.py` (single GPU, `MEGA_NO_DIST=1`)
  - `test_nvfp4_kernel_per_token_scale_matches_torch_reference[...]`, 7 cases: `regular-e4`, `tail-e4` (hidden 2880), `no-clamp`, `minimax-clamp` (swiglu 1.702/1.0, clamp 0.5) at 32 tokens per expert (first, shuffle-fed half of the 64-token epilogue subtile); `two-subtiles` (192 tokens, topk 2 of 4: both register halves carry valid tokens + a partial second subtile); `alpha-fold` (same routing with broadcast `fc1_alpha=2.0`, oracle fed `2*scale`: exercises the `alpha * scale_t` fold on both halves); `singleton-e1` (static expert extent 1, 3 subtiles). Kernel vs the scaled pure-torch oracle is bit-exact (`rel_l2 = 0`, same as the pre-existing oracle test on this setup); vs the *unscaled* oracle `rel_l2` is 0.17–0.66, so the test is discriminating.
  - `test_nvfp4_kernel_per_token_scale_with_epilogue_scalars[random-scalars|deploy-norm16]`: per-token scale combined with non-identity per-expert `fc1_alpha` / `fc2_alpha` / `fc1_norm_const` (the oracle now models all three with the kernel's semantics); `deploy-norm16` is the kernel-team recipe (norm const 16 in the fc1-out SF, `1/16` folded into `fc2_alpha` on the host) and also bounds its deviation from norm const 1 (`rel_l2` ≈ 0.005 here, coming only from blocks whose SF leaves the e4m3 normal range).
  - `test_nvfp4_per_token_scale_forward_validation`, `test_nvfp4_shim_per_token_scale_input_validation`: present-iff-enabled / shape / dtype / device checks at the FI backend and shim layers.
  - Tolerance model (`_oracle_atol`): `2e-3 * amax` (NVFP4 RTNE flips + accumulation order) plus `2 * bf16_ulp(amax)` for one bf16 rounding flip of a per-(token, topk) fc2 term (both sides store terms in bf16 before the top-k sum; observed once in the wide sweep where terms of ~300 cancel to a small output).
  - The 6 pre-existing cases still pass with the switch off (default ABI unchanged).
- `tests/moe_ep/test_moe_ep_nvfp4_cutedsl_mega_multirank.py` (torchrun, 4 ranks)
  - `test_moe_ep_nvfp4_cutedsl_mega_layer_per_token_scale_matches_reference[64|1024]`: `MoEEpLayer` forward with `MoEEpTensors.fc1_activation_per_token_scale` is bit-exact vs the direct shim launch staging the same scale (plumbing), at 64 and 1024 tokens per rank.
  - `test_moe_ep_nvfp4_cutedsl_mega_multirank_torch_oracle_per_token_scale[False-bf16|True-bf16|False-mxfp8]` (explicit reduce / in-kernel REDG reduce / mxfp8 combine wire): real cross-rank EP where every rank stages a different random per-token scale and tokens are routed across ranks, vs the pure-torch global-expert oracle. Validates the dispatch-side peer-pull of the scale, not only the epilogue fold. `rel_l2 = 0` (explicit reduce) / ≈0.003 (REDG, same band as the existing ikr oracle test).
  - `test_nvfp4_cutedsl_config_exposes_per_token_scale` (CPU).
  - The whole file (27 pre-existing + new cases) passes on all 4 ranks.

**Extended validation (off-CI, scripts + logs kept outside the repo).**

- Single-GPU kernel vs oracle sweep: 32 compiled configurations, 384 checks, all pass. Geometries 2048/1024/e4/k4, 2880/2880/e4/k4, 4096/2048/e8/k8, 7168/2048/e16/k8, 2048/1024/e1/k1, 4096/1024/e32/k2, 2880/1536/e8/k2; token counts 32/192/512/2048 per compiled session; epilogue scalars identity / random / norm16-recipe; activations standard, no-clamp, MiniMax (1.702, 1.0, clamp 0.5); switch off as control; 11 tuner knob sets (N=256 and N=64 tiles, 2-CTA M=256 and 256x256, the three token-back modes, atomic load balance, UBLK fc2 store, flag batches, in-kernel reduce). Max `rel_l2` vs oracle 1.9e-4 (explicit reduce, mostly 0), 4.3e-3 (in-kernel reduce); kernel vs the *unscaled* oracle ≥ 0.11 everywhere. Under the norm16 recipe the kernel matches the oracle also where SFs saturate (kernel e4m3 conversion saturates like the host clamp).
- 4-rank sweep: 16 tests x 4 ranks pass — layer parity at 256/2048/4096 tokens per rank with bf16 and pre-quantized inputs, mxfp8 and nvfp4 combine wires, in-kernel reduce at 1024 tokens, MiniMax activation, transformers graph (`apply_topk_in_fc1=False`); cross-rank oracles at 512/2048 tokens, nvfp4 combine, in-kernel reduce, MiniMax (`rel_l2 = 0` explicit / ≈0.003 REDG).

**Performance.** 4-rank steady-state launch timing (prebuilt `nvfp4_mega_launch_thunk`, 20 warmup + 100 timed launches, CUDA events, max over ranks, default knobs, 2 independent rounds each). The switch is `const_expr`-eliminated when off and adds ~2 LDG + 16 SHFL + 9 FMUL per lane per 64-token epilogue subtile when on. Off matches `main` within noise; on/off is -1.4% … +2.4%, the same magnitude as the round-to-round spread (up to 3%), largest for small token counts on small shapes where the epilogue is a larger fraction:

| shape (hidden / I / experts / topk) | tokens / rank | `main` (off) | this PR, off | this PR, on | on/off |

## Reviewer Notes

- The whole feature is a compile-time switch; with `enable_fc1_activation_per_token_scale=False` (default) the kernel `name()`, workspace carve-up and compile ABI are unchanged, and the epilogue code path is `const_expr`-eliminated back to today's instruction stream.

title: [Feature]: sm120 Cake MegaMoE for PCIe hosts: MXFP4-activation (W4A4) variant, int8/FP8 return codec, switch-level dedupe
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

On PCIe-only sm_120 hosts (8 GPUs behind two PCIe Gen5 switches, no NVLink; ~49-55 GB/s per direction on the x16 links and on the inter-switch fabric) `sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_bf16_cake` is slower per MoE layer than an unfused DeepEP-style all-to-all + DeepGEMM grouped-GEMM path, because its wire format carries roughly twice the bytes:

- dispatch records carry FP8 activations: 5120 + 160 (+224 header) B per row at H=5120, where an MXFP4 dispatch carries 2560 + 160 B;
- expert results return through the lossless BF16 codec, ~7.8 KB per route, where an int8 combine (per-128 fp32 scale) carries 5.3 KB;
- records are deduplicated per destination rank only; on a two-switch host, one copy per destination switch with the partial sums reduced inside the switch before crossing sends 2.2x fewer cross-switch bytes at EP8.

Measured at the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash routed geometry (E=384, H=5120, I=2304, top-k 6; EP8, 2048 tokens/rank, 6-layer CUDA graph, slowest rank, us/layer; the local-memory guard was raised to 16 B so the kernel loads at this geometry, see #6755):

| path | uniform | hot (one rank 2.5x) | recorded routing |
|---|---|---|---|
| unfused: all-to-all (one copy per destination switch, in-switch partial-sum reduction) + DeepGEMM grouped GEMM, **MXFP4 activations, int8 combine** | 3850 | 6243 | 4390 |
| same unfused path with **FP8 activations** (per-128 fp32 scales), int8 combine | 5623 | 9449 | 6447 |
| cake, `transport_table` = LSA inside each switch / GIN across (explicit table) | 4745-4936 (two runs) | 7478 | 5677 |
| cake `all_gin` / `all_lsa` | 6067 / 6050 | 7718 / 7615 | 7632 / 6247 |

Against the same-precision unfused path the fused kernel is 14-26% faster, so the overlap works; against the MXFP4-activation path it is 20-28% slower. Switching only the unfused path's activations from MXFP4 to FP8 moves its dispatch from 692 to 1328 us/layer (per-card egress 23.9 -> 46.4 MB/layer), so on these links bytes are time. Numerics for reference (rel L2 vs an fp32 reference with unquantized activations, 512 rows/rank): cake 4.7%, FP8-activation unfused path 4.8%, MXFP4-activation path 22%; cake vs the kernel-boundary oracle of `tests/moe_ep/test_moe_ep_sm120_w4a8_cake_mega.py` 1.6e-4 .. 3.2e-4.

### Requested outcome

A configuration of the sm120 Cake MegaMoE whose bytes on the wire match the unfused W4A4 path on PCIe hosts:

1. an MXFP4-activation variant (e2m1 + UE8M0 per-32 scales, `mma.sync kind::mxf4nvf4`): dispatch rows become 2560 + 160 B and both GEMMs run at the FP4 rate instead of the FP8 rate;
2. an int8 (per-128 fp32 scale) or FP8 return option in place of the lossless BF16 codec, selectable per deployment, with the combine summing the dequantized partials;
3. optionally, topology-aware dedupe in the transport table: one copy per destination LSA group (PCIe switch or host) with in-group fan-out on dispatch and in-group partial-sum reduction on return.

(1) + (2) alone remove the byte handicap, which is the whole 20-28% gap in the table above; what remains after that is the overlap efficiency of the protocol on PCIe (in these runs the kernel hides about a third of the communication time). The kernel's numerics already match the unfused FP8 path, so the request is about the transport format, not a new precision recipe.

### Target hardware

SM120 (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 50-series)

### Inference engine

vLLM

### Affected model or model family

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (MXFP4 routed experts: E=384, H=5120, I=2304, top-k 6, 1 shared expert)

### Workload and configuration

- Data type and quantization: MXFP4 expert weights (e2m1 + UE8M0 per-32) from the checkpoint; activations MXFP4 in our production path, FP8 (per-128 fp32 scale) in the same-precision control and FP8 (UE8M0 per-32) inside Cake; int8 combine (per-128 fp32 scale) on the unfused path, lossless BF16 codec in Cake
- Batch size or request concurrency: prefill, 2048 tokens per rank per step (also 384 and 1024 for the M64 schedule)
- Sequence lengths or token counts: 2048 tokens per rank per layer; routings: uniform, one rank 2.5x hot, and a recorded production routing
- Parallelism: DP8 / EP8 on one host (TP1, PP1); EP16/EP32 across hosts is the next step (GIN) and was not measured
- Relevant shapes: hidden 5120, intermediate 2304, 384 experts (48 per rank at EP8), top-k 6, swiglu_limit 10, max_tokens_per_rank 2048; 8x sm_120 72 GB GPUs, 110 SMs, two PCIe Gen5 switches x 4 GPUs, 2x 400G RDMA NICs per switch
- Environment: output of `python -m flashinfer.collect_env` is attached as a comment on #6755 (flashinfer 399b6c1d source tree, torch 2.13 + NCCL 2.30.7, CUDA 13.3)

### Current workaround

We run the unfused path: DeepEP-style all-to-all with MXFP4 activations on dispatch, DeepGEMM `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous` (FP4 x FP4) for both GEMMs, int8 combine, one copy per destination PCIe switch with in-switch partial-sum reduction. Its limitation is that communication and expert GEMMs are serial (about 1.97 ms + 1.93 ms per layer at this shape); a fused kernel could hide most of the smaller term, which is exactly what Cake does, but only if it does not double the bytes first.

### Impact

Throughput, Latency

### Acceptance criteria

- At E=384 / H=5120 / I=2304 / top-k 6, EP8, 2048 tokens per rank on an 8-GPU PCIe sm_120 host, the fused layer is not slower than the unfused MXFP4-activation path (3850 us/layer uniform, 4390 us/layer on recorded routing in our runs) and keeps the overlap gain measured against the same-precision unfused path (>= 10%).
- Per-card dispatch bytes at that shape ~24 MB/layer (MXFP4 rows) instead of ~46 MB; return bytes per route <= 5.3 KB.
- Correctness: passes `tests/moe_ep/test_moe_ep_sm120_w4a8_cake_mega.py`-style oracle checks (rel L2 <= 2%) for the new activation/return formats, protocol_error stays 0, CUDA-graph replay bit-identical to eager, across EP4/8/16 and both row schedules.

### Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

- #6755: at this geometry the shipped build spills one register (STACK 16 B) and the backend refuses to load the workspace; the measurements above used `LOCAL_BYTES_LIMIT=16` in the test rig. That needs to be resolved first for any sm120 Cake variant to be usable on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
- #6346 (the kernel), `kernel_src/sm120/cake_mxfp4_megamoe/README.md` (return codec, transport table, MOE_LSA_COPIERS).
- The SM100/SM107 `nvfp4_nvfp4` cutedsl families are the only W4A4 moe_ep kernels today; they use the NVFP4 recipe (e4m3 per-16 + per-tensor scale) rather than the MXFP4 checkpoint recipe (UE8M0 per-32) that the sm120 Cake weights already consume, so a W4A4 sm120 variant would ideally keep the MXFP4 recipe end to end.
- The dedupe/reduction scheme in (3) is what DeepEP's hybrid (two-hop) kernels do for NVLink+RDMA and what our PCIe variant does per switch; the per-pair transport table already carries the LSA/GIN topology needed to derive the groups.

### Timing or release need

_No response_

title: feat(attention): FA2 per-(token, head) FP8 KV scale
body:
Add a per-(token, head) FP8 K/V cache scale to the FA2 attention kernels. The scale is a separate float32 tensor mirroring the KV layout minus head_dim, following the NVFP4 block-scale design:

- kernel: one float32 scale per (KV row, head), staged into smem and applied in compute_qk (K scale on the S accumulator) and compute_sfm_v (V scale on the P fragment). Single/ragged derive the scale strides in-kernel from the KV strides (scale stride = KV stride / head_dim, as the NVFP4 path derives its SF strides); the paged path takes host-computed strides (GetFP8ScaleStrides) because its scale may be a non-contiguous view of an inline slot (last dim head_dim + 16).
- API: the scale is passed via the existing kv_cache_sf parameter (no signature change). single_prefill_with_kv_cache derives the feature from is_float8(kv) and kv_cache_sf is not None (mirroring the NVFP4 derivation); the ragged/paged prefill and paged decode wrappers take an explicit use_token_head_sf at plan time. The fa2 backend is required.
- decode: no CUDA-core kernel; the tensor-core (fa2 prefill) path is forced, reusing the prefill kernel.
- smem: the scale buffer (one float per KV row, K and V) is added to the shared-memory budget; on tight-smem configs (e.g. SM75 head_dim 256) the KV repack staging is disabled to make room.
- tests/bench: end-to-end coverage for single/ragged/paged prefill and paged decode, HND/NHD layouts, inline-slot views, the mirror-stride contract, and the negative validation paths.

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

vLLM implements a fine-grained, dynamic, inference-time FP8 KV cache quantization method known as `fp8_per_token_head`.
Compared to per-tensor FP8 quantization, it offers several advantages:
1. It eliminates the need for pre-calibration of per-tensor scales.
2. It employs a finer quantization granularity with dynamic scaling, resulting in superior quantization precision.
3. It calculates scales dynamically for each head, entailing lower computational overhead during quantization.

However, the current implementation relies on Triton and suffers from poor performance; a specially optimized native CUDA implementation is required.

title: fix(monomoe): fence fp8_act_full for the async proxy before the up-projection wgmma
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

**Summary.** In MonoMoE's fused kernel (`csrc/fused_moe/monomoe/src/moe.cuh`), no thread executes a proxy fence between the ordinary stores to `fp8_act_full` and the up-projection's `wgmma.mma_async` read of it, although the PTX ISA requires one. If a `wgmma` read the operand before the stores became visible to the async proxy, the up-projection would use stale FP8 activations, silently (the first `wgmma` read comes after two barriers and a weight TMA, so the window is likely closed in practice today). This PR adds `fence_proxy_async_shared_cta()` (`fence.proxy.async.shared::cta`) to `ptx_utils.h` and has every writing thread execute it.

#### Problem

- Phase 2 (`routing_phase_quantize`): warps 1–11 quantize the BF16 activations into `fp8_act_full` in shared memory with ordinary stores.
- Phase 3: after `__syncthreads()`, the up-projection reads `fp8_act_full` as a shared-memory operand of `wgmma.mma_async`.

#### Change

The new helper sits next to the existing fence helper. Every writing thread executes it after `routing_phase_quantize` and before the Phase 2 `__syncthreads()`. That is the pattern CUTLASS uses (`fence_view_async_shared()`, then the barrier, then the async-proxy read).

#### Why the fence is needed

PTX ISA 9.4, §9.7.17.7.1, the `wgmma.fence` page; §9.7.15.7.1 in ISA 8.8:

> An async proxy fence must be used to establish an ordering between prior writes to shared memory matrices and subsequent reads of the same matrices in a wgmma.mma_async instruction.

- `wgmma` reads shared memory through the async proxy.
- `__syncthreads()` synchronizes the threads but does not by itself order generic-proxy stores before async-proxy reads; PTX requires a proxy fence for that.
- `wgmma_fence()` (`wgmma.fence`) orders register accesses, not shared memory.

#### Cost

One fence per thread per launch.

#### Testing

- Evidence: found by reading the compiled PTX against the ISA. The first `wgmma` read comes after two barriers and a weight TMA, so the window is likely closed in practice today. This is a conformance fix, so the ordering does not depend on that timing.
- Not run: we have not run MonoMoE on hardware, and the change was not built or run in FlashInfer's tree.

title: perf(cake_gdn): one CTA per tile for ragged full-DV prefill batches (host launch grid)
body:
The `cake_gdn` package in `csrc/gdn/cake` ships 226 kernel records: 83 decode and 143 prefill. The prefill records cover 22 schedules: full-DV and DV-split chunked prefill, with and without an initial state, fp32, bf16 or fp8 recurrent state, bf16 or fp16 activations, and gate-stream and single-chunk forms. This PR changes only the host-side launch grid of the full-DV prefill records. No kernel body changes, every record keeps its shipped body byte for byte, and outputs are bit-identical to the previous launch on every measured shape. For a ragged batch on a full-DV program, the launch uses one CTA per (sequence, head) tile instead of the persistent residency grid (128 CTAs, or the SM count) when a host critical-path model predicts a critical path at least 4 % shorter. The model prices each tile at 2 x ceil(len / 128) + 4 chunk units and charges 1 extra unit per freshly dispatched CTA. It reads sequence lengths only when the caller passes `cu_seqlens_cpu`, so it adds no device synchronization. Equal-length batches, DV-split programs and launches of at most 128 tiles keep the previous grid. The two `8x1024` rows are equal-length controls of this kind, so both sides run the identical launch. The baseline is the same `cake_gdn` prefill kernels on FlashInfer main at 3e95a1fb with the previous launch grid. Speedup is previous time / this PR's time, so values above 1 mean this PR is faster. Every row uses `chunk_gated_delta_rule(backend="cake_gdn", use_cp=False, cu_seqlens_cpu=...)` with 16 query heads, 32 value heads and bf16 activations.

Timing: CUPTI activity kernel-time spans (101 launches per sample after 20 warm-up launches, L2 flushed before every launch; not CUDA events). The previous and new launches run in process order A,B,B,A, repeated 3 times. Each table cell is the median.

title: [CPU][Xeon6] Scope RedHatAI FP8 variants to validated hardware
body:
## Summary

Extend the variant-level hardware scoping introduced in #1029 to additional RedHatAI FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints.

The Xeon nightly recipe validation identified seven RedHatAI FP8 variants that failed during model startup. These variants were exposed because their parent recipes declare `xeon6: verified`, even though the specific checkpoints were not validated successfully on Xeon.

This PR adds explicit `supported_hardware` declarations to prevent unsupported variants from being selected for Xeon validation.

## Changes

- Add variant-level `supported_hardware` to 11 RedHatAI FP8/NVFP4 variants across five recipes.
- Restrict the seven failing FP8 variants to hardware already marked `verified` in their parent recipes, excluding Xeon.
- Preserve Xeon eligibility for the two RedHatAI FP8-block variants that passed validation.
- Ensure every new `supported_hardware` entry is a subset of the parent recipe's verified hardware list.
- Preserve existing BF16, INT8, INT4, and previously scoped variants.
- Do not introduce new hardware support.

Affected recipes:

| Recipe | Variants updated |
|---|---:|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 3 |
| Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct | 3 |
| Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct | 3 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct | 1 |
| Qwen3-4B | 1 |

The Llama 3.1 NVFP4 variant is left unchanged because its intended Blackwell targets are not included in the parent recipe's verified hardware list.

## Validation


Baseline results:
- 47 recipes tested.
- 40 passed.
- 7 failed during model startup, all RedHatAI FP8 checkpoints.
- Two additional RedHatAI FP8-block variants passed and remain Xeon-eligible.

Patch checks:
- All 11 new variant hardware declarations are subsets of their parent recipes' verified hardware lists.
- No existing variant-level hardware declarations are modified.

A follow-up nightly validation is required to confirm the updated Xeon discovery results and pass rate.

## Motivation

PR #1029 introduced variant-level hardware scoping to prevent model-level `xeon6: verified` from implicitly enabling unsupported checkpoint variants.

This PR closes the remaining gap for RedHatAI FP8 variants while retaining checkpoints that passed Xeon validation.

The change is limited to recipe metadata and does not modify vLLM runtime behavior.

title: [Bugfix] Make online FP8 MoE experts batch-invariant under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
body:
Fixes #57016

## Purpose

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a MoE model served with `--quantization fp8` (online per-tensor FP8, Triton experts) still produces output that depends on which other requests share its batch: greedy tokens flip within the first ~10 positions and prefix-cached K/V differs depending on who wrote it. Dense layers are invariant; only the experts are not.

Two things were wrong:

1. `Fp8PerTensorOnlineMoEMethod` (and `Fp8MoEMethod` for FP8-serialized per-tensor checkpoints with dynamic activations) quantize the expert inputs with one dynamic scale over the whole activation tensor (`kFp8DynamicTensorSym`), i.e. the max over every token of every co-batched request. Under batch-invariant mode this PR selects `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` and passes `per_act_token_quant=True`, mirroring what `Fp8LinearMethod` already does for dense layers.
2. Switching to per-token activations exposed a latent launcher bug: `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel` passed `stride_bse=0` for 1-D `[E]` weight scales (and `stride_bsn=1` for the singleton dim of `[E, 1, 1]`), so the kernel's `per_channel_quant` branch read expert 0's scale for every expert or indexed past the buffer. The combination tests already skipped "per-tensor weights + per-token activations" for the Triton experts as NYI, although `TritonExperts._supports_quant_scheme` advertises the pair. This PR passes the expert stride unconditionally and broadcasts singleton scale dims, and narrows the NYI gate to the still-unsupported "per-channel weights + per-tensor activations" case so the combination suite covers the fixed pair.

The bf16 Triton expert path is already invariant on `main` (`get_default_config`/`get_moe_configs` pin the tile config under the flag); the reporter's bf16 mismatch was on 0.27.1.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_online_fp8_moe_logprobs_bitwise_bs1_vs_bsN` (granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct, `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`, greedy, BS=1 vs BS=8 bitwise tokens+logprobs). Fails on `main`, passes with this PR.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: the per-tensor-weight + per-token-activation FP8 config is no longer skipped for `TritonExperts` / `BatchedTritonExperts` / `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts`.
- Reporter's reproducer (co-batch and writer-suffix modes) against a running server.
- Kernel check: `fused_experts` vs `tests.kernels.utils.torch_experts`, E=32, N=1024, K=2048, M=128, topk=4, per-tensor `[E,1,1]` weight scales: max abs err 0.010 with per-tensor activations, 0.003 with per-token activations (before the launcher fix the per-token case returned values in the thousands).
- Existing suites: `tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py::test_fused_moe`, pre-commit, `mypy-3.12`.

Hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120), WSL2, torch 2.13.0+cu130. The modular kernel combination suite itself does not run on this WSL2 machine (spawned worker fails with `CUDA error: invalid resource handle` on unmodified `main` too), so that part relies on CI and on the independent H20 run linked below.

## Test Result

- Reporter's probe, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 --quantization fp8`, before: A-alone vs A-with-B first token flip at 11 (logprob gap 0.166), warm-vs-cold flip at 11 (gap 0.347). After: every comparison identical, both rounds.
- gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct `--quantization fp8 --enforce-eager` (tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py): default (no flag) 34.1%, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on `main` 34.3%, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with this PR 32.7%. Per-token activation quantization is strictly finer than per-tensor, and the kernel-level error is lower, so the small delta is sampling noise from a 1B model.
- New e2e test: PASS with the PR, FAIL on `main` ("logprobs are not bitwise equal between BS=1 and BS=8; max abs diff 2.2e-01").
- Independent cross-architecture validation by @CarrotSwordsman on H20 (sm_90, real Linux GPU, driver 535), [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57092#issuecomment-5730213177): the same e2e test FAILS on a clean 0.28.0+cu129 wheel (max abs diff 2.8e-01) and PASSES with this PR's files applied, reproducing and eliminating the #57016 symptom on Hopper. Their `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py` run on the patched wheel was 8 passed / 2 failed / 1 skipped, the two failures being `deep_gemm`'s `NVCC >= 12.3` assert in a container pinned to 12.1. As they note, that suite does not discriminate against a release wheel (the pre-PR NYI skip is not present there to be removed), so the e2e pair is the evidence in that setup.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py` (non-DeepGEMM): 164 passed, 20 skipped. `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k test_fused_moe`: 241 passed. pre-commit and `mypy-3.12` clean on all changed files.

> Note: since #53585, online per-tensor FP8 is selected with `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`; commands above that use `--quantization fp8` predate that change.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #57016 (checked with `gh pr list --search "57016 in:body"` and by searching open PRs for "batch invariant moe"); #55881 is the XPU MoE variant and does not touch the CUDA Triton path or FP8 activation quantization.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation and drafting; every line was reviewed and every test run by the submitter.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>
