title: [AMD][DSV4.1Flash] Quantize MoE activations to MXFP8 before the MoRI dispatch
body:
## Motivation

MXFP4 W4A16 experts declare BF16 activations, so MoRI dispatches raw BF16 and
AITER quantizes to group-32 MXFP8 on arrival. A token routed to `k` distinct
ranks is therefore quantized `k` times — expected ~4.4 of 8 ranks at topk=6 for
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — and the dispatch carries 2 bytes/element instead of
1 + 1/32.

Quantizing in `prepare()` moves that to once per token on the rank that owns it,
and roughly halves the dispatch payload.

AITER already consumes the result: with a pre-quantized FP8 operand and E8M0
scales, its stage-1 path sorts the scales (`mxfp4_moe_sort_fwd`) instead of
running its own quant. This mirrors the MXFP4 W4A4 dispatch added in #59596,
which takes the same pre-quantized route for a4w4.

## Summary of changes

**`all2all_utils.py`** — adds `mori_use_mxfp8_dispatch()` and wires a third
dispatch mode into `maybe_make_prepare_finalize()`. MoRI infers the payload
dtype from the input tensor and transports `scale_dim` scales of
`scale_type_size` bytes per token, so the new branch sets
`scale_dim = hidden_dim / 32` and a 1-byte scale element. E8M0 exponents are
bytes, not the fp32 the per-token/per-tensor FP8 paths use.

**`prepare_finalize/mori.py`** — adds the `use_mxfp8_dispatch` flag and the
corresponding quant in `prepare()`, via `get_hip_quant(QuantType.per_1x32)` with
`scale_type=dtypes.fp8_e8m0`, matching the FP4 branch directly above it. The
mutual-exclusion assert becomes `sum(...) <= 1` now that there are three modes.

**Gating is deliberately narrow.** A pre-quantized operand is only safe when
AITER would have produced MXFP8 itself: a BF16-activation kernel would cast the
FP8 payload back to BF16 and never apply the scales, silently losing the
scaling. `mori_use_mxfp8_dispatch()` therefore asks AITER directly via
`resolve_activation_dtype()`, which is documented for exactly this case ("lets a
caller that produces the activations itself -- an all-to-all dispatch, a fused
epilogue -- emit that dtype directly") and returns `None` rather than guessing
when the answer would have depended on a token count that does not exist yet.
It also fails closed on `ImportError` and on a hidden dim that is not a multiple
of 32.

## Results

8x MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP8/EP8 with `mori_high_throughput`,
speculative decoding off. 8192 in / 1024 out, 256 prompts at concurrency 64,
against a stock nightly (`0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82`) with **only this change
applied** — this PR was measured on its own, with no AITER-side patches, so the
numbers are attributable to the dispatch change alone.

Engagement was confirmed rather than assumed: `resolve_activation_dtype(M=None)`
returns `torch.float8_e4m3fn` under the `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` that vLLM
pins for this model, and the dispatch kernel switches from
`EpDispatchIntraNodeKernel_bf16` to `EpDispatchIntraNodeKernel_fp8_ocp`.

### Performance

| Metric | Baseline | With patch | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 1103.58 | 1309.33 | **+18.6%** |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 9932.18 | 11783.95 | **+18.6%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 54.16 | 46.83 | **-13.5%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 54.68 | 46.69 | **-14.6%** |
| Median ITL (ms) | 51.40 | 44.29 | -13.8% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 3392.14 | 2248.40 | -33.7% |
| Benchmark duration (s) | 237.54 | 200.21 | -15.7% |

### Accuracy

gsm8k, 5-shot, all 1319 questions.

| Arm | strict-match | stderr | Delta | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0.9196 | 0.0075 | — | 0.9196 |
| With patch | 0.9280 | 0.0071 | +0.0084 | 0.9287 |

Within ~1 sigma of baseline. The same mxfp8 quantization is applied either way;
this only changes which rank performs it and how many times.

### Reproduction

Server:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1

vllm serve /model/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --language-model-only \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'
```

Benchmark:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tokenizer /model/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 256 \
  --max-concurrency 64 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 0 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

Accuracy:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --model_args base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,timeout=3600
```

title: [ROCm] Add gelu_tanh to the AITER fp8 fused MoE and zero-allocate the padded expert weights
body:
## Purpose

Supersedes #53259 (draft; its two commits are carried here unchanged, authored by @simondanielsson, co-authored with @elliotz-ai) and adds the one thing that PR's round-up needs to be safe: **allocating the padded fp8 MoE expert weights zeroed.**

1. Add `gelu_tanh` to the AITER fp8 fused-MoE backend (Gemma4-style models), via `ActivationMethod.GELU_TANH = 4` from aiter v0.1.21 (ROCm/aiter#4620). **Depends on the AITER bump in #52826.**
2. AITER's 2-stage CK fp8 MoE GEMM is numerically broken for non-128-aligned intermediate sizes (Gemma4-26B-A4B: 704), so #53259 rounds the size up to 768 for the AITER backend. Its comment claims the padded tail is zeroed by the loader — it is not: `create_weights` allocates `w13_weight`/`w2_weight` with `torch.empty` and the loader only narrow-copies the checkpoint's real 704 rows/columns. Rows 704–767 of `w13` (gate/up) and columns 704–767 of `w2` keep whatever the caching allocator hands out — device memory freed earlier in the same process — and that is live weight for the kernel: non-zero pad activations after GELU pollute the per-token `a2` quant scale and leak through the `w2` tail into the layer output.

## How this shows up

Whether a given process gets harmful leftovers in the padding depends on the allocation order at load time, so most processes look fine and an occasional one produces sporadically implausible tokens (typo-like output) with no error or warning. A load-time probe of the padded region in fresh processes finds non-zero bytes there; deliberately filling one layer's padding with stale-weight-like bytes reproduces the symptom, and filling every layer collapses the model. Zero-allocating removes the effect.

The other users of `maybe_roundup_sizes` (mxfp4, quark nvfp4) already allocate with `torch.zeros`; this makes the fp8 methods do the same and corrects the comment. The memset is a one-time cost at load.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests from #53259 (`test_fp8_round_up_intermediate_size_for_aiter`, `test_activation_method_enum_values`, `test_aiter_fused_moe_gelu_tanh_accuracy`).
- Gemma4-26B-A4B compressed-tensors FP8 (per-channel weights, per-token activations) on MI325X with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`: with zeroed allocation, sampled reply length and plausibility under the bf16 model match the non-AITER path; with `torch.empty` and garbage in the padding, the corruption reproduces.

## Test Result

ROCm-only; needs a runner with aiter ≥ v0.1.21 (after #52826).



**Tracking the AITER-side fix** (remove the manual padding requirement so the round-up here can go away): ROCm/aiter#5413

title: [Quantization] Support compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE with FP8 activations via Mxfp4MoEMethod
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Load compressed-tensors checkpoints with MXFP4 weights and dynamic FP8 activations (e.g. `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4-DSFP8`, `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK`, `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash converted to CT) and run them with the FP8 activations the checkpoint declares. Alternative to #59376 (cc @kylesayrs).

**Depends on #61556.** Humming 0.1.16, which `main` pins today, rejects FP8 (GS128) activations with MXFP4 weights, so these checkpoints fail to load with `--moe-backend humming` until #61556 lands.

## Claims

- MoE experts: `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4MoEMethod(Mxfp4MoEMethod)` only handles the `*_weight_packed` checkpoint naming and the declared activation scheme. Backend selection, weight conversion, size round-up, monolithic kernels and EPLB are inherited from the native MXFP4 method.
- The checkpoint's FP8 activation key reaches the Humming MoE backend. Before, it was dropped and Humming ran BF16 activations (W4A16) unless `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` was set.
- Dense linears with MXFP4 weights and FP8 inputs (GLM-5.3's dense MLPs target `Linear`) use a new `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4` scheme that requests FP8 activations, instead of the W4A4 scheme requesting MXFP4 activations.
- `get_moe_method` looks up the expert scheme with the layer's `ckpt_*_proj_name`, and DeepSeek-V4 (NVIDIA) passes `ckpt_names=("w1", "w2", "w3")`, so name-based targets such as `re:.*experts\.\d+\.w\d+$` match.

## Validation

H200 (SM90), `--moe-backend humming`, checked by inspecting the loaded layers.

| Model | Config | Dense MXFP4 linear | MoE experts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4-DSFP8 (real weights) | TP1 | n/a (FP8 block) | Humming, FP8 GS128 (W4A16 before this PR's 2nd commit) |
| GLM-5.3-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK (dummy weights, 5 layers) | TP1, TP2, TP2+EP | Humming, FP8 GS128 (FP8 per-token before) | Humming, FP8 GS128 (BF16 before) |

These runs used the v0.32.0 release branch with #61556, and `main` with #61556 applied. With `main` alone, the Humming 0.1.16 schema check rejects the combination. EP selects `HummingGroupedExperts` and TP selects `HummingIndexedExperts`. Greedy outputs match between TP2 and TP2+EP.

GSM8K, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 1x H200 (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --temperature 0 --max-tokens 1024`, 1319 questions, 5-shot):

| Checkpoint / activations | Accuracy |
|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` BF16 | 0.956 |
| MXFP4-DSFP8, MoE W4A16 (previous behavior) | 0.958 |
| MXFP4-DSFP8, MoE W4A8 (this PR) | 0.961 |

Tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k mxfp4 -v  # 4 passed (H200, main)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>  # incl. mypy
```

The original commit was also validated on B300 (SM103): a layer harness loading a real `RoutedExperts` with random MXFP4 weights was bitwise equal to native `Mxfp4Config` across the default, monolithic TRTLLM, unaligned-shape, `triton_unfused`, `marlin`, `deep_gemm`, `flashinfer_cutlass` and `flashinfer_trtllm` backends. Converted DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 generated the same token ids and logprobs as the original checkpoint on 8 prompts.

## Details

**Root cause of the BF16 fallback.** For `Mxfp4MoeBackend.HUMMING`, the MoE conversion built Humming's input schema only from `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` (`TODO: read input_quant_config from quant_config`), so an unset env meant BF16. With schema fallback enabled, Humming also demotes group-scaled FP8 to A16 (`prefer wna16 for groupwise weight or groupwise input`). Output still looked correct, so the slower path went unnoticed. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` now takes an optional `activation_key`. The HUMMING conversion uses it with fallback disabled, unless the env override is set. Other backends ignore the key.

**Performance.** At the GLM-5.x expert GEMM shapes (N/K 4096/6144 and 6144/2048, 32 experts, top-8; `benchmarks/bench_humming.py` at the #61556 Humming pin), W4A8 is 1.4-1.8x faster than W4A16 for M >= 256. End to end, the small Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 1x H200 is 3-8% slower with W4A8 than with W4A16 across prefill- and decode-heavy runs (hidden 2048, expert intermediate 512, so the per-layer activation quantization is not amortized). This PR follows the checkpoint's declared scheme. `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` still overrides it.

**Limitations**
- ROCm, XPU and CPU have no MXFP4 linear kernel for FP8 activations, so MXFP4 x FP8 dense layers keep the previous MXFP4-activation path there, with a warning. MI300 CI hit this; the linear test is CUDA-only.
- Blackwell: dense linears now use Humming FP8, which is slower than FlashInfer W4A4 on SM100 but matches the checkpoint. The MoE still picks its Blackwell backend without the activation key, so it uses MXFP8 or BF16 activations instead of `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` (FP8 GS128 x MXFP4). Hooking that up is left for a follow-up issue.
- The AMD, XPU, CPU and V4.1 DeepSeek model variants still need the same `ckpt_names` one-liner; untested here.
- The rename breaks the pre-processed weight cache, so `supports_pre_processed_weights` is off for this method.
- Converting DeepSeek-V4-Flash with vllm-project/compressed-tensors#902 also emits `shared_experts.w\d+` targets, while vLLM names that layer `shared_experts.down_proj`; that needs a fix in the converter or model.

**Not a duplicate:** #59376 targets the same scheme with a different design; only one should merge. #58714 adds a separate CT -> `HummingMoEMethod` route for the same checkpoints; this PR covers that path through the native MXFP4 method. #56523 and #56306 migrate the W4A4 method to the oracle and do not touch this scheme.

title: [Perf] [NPU] deepep: enable MXFP8 low-latency dispatch for Fp8MoEMethod FP4 experts
body:
## Motivation

On NPU, FP4-expert models routed through Fp8MoEMethod ( is_fp4_expert=True , e.g. MiMo-V2.5-Pro with modelopt_fp4) delegate execution to NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod kernels via the ASCEND MoE runner. However, process_weights_after_loading only runs Fp8MoEMethod 's own body, so the DeepEP dispatcher quant config was never set — dispatch fell back to BF16 and a separate DynamicMxQuant kernel ran before every grouped matmul (~15ms/layer at 16K-token prefill).

The native FP4 path ( NPUW4A8MXFP4FusedMoEMethod , DSV4) already sets the same dispatcher config; the Fp8MoEMethod path was simply missing it.

## Modifications

- Declare the dispatch wire format as a DISPATCHER_QUANT_CONFIG class attribute on NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod ( low_latency=mxfp8 ; normal stays BF16 since A5 MXFP8 normal dispatch is intranode-only). The kernel that consumes the activations now owns the declaration, instead of each caller hand-writing platform-specific if/else patches.
- In Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading , pick the config up from the attached layer.w13_kernel when it declares one; otherwise keep the original checkpoint-dtype config. No _is_npu / is_fp4_expert branching — the attached kernel already encodes both.
- Reuse the same declaration in NPUW4A8MXFP4FusedMoEMethod , replacing its hand-written copy.
With this, A5 low-latency dispatch quantizes activations to MXFP8 in-kernel (with E8M0 block scales) and the GMMs consume them directly; the three previously duplicated config dicts collapse into a single kernel-owned declaration.

## Accuracy Tests

```
echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1

source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=300
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=32
export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2500
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=20
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=4096
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE=auto
export SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1

sglang serve \
        --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
        --served-model-name $MODEL_PATH \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \
        --tp-size 8 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \
        --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 600000 \
        --max-running-requests 32 \
        --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
        --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 \
        --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
        --speculative-draft-model-path $DFLASH_PATH \
        --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8 \
        --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
```

title: feat(jit): support native MUSA compilation
body:
## Overview

This PR adds native MUSA compilation to SGLang's Ninja-based JIT build path.
The MUSA branch selects `mcc`, passes `-x musa` and
`--offload-arch=mp_*`, and uses MUSA include paths and runtime libraries.
HIP retains precedence, and CUDA remains the fallback.

MUSA JIT uses C++20, aligned with the LLVM20-based mtcc20x path. CUDA and HIP
retain C++20. Shared JIT headers use the upstream C++20 facilities directly;
SGLang no longer carries a duplicate C++17 compatibility layer. The JIT cache
fingerprints the selected compiler path and version.

Runtime and FP8 aliases are supplied by TorchADA through
`stable_compat_include_dir()`. This path depends on
[yingzhou-bjtu/torchada#4](https://github.com/MooreThreads/torchada/pull/132),
currently a fork Draft. A TorchADA release containing that change is required
before this PR can be merged.

[sgl-project/sglang-omni#2442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2442)
is the downstream consumer integration: it exposes the existing joint-RoPE
provider on MUSA. JIT compilation remains in SGLang.

Part of #16565.

## Validation

Recorded real mtcc20x evidence: MTT S5000, LLVM20-based `mcc` (clang 20.1.8),
`--offload-arch=mp_31`; 5.3 GA `mcc3` and M1000 were not verified.

- Static checks pass in the current worktree; the recorded mtcc20x focused cache run passed `67 tests` before this C++20-only cleanup.
- The current source selects `mcc`, `-x musa`, `--offload-arch=mp_31`,
  `-DUSE_MUSA`, and `-std=c++20` for MUSA JIT; the recorded mtcc20x run
  confirmed matching host/device standard flags.
- Recorded mtcc20x evidence: `fused_rope` real MUSA JIT build, module load,
  and numerical smoke passed; `q_max_abs_error=0.0`, `k_max_abs_error=0.0`.
- Recorded mtcc20x evidence: `speculative_tree` and `ngram_embedding` real
  MUSA JIT build and module load passed.
- `speculative_sampling`: dependency-blocked because
  `flashinfer/sampling.cuh` is absent from the validation image.

### C++ standard decision

The recorded LLVM20-based mtcc20x probe passed the public-header closure in
C++20 (`bits.h`, `utils.h`, `tensor.h`, `type.cuh`, and `utils.cuh`). The MUSA
JIT path therefore uses C++20 directly, matching the CUDA/HIP upstream model.
The legacy clang14 path and M1000 remain explicit follow-up evidence items;
this PR does not claim they were freshly verified.

## MUSA JIT Build Overview

The production inventory below is generated from every `load_jit` call site
under `python/sglang/kernels/ops/**/*.py`: 194 call sites and 165 unique source
selections. Build, load, runtime smoke, dependency, and backend-specific
states are kept separate.

| Operator / module | Source | Result |

| `fused_rope` | `csrc/elementwise/rope.cuh` | `PASS_BUILD_LOAD_SMOKE`; numerical smoke passed |
| `speculative_tree` | `csrc/speculative/tree.cuh` | `PASS_BUILD_LOAD` |
| `ngram_embedding` | `csrc/speculative/ngram_embedding.cuh` | `PASS_BUILD_LOAD` |
| `speculative_sampling` | `csrc/speculative/sampling.cuh` | `BLOCKED_DEPENDENCY`; `flashinfer/sampling.cuh` is unavailable in the validation image |

| `PASS_BUILD_LOAD_SMOKE` | Real MUSA `mcc` build, module load, and numerical smoke |
| `PASS_BUILD_LOAD` | Real MUSA `mcc` build and module load |

title: [Refactor] kernels/diffusion/tests: Prune dead code and fix tests that never ran
body:
## Motivation

Six months of fast kernel and diffusion work left a lot behind in `python/sglang/kernels`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` and the kernel/diffusion test trees: kernels nothing calls, registry metadata nothing reads, per-model copies of the same fused-op glue, env knobs that do nothing, and tests that pass without testing anything. This PR removes that, and fixes the real bugs the audit turned up along the way (several were silently shipping).

**408 files, +3,629 / -26,346.** About 1.3K of the additions are test oracles and helpers moved out of production modules into `python/sglang/test/kernels/`.

## Bugs fixed (please review these first)

| Area | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| SANA (diffusion) | Since #37816 the VAE loader calls `vae.state_dict()` before `load_state_dict`; `AutoencoderDC` builds its inner diffusers model lazily, so that call built it with random init and the later load returned early. **All 375 VAE tensors were random; every SANA T2I image on main is noise.** | `load_state_dict` loads into an already-built inner model. Regression test in `test_vae_loader.py` (fails on main). |
| GLM-Image (diffusion) | #33555 added an unconditional `query[:, t:] = q_img` write-back after an in-place RoPE; torch 2.14 rejects the self-copy, so **every GLM-Image request fails** in the first DiT block. | Copy back only when the rotation returned new memory. Regression test `test_glm_image_attention.py`; `test_ar_models` re-enabled (fails on main, passes here in 175 s on 2xH200). |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE | The default-on `h3_vae_qk_rmsnorm_rope` path ran in `quality=exact` but was not bit-exact (~25% of rotated channels differ). A second, faster, quality-gated fused path for the same op already existed. | Removed the non-bit-exact path. **Behavior change:** the exact tier now runs the native chain (bit-identical to native); lossless is unchanged. |
| Diffusion CI | `STANDALONE_FILES` moved to `server/gpu_cases.py` in #24630 but the CUDA partition planner kept reading the runner, so **no CUDA standalone file has run since June** (12 2-GPU files + the 1-GPU ones). | Planner reads the case config. All 15 newly scheduled files were run on H200 through the CI code path; one rotted test fixed. |
| Env vars | Code read the legacy `SGL_*` names while docs/`environ.py` define `SGLANG_*`, and the rewrite is one-directional, so the documented names did nothing: `SGLANG_USE_DEEPGEMM_BMM` (5 models), `SGLANG_DG_USE_NVRTC`, `SGLANG_CPU_QUANTIZATION`, `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_ROW_SPLIT`. | Read via `envs`; legacy names still work. |
| `BaseFusedOp` | `KernelBackend.FLYDSL` mapped to a missing `forward_flydsl`, so `SGLANG_FORCE_FUSED_OP_BACKEND=flydsl` raised `AttributeError`. | Stub added + test. |
| Tests that never ran | `test_fp8_kernel` returned early on every CUDA GPU with sm>=90; `test_swapab_attention` was registered on H100 but gated to sm_10x (production SM100 kernel had no CUDA coverage); sm_100 / sm_120 / 2-GPU / 4-GPU diffusion unit tests sat on a 1-GPU H100 lane; `test_qwen_image21` cache tests exercised a test-local re-implementation of the fix. | Each now runs on hardware that satisfies its gate (or was deleted with its dead kernel); the qwen_image21 tests drive the real block and fail when the fix is reverted. |
| SenseNova-U1 | `FlowMatchingHead` called `SimpleMLPAdaLN` with a signature the class doesn't have (crash for `fm_head_layers > 2`). | Restored the timestep-conditioned head; test fails on main. |

## Modifications

### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, -13.8K)
- **Dead / test-only kernels removed** (each re-verified with whole-repo grep incl. string lookups): seg_la kernel, dsv4 `fused_ape_pool_norm_rope`, tilelang `fp8_index`, KDA prefill timing scaffolding, nvlink push/pull all-reduce wrappers, inkling two-shot all-reduce, `cutedsl_gdn_mtp_ring` T=1 entry, non-`f_b` FlyDSL KDA decode, dsa `GetK/GetS`, adler32 whole-tensor entry points, ReplaySSM circular commit, cvt helpers, mxfp8 v-cache update, fp8 ue8m0/hopper/transpose helpers, `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, `awq_gemm_triton`, rocm `tkw1`, `moe_fused_gate_jit`, inkling gate v1, `post_reorder_triton_kernel`, `fused_inplace_qknorm_across_heads`, elementwise `silu_and_mul_triton`/autotune path, `rms_normalize_triton`, stale `top_p_renorm_triton` copy, and others.
- **Legacy DSV4 compressor path removed** (`compress_old.py`, `fused_compress_triton.py`, srt `dsv4/compress_hip.py`, the old `CompressorBackendMixin`): every CUDA/HIP backend uses `compressor_v2`; `fused_norm_rope_inplace` (live) moved to `dsv4/elementwise.py`. AOT dsv4 q/k norm+RoPE ops (duplicates of the JIT ones) removed.
- **Registry (option A):** the KernelSpec inventory stays; write-only metadata goes (`FormatSignature`, `KernelSpec.format_signature/description/group/name`, `BaseFusedOp.format_signature/descriptions/dispatch_forward`, unused selector/platform helpers). `spec.CUDA_ONLY` replaces ~44 inline frozensets. Unused `BaseFusedOp`s (4 RMSNorm, Gelu/GeluTanh/ReLU2/QuickGELU) removed; facade wrappers nobody imports removed (this also fixes facade functions shadowed by same-named submodules). `Fp8ScaledMMOp` no longer declares an SM90 heuristic as a capability.
- **#42184 criteria applied** to the four remaining gate sites (route-quant, engram, vision_rope, minimax_m3): gates check eligibility, launchers enforce contracts.
- **Duplicates:** sparse-MLA decode reuses the shared kernels (bit-exact, 720 cases x 2 archs incl. fully masked rows); mxfp8 gfx95 reuses `mxfp8_quant`. Forks that are *not* bit-exact stay, each with a one-line comment (grok RMSNorm, gfx1250 qk-RMSNorm, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU, minimax Gemma RMSNorm).
- **Test oracles shipped in op modules moved to `sglang.test.kernels`** (LPLB, dsa transform index, DCP LSE combine, dsv4 K-cache quant refs, extend attention, dspark window, multigpu launcher, mhc, per-token-group quant dispatch).

### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, -9.4K)
- **Dead code:** SenseNova-U1 unreachable chat/interleave/it2i paths (~2.6K; T2I output byte-identical), auto-residency estimators and the warmup stage-iteration calibration chain nothing read, SANA-WM parity debug harness (`SANAWM_*` env hooks incl. `torch.load` input injection), `MINIMAX_H3_USE_FUSED_NORM` path, unresolved MiniMax-H3 euler scheduler, registry subprocess-inspect path (pointed at a nonexistent module), delta-gzip realtime encoding (server + web UI), bundled-overlay lookup, `EncodingStage`, bitsandbytes 4-bit swap, `generate_with_lora` (could never run), `convert_hf_to_fp8.py`, unused platform hooks, unread `ServerArgs` fields, etc.
- **Env:** 12 `envs.py` entries nothing read removed (+ the docs rows presenting 5 of them as working knobs); raw reads of `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_QKNORM_ROPE` / `MINIMAX_H3_VAE_*` declared in `envs.py` with identical parsing; unprefixed GDN dev knobs dropped.
- **Refactors (bit-exact):** `BitExactFusionGate.run()` replaces 24 hand-written verify-once/fallback blocks and the `mismatch_msg` boilerplate; one LayerNorm+modulate helper for FLUX.3/GLM/LongCat; `sites/` exports one `QualityGatedFusion` per family instead of four wrappers each (~50 facade entries, 28 imports gone). Sites that are hand-tuned for launch overhead, re-raise, verify inside the try, or differ in reference were left as they are (listed in the commit messages).

### Tests and CI
- Deleted always-skipped tests (env var set nowhere, `skipif(True)`, hard-coded dev paths), tautologies (default/literal echoes, `inspect.getsource` shape tests, log-format echoes, torch-behavior tests), duplicate cases and duplicate helpers; trimmed grids with no extra coverage (`fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache` 1,344 -> 288 cases, AOT `moe_align` 4,368 -> 144, AOT per-token-group quant 3,632 -> 320). CI-tooling meta-tests are intentionally kept.
- New lane wiring: swapab on B200; Blackwell, SM120 and 4-GPU diffusion unit steps; 2-GPU diffusion unit files as 2-gpu standalone files; `quant-videogen` installed for its tests; comm benches no longer register no-op AMD runs; HPC-Ops tests (always skipped: the package isn't in the CI venv) disabled explicitly.
- **CI cost:** the standalone-file fix adds runners (1-GPU H100: 5 -> 6 partitions; 2-GPU: 3 -> 5 by current estimates). The estimates are 2-15x above the measured H200 times; I'll copy this PR's CI-measured values into `STANDALONE_FILE_EST_TIMES` before merge.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end, same GPU, fixed seed, base vs this branch (fused paths confirmed active by a gate tracer on both sides; no gate disabled):

| Model | Paths exercised | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-Image, LongCat-Image, FLUX.2-klein-4B, Joy, MOSS-Image, Anima, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-1.3B, Helios-Distilled | `BitExactFusionGate.run`, LN+modulate helper, QK-norm+RoPE, handler-table sites, gated residual | byte-identical |
| GLM-Image (1024², 30 steps) | LN+modulate helper, QK-LN | identical to main+fix; fused == native |
| SANA 600M (512², 20 steps) | VAE fix | identical to main+fix; reproducible across processes (main is noise) |
| SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT T2I | dead-path removal | PNG md5 identical |
| Z-Image-Turbo server warmup | residency/warmup cleanup | PNG identical, same peak memory |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE decoder | lossless in-place path / exact tier | lossless identical; exact == native |

Kernel dedups were checked bit-for-bit on H200 and GB300 (scripts in the commit messages' descriptions).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No perf-path changes intended. `BitExactFusionGate.run` was not applied to the launch-overhead-tuned sites (the closures add ~160-180 ns per call on the host).

## Validation

- **H200 (sm_90):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops`, `test/registered/unit` and `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (1,624 files). Failures were re-run on main: identical failing test ids (rust extensions not built in the source tree, NPU-only, multi-GPU tests on one GPU, pre-existing diffusion kernel failures); 2 port collisions from parallel runs pass alone. 
- **GB300 (sm_103):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops` (334 files): failing ids identical to main.
- **RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120):** FA4 sm120 + FA4 + dense FA4 + sm120 paged MQA logits + sm120 fp8 linear + mxfp4 sm120 + diffusion fp8 FA sm120 + kernel namespace: all pass, same as main.
- **Multi-GPU:** every CUDA diffusion standalone file run on 2xH200 through the CI runner path (incl. `test_ar_models` and `test_diffusion_bcg_tp2_zimage_turbo` at the final head); Kandinsky 6 4-GPU cases on 4xH200.
- `pytest --collect-only` over the test trees: no new collection errors; import walk over `sglang.kernels`, `sglang.multimodal_gen`, `sglang.srt.{layers,models,...}`: no new import failures.
- **Not validated:** ROCm, NPU, XPU, MUSA (HIP-only deletions are traced through backend selection and import-checked on CUDA), a full AOT wheel link (affected TUs compiled for sm90/sm100), 4-GPU cases on Blackwell.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: github:vllm-project/FlashMLA:26 fetched implementation patch
Holding the FP8 Quality Ceiling at 8-Bit Weights and Activations: INT8 and GGUF Post-Training Quantization of Ideogram 4.0 for Consumer GPUs
body: We study post-training quantization (PTQ) of Ideogram 4.0, a 9.3B flow-matching diffusion transformer (DiT) that realizes classifier-free guidance with two separate-weight copies of a single-stream backbone and is conditioned by a Qwen3-VL text encoder, targeting Ampere RTX~3090 GPUs, which lack FP8 tensor cores. Because Ideogram~4.0 is trained on structured JSON captions, we evaluate every variant under schema-valid JSON prompts produced by an LLM expander built to Ideogram's published caption specification, and score them with a battery spanning human-preference (HPSv2), CLIP, and PickScore for standalone quality; PP-OCR exact-match and edit distance for text; and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS for fidelity to the FP8 reference (the highest-precision public checkpoint) output. On a 300-prompt benchmark with paired bootstrap confidence intervals, an INT8 W8A8 recipe (per-channel weights, per-token dynamic activations, SmoothQuant, and bf16 protection of a small high-fragility layer set) is statistically indistinguishable from FP8 on CLIP and PickScore (paired CIs include zero) and within ~0.004 HPSv2, and, at its 8-bit size, is the most faithful reproduction of the FP8 output (LPIPS 0.243 vs 0.277/0.306 for the half-size 4-bit baselines; the INT8-Q4_K gap excludes zero). A GGUF Q4_K quantization reaches the same standalone quality as the published NF4 baseline at the same on-disk size, making it the Pareto choice on the quality-memory frontier. We further show that under JSON prompts all four variants reach parity on standalone quality, the variants separate on fidelity and text rendering, not on aggregate image-quality scores, and that text legibility, near-zero when the model is prompted with raw strings, reaches 55% OCR exact-match under the JSON captions it expects. We release the INT8 W8A8 and GGUF Q4_K quantized weights on Hugging Face under a gated, non-commercial license.

title: BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks
body: Reducing memory use in large language model (LLM) training is an ongoing challenge. Activation checkpointing saves memory by recomputation, while lossy compression changes the stored activations. The reemergence of sparse $\relu$ and $\relu^2$ activations creates a third opportunity: losslessly compressing the activation cache itself. We present BitSparse, a GPU-resident lossless compression format for sparse activations. Compression and reconstruction run in custom Triton kernels fused into an autograd function, shrinking the activation cache while recovering it exactly for the backward pass. Bfloat16 (BF16) and FP8 activations are supported. Optional sign-bit packing further increases compression up to close to the theoretical limit. We analyze its compression ratio and compare it to the theoretical optimum. BitSparse lowers per-token VRAM by 31\% and 30\% Modded-NanoGPT and Nemotron-H respectively, with overheads of no more than 1\% at practical sequence lengths. Additionally, a new preallocated buffer system avoids host synchronization during training when variable size tensors are allocated.

title: Beyond Per-Token Pricing: A Concurrency-Aware Methodology for LLM Infrastructure Cost Estimation
body: Every public LLM cost calculator we surveyed treats GPU utilization as a fixed input -- entered by the user, baked in as a preset, or silently assumed at 100% -- never measured against the operator's actual load. We show that this assumption is the dominant source of error: on identical H100 hardware, effective cost spans \$0.21 to \$15.25 per million output tokens, an underutilization penalty of 2.5-24x across low-to-moderate enterprise loads (1-10 rps) and up to 36.3x near idle -- driven by one operator-controlled variable, offered request rate lambda, which sets in-flight concurrency via Little's Law and which no open-source calculator exposes. Because calculators take utilization as a user-supplied input, any utilization-naive estimate understates true cost by exactly 1/U, systematically mispricing self-hosting -- most severely over-selling it for low-traffic workloads. We propose a measurement methodology that parameterizes the relationship as C_eff = f(H, M, Q, lambda, L), validate it with 42 benchmarks across dense, ultra-sparse MoE, and sparse MoE models, and release vllm-cost-meter, an open-source cost meter that attaches to a live vLLM server and reports real \$/M-tokens against the operator's own traffic. We further show that FP8 quantization benefits the MoE architectures we tested roughly 2.2-2.4x more than the dense model (+69 to +74% vs. +31% peak throughput; n=3, broader validation needed), and our data are consistent with active parameter count, not total model size, being a primary predictor of saturation economics. To rule out single-hardware confounding we repeat the core sweep on A100 80GB PCIe (56 runs): the load-driven spread reproduces at 7.0-11.4x, the active-parameters ordering survives at FP8, and the dense-FP8 advantage inverts on silicon without native FP8 tensor cores -- a hardware-conditional caveat the framework already accommodates.

title:
InfiR2: A Comprehensive FP8 Training Recipe for Reasoning-Enhanced
  Language Models
body:
The immense computational cost of training Large Language Models (LLMs)
presents a major barrier to innovation. While FP8 training offers a promising
solution with significant theoretical efficiency gains, its widespread adoption
has been hindered by the lack of a comprehensive, open-source training recipe.
To bridge this gap, we introduce an end-to-end FP8 training recipe that
seamlessly integrates continual pre-training and supervised fine-tuning. Our
methodology employs a fine-grained, hybrid-granularity quantization strategy to
maintain numerical fidelity while maximizing computational efficiency. Through
extensive experiments, including the continue pre-training of models on a
160B-token corpus, we demonstrate that our recipe is not only remarkably stable
but also essentially lossless, achieving performance on par with the BF16
baseline across a suite of reasoning benchmarks. Crucially, this is achieved
with substantial efficiency improvements, including up to a 22% reduction in
training time, a 14% decrease in peak memory usage, and a 19% increase in
throughput. Our results establish FP8 as a practical and robust alternative to
BF16, and we will release the accompanying code to further democratize
large-scale model training.

title:
Training and inference of large language models using 8-bit floating
  point
body:
FP8 formats are gaining popularity to boost the computational efficiency for
training and inference of large deep learning models. Their main challenge is
that a careful choice of scaling is needed to prevent degradation due to the
reduced dynamic range compared to higher-precision formats. Although there
exists ample literature about selecting such scalings for INT formats, this
critical aspect has yet to be addressed for FP8. This paper presents a
methodology to select the scalings for FP8 linear layers, based on dynamically
updating per-tensor scales for the weights, gradients and activations. We apply
this methodology to train and validate large language models of the type of GPT
and Llama 2 using FP8, for model sizes ranging from 111M to 70B. To facilitate
the understanding of the FP8 dynamics, our results are accompanied by plots of
the per-tensor scale distribution for weights, activations and gradients during
both training and inference.

title: Scaling FP8 training to trillion-token LLMs
body:
We train, for the first time, large language models using FP8 precision on
datasets up to 2 trillion tokens -- a 20-fold increase over previous limits.
Through these extended training runs, we uncover critical instabilities in FP8
training that were not observable in earlier works with shorter durations. We
trace these instabilities to outlier amplification by the SwiGLU activation
function. Interestingly, we show, both analytically and empirically, that this
amplification happens only over prolonged training periods, and link it to a
SwiGLU weight alignment process. To address this newly identified issue, we
introduce Smooth-SwiGLU, a novel modification that ensures stable FP8 training
without altering function behavior. We also demonstrate, for the first time,
FP8 quantization of both Adam optimizer moments. Combining these innovations,
we successfully train a 7B parameter model using FP8 precision on 256 Intel
Gaudi2 accelerators, achieving on-par results with the BF16 baseline while
delivering up to a sim 34 % throughput improvement.

title: config: switch MI355X DSv4.1 Flash to the ROCm nightly image / MI355X DSv4.1 Flash 切换到 ROCm nightly 镜像
body:
Switch the MI355X DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe from the `deepseekv41-flash-0909` release tag to the upstream ROCm nightly, so it picks up [vllm-project/vllm#56503](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56503) (merged 2026-09-12, commit `46d2b23`). That PR moves the mHC delayed pre block off the eager Torch reference and onto AITER; on this model the mHC block is 85% of the decoder's kernel launches, so the `0909` tag leaves most of the decode cost unaddressed.

**The nightly is now published**, so the earlier `nightly-TBD` placeholder is replaced with the real pin:

| median cold-prefix TTFT | 10,236 ms | **1,440 ms** |
| gsm8k strict-match | 0.9704 | 0.9719 ± 0.0045 |

Decode is 6.6x faster at an identical pinned `synthetic_acceptance_length` of 3.51, and accuracy is within one standard error, so this is a kernel-cost change rather than a numerics change. Uncached prefill measures 27,273 tok/s at 16k context and 22,012 tok/s at 128k.

Also raises `max_num_seqs` to the upstream default of 128. The old `2*CONC` cap was below AgentX's subagent fan-out, so requests queued instead of being admitted — vLLM reported queue times up to 16.2 s at CONC=1, and removing the cap takes them to zero. Verified by an A/B over the same 393 traces, same seed and duration, one arm per GPU half: identical output token counts, TTFT max 9,003 ms to 4,263 ms, no regression elsewhere.

将 MI355X 的 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 配方镜像从 `deepseekv41-flash-0909` 发布标签切换到上游 ROCm nightly，以纳入 [vllm-project/vllm#56503](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56503)（2026-09-12 合入，提交 `46d2b23`）。该 PR 将 mHC delayed pre 块从 eager Torch 参考实现切换到 AITER；该模型中 mHC 块占解码器内核启动数的 85%，因此 `0909` 标签会浪费大部分解码开销。

**nightly 已发布**，此前的 `nightly-TBD` 占位符已替换为真实标签 `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-eed1f3d0c6043bd494424a22443ee198dd56f657`（摘要 `sha256:960228cf...`，发布于 2026-09-12T05:27:48Z）。`eed1f3d` 比 #56503 的合并提交领先 11 个提交、落后 0 个，因此已包含该改动。上游 vLLM 配方正在 **[vllm-project/recipes#962](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/pull/962)** 中切换到同一镜像，使 `recipes.vllm.ai` 与 `amd-master.yaml` 指向同一标签。

**仍保持 draft，等待在该镜像上完成 GPU 验证。** #2962 已合入，本 PR 已 rebase 到 `main`。

在 MI355X（8x gfx950、TP4、fp4、五 token DSpark）上实测：并发 1 时 token 间延迟 p50 从 25.58 ms 降至 3.85 ms，单用户输出吞吐从 39.1 提升到 260.0 tokens/s，聚合输出吞吐从 35.9 提升到 132.9 tokens/s，冷前缀 TTFT 中位数从 10,236 ms 降至 1,440 ms，gsm8k strict-match 为 0.9719 ± 0.0045（基线 0.9704）。在相同固定的 `synthetic_acceptance_length` 3.51 下解码快 6.6 倍，准确率变化在一个标准误内，说明这是内核开销变化而非数值变化。未缓存 prefill 在 16k 上下文为 27,273 tok/s，128k 为 22,012 tok/s。

同时将 `max_num_seqs` 提升到上游默认值 128。此前的 `2*CONC` 上限低于 AgentX 的子代理扇出，导致请求排队而非被接纳——vLLM 在 CONC=1 时报告排队时间最高达 16.2 秒，取消该上限后归零。已通过 A/B 验证：相同的 393 条 trace、相同随机种子与时长，每个 GPU 半区一组，输出 token 数完全一致，TTFT 最大值从 9,003 ms 降至 4,263 ms，其余指标无回退。

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Pins a new serving image and changes vLLM admission limits for a benchmark recipe, which materially affects measured throughput/latency and sweep comparability until GPU validation completes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates the MI355X **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** AgentX DSpark recipe (`dsv41flash-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark`) from `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:deepseekv41-flash-0909` to pinned upstream ROCm nightly `nightly-eed1f3d0c6043bd494424a22443ee198dd56f657`, so runs pick up **vllm#56503** (mHC delayed pre on AITER instead of eager Torch).
> 
> The benchmark script sets **`MAX_NUM_SEQS=128`** (replacing `2*CONC`) so vLLM can admit AgentX subagent fan-out without multi-second queue times at low concurrency, and exports **`AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR`** to suppress repetitive Gluon-unavailable Triton warnings on gfx950 (log hygiene only).
> 
> **`amd-master.yaml`**, EN/ZH configuration docs, and **`perf-changelog.yaml`** are aligned with the new image pin and scheduler change. GPU validation on this exact image remains pending.

title: [AMD][MI355X] DSv4.1-Flash vLLM: enable sparse-MLA Gluon kernel / DSv4.1-Flash vLLM：启用 sparse-MLA Gluon kernel
body:
## Description

Add `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True` to
`dsv41flash-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark` to force
[vllm-project/vllm#53492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53492)'s
Gluon sparse-MLA kernel path (matches what was actually set in the local
validation runs referenced below).

Unpins `image`/`model.container` to `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-TBD`
(only the trailing hash needs updating later): the current pin predates this
recipe's cherry-picked AMD vLLM PRs and is unrelated to them. A maintainer
should fill in the hash once these land upstream and are released in a
nightly image:

- [vllm-project/vllm#58208](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58208) — faster DSA candidate block-selection topk
- [vllm-project/vllm#58655](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58655) — fused mHC Triton kernel for the delayed seams
- [vllm-project/vllm#53492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53492) — sparse MLA Gluon kernel from Aiter (this PR's env var)

Together these bring better topk/mHC/MLA kernels with better
compute/communication stream overlap for DSv4.1-Flash on MI355X.

This PR previously also added `--attention-config
'{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'` and a
`--block-size 128` workaround to exercise
[vllm-project/vllm#58671](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58671)'s
ROCm paged MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer kernel. Both are dropped: #58671 isn't
merging in time, and the `--block-size 128` pin's entire justification (vLLM's
block-size auto-resolution otherwise picking 64 across this model's 4+
attention backends) was specifically about the 128 that
`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend.get_preferred_block_size` requests once
the fp4 indexer is active — moot without it. A live A/B test (TP2, conc=16,
matched 900s profiling window, `#58208` reverted upstream via
[vllm-project/vllm#59125](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59125) so
the dense fallback path doesn't crash) measured the dense fp8 indexer path
that `#58671` would otherwise replace: interactivity p50/p90 -14.7%/-14.9%,
e2e latency p50/p90 +9.5%/+10.8% worse, throughput/GPU unchanged (+0.5%,
within noise), TTFT unchanged. So `#58671` is a meaningful interactivity/tail-
latency win, not just a config toggle, but it's still not ready to merge, so
this recipe leaves it out for now.

This PR does not touch `--max-num-batched-tokens`: the existing TP2 c64 (8192)
/ c128 (4096) values in this recipe already avoid the KV-headroom regression
that a separate, since-closed draft (#3451) flagged as unvalidated.

Duplicate-check: searched open PRs for `dsv41flash mi355x`, `attention-config`,
`indexer_kv_dtype`, `mxfp4 indexer`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA`
and `block-size 128` on this repo; no open PR adds this env var or touches
this recipe's image pin.

## AI model disclosure

- Model/version: Claude Sonnet 5 (Cursor)
- Role: Investigated ATOM's official AgentX benchmark results for this model,
  reviewed the unmerged AMD vLLM cherry-pick PRs, ran a KV-headroom
  root-cause investigation and validation sweep for a related TP2 c64
  regression, root-caused a pre-existing `#58208` Triton bug hit only by the
  dense fp8 indexer fallback path at AgentX-scale context, fixed the DCO on
  and helped land its revert (`vllm-project/vllm#59125`), ran a live A/B test
  measuring `#58671`'s actual perf contribution once that confound was
  removed, and revised this PR to drop `#58671`-specific changes once it was
  clear it wouldn't merge in time. The submitting human reviewed the
  recipe/config changes and is responsible for validating the env var on the
  current image once one is available.

## Related Issue

Fixes #

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Configuration change
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Other (please describe)

## Checklist

- [ ] I have tested my changes locally (draft: pending a nightly image with the three remaining cherry-picks; the env var was validated against a stale pre-migration copy of this recipe)
- [ ] I have updated documentation if necessary
- [x] For every change that can affect benchmark performance and every recipe addition or modification, I have appended a new entry to the physical end of `perf-changelog.yaml` and have not edited historical entries
- [ ] Before merging via reuse, an authorized maintainer (`OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`) has commented `/use <run_id>` (or the legacy `/reuse-sweep-run`) on this PR

<summary>中文</summary>

为 `dsv41flash-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark` 添加
`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True`，以强制启用
[vllm-project/vllm#53492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53492) 的
Gluon sparse-MLA kernel 路径（与下方本地验证运行实际设置的配置保持一致）。

将 `image`/`model.container` 取消固定为
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-TBD`（之后只需更新末尾的哈希值）：当前
固定的镜像早于本配方所 cherry-pick 的 AMD vLLM PR，与其无关。待以下改动合并
至上游并随 nightly 镜像发布后，维护者应填入实际哈希值：

- [vllm-project/vllm#58208](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58208) —— 更快的 DSA 候选块 topk 选择
- [vllm-project/vllm#58655](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58655) —— 延迟 seam 的融合 mHC Triton kernel
- [vllm-project/vllm#53492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53492) —— 来自 Aiter 的 sparse MLA Gluon kernel（本 PR 的环境变量）

这些改动共同为 MI355X 上的 DSv4.1-Flash 带来更优的 topk/mHC/MLA kernel，以及
更好的计算/通信流重叠模式。

本 PR 此前还添加了
`--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'`
与 `--block-size 128` 的绕过配置，用于启用
[vllm-project/vllm#58671](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58671) 的
ROCm 分页 MXFP4 稀疏 logits indexer kernel。二者均已移除：#58671 无法及时合并；
而 `--block-size 128` 的全部依据（vLLM 的 block-size 自动推断在该模型 4 个以上
attention backend 同时生效时会退化为选出 64）本身就是针对 fp4 indexer 生效后
`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend.get_preferred_block_size` 所请求的 128 —
在不启用该 indexer 的情况下已不适用。一次真实的 A/B 测试（TP2、并发 16、匹配
900 秒 profiling 窗口，并已通过
[vllm-project/vllm#59125](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59125) 在
上游回滚 `#58208` 以避免稠密回退路径崩溃）测得：`#58671` 本应替换的稠密 fp8
indexer 路径，其 interactivity p50/p90 降低 14.7%/14.9%，e2e 延迟 p50/p90
增加 9.5%/10.8%（更差），throughput/GPU 基本不变（+0.5%，在噪声范围内），
TTFT 不变。也就是说 `#58671` 确实带来了可观的 interactivity/尾部延迟提升，
而不只是一个配置开关，但目前仍未准备好合并，因此本配方暂不启用它。

本 PR 未改动 `--max-num-batched-tokens`：该配方现有的 TP2 c64（8192）/
c128（4096）取值已经规避了另一个已关闭的草稿 PR（#3451）标记为"尚未验证"的
KV 显存余量回退问题。

重复性检查：已在本仓库搜索 `dsv41flash mi355x`、`attention-config`、
`indexer_kv_dtype`、`mxfp4 indexer`、`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA`
与 `block-size 128` 相关的未关闭 PR，未发现任何未关闭 PR 添加该环境变量或
改动本配方的镜像固定值。

</details>

title: Add B300 Dynamo+SGLang AgentX configs for DeepSeek V4 with NIXL KV transfer / 添加使用 NIXL KV 传输的 DeepSeek V4 B300 Dynamo+SGLang AgentX 配置
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Summary

Adds DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 FP4 B300 Dynamo+SGLang AgentX recipes. The recipes come from #3631, with disaggregated KV transfer over NIXL instead of Mooncake, and now run on `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-efa-20261019-3c560089`.

- **Points:** aggregate TP8 c1, TP4 c4, TP4 c8 (HiCache) and DEP8 c384 (HiCache); disaggregated 1P1D DEP8 c64/c240 and 1P2D DEP8 c64 (HiCache prefill). Topology, concurrency, cache sizes and memory fractions are unchanged.
- **Image:** `nightly-dev-efa-20261019-3c560089`, the AWS EFA variant of the 2026-10-19 nightly (sgl-project/sglang#41006), replaces `nightly-dev-20260916-c9a8fba9`.
  - On `nightly-dev-20261013-7224fce1`, the disaggregated workers failed at NIXL startup with `createBackend: unsupported backend 'LIBFABRIC'`. The LIBFABRIC plugin of NIXL 1.5.0 needs libfabric's `FABRIC_1.7` symbol version, and the regular image ships only Ubuntu's libfabric 1.17, which stops at `FABRIC_1.6`. The cluster no longer injects the host's libfabric into containers, so nothing newer was available.
  - The EFA variant adds AWS EFA installer 1.50.0 (libfabric 2.6.0) and puts `/opt/amazon/efa/lib` first on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Its build checks that the NIXL plugin resolves libfabric there.
- **Attention DP:** DEP8 workers set `attn-dp-size: 8` in place of `dp-size: 8` + `enable-dp-attention: true`, which sgl-project/sglang#41818 deprecated.
- **Dynamo:** the recipes use the image's bundled Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261018` (`dynamo.install: false`), which is also the router version in the master config.
  - It includes ai-dynamo/dynamo#16005, which counts attention-DP ranks from `attn_dp_size`. In this SGLang, both DP spellings resolve to `dp_size=1, attn_dp_size=8`. A Dynamo without that fix registers one DP rank per DEP8 worker and subscribes only to rank 0's KV events, so the KV router sends every request to DP rank 0.
  - The previous revision built Dynamo `b208989fbe` from source, because the 1013 image's bundled `1.6.0.dev20261010` predated that fix.
- **Disaggregated KV transfer:** NIXL with the LIBFABRIC backend (`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=LIBFABRIC`, which the EFA image also sets by default). The image's NIXL 1.5.0 ships the plugin and the image ships the libfabric it needs, so there is no setup script, waiver or package change.
  - Both disaggregated workers set `FI_EFA_USE_UNSOLICITED_WRITE_RECV=0`. NIXL's LIBFABRIC backend disables the EFA provider's unsolicited write recv only when built against libfabric 2.3 or newer. The image's NIXL is not (its "Successfully disabled unsolicited write recv" log line never appears), so with the image's libfabric 2.6 the feature stays on.
  - With it on, the previous sweep of this PR (run 39191181928, two attempts of 1P1D c240) had about 1.4% of requests time out on decode after 900 s. Prefill had already sent their KV, but the completions never reached decode. Throughput per GPU fell from about 60k (0916 image) to 44k tok/s.
- **Image behavior to note:**
  - This SGLang fuses the shared expert into the DeepGEMM Mega-MoE kernel by default (sgl-project/sglang#39313), so DEP8 throughput may differ from earlier runs of these recipes for that reason too.
  - The EFA image sets `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` and `NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi` (aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1) by default. Every worker in these recipes fits on one node.
- No recipe enables the W4A4 MXFP4 Mega-MoE path. Prefill and decode use the same DSpark K=6 method.
- On `b300-dsxe`, Dynamo+SGLang serves DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 from the node-local NVMe copy (`DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813@scratch`), as vLLM already does.
- **Aggregate DEP8 c384 scheduling:** adopts the scheduling settings of the single-node SGLang EAGLE DEP8 recipe (`dsv4-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-hicache-eagle`): `enable-mixed-chunk: true`, `schedule-policy: shortest-prefill-first`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_SPEC_PREFILL_COORDINATION=1` and `prefill-decode-interval: 32` (was 20).
  - In run 39191181928 this point queued prefills behind decode: TTFT p50 33.5 s and p90 89 s, against 2.9 s and 12.7 s for the EAGLE standalone c384 point.
  - The gap came from these settings, not from Dynamo routing. About 96% of requests followed session affinity, and uncached prefill per DP rank was within ±3%. The DSpark standalone recipe this point was ported from has the same gap.
  - With mixed chunk, a step carries at most 8192 prefill tokens plus 96 one-token decodes per rank, within the existing `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320`.
- **Recipe format:** the master config selects the recipes with `srt-recipe-dir` and `srt-recipe` (#3805), and the recipes are fragments without the keys the launcher binds (#3818), as on current `main`.

<details>
<summary>Settings removed or renamed since the 0916 image</summary>

Checked against the SGLang source at `7224fce1` and the Dynamo source at `b208989fbe`, then rechecked for the current image. Between SGLang `7224fce1` and `3c560089`, no arg or env var these recipes use was renamed, removed or given a new default. Between Dynamo `b208989fbe` and the bundled `1.6.0.dev20261018`, the Dynamo flags and env vars the recipes set, and the defaults cited below, are unchanged. Topology declarations (`tp-size`, `ep-size`, and `dp-size: 1` on TP points) are kept.

| Setting | Roles | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_SPLIT_LEAF_ON_INSERT`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_NORM`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE`, `SGLANG_DSV4_MHC_PREWARM` | various | The image no longer reads them. `moe-a2a-backend: megamoe` selects Mega-MoE, and MHC prewarm always runs. |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE`, `NCCL_TIMEOUT` | disagg | Never defined: the first is a misspelling, and the second is not an NCCL variable. |
| `SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING`, `SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT`, `SGLANG_REQUEST_STATE_WAIT_TIMEOUT` | all, disagg | Only SGLang's own HTTP server reads them. Behind Dynamo, the frontend applies the chat template with thinking and reasoning effort taken from the request, and the worker calls the engine directly. |
| `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static`, `SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=0`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=True` | various | Defaults on B300. |
| `attention-backend: dsv4`, `page-size: 256` | various | Set by SGLang's DeepSeek-V4 model override. |
| `speculative-num-steps: 1`, `speculative-eagle-topk: 1`, `speculative-num-draft-tokens: 7` | all | Derived by DSpark from `speculative-dspark-block-size: 6`, which also selects the golden acceptance length. |
| `swa-full-tokens-ratio: 0.1`, `hicache-write-policy: write_through` | TP agg | Defaults for this model. |
| `cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill` | disagg prefill | SGLang disables the prefill CUDA graph for DeepSeek-V4. |
| `disable-shared-experts-fusion` | agg DEP8 | DeepSeek-V4 only fuses shared experts into the routed weights when enforced. Mega-MoE's in-kernel fusion is controlled by `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS`, not by this flag. |
| `incremental-streaming-output`, `enable-cache-report` | agg DEP8, all | Dynamo always turns incremental streaming on. The cache report only affects SGLang's OpenAI server. |
| Frontend `active-decode-blocks-threshold`, `active-prefill-tokens-threshold`, `active-prefill-tokens-threshold-frac` set to `"None"` | frontend | Dynamo's router rejection thresholds are off by default. |
| `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_RELEASE_LEAF_LOCK_AFTER_WINDOW` → `SGLANG_OPT_RELEASE_PREFILL_SWA` | disagg | Renamed in the image. The new name defaults to off, so the setting is kept under the new name. |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Recipe details (carried over from #3631)</summary>

### Aggregate DEP8 c384

Ported from the single-node SGLang DEP8 c384 point (`dsv4-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-hicache-mtp`, `benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/dsv4/sglang/b300-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`, `override_dep8_c384`):

- **Engine settings kept:** DP8 attention + EP8 Mega-MoE, FP4 indexer, DP LM head, local control broadcast, prefill delayer (interval now 32, see above), `stream-interval: 20`, `chunked-prefill-size: 65536` with `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320`, `max-running-requests: 768` (96 per DP rank, twice concurrency), `mem-fraction-static: 0.88`, `swa-full-tokens-ratio: 0.075`, HiCache ratio 3 (`write_back`, `direct`, `page_first_direct`), DSpark K=6.
- **Decode graph limit:** `cuda-graph-max-bs-decode: 96`, the per-rank request cap (768 / 8).
- **Routing:** the Dynamo KV router replaces the SGLang router's DP-aware consistent hashing. Sessions stay sticky through `X-Dynamo-Session-ID`, and each DP rank publishes KV events (`kv-events-config`). The frontend sets `DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT: "60"`, as the disaggregated recipes do, so the c384 warmup burst does not exceed Dynamo's 5 s request-plane ack timeout.
- **Dropped:** settings that only apply to SGLang's own HTTP server and have no effect behind the Dynamo frontend: `tokenizer-worker-num`, tool-call and reasoning parsers, chat template, `skip-server-warmup`, `SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE`.

### Gap-filling points: agg TP4 c8 and disagg 1P2D DEP8 c64

- **Agg TP4 c8:** the TP4 c4 recipe with `max-running-requests: 16` and `cuda-graph-max-bs-decode: 16`, plus a HiCache DRAM tier (`hicache-ratio: 2.75`, `write_through`, `direct`, `page_first_direct`), because TP4 c4 already fills about 60% of the GPU KV pool.
- **Disagg 1P2D DEP8 c64:** the 1P1D c64 recipe with a second decode worker (3 nodes), which halves each decode rank's load.

### NIXL instead of Mooncake

On AWS EFA, Mooncake needs the separate `mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13` wheel in place of the image's Mooncake package, which #3631 installed during container setup ([review](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3631#discussion_r4201491559)). NIXL ships its own LIBFABRIC plugin, and the EFA image provides the libfabric it needs, so these recipes drop that setup script, its waiver and the Mooncake-only settings (`MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL`, `MC_MS_FILTERS`, `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM`). The NIXL LIBFABRIC settings come from #3597.

## 摘要

新增 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 FP4 B300 Dynamo+SGLang AgentX 配方。配方沿用 #3631，分离式 KV 传输由 Mooncake 改为 NIXL，现运行于 `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-efa-20261019-3c560089`。

- **测试点：**聚合式 TP8 c1、TP4 c4、TP4 c8（HiCache）与 DEP8 c384（HiCache）；分离式 1P1D DEP8 c64/c240 与 1P2D DEP8 c64（prefill 使用 HiCache）。拓扑、并发、缓存大小与显存比例均不变。
- **镜像：**以 2026-10-19 nightly 的 AWS EFA 变体 `nightly-dev-efa-20261019-3c560089`（sgl-project/sglang#41006）取代 `nightly-dev-20260916-c9a8fba9`。
  - 在 `nightly-dev-20261013-7224fce1` 上，分离式 worker 在 NIXL 启动时报错 `createBackend: unsupported backend 'LIBFABRIC'`。NIXL 1.5.0 的 LIBFABRIC 插件需要 libfabric 的 `FABRIC_1.7` 符号版本，而常规镜像只带有 Ubuntu 的 libfabric 1.17，最高只到 `FABRIC_1.6`。集群也已不再把宿主机的 libfabric 注入容器，因此没有更新的版本可用。
  - EFA 变体加入 AWS EFA 安装包 1.50.0（libfabric 2.6.0），并把 `/opt/amazon/efa/lib` 放在 `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` 最前。镜像构建时会检查 NIXL 插件是否从该目录解析 libfabric。
- **注意力 DP：**DEP8 worker 改用 `attn-dp-size: 8`，取代已被 sgl-project/sglang#41818 弃用的 `dp-size: 8` + `enable-dp-attention: true`。
- **Dynamo：**配方使用镜像自带的 Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261018`（`dynamo.install: false`），主配置中的 router 版本也记为该版本。
  - 该版本包含 ai-dynamo/dynamo#16005，按 `attn_dp_size` 计算注意力 DP rank。在该版本 SGLang 中，两种 DP 写法都会解析为 `dp_size=1, attn_dp_size=8`。缺少该修复的 Dynamo 会为每个 DEP8 worker 只注册一个 DP rank，并且只订阅 rank 0 的 KV 事件，KV 路由器会把所有请求发往 DP rank 0。
  - 上一版本从源码构建 Dynamo `b208989fbe`，因为 1013 镜像自带的 `1.6.0.dev20261010` 早于该修复。
- **分离式 KV 传输：**使用 LIBFABRIC 后端的 NIXL（`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=LIBFABRIC`，EFA 镜像也默认设置该值）。镜像中的 NIXL 1.5.0 自带该插件，镜像也提供其所需的 libfabric，因此无需初始化脚本、豁免文件或软件包改动。
  - 两个分离式 worker 均设置 `FI_EFA_USE_UNSOLICITED_WRITE_RECV=0`。NIXL 的 LIBFABRIC 后端仅在基于 libfabric 2.3 及以上版本构建时才会关闭 EFA provider 的 unsolicited write recv。镜像中的 NIXL 并非如此（日志中从未出现 "Successfully disabled unsolicited write recv"），因此在镜像的 libfabric 2.6 下该功能保持开启。
  - 开启时，本 PR 上一次扫描（运行 39191181928 的 1P1D c240 两次尝试）中约 1.4% 的请求在 decode 端等待 900 秒后超时：prefill 已发出其 KV，但完成通知始终未到达 decode。每 GPU 吞吐由约 60k（0916 镜像）降至 44k tok/s。
- **需注意的镜像行为：**
  - 该版本 SGLang 默认把共享专家融合进 DeepGEMM Mega-MoE kernel（sgl-project/sglang#39313），因此 DEP8 吞吐与这些配方早先的结果相比，也可能因此有所不同。
  - EFA 镜像默认设置 `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` 与 `NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi`（aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1）。这些配方中的每个 worker 都位于单个节点内。
- 所有配方均不启用 W4A4 MXFP4 Mega-MoE 路径。Prefill 与 decode 使用相同的 DSpark K=6 方法。
- 在 `b300-dsxe` 上，Dynamo+SGLang 从节点本地 NVMe 副本（`DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813@scratch`）加载 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813，与 vLLM 现有做法相同。
- **聚合式 DEP8 c384 调度：**采用单节点 SGLang EAGLE DEP8 配方（`dsv4-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-hicache-eagle`）的调度设置：`enable-mixed-chunk: true`、`schedule-policy: shortest-prefill-first`、`SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_SPEC_PREFILL_COORDINATION=1`，并将 `prefill-decode-interval` 由 20 改为 32。
  - 在运行 39191181928 中，该测试点的 prefill 排在 decode 之后：TTFT p50 为 33.5 秒、p90 为 89 秒，而 EAGLE 单机 c384 测试点为 2.9 秒与 12.7 秒。
  - 差距来自上述设置，而非 Dynamo 路由：约 96% 的请求按会话亲和路由，各 DP rank 的未缓存 prefill 量相差不超过 ±3%。该测试点所移植的 DSpark 单机配方也有同样的差距。
  - 启用 mixed chunk 后，每个 rank 每步最多包含 8192 个 prefill token 与 96 个单 token decode，仍在现有 `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320` 之内。
- **配方格式：**与当前 `main` 一致，主配置使用 `srt-recipe-dir` 与 `srt-recipe` 选择配方（#3805），配方为片段形式，不含由启动器绑定的键（#3818）。

### 自 0916 镜像以来删除或重命名的设置

均已对照 SGLang `7224fce1` 与 Dynamo `b208989fbe` 源码核实，并针对当前镜像重新核对。在 SGLang `7224fce1` 与 `3c560089` 之间，这些配方使用的参数与环境变量均未重命名、删除或改变默认值。在 Dynamo `b208989fbe` 与镜像自带的 `1.6.0.dev20261018` 之间，配方设置的 Dynamo 参数与环境变量以及下文引用的默认值均无变化。拓扑声明（`tp-size`、`ep-size` 以及 TP 测试点上的 `dp-size: 1`）予以保留。

- 镜像已不再读取：`SGLANG_OPT_SWA_SPLIT_LEAF_ON_INSERT`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_NORM`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE`、`SGLANG_DSV4_MHC_PREWARM`。Mega-MoE 由 `moe-a2a-backend: megamoe` 选择，MHC 预热始终执行。
- 从未定义：`SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE`（拼写错误）与 `NCCL_TIMEOUT`（并非 NCCL 变量）。

- B300 上的默认值：`SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static`、`SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=1`、`SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2=1`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=0`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=True`。
- 由 SGLang 的 DeepSeek-V4 模型覆盖设置：`attention-backend: dsv4`、`page-size: 256`。
- 由 DSpark 根据 `speculative-dspark-block-size: 6` 推导：`speculative-num-steps: 1`、`speculative-eagle-topk: 1`、`speculative-num-draft-tokens: 7`。golden 接受长度同样由 block size 选择。

- SGLang 对 DeepSeek-V4 关闭 prefill CUDA graph：`cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill`。
- `disable-shared-experts-fusion`：DeepSeek-V4 仅在强制时才把共享专家融合进路由专家权重；Mega-MoE 的 kernel 内融合由 `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS` 控制，而非此参数。

### 配方细节（沿用自 #3631）

**聚合式 DEP8 c384**：移植自单节点 SGLang DEP8 c384 测试点（`dsv4-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-hicache-mtp`，`benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/dsv4/sglang/b300-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`，`override_dep8_c384`）。

- **Decode CUDA graph 上限：**`cuda-graph-max-bs-decode: 96`，即每个 rank 的请求上限（768 / 8）。
- **路由：**以 Dynamo KV 路由器取代 SGLang 路由器的 DP 感知一致性哈希。会话通过 `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` 保持亲和，各 DP rank 发布 KV 事件（`kv-events-config`）。前端与分离式配方一样设置 `DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT: "60"`，避免 c384 预热突发请求超过 Dynamo 请求平面默认 5 秒的确认超时。

**补充测试点：**

- **聚合式 TP4 c8：**基于 TP4 c4 配方，`max-running-requests: 16`、`cuda-graph-max-bs-decode: 16`，并增加 HiCache DRAM 层（`hicache-ratio: 2.75`、`write_through`、`direct`、`page_first_direct`），因为 TP4 c4 已占用约 60% 的 GPU KV 池。

**以 NIXL 取代 Mooncake：**在 AWS EFA 上，Mooncake 需要用单独的 `mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13` wheel 替换镜像自带的 Mooncake 包，#3631 在容器初始化时完成这一替换（[review](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3631#discussion_r4201491559)）。NIXL 自带 LIBFABRIC 插件，EFA 镜像也提供其所需的 libfabric，因此这些配方移除了该初始化脚本、其豁免文件以及仅供 Mooncake 使用的设置（`MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL`、`MC_MS_FILTERS`、`WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM`）。NIXL LIBFABRIC 设置来自 #3597。

title: [NVIDIA][AgentX] GB300 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Dynamo+SGLang: DEP2/DEP16 disaggregated points on the 20261020 nightly with the Mooncake linker / [NVIDIA][AgentX] GB300 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Dynamo+SGLang：基于 20261020 nightly 与 Mooncake linker 的 DEP2/DEP16 分离式配置点
body:
Follows #4180 (merged) and moves the GB300 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Dynamo + SGLang disaggregated points to `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261020-ab580b2e` (multiarch digest pinned) with the ai-dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261019` it ships. The disaggregated points switch from prefill HiCache to the Mooncake external cache linker on both roles, and use the `flashmla_mega` attention backend. c1228 now runs 3 DEP2 prefill workers instead of 4 and c2884 5 instead of 6, and a c4096 point is added. A setup script applies the one SGLang change the image does not contain yet (#44623). The aggregated points from #4180 are unchanged.

| Config key | Topology | Conc | Nodes (GPUs) | Key settings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dsv41flash-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-dspark-disagg` | 3x DEP2 prefill + 1x DEP16 decode | 1228 | 7 (22) | Mooncake store segment 80gb prefill / 140gb decode, 24 requests per decode rank, 36 extra decode slots |
| | 5x DEP2 prefill + 1x DEP16 decode | 2884 | 8 (26) | segment 80gb prefill / 140gb decode, 40 requests per decode rank, 80 extra decode slots, prefill batches capped at 32768 tokens |
| | 7x DEP2 prefill + 1x DEP16 decode | 4096 | 9 (30) | segment 80gb prefill / 140gb decode, 64 requests per decode rank, 128 extra decode slots, prefill batches capped at 32768 tokens |

An odd number of DEP2 workers leaves two GPUs of the last prefill node idle (c1228: 2 prefill nodes, c2884: 3, c4096: 4). The master rows count only the GPUs in use: 6, 10 and 14 prefill + 16 decode = 22, 26 and 30 GPUs. Like #4180, both points use a dedicated CPU node for the frontend and the AgentX client.

Shared disaggregated settings:

- MegaMoE all-to-all, `dsv4-attn-backend: flashmla_mega`, DSpark block size 5, Mooncake KV transfer, local DP control broadcast (`enable-dp-attention-local-control-broadcast`), host Engram tables, 2048 SWA prefix tails and decoder SWA bounded replay on both roles.
- Mooncake external cache linker on both roles (`enable-unified-cache-external-linker`, Mooncake backend, group semantics), with a `mooncake-master` service (`--eviction_high_watermark_ratio=0.90 --client_ttl=60 --rpc_thread_num=64`). The linker and `enable-hierarchical-cache` are mutually exclusive in SGLang, so the master rows now declare `kv-offload-backend: mooncake 0.3.13.post1`.
- Prefill: mega mHC (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL=1`), MegaMoE cap of 32768 tokens per rank, chunked prefill of 65536.
- Decode: stream interval 32, polling interval 8, MegaMoE cap of 16384 tokens per rank, 8 gateway workers, metrics off.
- Drops `SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH`: the image already exchanges the scheduler's MLP sync rows with a gloo gather + broadcast (sgl-project/sglang#44622).
- Dynamo uses the ZMQ event plane with the TCP request plane, so the NATS service is dropped. The frontend is NUMA-bound.

SGLang patches (`configs/dsv41flash-sglang-patches.sh` applies `configs/dsv41flash-sglang-patches/*.patch` to `/sgl-workspace/sglang`, which is the image's editable install; it uses `git apply`, is idempotent, holds a lock across workers on the same node, and fails the worker if any hunk does not apply):

| Patch | Upstream | Fixes |
|---|---|---|
| `sglang-pr44623.patch` | sgl-project/sglang#44623 (open) | Lets the external cache linker register DeepSeek-V4.1's hybrid KV pools (pool assemblers, unified linker, Mooncake/UMBP direct linkers) |

Drop the patch once the pinned image contains it. The 20261020 image already contains sgl-project/sglang#44580 and #45062, which earlier revisions of this PR carried as patches.

### Local validation

One or two 3600 s AgentX runs per point on GB300 NVL72 with the CI benchmark script and launch environment, golden acceptance 3.51, 0 failed requests. Throughput counts input tokens per GPU in use (22, 26 and 30).

| Point | Image and SGLang changes | tok/s/GPU | P90 TTFT (p50) | P90 / median tok/s/user |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c1228, 3P1D | 20261016 image + #44623, #44580 and the prefill fixes the 20261019 image later shipped | 364.5k / 362.1k (2 runs) | 2.6 s (0.9 s) | 235-237 / 251-252 |
| c2884, 5P1D | 20261019 image + #44623, #44580, #45062 (this PR's previous head) | 604.4k | 10.3 s (4.4 s) | 178 / 191 |
| c4096, 7P1D | same as c2884 | 630.1k | 15.0 s (8.7 s) | 137 / 145 |

#44580 and #45062 are in the 20261020 image, so these stacks match this PR apart from the nightly date. The c1228 and c4096 runs also carried a decode admission-ordering patch that this PR does not include; it measured no difference (P90 230/232 without vs 230/228 with, two same-time pairs at c1228). The 20261020 image itself has not been run yet.

<summary>中文</summary>

本 PR 接续已合并的 #4180，将 GB300 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Dynamo + SGLang 分离式配置点迁移到 `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261020-ab580b2e`（固定 multiarch digest），并使用镜像自带的 ai-dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261019`。分离式配置点的 prefill HiCache 改为两个角色都使用 Mooncake external cache linker，attention 后端改为 `flashmla_mega`。c1228 的 DEP2 prefill worker 由 4 个减为 3 个，c2884 由 6 个减为 5 个，并新增 c4096 配置点。镜像中尚未包含的一项 SGLang 改动（#44623）由 setup 脚本以补丁形式应用。#4180 中的聚合模式配置点保持不变。

- `dsv41flash-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-dspark-disagg`：
  - c1228：3 个 DEP2 prefill + 1 个 DEP16 decode，7 个节点（22 个 GPU）；Mooncake store segment 为 prefill 80gb、decode 140gb，每个 decode rank 24 个请求，36 个 decode extra slot。
  - c2884：5 个 DEP2 prefill + 1 个 DEP16 decode，8 个节点（26 个 GPU）；segment 为 prefill 80gb、decode 140gb，每个 decode rank 40 个请求，80 个 decode extra slot，prefill 批次上限 32768 token。
  - c4096：7 个 DEP2 prefill + 1 个 DEP16 decode，9 个节点（30 个 GPU）；segment 为 prefill 80gb、decode 140gb，每个 decode rank 64 个请求，128 个 decode extra slot，prefill 批次上限 32768 token。
- DEP2 worker 数为奇数时，最后一个 prefill 节点有 2 个 GPU 空闲（c1228 分配 2 个 prefill 节点，c2884 为 3 个，c4096 为 4 个）；master 配置只计实际使用的 GPU：6、10、14 个 prefill GPU + 16 个 decode GPU，共 22、26、30 个。与 #4180 相同，各配置点都使用 1 个专用 CPU 节点运行前端与 AgentX 客户端。
- 分离式公共设置：
  - 两个角色均使用 MegaMoE all-to-all、`dsv4-attn-backend: flashmla_mega`、DSpark block size 5、Mooncake KV 传输、本地 DP control broadcast（`enable-dp-attention-local-control-broadcast`）、主机内存 Engram 表、2048 SWA prefix tails 与 decoder SWA bounded replay。
  - 两个角色均启用 Mooncake external cache linker（`enable-unified-cache-external-linker`，Mooncake 后端，group semantics），并启动 `mooncake-master` 服务（`--eviction_high_watermark_ratio=0.90 --client_ttl=60 --rpc_thread_num=64`）。SGLang 中 linker 与 `enable-hierarchical-cache` 互斥，因此 master 配置改为声明 `kv-offload-backend: mooncake 0.3.13.post1`。
  - Prefill：mega mHC（`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL=1`），每个 rank 的 MegaMoE 上限 32768 token，chunked prefill 65536。
  - Decode：stream interval 32，polling interval 8，每个 rank 的 MegaMoE 上限 16384 token，8 个 gateway worker，关闭 metrics。
  - 删除 `SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH`：镜像已通过 gloo gather + broadcast 交换调度器的 MLP 同步数据（sgl-project/sglang#44622）。
  - Dynamo 使用 ZMQ event plane 与 TCP request plane，因此去掉 NATS 服务；前端进程绑定 NUMA。
- SGLang 补丁：`configs/dsv41flash-sglang-patches.sh` 将 `configs/dsv41flash-sglang-patches/*.patch` 应用到镜像的 editable 安装目录 `/sgl-workspace/sglang`；脚本使用 `git apply`，可重复执行，在同一节点的多个 worker 之间加锁，任一 hunk 无法应用时 worker 直接失败。
  - `sglang-pr44623.patch`：sgl-project/sglang#44623（未合并），使 external cache linker 能注册 DeepSeek-V4.1 的混合 KV pool（pool assembler、unified linker、Mooncake/UMBP direct linker）。
  - 镜像包含该改动后即可删除补丁；20261020 镜像已包含此前版本以补丁形式携带的 sgl-project/sglang#44580 与 #45062。

- 本地验证：每个配置点在 GB300 NVL72 上运行一到两次 3600 s AgentX，使用 CI 的 benchmark 脚本与启动环境，golden 接受长度 3.51，失败请求为 0。吞吐按实际使用的 GPU（22 / 26 / 30 个）统计输入 token。
  - c1228（3P1D）：20261016 镜像 + #44623、#44580 及 20261019 镜像随后包含的 prefill 修复；两次运行 364.5k / 362.1k tok/s/GPU，TTFT p50 / p90 为 0.9 / 2.6 s，P90 / 中位数交互性 235-237 / 251-252 tok/s/user。
  - c2884（5P1D）：20261019 镜像 + #44623、#44580、#45062（本 PR 上一版 head）；604.4k tok/s/GPU，TTFT p50 / p90 为 4.4 / 10.3 s，P90 / 中位数交互性 178 / 191 tok/s/user。
  - c4096（7P1D）：与 c2884 相同；630.1k tok/s/GPU，TTFT p50 / p90 为 8.7 / 15.0 s，P90 / 中位数交互性 137 / 145 tok/s/user。
  - #44580 与 #45062 已包含在 20261020 镜像中，因此除 nightly 日期外与本 PR 一致。c1228 与 c4096 的运行额外带有一个本 PR 未包含的 decode 接收顺序补丁，实测无差异（c1228 两组同时运行的对照，P90 不带为 230/232，带为 230/228）。20261020 镜像本身尚未实测。

</details>



<details>
<summary>AI model disclosure</summary>

- Model/version: Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`), for the main session and every delegated agent.
- Main session: chose the configuration from the local experiments, reviewed the changes and edited this description.
- Delegated agents (same model): ran the local tuning experiments behind these settings, ported the recipe, master rows, setup script and patch files, resolved the merges with main, ran the repository checks and the two local validation runs, and drafted this description.

</details>

title: [PowerX] isolate AMD monitor windows and worker lifecycle / 隔离 AMD 监控窗口与工作节点生命周期
body:
## Description

Make AMD monitor shutdown wait for usable end samples and coordinate native worker collectors without masking serving failures. Validate nine complete configuration curves across MI300X, MI325X and MI355X; exclude retired DSV4 8k1k. Default `KV_OFFLOADING` to `none` in AMD `submit.sh`: fixed-sequence rows never carry it, so since #3141 required it every AMD multi-node fixed-sequence submission failed before sbatch.

**Testing:** 1649 CPU tests, Bash/YAML and changelog/matrix checks pass.

**Pending:** 89 `full-sweep-enabled` jobs and hardware power acceptance.

<summary>中文</summary>

AMD 监控停止前等待有效终点样本，并协调各工作节点采集器，同时保留服务失败状态。使用 MI300X、MI325X 和 MI355X 的九条完整配置曲线验证，排除已退役 DSV4 8k1k。另在 AMD `submit.sh` 中给 `KV_OFFLOADING` 补上默认值 `none`：定长序列矩阵行从不携带该字段，而 #3141 开始强制校验它，导致所有 AMD 多节点定长序列作业在 sbatch 之前就提交失败。

**测试：** 1649 项 CPU 测试、Bash/YAML 与 changelog/矩阵校验通过。

> **AMD single-node monitoring** in `benchmark_lib.sh` no longer uses a fixed sleep before killing `amd-smi`. Stop now polls `gpu_metrics.csv` until every GPU has a positive power sample at or after the first whole second past the stop request (`AMD_MONITOR_STOP_TIMEOUT_S`, default 30; `0` skips). With the evolution of hardware, networking, and model architectures, the previous DeepEP V1 had accumulated too much legacy baggage and performance issues. Today, we are excited to introduce
DeepEP V2
, which includes a complete refactoring of Expert Parallelism — achieving extreme performance with several times fewer SM resources compared to V1, while supporting significantly larger scale-up and scale-out domains — as well as experimental 0 SM Engram, 0 SM Pipeline Parallelism, and 0 SM Context Parallelism all-gather.
We are also happy to announce that we have switched from the NVSHMEM backend to the more lightweight
NCCL Gin backend
.
New Features
Fully JIT (Just-In-Time compilation)
NCCL Gin backend
Header-only & lightweight
Able to reuse existing NCCL communicators
EPv2
CUDA graph compatible, or faster CPU sync in saving memory mode
High-throughput and low-latency APIs unified into a single interface, with a new GEMM layout
Larger scale-up & scale-out domain support (up to EP2048)
Analytical SM & QP count calculation — no more auto-tuning needed
Both hybrid & direct modes remain supported
For V3-like legacy training, SM usage reduced from 24 to 4 - 6 while maintaining equivalent or better performance
0 SM Engram (with RDMA)
0 SM PP (with RDMA)
0 SM CP (with Copy Engine)
Notes
Buffer size consumption is larger than V1
0 SM RDMA low-latency EP is no longer supported
Engram, PP, and CP are experimental features
Still On-going Features
Elastic GPU & CPU buffers
: A contiguous virtual address space that maps to a hybrid of GPU and CPU physical memory under the hood, enabling fully automatic and transparent Engram or imbalanced EP
Reducing intermediate buffer sizes by leveraging EP replay to handle load imbalance
All-gather updates and reduce-scatter implementations for DP & TP
Performance
Following V3's configuration, we tested with 8K tokens per batch, 7168 hidden dimensions, top 8 experts, FP8 dispatching, and BF16 combining, and obtained the following results:
