title: feat(comm): add experimental allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm
body:
## 📌 Description Adds an **experimental** fused kernel, `flashinfer.comm.allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm`, that performs the tensor-parallel MNNVL one-shot all-reduce **and** the mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connection) post-map + pre-norm partials in a single launch. It targets the decode path of **GLM-5.3-Flash** served with TP8 on Blackwell MNNVL systems (e.g. two 4-GPU GB300 trays). ### Where it is used GLM-5.3-Flash replaces the single residual stream with **4 mHC residual streams** (hidden 4096). After every attention and every MoE/MLP sublayer, the row-parallel sublayer output has to be all-reduced across the 8 TP ranks, mixed into the 4 residual streams (mHC *post*), and projected for the next sublayer's mHC *pre* mapping (24 mix logits = 4 pre + 4 post + 16 comb). In a decode step this boundary runs **89 times** (every sublayer boundary except the last one, whose all-reduce feeds the final mHC post). At decode batch sizes (1 to 32 tokens) each of these steps is tiny and latency-bound, so the boundary is dominated by launch and synchronization cost rather than math. ### What is fused One sublayer boundary, on each of the 8 GPUs. The two red kernels (dashed box) are merged into the one green kernel; the gray steps do not change. ```mermaid %%{init: {"flowchart": {"wrappingWidth": 420, "nodeSpacing": 40, "rankSpacing": 40}}}%% flowchart LR subgraph BEFORE["Before: 3 kernels per boundary"] direction TB b0["Sublayer output
(this GPU's partial sum)"] subgraph MERGED[" "] direction TB b1["Kernel 1: all-reduce
sum the partials of all 8 GPUs → x"] b2["Kernel 2: mHC post + pre-norm partials
mix x into the 4 residual streams,
start the next sublayer's projection"] b1 -->|"x written to HBM,
then read back"| b2 end b3["Kernel 3: mHC pre finalize
(Sinkhorn + RMSNorm)"] b4["Next sublayer"] b0 --> b1 b2 --> b3 --> b4 end subgraph AFTER["After: 2 kernels per boundary"] direction TB a0["Sublayer output
(this GPU's partial sum)"] a1["Fused kernel: allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm
sum the partials of all 8 GPUs → x
(x stays in registers)
then mHC post + pre-norm partials"] a3["Kernel 3: mHC pre finalize
(unchanged)"] a4["Next sublayer"] a0 --> a1 --> a3 --> a4 end BEFORE ~~~ AFTER classDef removed fill:#f8d7da,stroke:#b02a37,color:#000 classDef fused fill:#d1e7dd,stroke:#146c43,stroke-width:2px,color:#000 classDef same fill:#f1f3f5,stroke:#868e96,color:#000 class b1,b2 removed class a1 fused class b0,b3,b4,a0,a3,a4 same style BEFORE fill:#ffffff,stroke:#adb5bd style AFTER fill:#ffffff,stroke:#adb5bd style MERGED fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#b02a37,stroke-dasharray: 5 5 ``` Inside the fused kernel: steps ① and ② are the unchanged stock one-shot all-reduce, and steps ③ and ④ are the old kernel 2, now run as an epilogue on `x` while it is still in registers. ```mermaid %%{init: {"flowchart": {"wrappingWidth": 420}}}%% flowchart LR subgraph AR["from Kernel 1 (stock one-shot all-reduce, unchanged)"] direction LR s1["① write this GPU's partial
to the 7 peers over NVLink"] s2["② wait for all 8 partials,
sum in fp32 in rank order → x"] s1 --> s2 end subgraph EPI["from Kernel 2 (now an epilogue on x in registers)"] direction LR s3["③ mHC post
new_r = post·x + comb·residual
→ residual_out (bf16)"] s4["④ pre-norm partials
yp = fn·new_r, rp = Σ new_r²"] s3 --> s4 end s2 --> s3 classDef ar fill:#f1f3f5,stroke:#868e96,color:#000 classDef epi fill:#d1e7dd,stroke:#146c43,color:#000 class s1,s2 ar class s3,s4 epi style AR fill:#ffffff,stroke:#adb5bd style EPI fill:#ffffff,stroke:#146c43 ``` Per token `m`, with `x` the all-reduced sublayer output: ``` new_r[m, j] = post_layer_mix[m, j] * x[m] + sum_k comb_res_mix[m, k, j] * residual[m, k] (fp32) residual_out = bf16(new_r) yp[s, m, n] = sum_{j, h in split s} fn[n, j*H + h] * new_r[m, j, h] (8 splits of H/8) rp[s, m] = sum_{j, h in split s} new_r[m, j, h]^2 ``` The fused kernel removes one launch (one CUDA-graph node) per boundary, the HBM round trip of `x`, and the second kernel's fixed latency. ### Design - **Same all-reduce, bit-identical.** The kernel uses the stock MNNVL one-shot Lamport protocol and the same `MNNVLAllReduceFusionWorkspace` (buffers, flags, rotation, clearing), so it interleaves freely with `trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce` on one workspace. The reduction is fp32 in rank order with one bf16 rounding, identical to `oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel`. - **Epilogue in registers.** After the peer reduction, each CTA applies the post-map to its hidden slice and accumulates the `yp` / `rp` split-K partials in fp32. Seven token-count-specialized kernels cover T = 1..32; every grid stays co-resident so the Lamport polling cannot deadlock. - **Numerics.** No fast-math (`use_fast_math=False`, no `.ftz` in PTX). `residual_out` is bit-exact against an fp32 reference; `yp` / `rp` differ only by fp32 summation order. - **CUDA-graph safe.** `allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm_prepare()` builds the JIT module outside graph capture; `allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm_supported()` lets a caller check whether a call takes the fused path. Outside the supported surface the API falls back to the stock all-reduce plus a PyTorch epilogue with the same outputs. ### Experimental scope - **Experimental API and backend.** Core holds only a thin `@flashinfer_experimental_api` entry point in `flashinfer/comm/allreduce_mhc.py`; the kernels, JIT spec, support checks and fallback live in `flashinfer/experimental/allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm/`. JIT-only, nothing in `aot.py`. - **Opt-in:** calling the API is the opt-in. It takes no part in automatic backend selection, dispatch, autotuning or trace-apply. - **Supported surface:** world size 8 on one MNNVL domain, hidden 4096, 4 residual streams, bf16, 1 to 32 tokens, SM100 / SM103. ```python import flashinfer.comm as comm comm.allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm_prepare(...) # once, outside CUDA-graph capture if comm.allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm_supported(...): yp, rp, residual_out = comm.allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm( input, residual, post_layer_mix, comb_res_mix, fn, workspace) ``` See `examples/experimental/allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm.py` for a runnable 8-rank example (`torchrun --nnodes 2 --nproc-per-node 4 ...`). ### Kernel-level results 8x GB300 (two trays, MNNVL), CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer main. Unfused = MNNVL one-shot all-reduce + the TileLang mHC post-map / pre-norm kernel used by the serving stack. Each variant is a CUDA graph of 90 back-to-back boundaries; microseconds per boundary, max over the 8 ranks, the two graphs replayed alternately in one process. | tokens (T) | unfused (µs) | fused (µs) | saved (µs) | speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 10.91 | 5.40 | 5.51 | **2.02x** | | 2 | 11.88 | 6.17 | 5.71 | 1.93x | | 4 | 11.82 | 5.83 | 5.99 | 2.03x | | 8 | 12.31 | 7.05 | 5.26 | 1.75x | | 16 | 12.84 | 7.75 | 5.09 | 1.66x | | 24 | 14.09 | 9.26 | 4.83 | 1.52x | | 32 | 14.32 | 9.66 | 4.66 | 1.48x | - Faster at every token count 1..32: **1.48x to 2.05x**, 4.7 to 7.7 µs saved per boundary. - **1.86x** weighted by GLM-5.3-Flash's decode token-count mix (1.91x when each graph is timed alone). - The all-reduce output and `residual_out` are bit-exact; `yp` / `rp` stay within 0.13 / 0.02 of the fp32 tolerance; 280/280 fused calls interleaved with stock all-reduces on one workspace are exact. Inside the model (CUDA-graph replay at T = 1, one boundary): ``` unfused all-reduce ████████████████████ 4.93 µs + post/pre-norm ███████████████████████ 5.86 µs = 10.78 µs fused ████████████████████████ 6.02 µs ``` Per decode step that is 89 boundaries x ~5.5 µs ≈ 0.49 ms, and 89 fewer CUDA-graph nodes (1372 → 1283). ### End-to-end results GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on vLLM, TP8 across two GB300 trays (MNNVL), CUDA graphs, multi-turn conversation trace replay (~30 min per point). Baseline: the same vLLM with stock FlashInfer main. | | c=1 baseline | c=1 fused | Δ | c=8 baseline | c=8 fused | Δ | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | mean ITL (ms) | 4.401 | 3.964 | **−9.9%** | 5.636 | 5.052 | **−10.4%** | | p50 ITL (ms) | 4.583 | 4.165 | −9.1% | 5.439 | 4.894 | −10.0% | | p90 ITL (ms) | 5.068 | 4.568 | −9.9% | 7.105 | 6.242 | −12.1% | | p99 ITL (ms) | 6.077 | 5.790 | −4.7% | 9.418 | 8.283 | −12.1% | | output tok/s | 123.5 | 129.6 | +5.0% | 348.8 | 349.4 | +0.2% ¹ | | mean TTFT (ms) | 660 | 655 | −0.8% | 487 | 518 | +6.4% ² | - Median decode step is **0.43 to 0.50 ms shorter** at every batch size, matching the kernel-level projection. With the fused path disabled in the same build the numbers match the baseline within run-to-run drift. - ¹ At c=8 the replay is demand-bound, so throughput cannot rise; latency is the signal. - ² Mean TTFT at c=8 is pulled up by a few requests beyond p99; median (388 vs 416 ms) and p90 are not worse. Prefill does not use this kernel; the cause is not isolated yet. ## 🔍 Related Issues ## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete. ### ✅ Pre-commit Checks - [ ] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method). - [ ] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`. - [ ] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues. > If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/). ## 🧪 Tests - [ ] Tests have been added or updated as needed. - [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.). ## 🔬 Experimental Track - [x] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: # - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release. - [x] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff). - [x] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included. - [x] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.) - [x] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows. ```experimental-tests # One target per line: a directory or a file. (A pytest ::selector is not # supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under # tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g. # # tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py # tests/experimental/my_backend/ # # Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every # experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell. ``` ## Reviewer Notes ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added an experimental fused all-reduce operation that combines mHC post-map and pre-norm processing for supported hardware and input configurations. * When the fused operation is unavailable, processing uses standard all-reduce followed by PyTorch operations. * Added an example and guidance on hardware requirements and preparation for CUDA graph capture.

title: feat(mhc): add experimental mhc_fused_post_pre
body:
## 📌 Description Adds an **experimental** fused kernel for the mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections) block boundary on **SM103 (GB300)**: `flashinfer.mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre`, plus `mhc_fused_post_pre_supported` and `mhc_fused_post_pre_warmup`. All three are marked `@flashinfer_experimental_api`, and the implementation lives in `flashinfer/experimental/mhc_fused_post_pre/` (JIT-only). ### Which model and when it is used The target is **GLM-5.3-Flash**. It carries **4 hyper-connection residual streams** (`[T, 4, 4096]`, BF16) over 45 layers with an attention and a MoE sublayer each. Between every two sublayers the model runs an mHC *post → pre* boundary: 1. **post map**: fold the sublayer output `x` back into the 4 streams, `residual_cur[j] = post_mix[j]·x + Σᵢ comb_mix[i,j]·residual[i]`; 2. **pre-norm projection**: project the flattened 4×4096 vector onto 24 mixing coefficients (`fn` is `[24, 16384]`) and compute its RMS statistic; 3. **pre map + input norm**: sigmoid gates, a 4×4 mixing matrix normalized by **20 Sinkhorn iterations**, then the weighted sum of the 4 streams and RMSNorm. This produces the next sublayer's input. This happens at **89 boundaries per forward pass**. The new op covers **T = 33 … 16384 tokens**: - **decode batches of 33–64 tokens**, inside CUDA graphs; - **prefill / mixed prefill+decode steps**, run eagerly. `T ≤ 32` keeps the existing single-kernel path. ### What is fused **Where it runs.** Every layer has two boundaries, one after attention and one after the MoE. That is 89 fused boundaries per forward pass: ```mermaid flowchart LR ATT["Attention"] --> B1{{"post → pre"}} B1 --> MOE["MoE"] MOE --> B2{{"post → pre"}} B2 --> NEXT["next layer"] style B1 fill:#ffd966,stroke:#b8860b style B2 fill:#ffd966,stroke:#b8860b ``` **What changes.** Boxes are kernels; cylinders are tensors in GPU memory. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph BEFORE["Before: 3 kernels"] direction TB a_in[("x, residual")] --> a1["① post map"] a1 -->|write| a_rc[("residual_cur")] a_rc -->|re-read| a2["② pre-norm GEMM"] a2 --> a_mix[("mix")] a_rc -->|re-read| a3["③ Sinkhorn + RMSNorm"] a_mix --> a3 a3 --> a_out[("layer_input")] end subgraph AFTER["After: 1 kernel (this PR)"] direction TB b_in[("x, residual")] --> b1["mhc_fused_post_pre
① + ② + ③ in one pass"] b1 --> b_out[("residual_cur,
layer_input")] end BEFORE ~~~ AFTER style a_rc fill:#f4cccc,stroke:#cc0000 style b1 fill:#b6d7a8,stroke:#38761d ``` The 4-stream intermediate `residual_cur` (`[T, 4, 4096]`) is written to memory once and read back twice, and the fused kernel removes that round trip: | per boundary | before | after | |---|---|---| | kernel launches | 3 | 1 | | passes over the 4-stream residual | 3 (1 write + 2 re-reads) | 1 | | memory traffic at T = 11476 | ~1.69 GB | ~0.94 GB | Why the unfused path is slow: - **Decode:** the three kernels each launch a tiny grid (48 / 64 / 48 CTAs on 152 SMs), so a boundary costs ≈ 15 µs for ~3.8 MB of traffic. - **Prefill:** the residual is written once and read twice, moving ~1.69 GB at T = 11476 against a one-pass floor of ~0.94 GB. The fused kernel has four regimes, all compiled into one JIT module: - split-hidden decode kernels for small T; - short-stream, crossover and long-stream kernels for larger T. ### Numerics The op is numerics-preserving relative to the unfused path: - FP32 accumulation for the projection and the square sum (TF32-class operands, no BF16/FP16 operands); - all 20 Sinkhorn iterations in order; - FP32 RMS statistics; - BF16 outputs; - no fast-math. `residual_cur` is bit-exact against an FP32 reference. The other outputs are as close to the reference as the unfused path is. ### Kernel-level performance (GB300) Method: GB300 (sm_103), CUDA-graph replay with a cold L2 (1 GiB flush before every replay), CUPTI span from the first kernel start to the last kernel end, median. The baseline is the unfused three-kernel path as deployed in vLLM for this model (TileLang `mhc_post`, DeepGEMM TF32 pre-norm GEMM, TileLang `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm`), timed in the same process. | tokens T | step type | unfused (µs) | fused (µs) | speedup | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:| | 40 | decode | 13.81 | 6.72 | 2.06× | | 48 | decode | 14.88 | 6.88 | 2.16× | | 56 | decode | 14.69 | 7.07 | 2.08× | | 64 | decode | 15.28 | 7.31 | 2.09× | | 1284 | mixed | 40.06 | 32.17 | 1.25× | | 2048 | mixed | 57.60 | 42.93 | 1.34× | | 3230 | mixed | 91.31 | 65.23 | 1.40× | | 6245 | mixed | 164.70 | 106.93 | 1.54× | | 11476 | mixed | 310.96 | 186.27 | 1.67× | | 16128 | mixed | 394.25 | 256.05 | 1.54× | ### End-to-end impact Setup: - **Model and server:** GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on vLLM 0.31.1rc1 (nightly), TP8 across 2× GB300 NVL4 nodes. - **Workload:** agentic-coding trace replay at concurrency 64, 1800 s per run. - **Comparison:** unfused vs fused, two paired runs. - **Routing:** a small vLLM-side change calls this API for `T > 32`; it is not part of this PR. | | result | |---|---| | Graph census (decode) | the fused kernel is CUDA-graph node content at all 89 boundaries per step; the 3 unfused kernels drop from 90 to 1 each per step; in-graph time per boundary falls from 20.1 µs to 10.9 µs | | Decode steps, batch 33–64 | **−0.37 ms per step** (median 7.54 → 7.20 ms, −4.5 %), consistent in every pairing | | Decode steps, batch ≤ 32 (not routed) | unchanged (+0.04 ms, within noise) | | Prefill / mixed steps | boundary GPU time −2.5 ms at T ≈ 3.5k and −5.8 ms at T ≈ 6.6k per step; host launch time ~−18 ms per eager step | | ITL / output throughput at c=64 | pooled ITL +4.8 % / throughput −1.0 %; within run-to-run variance (same-arm spread up to 21 % ITL); run 2 alone ITL −7.1 % / throughput +3.0 % | In decode, the stock kernels partly overlap their neighbours, so the step only shortens by 0.37 ms. That is less than the 0.85 ms of GPU work removed per step. ## 🔍 Related Issues ## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete. ### ✅ Pre-commit Checks - [ ] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method). - [ ] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`. - [ ] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues. > If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/). ## 🧪 Tests - [ ] Tests have been added or updated as needed. - [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.). ## 🔬 Experimental Track - [x] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.) - [x] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows. ```experimental-tests # One target per line: a directory or a file. (A pytest ::selector is not # supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under # tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g. # # tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py # tests/experimental/my_backend/ # # Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every # experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell. ``` ## Reviewer Notes ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added experimental fused mHC post-to-pre processing for supported SM103 GPUs, with automatic fallback to the reference implementation when specialized execution is unavailable. - Added support checks and warmup to prepare kernels before CUDA graph capture. - Added an example and documentation covering usage, supported inputs, and behavior. - **Tests** - Added coverage for reference agreement, supported inputs, fallback behavior, and CUDA graph capture.

title: [Feature][Rubin] Add H1536 and H4096 to existing CAKE RMSNorm training kernels
body:
## Problem

The existing CAKE RMSNorm training implementation from closed [#5679](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5679) / [PR #5741](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5741) covers hidden widths 512, 2048, and 6144 in its [exported registry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/e403d30785ea9ece65a88b3337db86dcac19fef5/flashinfer/jit/cake_rmsnorm_train.py). GLM-5.3-Flash also needs H1536 and H4096.

Ordinary RMSNorm consumes 0.848 s in the motivating two-update GB200 profile, including forward/replay and backward. That total includes existing H512 calls too; it is not all attributable to the two missing widths.

## Requested outcome

Add H1536 and H4096 forward/backward routes to the existing training API and kernel registry, preserving runtime-variable token counts. These are model feature widths, not CP-sharded dimensions; this remains a narrow width extension, not a new normalization family.

## Target hardware

SM100 (B200, GB200), SM103 (B300, GB300), and Future architecture: SM107 / Rubin, matching the existing training family's architecture scope. The motivating profile is GB200 only.

## Inference engine

PyTorch native; Custom / other. Training with activation checkpointing.

## Affected model or model family

[GLM-5.3-Flash public configuration](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash/blob/eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a/config.json): hidden size 4096 and query LoRA rank 1536.

## Workload and configuration

- **Shapes:** `x,dy[T,H]`, `weight[H]`; `H ∈ {1536,4096}`.
- **Tokens:** observed `T ∈ {14928,15288,15566,15590,16114,16132,16164,16263}`; benchmark examples, not supported-length limits. Preserve runtime-varying `T`, including smaller/larger and irregular row counts as batch layout and CP vary.
- **Layout:** contiguous row-major activations with strides `[H,1]`; contiguous weights.
- **Precision:** BF16 activations, upstream gradients, and affine weights; FP32 RMS/reduction arithmetic. Preserve the existing API's FP32 reciprocal-RMS and deterministic FP32 `dweight` accumulation/output; the caller can cast the final parameter gradient to its storage dtype.
- **Function:** `y = BF16((float32(x) * rsqrt(mean(float32(x)**2) + eps)) * float32(weight))`, with epsilon inside the square root.
- **Epsilon:** retain the existing configurable argument; test `1e-5` and `1e-6`.
- **Parallelism:** the profile uses CP16/EP32; the local operator requires no communication or fixed CP size. CP changes row count `T`, not the complete normalized feature width `H` in this path.
- **Environment:** `python -m flashinfer.collect_env` output is unavailable.

## Current workaround

Compiled PyTorch RMSNorm forward/backward for unsupported widths. H512 can continue using the already-supported route.

## Impact

Missing model or hardware support; Throughput; API usability or integration complexity.

## Acceptance criteria

- New forward/backward routes pass the existing training RMSNorm correctness and deterministic-reduction tests at both widths.
- Validate output, `dx`, and `dweight` at small, large, and irregular `T`, not only the observed counts; benchmark representative sizes against the current fallback and report `T` explicitly.
- Preserve existing 512/2048/6144 routes and runtime token-count behavior without recompiling for each `T`.

## Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

Small follow-up to [#5679](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5679) / [#5741](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5741). Sigmoid-gated RMSNorm, mHC normalization, new FP32 affine-weight modes, residual fusion extensions, and CP layout changes are outside scope.

title: [Bugfix] Package the SM90 DeepGEMM mHC register lifetime fix
body:
## Purpose

Package the SM90 mHC prenorm GEMM register-lifetime fix from [deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#448](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/448), authored by jason (leevan). In a multi-stage K loop, the next iteration can overwrite register A operands before the previous asynchronous WGMMA has finished. Repeated calls with identical inputs can therefore produce different outputs. The upstream fix waits immediately after committing the WGMMA batch.

This integrates that existing fix into vLLM's packaged JIT header until the pinned DeepGEMM dependency contains it; it is not a new kernel implementation. DeepGEMM #448 is currently open. Remove the temporary integration once the dependency pin includes the fix.

This correctness change was split out of [vLLM #58986](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58986), which now contains only the H20 block-FP8 MoE tuning. This branch starts from main `07f1ba2ec66776650a490630ddfa9e3c92713c33` and does not depend on that performance PR. The corresponding v0.30 backport remains [mengziheng/vllm#3](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/pull/3). There is no throughput improvement claim for this correctness repair.

## Changes

- Generate a patched header during CMake configuration and install it without modifying a supplied `DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR`. Exclude the original header from the directory install to prevent a same-timestamp overwrite.
- Use the same helper in the standalone DeepGEMM installer. Recognized patched input is idempotent; unrecognized source fails without overwriting the destination.
- Extend the existing mHC suite with six SM90 regressions: 256/512/1024 tokens, different split-K counts, default and side streams, independent FP32 references and exact repeatability. Skip when DeepGEMM is unavailable.

## Validation

The following GPU results were recorded on H20/v0.30 before this PR split. The main test path is `tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py`; the v0.30 suite used `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'sm90_mhc_prenorm_preserves_register_operands or test_mhc_fused_post_pre' -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k sm90_mhc_prenorm_preserves_register_operands -v
```

- The pinned original header fails the new regression; the fixed header passes all six cases. The final test including its DeepGEMM availability guard returned **6 passed, 212 deselected**.
- The broader selection returned **17 passed, 9 skipped, 1 failed**. The existing H=7168/M=128 BF16 reference case fails with both original and repaired headers. No tolerance was loosened; this is not a full-suite pass.
- A fresh-process audit of the complete mHC operation covers 12 shape/seed groups with five repeats each. Repaired results are exactly repeatable; the original produces inconsistent results at 256/512 tokens. This does not establish whole-model token determinism.
- An installation fixture using the actual CMake integration verified installed bytes equal the upstream fix, repeated configure/install preserves it, and supplied source content remains unchanged. Standalone idempotence and rejection of unknown input without destination overwrite also passed. A full wheel build was not performed.

Fresh local checks for this split:

```bash
pre-commit run --from-ref 07f1ba2ec66776650a490630ddfa9e3c92713c33 --to-ref HEAD
git diff --check 07f1ba2ec66776650a490630ddfa9e3c92713c33 HEAD
```

All applicable pre-commit checks pass. The three integration/helper files are byte-identical to the previously tested implementation, and the new regression's AST is identical. A local helper check again passed original-to-fixed conversion, idempotence, source preservation and unknown-input rejection. The generated header SHA256 is `b90beeaed11e279d3451ad3d438b8a64a41fd003c4b7f4d5e0a8fb79a20ad80b`. GPU tests were not rerun on this latest-main branch; these checks establish split equivalence, not a full main-wheel or full-model validation.

### Model evaluation

Historical validation uses the same GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint on 4×H20, TP4, FP8 weights/BF16 activations and MTP3, with v0.30 native extensions and the patched JIT header. The corrected control without the MoE tuning and the corrected candidate with the tuning each score **121/128** on a GSM8K first-128, five-shot raw-completion diagnostic (greedy, concurrency 8, output cap 768). Each has 128 successful requests and no truncation. Only 39/128 output texts match exactly; each arm uniquely answers three questions correctly. This subset is not an accuracy-improvement claim or proof of full-model equivalence.

The corrected control completed **1,152/1,152** measured serving requests successfully; all three recorded control/candidate blocks completed **3,456/3,456** in total. The corrected candidate also passed six context-retrieval checks at 511/2047/2048/2049/4097/8193 tokens. Full serving settings, paired measurements and limitations remain in [#58986](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58986). Those performance differences belong to the MoE tuning, with this fix present in both arms.

B200, production traffic, long soak tests and full-model serving on latest main were not validated.

## Related work

The open-PR duplicate search was refreshed before splitting. [#50645](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50645) and [#53055](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53055) address missing-DeepGEMM fallbacks, [#52165](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52165) changes detection, [#48619](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48619) ports the SM100 kernel to CuTeDSL, and [#41834](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834)/[#42856](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42856) concern SM12x support. [#55184](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55184) repairs sparse MLA on SM8x; [#54955](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54955) is an opt-in batch-invariant execution preview using explicit mHC operations. Neither addresses packaging this register-lifetime fix in the default SM90 path. No duplicate integration was found. The same code has been removed from #58986 so the two community PRs do not duplicate it. No second DeepGEMM fix PR is proposed.

AI assistance was used for investigation, integration, tests and this description. Human review has not been asserted.

title: [Bugfix] Warm GLM DeepGEMM mHC pre-norm specializations
body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash can finish startup and still pause to compile an mHC kernel when a new prompt length arrives. This PR moves those missing compilations to startup without changing the kernel math or split-K heuristic.

Addresses #60536. Depends on https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/29 for the compile-only entry point used by this implementation.

## Claims

- Register every reachable DeepGEMM mHC pre-norm specialization for GLM's configured token range, deduplicated by `(N, K, num_splits)`.
- Compile them through the existing startup warmup registry, without allocating input tensors or launching dummy kernels.
- Keep runtime split selection, kernel math, and backend selection unchanged.

## Details

### Why startup misses these kernels

The mHC pre-norm path contains a matrix multiplication implemented by DeepGEMM. It selects a split-K count (how many pieces to divide the reduction into) based on the number of tokens in the current engine step. Each distinct split count requires a separately compiled kernel. The row count `M` itself is dynamic, so there is no need to compile once per prompt length.

The existing selection is:

```python
num_splits = max(1, min(num_sms // ceil(M / 64), ceil(K / 64) // 4))
```

Here `M` is the step's token count, `K` is the input width, and `N` is the output width. For example, with 78 SMs and `K=16384`, `M=64`, `192`, and `16384` select 64, 26, and 1 splits respectively. Compiling the first and last does not compile the middle one. The number of required specializations depends on the GPU and configured token range; the issue's count of missing variants is not a universal constant.

The startup profile run and CUDA-graph capture exercise only some split counts. GLM does not register the remaining DeepGEMM variants for explicit warmup. The first real request that reaches a missing split therefore compiles it while serving, delaying that engine step and potentially other in-flight requests. This is a JIT coverage gap, not evidence of incorrect model arithmetic.

```text
Before: startup warms some splits -> request reaches a new split -> compile -> run
After:  startup warms all reachable splits -> request -> reuse compiled kernel
```

### What this changes

When GLM selects the DeepGEMM path, register its projection dimensions with a small kernel wrapper. The wrapper enumerates token counts up to `max_num_batched_tokens` at the heuristic's 64-token boundaries, maps them to `(N, K, num_splits)`, and deduplicates the keys. Startup compiles those keys; requests continue to call the same DeepGEMM runtime kernel.

### Why a companion DeepGEMM change?

The first proposal in #60536 is to warm each reachable split by executing one dummy row through the existing API. That can trigger compilation **without changing DeepGEMM**. This PR uses the same coverage strategy, but chooses compile-only warmup to follow the [current warmup contract](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/contributing/jit_kernel_warmup.md), which excludes real tensor allocation and dummy kernel launches.

The companion PR exposes `compile_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm(n, k, num_splits)`, reusing the runtime JIT source and cache keys but stopping before launch. The trade-off is a cross-repository dependency and additional cold-start compilation time, rather than pauses during requests. This dependency is a choice of implementation, not a requirement inherent to fixing the issue.

### Relationship to earlier work

This builds on existing warmup work; the idea of warming mHC or DeepGEMM specializations is not new. The remaining gap is **GLM's DeepGEMM pre-norm GEMM with its existing token-dependent split heuristic**.

Status checked on 2026-10-08:

| Earlier work | Status | What it covers | Why it does not already complete this fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #50178, Roberto L. Castro | Merged Sep 13 | Migrates the mHC **TileLang** kernels to the shared registry, including GLM registration, and adds a TileLang compile-only helper. | It explicitly keeps TileLang and DeepGEMM dispatch separate. Compiling the TileLang kernels does not compile the DeepGEMM GEMM called within the same mHC path. |
| #56683, Woosuk Kwon | Merged Sep 14 | Adds `compile_many()` and parallel compilation for existing TileLang pre-norm keys. | Changes how registered keys compile, not which DeepGEMM keys GLM registers. |
| #56761, Chauncey | Open | Proposes parallel **TileLang** mHC warmup for GLM-5.3-Flash. | Optimizes startup compilation of another backend; it does not register this DeepGEMM GEMM. |
| #57843, Woosuk Kwon | Open | Warms **DeepSeek-V4.1's DeepGEMM** projection widths and bounded `1/4/16` splits by executing one dummy row per key. | This is the closest prior implementation and the precedent cited by #60536. Its model registration and split mapping target DeepSeek-V4.1, not GLM's wider split set. |
| #57643, Woosuk Kwon | Merged Sep 21 | Fuses DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder-boundary operations. | Its independent DeepGEMM warmup was **removed and extracted to #57843** before merge. The merged fusion PR must not be treated as delivering that warmup. |
| #51802, SyaOtiLan | Open | Continues DeepSeek-V4 **TileLang** registration/fallback coverage, including MTP/DSpark paths. | Different model registration and backend; not the GLM DeepGEMM specialization gap. |

I checked these descriptions and changed-file scopes, searched vLLM PRs for `DeepGEMM mHC`, `GLM warmup`, and `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`, and checked related DeepGEMM PRs. I did not find a separate merged fix for this GLM DeepGEMM path; the base of this PR still lacks its warmup registration. This is a scoped search result, not a claim that no overlapping work can exist.

The contribution here is to cover GLM's reachable keys using the existing registry, preserve its split heuristic, and expose the metadata-only DeepGEMM compilation needed by this implementation. It does not replace the TileLang work or claim to implement #57843's DeepSeek-V4.1 registration.

### Scope and alternatives

- The issue's dummy-row proposal is a valid way to trigger compilation through the existing DeepGEMM API. The compile-only choice and its dependency are explained above; the dependency is not necessary for every possible solution.
- The issue also suggests bucketing splits into `1/4/16`. That changes runtime tuning and needs prefill/decode performance evaluation. This PR deliberately leaves that heuristic unchanged.
- #49905 tracks broader DeepGEMM warmup gaps. This PR only covers this GLM mHC entry point, not all DeepGEMM kernels, module-loading costs, or a general JIT-monitor extension. It does not promise zero runtime compilation across the whole model.

## Validation

- H20 regression: **42 passed** with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_jit_warmup.py -q`. Coverage includes split selection, token-range boundaries, and metadata-only compilation.
- Isolated kernel A/B: a 258-shape sweep with separate empty caches produced **13 runtime compilations before explicit warmup, 0 after**. Six numerical reference checks passed in each run. Added warmup took 21.64 s; maximum observed kernel-call latency was 1687.62 ms versus 0.369 ms. These are single-run kernel measurements, **not end-to-end TTFT**.
- Real serving: **41/41 requests passed; 0 new mHC cubins during requests**. All 16 required mHC cubins existed at readiness.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and the test-tethering check. The human submitter confirms reviewing every changed line and personally running the relevant tests.

<details>
<summary>Serving validation configuration</summary>

GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 on H20, TP8, max batch 16384, max sequences 32, prefix caching off. This PR's Python diff was applied to the v0.31.0 image with the patched DeepGEMM build; this was not a full build of main.

Requests comprised 16 split buckets twice, one arithmetic chat, and eight streaming requests at concurrency four. Serving used `-cc.mode=none -cc.cudagraph_mode=none` with JIT warmup enabled. `--enforce-eager` also disables JIT warmup in this version and was not used for the passing run.

</details>

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Overlap mHC coefficients for small TP batches
body:
## Purpose

Overlap shifted mHC coefficient generation with attention/FFN on small batches. The decoder keeps one post/pre path: the existing mHC dispatcher
selects overlap or native execution, while the decoder joins the coefficient
stream before consuming its outputs.

`supports_mhc_overlap` in `.ops.mhc` requires SM100/DeepGEMM, no ubatching,
and compatible projection dimensions: hidden width divisible by 64, and
`hc_mult * (hc_mult + 2)` a positive multiple of 8 no greater than 32.
The exact H5120/hc4 restrictions and helper assertion are removed.
Compatible tensor/data/pipeline/expert-parallel configurations, attention backends,
and LoRA configurations use the same token cutoff, without a separate performance
allowlist. Larger batches, draft layers, and piecewise/breakable graphs retain
native execution. The cutoff is generalized from the TP4 measurements below;
those measurements do not establish a gain for every newly enabled configuration.

The cutoff is **16 tokens**, based on same-instance paired full-forward
measurements with matching tuned GEMM tactics (three samples per arm):

| Tokens | Native ms | Overlap ms | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.763 | 4.692 | 1.49% |
| 6 | 6.204 | 5.929 | 4.42% |
| 8 | 6.644 | 6.360 | 4.28% |
| 12 | 7.408 | 7.292 | 1.57% |
| 16 | 7.966 | 7.877 | 1.12% |
| 24 | 9.153 | 9.365 | -2.31% |
| 48 | 11.915 | 12.040 | -1.05% |
| 96 | 15.292 | 15.247 | 0.29% |
| 192 | 18.820 | 18.977 | -0.84% |
| 252 | 20.040 | 20.230 | -0.95% |

All samples are retained; the 24/48-token overlap arms contain outliers
(SD 0.390/0.388 ms). Larger shapes show no reliable useful gain, so keep native
execution there. Selection uses the captured token shape, never actual KV
length. Split-kernel warmup is bounded by the same cutoff.

## Validation

Based on main `17e50b9b76`. Latest validation: **79 GPU tests pass**, covering
exact output parity and changed-input CUDA graph replay across `(hidden_size,
hc_mult)` = `(4096, 2)`, `(5120, 4)`, `(7168, 4)`, plus decoder/reference parity
and graph/batch fallbacks. Pre-commit passes.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'overlap_preserves_outputs or decoder_mixes_match_torch' -q -rs
```

Only transient input/scratch tensors (`x`, `mix`, `sqr`) need side-stream allocator
recording. The model retains weights, and callers retain coefficient outputs
until joining the side stream; the helper documents that ownership requirement.

Model/performance measurements below are prior results, not reruns on the new
main base or measurements of every newly enabled configuration.

Measured on GB200×4, model revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`,
FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, TP4, DSpark fixed length 5, and synthetic 100K ±5% KV.
These are fixed-forward GPU latencies; no default-O2 piecewise-serving gain is
claimed. The prior ten-sample native/automatic pair measured 6.206→5.932 ms (4.42%).

The refactored commit's three-sample same-instance native/automatic comparison
measures **6.210→5.928 ms (4.55%)**, with identical inputs, KV and tuned GEMM
tactics. Automatic selection activates all 40 target layers. Both arms have
finite outputs and zero eager/graph, changed-input and restored-input replay
errors. Replay checks do not assert native/overlap full-model bitwise parity.

Prior matched real-weight GSM8K: 1271→1268/1319 (96.36→96.13%; 7 improve, 10 regress).
DSpark acceptance length 3.870→3.874. Local FP64 and serialized/async checks support
the numerical change; full-model hidden states are rounding-sensitive. The
refactor preserves the evaluated kernel math and launch order, so this accuracy
evaluation is reused. Prior same-instance allocator peaks increased 16 MiB allocated
and 74 MiB reserved per rank; this is not a serving-capacity measurement.

The projection-width limit of 32 follows DeepGEMM's device-side output-swizzle
constraint. Newly enabled dimensions have correctness coverage, not additional
end-to-end performance measurements.

## Final-head validation (2026-09-21)

Exact head `479b025e45`, GB200×4, pinned model revision above, TP4 **without
DSpark or all-reduce+mHC fusion**, FlashInfer FP8 attention/MXFP4 sparse indexer.
Baseline uses the same head with overlap disabled before loading.

| Metric | Overlap disabled | Enabled |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Forward-only, KV8704 | 4.727 /4.730 ms (before/after) | 4.657 ms (−1.5%) |
| Real8K/1K C1 mean TPOT | 5.013 ms | 4.992 ms (−0.4%) |
| Median ITL | 5.011 ms | 4.974 ms |
| P99 ITL | 5.228 ms | 6.049 ms |
| Full GSM8K flexible extraction | 1266/1319 (95.98%) | 1271/1319 (96.36%) |

Forward harness: same initialized synthetic weights/KV, five samples ×20
CUDA-graph replays after5s warmup per arm; slowest-rank GPU time, excluding
lm_head/sampling/scheduler/HTTP. All arms pass finite-output and changed-input
replay checks (zero replay error). This is not cross-arm bitwise parity.

Serving: ten exact8192-input/1024-output requests per arm, greedy, C1, two
warmups; FULL_DECODE_ONLY with eager prefill. All requests succeed; candidate
tail bursts in2/10 requests mean this is not a strong serving-speed claim.
GSM8K: lm-eval0.4.12, five-shot chat, greedy, seed123, C8, max output1024;
matching prompts/targets,10 improve and5 regress, strict formatting79.68% both.

**Warmup caveat:** initial overlap-disabled GSM8K reproduced cached FlashInfer
CuTe tactic compilation under strict JIT monitoring. Final arms use identical
startup-only cached-tactic and DeepGEMM split warmup from the existing fix in
#57643, plus identical pinned tactics. Zero monitored runtime JIT afterward;
these workarounds are not part of this PR. No claim of stock-stack zero JIT or
coverage of every newly enabled topology/backend. The79 focused GPU tests
above validate the exact head.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR found for shifted mHC coefficient/sublayer overlap. #52725 concerns
XPU norm fusion; #42735 changes BF16 shared staging in the older mHC kernel;
#56761 changes GLM JIT warmup; #51802 registers NVIDIA V4 warmup variants.
None implements this scheduling change.

AI assistance was used to implement, benchmark and test this change.

Purpose
GLM-5.3-Flash at TP4 uses 288 FP8 experts with a per-rank intermediate size of 512 and 128×128 weight blocks. H20 currently has no matching tuned configuration, so the default 64-row tile pads many expert assignments unnecessarily. Add a shape-specific configuration that selects 16- and 32-row tiles where measured faster and preserves defaults elsewhere. Also teach
benchmark_moe.py
to read the nested text configuration of the GLM-5.3-Flash architectures, so this shape can be benchmarked and retuned through the existing tool.
This does not replace the general heuristic in
#47593
. That PR's 16/64-row rule is an explicit control in the experiments: the small-batch improvement overlaps it and is credited to that approach. The new 32-row regions provide additional gains at the tested 640–1216 and 2560–3328 token sizes. Existing H20 configuration PRs
#44152
,
#44273
and
#54500
address other expert counts, shapes or quantization schemes; no open PR for this E=288, N=512 block-FP8 configuration was found.
The SM90 mHC correctness integration previously included here has been split into
independent PR #59129
. This PR now changes only the H20 MoE configuration and benchmark model-config handling. The two changes can be reviewed and merged separately. The full-model results below require the mHC fix in both benchmark arms; they are not measurements of an unrepaired dependency.
Test Plan
Retune/benchmark the model shape on H20 with the existing tool:
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py \
  --model /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash --tp-size 4 --dtype fp8_w8a8 \
  --batch-size 1 16 64 96 128 512 640 768 1024 1152 1280 2048 2560 2816 3072 4096
Independent measurements call that tool's
benchmark_config
directly, using 30 timing iterations (10 CUDA graph calls per iteration), seeds 1051/2077/3091, rotating arm order and changing routing between measurement iterations. All three arms receive the same seeds.
try_get_optimal_moe_config
selects the checked-in config through its normal nearest-entry lookup. Numerical comparisons against the previous default cover 31 batch sizes including lookup boundaries, three seeds each, BF16 activations and block-FP8 expert weights. This direct-function harness imports Ray but does not start a cluster.
Test Result
93/93 numerical comparisons pass with atol=0.002 and rtol=0.01; all results finite. Maximum absolute difference 0.00015259, maximum relative RMSE 0.0002718.
Applicable pre-commit checks pass for the release and main branches.
Kernel timing results are microbenchmarks, not end-to-end throughput claims. Ratios below are inverse-latency throughput ratios, medians over three seeds.

The earlier +27.10% / +9.46% / +8.02% results used an unrepaired mHC dependency. They remain historical observations and are superseded for the current code by the corrected comparison below. C0 is v0.30

C0+C1 → C0+O1+C1
, keeping the header fix in both arms and switching only the O1 JSON. The benchmark helper is not imported by serving.
Both arms use the same 62-shard checkpoint (config SHA256
bb8f01c42cb92a52ca72e65afb4d5bd8d11aef083cd210e8de25dfb904f23e9f

Weight memory is 77.62 GiB/card and KV cache 5.72 GiB/card (221976 tokens). Software is vLLM 0.30.0+cu129 native artifacts, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, Triton 3.7.1, driver 535.261.03 with CUDA 12.9 compatibility libraries.

Model quality and scope
O1+C1: GSM8K first 128, five-shot raw-completion diagnostic, greedy, concurrency 8, output cap 768:
121/128 correct
, all 128 requests successful, zero truncation. All six retrieval checks at 511/2047/2048/2049/4097/8193 tokens pass. The corrected control also scores 121/128 with zero failed or truncated requests. Prompts and dataset hashes match. Only 39/128 output texts are identical across these two runs; each arm uniquely answers three questions correctly. Previous C0 diagnostics scored 117/128 and 118/128; O1 scored 120/128 and 123/128. These subsets do not demonstrate an accuracy improvement or full-model equivalence. Whole-model exact repeatability is not asserted.
The full model was tested on the requested v0.30 release with the correctness backports. The upstream port was separately validated on H20 using main Python/Triton sources at
4a190dc51
plus this change: 35 batch sizes × three seeds = 105 numerical comparisons, including batch sizes 577, 1217, 2305 and 3329 immediately across configuration lookup boundaries. All pass with the same tolerance; maximum absolute difference 0.00015259 and maximum relative RMSE 0.0002718.
Main's MoE alignment API has an additional optional argument, so its MoE native extension was rebuilt from unmodified main sources with CUDA 12.9, GCC 12 and PyTorch 2.13. The other native extensions came from the release wheel. This validates the relevant main FP8 MoE path, not a full main-branch wheel or full-model serving on main. The initial attempt to reuse the release MoE binary failed on that ABI mismatch and was not counted as a successful test.
The mHC header repair and its regression test are submitted separately. GPU model validation remains v0.30. During the PR split, the complete performance-branch tree was verified identical to the previously validated O1-only commit
f2e71f998
. GPU tests were not rerun for this packaging-only split. B200, expert parallelism, other TP sizes/quantization formats, production traffic and long soak tests were not performed. Saturation throughput is not a production capacity/SLO guarantee.
AI assistance was used for investigation, code, tuning, test execution and this description. Human review has not been asserted.

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Fuse TP all-reduce with mHC input preparation
body:
## Purpose

Fuse TP all-reduce, mHC post mixing, delayed collapse, and RMSNorm at DSV4.1 decoder boundaries. This replaces three launches with one, preserves the BF16 boundaries, and retains coefficient overlap. The kernel reuses the existing MNNVL workspace without an additional persistent communication allocation.

Enabled by default for eligible SM100 TP4 forwards with 1–16 tokens, including speculative decoding. The selector requires hidden size 5120, hc_mult=4, EP disabled, and a multicast workspace; it does not restrict DP/PP size, LoRA, or attention backend. The existing overlap-support checks still apply, including disabling overlap for ubatching. Larger batches and graph boundaries use the existing operations. Sixteen is the largest size with a validated gain, not a measured crossover.

Builds on #57603, now merged into main, which overlaps coefficient computation but does not fuse collectives. This differs from #51244's terminal mHC/head fusion. Open-PR searches for `mhc allreduce` and `mhc fusion` found no duplicate of this decoder-boundary collective fusion.

The independent startup warmup fixes have been extracted: DeepGEMM mHC projection coverage is in #57843, and cached FlashInfer MXFP8 tactics are in #57842. Neither is included in this fusion PR.

## Communication choice and token cutoff

Keep multicast and the 16-token cutoff. A controlled GB200 TP4 experiment replaced multicast stores with explicit stores to each of the four peers, retaining the same math, Lamport synchronization, cleanup, and PDL. Push did not consistently improve performance:

| Tokens | Multicast kernel | Push kernel | Multicast model forward | Push model forward |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 14.348 µs | 14.634 µs | 4.054 ms | 4.060 ms |
| 8 | 14.395 µs | 14.972 µs | 5.724 ms | 5.728 ms |
| 16 | 13.910 µs | 15.795 µs | 7.133 ms | 7.130 ms |

Kernel timings use cold-L2 CUDA-graph replay, five samples of 50 replays, and the maximum rank time. Model timings use the same synthetic-weight model instance, KV8704, identical tactics, and three samples of 20 replays; they exclude the output head and serving. Multicast and push model outputs were byte-identical on every rank at all nine tested sizes (1–128).

Extending fusion to 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, and 128 tokens regressed model-forward time in this screen, despite isolated kernel gains; coefficient overlap remained disabled above 16. Some nonstandard sizes used default tactics because exact cache buckets were absent. A follow-up using normal serving autotune buckets confirmed the gain at 1 and 16 tokens (4.667→4.060 ms and 7.783→7.127 ms). Near-boundary runs at 17 and 20 tokens failed the unfused baseline's native-top-k correctness check, so no timings from those shapes are accepted. This supports retaining 16 conservatively; it does not establish the exact crossover. No new model accuracy evaluation was run for the experimental variants.

Multicast requires a supported NVLink/NVSwitch configuration and successful group memory setup; GPU generation alone does not establish support. Explicit peer stores could broaden support to Hopper-or-newer systems with suitable peer-memory access without multicast. That would require separate allocation/dispatch support and hardware validation: this PR remains SM100 TP4, and the experimental push variant reused the existing workspace. Push is a possible portability fallback, not a demonstrated GB200 performance improvement.

## Latest model-forward comparison against main

Measured candidate `dd63c1fa00` (runtime source identical to the subsequently merged PR head `7be123b000`) versus main `d2983f2f16` fetched at benchmark start, including merged overlap and the latest DSpark block-table fix in both arms. GB200 ×4, TP4/DP1, FlashInfer FP8 attention, MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer, auto MoE, KV8704, max model length 1M. Matched synthetic weights/KV and 210 cached tactics with normal hybrid token buckets. Five samples ×20 full-forward CUDA-graph replays after warmup, maximum rank time per sample; median reported below.

| Mode | Batch | Component / tokens | Main | Candidate | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No DSpark | 1 | main / 1 | 4.651 ms | 4.055 ms | 12.8% |
| No DSpark | 8 | main / 8 | 6.236 ms | 5.668 ms | 9.1% |
| No DSpark | 16 | main / 16 | 7.806 ms | 7.127 ms | 8.7% |
| DSpark | 1 | main / 6 | 5.867 ms | 5.280 ms | 10.0% |
| DSpark | 1 | draft / 5 | 0.353 ms | 0.344 ms | 2.4% |

DSpark uses fixed draft length5. These are model-forward measurements, excluding the output head, sampling, scheduling, HTTP and acceptance effects. The draft implementation is unchanged, so its small difference is not attributed directly to fusion. All accepted cases pass eager/graph and changed/restored-input replay checks with zero error. Initialization manifests and source/final tactic hashes match between arms.

An additional candidate DSpark B2 target case failed the harness native-top-k score check at layer2; no timing from that shape is accepted, and main B2 was not measured. This run does not establish B2 correctness or new model accuracy. Untimed setup permits compilation and strict JIT checking resumes before validation/timing; neither arm includes the extracted startup fixes #57842/#57843. The comparison measures warmed execution.

## Test Result

GB200 ×4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4/DP1, FlashInfer FP8 attention, MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer, auto MoE, no DSpark. Baseline disables only this fusion before model construction; it includes #57603. Both arms use the same checkpoint, configuration and FlashInfer autotuning cache (all 168 entries reused, checksum unchanged).

The latest polling/RMSNorm follow-up loads peer payloads together and distributes norm partials for local shared-memory reads. PDL completion stays early for multi-token forwards and moves to the end for one token. Compared with the previous fused kernel, a same-instance synthetic KV8704 forward comparison measured B1 4.558/4.588→4.044/4.044 ms, B8 6.014/6.012→5.969/5.979 ms, and B16 7.787/7.782→7.794/7.822 ms. B1 baseline varied between runs (4.184 ms in the prior controlled run), so the largest paired percentage is not a robust gain estimate. B16 is 0.1–0.5% slower in the final screen. Output bytes match on every rank for all three sizes; the final collective test also covers signed-zero sentinel collisions.

The serving and GSM8K measurements below are from the initial fused implementation (`fa59bb3883`). They have not been rerun after this output-equivalent follow-up.

8K input / 1K output serving, concurrency 1, three requests per run, forced output length:

| Run | Mean TPOT | Median ITL | P99 ITL |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 4.947 ms | 4.951 ms | 5.034 ms |
| Candidate, initial | 5.361 ms | 4.510 ms | 16.240 ms |
| Candidate, repeat after GSM8K | 4.578 ms | 4.506 ms | 7.676 ms |

The warmed repeat reduces mean TPOT by 7.5%, but the initial candidate had stalls and tail latency remains higher. These short serving runs do not establish a tail-latency improvement. All requests completed, with 8192 input and 1024 output tokens each.

A separate fixed-forward screen measured B8 6.565→6.028 ms (−8.2%) and B16 8.421→7.785 ms (−7.6%). B32 exercises fallback: 11.382→11.353 ms with identical output. These are three-sample synthetic-weight/cache measurements at KV8704, excluding the output head and serving.

Full GSM8K, 1319 questions, five-shot chat, thinking disabled, greedy generation, seed 123, maximum 1024 generated tokens, concurrency 8:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Flexible extraction | 1267/1319 (96.06%) | 1275/1319 (96.66%) |
| Strict match | 79.08% | 79.98% |

Prompt and target hashes match for every question. Floating-point ordering changes outputs; this is not bitwise model equivalence. The paired results have 11 candidate-only correct answers and 3 baseline-only correct answers.

- Four-GPU collective test passed: changing sizes, all-gather interleaving in the shared workspace, changed-input CUDA-graph replay.
- mHC regression selection: 137 passed.
- 77 saved real operator inputs: maximum relative RMS 2.3e-5 for residuals and 1.5e-4 for normalized inputs.
- CMake `_C_stable_libtorch` build and pre-commit checks passed.



Serving uses max model length 1048576, max sequences 8, max batched tokens 8192, 10 GiB KV cache, prefix caching disabled, Engram CPU offload, and `--compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}'`. The sequence cap is a validation setting, not a recipe recommendation.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. The human submitter confirmed review and relevant tests for the original submission; the warmup follow-up validation is reported separately below.

## Warmup validation

The sparse-candidate alignment fix and its tests were extracted into #57667. The validation below was run on combined commit `2219a281f8`, before the split, and includes that fix.

The missing mHC specialization was DeepGEMM split=4, not a TileLang epilogue. Warmup now covers splits 1/4/16 for both projection widths on GB200. A fresh-cache test compiled six variants, then successfully checked 26 runtime shapes with further compiler invocations forbidden.

A fresh real-weight TP4 server with `enable_jit_warmup=true` and `--jit-monitor-mode error --jit-monitor-verbose` completed 23 requests (736 generated tokens), spanning 3–8192 prompt tokens and mixed batches of up to eight requests. All four ranks enabled the monitor before requests: zero runtime Triton/TileLang/CuTeDSL JIT events, and no DeepGEMM compiler commands in this run. The 66 focused tests below and pre-commit checks passed.

The original serving measurements above explicitly disabled JIT warmup. These fixes close reproduced intermediate-prefill compilation gaps; they do not establish the cause of the original decode tails or a new steady-state speedup. GSM8K was not repeated for this startup/specialization follow-up, which leaves model arithmetic unchanged.

## Test Plan

```bash
RAY_ADDRESS=local .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py -k all_reduce_mhc -q -rs
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'deepseek_v41 or delayed_custom_op' -q -rs
```

Combined warmup follow-up at `2219a281f8` (66 passed, 2 deselected):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_jit_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  -k 'not sparse_mqa_logits_prefill_matches_dense_masked and not deep_select' -q -rs
```

## Rebase validation

Rebased onto main `9b49f92344` (merged #57603). Retained the simplified overlap helper and existing fusion eligibility, multicast transport, and 16-token cutoff. The fused CUDA kernel and dispatcher are unchanged. Dropped the obsolete extraction commit so the sparse-indexer alignment fix already on main remains intact.

At `75e3082ab1`, all pre-commit hooks passed and the focused GB200 GPU suite passed (176 passed, 135 deselected):

```bash
RAY_ADDRESS=local .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'all_reduce_mhc or deepseek_v41 or delayed_custom_op' -q -rs
```

Serving benchmarks and GSM8K were not repeated for this rebase; the earlier results above retain their stated scope.

## Broader dispatch validation

Removed benchmark-only restrictions on DP/PP size, attention backend, LoRA, and speculative decoding. The TP4 group, fixed kernel dimensions, EP exclusion, and multicast workspace checks remain. The kernel and 16-token cutoff are unchanged. The distributed replay test now includes 6/12-token fixed verification and shrinking/growing token counts.

The completed TP4 DSpark comparison (2026-09-19, before the rebase) used draft length five, FlashInfer FP8 attention, the same checkpoint and matched 210-entry tactics. Baseline retained overlap and disabled only fusion. Both arms scored 125/128 on a matched GSM8K subset; mean acceptance lengths were 3.739 and 3.730. All ten 8K-input/1K-output serving requests per arm succeeded. Mean TPOT was 1.451→1.247 ms, but random-prompt acceptance also changed (5.241→5.803), so this is not an isolated fusion speedup.

That validation used identical pinned-tactic and startup warmup workarounds in both arms. It is a subset accuracy check for fixed DSpark, not validation of every admitted backend, topology, LoRA configuration, or speculative method. Adaptive shape changes are covered at the distributed-kernel level. No new full GSM8K evaluation was run for this dispatch-only follow-up.

Follow-up `2b4ce61608`: 182 GPU/dispatch tests passed, 135 deselected, using the focused command above on GB200 ×4; all pre-commit hooks passed.

## Cached-tactic warmup extraction

Removed `_warmup_flashinfer_mxfp8_tactics`, its call site, and its unit test in `f6232a4f7f`. The independent two-file fix is in #57842 at `622e20e1ee`. The mHC projection-split warmup was subsequently extracted to #57843. The remaining autotune suite passed (4 tests), and pre-commit passed. Historical validation above that included the cached-tactic warmup still depends on the extracted fix; this PR alone does not close that runtime compilation gap.

## DeepGEMM projection warmup extraction

Removed `MHCPrenormGemmWarmup`, its model registration, and tests in `ef850bb5c3`; the standalone fix is #57843. Historical combined validation above included both startup fixes (#57842 and #57843). The fusion kernel and dispatch are unchanged by the extraction.

## Dispatch organization

At `70f0cb7be4`, `mhc.py` owns the shared `mhc_shifted_post_pre` dispatcher and `supports_mhc_all_reduce` eligibility check. `mega_mhc.py` contains only the DeepGEMM implementation and its support check. This is a code move with unchanged arithmetic, eligibility, and 16-token cutoff. Pre-commit passed; the GPU regression command below passed 192 tests (125 deselected). No accuracy/performance rerun for this structural change.

```bash
RAY_ADDRESS=local .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'all_reduce_mhc or deepseek_v41 or delayed_custom_op or deep_gemm_mega_mhc' -q -rs
```

title: [Feat] dsv4: Support deterministic inference for DeepSeek-V4
body:
## Motivation

Closes #36174.

`--enable-deterministic-inference` rejects DeepSeek-V4 at startup, and because the
model's config-time overrides pin `--attention-backend dsv4`, there is no backend to
fall back to — the flag is unusable on V4 in every configuration:

```
ValueError: Currently only ['ascend', 'fa3', 'fa4', 'flashinfer', 'intel_xpu', 'triton']
attention backends are supported for deterministic inference, but you explicitly
specified 'dsv4'.
```

Allowlisting the backend alone is not enough: with it allowlisted but nothing else
changed, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 still produces 3 distinct outputs over 20 batch sizes.
The V4 path has four separate dispatches that key off the token count.

## Modifications

Each site below picks a kernel, a tile size, or a split-K count from the number of
tokens in the batch, which is exactly what deterministic inference must not do.

1. **mHC pre-norm split-K** — `_compute_num_split_for_mhc_pre` derives `n_splits`
   from `n_sms // ceil(num_tokens / 64)`, and `n_splits` is the number of partial
   sums the K reduction is folded from, so it fixes the summation order. This is the
   first op of every layer, so a prompt prefilled alongside two others differs from
   the same prompt prefilled alone in *every* token's logprob by ~1e-2. Pinned to the
   token-independent `num_block_k // 4`. `mhc_fused_post_pre` carries the same term
   plus a `num_tokens <= 32` FMA-kernel switch, and
   `_flashinfer_mhc_pre_num_splits` is a third copy.
2. **FlashMLA sparse decode tile scheduler** — `sparse_attn_decode_interface`
   computes `payload = ceil(total_num_blocks / num_sm_parts)` over the whole batch,
   so where a request's KV range is cut depends on its co-batched requests.
   Deterministic mode issues one launch per request, which makes the schedule a
   function of that request alone.
3. **Non-paged indexer** — taken only when `batch_size == 1 and query_rows >= 8192`.
4. **Router GEMM** — `MoEGate` switches to `dsv3_router_gemm` at
   `hidden_states.shape[0] <= 16`, and `linear_bf16_fp32`'s HPC-Ops path at `M >= 8`.
   Fixing the first also fixes a startup crash: the deterministic branch of `MoEGate`
   returned bf16 router logits, and V4's fused `hash_topk` kernel requires fp32
   (`Dtype value [bfloat16] not in the allowed options: [float32]`).

Also probed and ruled out on H200, so left alone: the DeepGEMM fp8 block GEMM is
M-invariant at every V4 shape, `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` (prefill) is s_q-invariant,
and the MoE runner choice makes no difference.

Deterministic inference on `dsv4` is rejected on SM120, whose attention kernel is an
autotuned Triton kernel that picks its tile size — and with it the softmax rescaling
order — from measured timings.

Everything above is gated: with the flag off, the only changes are an extracted
`_use_sparse_prefill` predicate, two algebraically identical `max_splits` locals and
a `use_fma` local. Verified below.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, 4xH200, TP=4.

**The feature.** Distinct outputs over 32 batch sizes,
`sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode single`:

| | distinct outputs / 32 |
| --- | --- |
| without the flag | 6 |
| with `--enable-deterministic-inference` | **1** |

All three harness modes pass with radix cache and CUDA graphs on: `single` (n=32),
`prefix` + logprobs (temperature 0.5, shared prefixes of 1 / 511 / 2048 / 4097), and
`radix_cache`. Chunked prefill was checked separately at
`--chunked-prefill-size 512` over 4097-token prompts.

**No regression with the flag off.** Same box, arms run back to back, benchmark client always from `main` so only the
server tree varies.

The strongest check pins the batch at one request, which removes batch-composition
noise entirely: 150 GSM8K completions issued serially are **150/150 byte-identical**
between `main` and this branch, as are 8/8 fixed greedy prompts.

GSM8K, 400 questions, 5-shot, greedy, `--parallel 64`:

| tree | runs |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | 0.965, 0.965, 0.968, 0.968, 0.968 |
| this branch | 0.960, 0.963, 0.970, 0.960 |

Repeats within one warm server span 0.960-0.970 on this branch, bracketing every
`main` number; at 400 questions the harness cannot resolve better than about +/-4
questions. That spread is DeepSeek-V4's own batch-composition non-determinism -- the
thing the new flag removes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**With the flag off** — `sglang.benchmark.serving`, random 1024/512, 200 prompts,
concurrency 32: 

| order | tree | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1st | `main` | 1849.80 | 5549.39 | 14.01 ms |
| 2nd | this branch | 1919.93 | 5759.80 | 13.99 ms |
| 3rd | `main` | 1919.67 | 5759.01 | 13.99 ms |

This branch lands within 0.01% of the warm `main` run. The first run is the cold
outlier (JIT and autotune caches), and that cold-start effect (+3.8%) is far larger
than anything between the trees. `MHC prenorm prewarm: 21 n_splits buckets` is logged
by both trees with the flag off, i.e. the split-K schedule is untouched there.

**With the flag on**, decode throughput (fixed batch, 128 output tokens, best of 3):

| | bs=1 | bs=16 | bs=32 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no flag | 131 | 1611 | 3045 tok/s |
| deterministic | 50 | 354 | 444 tok/s |

Deterministic inference costs ~2.1-2.5x on its own (batch-invariant matmul/rmsnorm,
pytorch sampling, NCCL tree with pinned channels, pinned MoE and mHC split-K), flat
in batch size. The per-request FlashMLA launch adds a further 2.3x at bs=16 and 3.2x
at bs=32, and is free at bs=1. It is not optional: an ablation that keeps the single
batched launch and everything else is still non-deterministic (2 distinct outputs
over 32 batch sizes).

That ablation is also the opening for a follow-up. `sparse_decode_fwd` accepts
`tile_scheduler_metadata` and `num_splits` as inputs and only computes them when
absent, so a supplied no-split schedule would recover the single launch. This PR
takes the loop instead: it is 15 lines, obviously correct, and carries no coupling to
a pinned third-party struct layout — and its bit-exact output is the oracle a
schedule builder would be validated against.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
