title: [Perf] dsv41: Speed up decode-size mHC mixing with a vectorized split-K reduce and 160 K slices on SM120
body:
## Motivation

`hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` is the CUDA Triton path for DeepSeek-V4.x mHC mixing statistics and Sinkhorn, run twice per layer. It is used at every row count on SM120, on SM100 when the DeepGEMM prenorm GEMM is not used (including below 128 rows), and on SM90 at one row. It has two launches:

1. `_hc_mix_stats_partial_kernel`: one CTA per (row tile, K slice). K=20480 is split into 80 slices.
2. `_hc_mix_reduce_sinkhorn_kernel`: one single-warp CTA per row, which adds the 80 slice partials in a serial `static_range` loop before the Sinkhorn.

At decode sizes the serial loop takes about as long as the partial kernel. With one row tile, 80 CTAs also occupy fewer than half of the 188 SMs on an RTX PRO 6000.

## Modifications

- `_hc_mix_reduce_sinkhorn_vec_kernel`: loads the partials as one `[slices, cols]` tile and reduces them with `tl.sum`, then runs the unchanged Sinkhorn. There is still one CTA per row, and the reduction tree depends only on the slice count, so results are deterministic and batch-invariant. The summation order differs from the serial loop. `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` uses it on SM120 (compute capability 12.0), where it was measured; other GPUs keep the serial reducer, so their results are unchanged. The bf16x3 and DeepGEMM paths keep the serial reducer with 16 slices; DeepGEMM also keeps its residual input.
- `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn(..., decode=False)`: with `decode=True` on SM120 (compute capability 12.0 only), it splits K into 160 slices when the number of 64-wide K blocks is a multiple of 160. `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward_hc_pre_from_prev` sets `decode` for decode/idle and target-verify forward passes and passes it through `mhc.run_attn_post` / `run_moe_post`, `_compute_triplet`, `mix_stats` and `_mix_stats_impl` to `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn`. Each new `decode` parameter defaults to False. Prefill/extend, other callers (including the DSpark draft layer, which calls `mix_stats` directly), other GPUs, and the unfused `hc_mix_stats` keep the existing choice (80 for K=20480). The slice count depends on K, the device, and the forward mode, never on M. A row therefore gets the same bits at any batch size within decode/verify on this backend, and likewise within prefill. A decode row can also run beside prefill rows in a MIXED batch, which takes the prefill split, so with batch-invariant mode enabled (`--enable-deterministic-inference`) `_mix_stats_impl` passes `decode=False` in every mode, as it already disables the compensated projections in that mode.

## Accuracy Tests

New `test_hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn.py` (GPU) and `test_deepseek_v4_mhc_decode_split.py` (CPU). With this branch head's `mhc.py` and tests, all 23 tests in `test_hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn.py` passed on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), and the 4 tests in `test_deepseek_v4_mhc_decode_split.py` passed on CPU. I have not run the ported model code end to end on a GPU (`deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_v4_mhc.py` on current main). The tests cover:
- Slice selection: 160 for decode and 80 for prefill on SM120; 80 for both on SM100 and SM121; 80 for a K whose 64-wide block count is not a multiple of 160.
- Accuracy: K=20480 in decode mode at M = 1, 6, 48 and 300 (160 slices) and in prefill mode at M = 6 and 300 (80 slices), plus K = 5120, 4096 and 192 (80, 64 and 1 slices). The fused op matches the unfused `hc_mix_stats` (serial sum, 80 slices at K=20480) followed by the Sinkhorn within rtol 1e-5 / atol 1e-6. It also matches FP64 mixing statistics followed by the FP32 Sinkhorn within rtol 1e-4 / atol 1e-5.
- Determinism and batch invariance in each mode, with the device forced to SM120 (vectorized reduce) and to SM100 (serial reduce) on any host GPU, as in the accuracy cases. The test checks the selected reducer and slice count, that repeated calls are bitwise equal, and that rows computed alone, as the first 8, 9, 2048 and 2049, and as every 7th of a 2056-row batch are bitwise equal to the same rows in that batch. These subsets use all three row tiles (8, 16 and 32 rows; 32 starts at 2049 rows).
- Model wiring, on CPU with a mocked layer and no weights: the real `forward_hc_pre_from_prev`, posts and `mix_stats` pass `decode=True` to `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` for both hyper-connections in decode, idle and target-verify forward passes, and `decode=False` in extend, mixed, draft-extend and split-prefill passes. With batch-invariant mode enabled, every forward mode passes `decode=False`, so decode and MIXED batches select the same slice count (80 on SM120). A direct `mix_stats` call defaults to `decode=False`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per call (partial + reduce/Sinkhorn, `us`) on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (SM120, 188 SMs, 250 W power limit, used only by the benchmark), torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Inputs are BF16 `[M, 20480]`. Each CUDA graph covers 24 distinct `[24, 20480]` FP32 weights at M <= 64 and 4 weights above; the time is the best of 20 graph replays divided by the number of calls. Columns:
- main: `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` from the base commit's `mhc.py` (serial reduce, 80 slices);
- `decode=False`: this PR's `mhc.py` (vectorized reduce, 80 slices);
- `decode=True`: this PR's `mhc.py` (vectorized reduce, 160 slices, the SM120 decode/verify setting);
- max abs diff: the largest absolute difference over the `pre`, `post` and `comb` outputs between `decode=True` and main, for the first weight.

| M | main | `decode=False` | `decode=True` | max abs diff |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8.45 | 7.59 | 6.23 | 2.38e-07 |
| 2 | 9.97 | 7.74 | 6.52 | 2.38e-07 |
| 4 | 10.08 | 7.77 | 6.57 | 3.58e-07 |
| 8 | 10.18 | 7.84 | 6.66 | 2.38e-07 |
| 16 | 11.02 | 8.56 | 7.21 | 2.38e-07 |
| 32 | 11.20 | 8.78 | 8.22 | 3.58e-07 |
| 48 | 12.54 | 10.17 | 10.60 | 3.58e-07 |
| 64 | 12.76 | 10.42 | 10.97 | 3.58e-07 |
| 96 | 15.53 | 13.28 | 13.85 | 3.58e-07 |
| 128 | 19.46 | 17.21 | 16.35 | 3.58e-07 |
| 256 | 27.24 | 25.13 | 26.02 | 5.36e-07 |

With 80 slices, the vectorized reduce lowers latency by 8-23% versus main at every M measured. With 160 slices, latency is a further 15-18% lower up to 16 rows (26-35% lower than main) and 6% lower at 32 rows. At 48-256 rows, 160 slices changes latency by -5% to +5% relative to 80 slices (these sizes occur in large verify batches) and is 4-16% lower than main.

I measured the following with the same kernel change on my branch before the port onto #42245, and have not repeated them on this port.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (PCIe), TP4/EP2, DSpark speculative decoding:
- Vectorized reduce: the reduce took 6.0 -> 3.5 us per call at 6 rows. End-to-end decode throughput (median of 3 runs, temperature 1) on two consecutive builds, the second adding this reduce, changed by -0.5 / -1.6 / +3.5 / +0.1% at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 concurrent requests.
- 160 slices: in a decode profile, the mix partial kernel took 9.0 -> 6.5 us per call.

160 slices is limited to SM120 decode/verify, the only architecture and mode where I measured it; I have no same-build prefill A/B, so prefill keeps 80 slices.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4: DSpark draft stages take the TF32 mHC statistics path from 32 rows on SM100
body:
## Motivation

Under DSpark decode, the three draft stages compute the mixing statistics of their six mHC boundaries with the Triton split-K kernel (`hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn`) at every batch, while the target layers run DeepGEMM's `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` from 128 rows. Two reasons: the DSpark model never calls `refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache`, so its stages have no TF32 weight parts, and `_mix_stats_impl` keeps the DeepGEMM path off under 128 rows on SM100 (SM90 uses it from 32).

Measured on GB300 (DEP16 decode, DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash, 128K contexts, torch profiler, kernel durations):

| Draft rows (= requests per rank) | `_hc_mix_stats_partial_kernel`, 6 launches | `_hc_mix_reduce_sinkhorn_kernel`, 6 launches | Per cycle |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | 6 x 23.8 us | 6 x 9.0 us | 0.197 ms |
| 64 | 6 x 42.2 us | 6 x 9.1 us | 0.307 ms |
| 256 | 6 x 150 us | 6 x 10.5 us | 0.963 ms |

In the same traces the target's unfused boundaries run `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_impl` at 7.4-7.9 us per launch (160 and 320 rows) plus a 16-slice reduce of 7.8 us: about 23 us per boundary against 52 us on the Triton path at 64 rows. The 128-row floor is not a kernel requirement: DeepGEMM's SM100 kernel uses `block_m = 64` with a grid of `num_splits x ceil_div(m, 64)` and no assertion on M.

## Modifications

- `DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark.post_load_weights` calls `refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache` on each stage, which builds the TF32 parts of the 24 x 20,480 mixing weights (24 MB per GPU for three stages).
- `_mix_stats_impl`: the row floor for the TF32 parts becomes 32 on SM100 as on SM90 (`x_flat.shape[0] >= 32` replaces `>= 128 or hopper_medium`, which already meant 32 on SM90). Batch-invariant mode and rows under 32 are unchanged.

Expected: about 0.17 ms less per decode cycle at 64 requests per rank (22.6 ms cycle), 0.06 ms at 32.

## Accuracy Tests

The draft's statistics move from the Triton tf32x3 kernel to the two-part TF32 split the target already runs at 128 rows and above. Accept length from the A/B decode logs will be posted here; GSM8K at native acceptance on request.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The A/B at 64 requests per rank (same recipe, base main 49766a74f9 against this branch) is running; the six draft launches and the log cycle will be posted here.

Single-node H20-3e report: vision CP + DSpark, long-prefill improvements, and three upstream PRs
Thanks for maintaining this roadmap and for the kernel/CP work behind it. We have been integrating and testing DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on
one 8× NVIDIA H20-3e server
, with text, image+text, tool calling, streaming, and cache reporting as requirements.
Our October 5–7 experiments started from
unmodified SGLang v0.5.21
and ended with a production deployment of a pinned integration build. The strongest paired comparisons were:
524,032-token cold TTFT: 323.261 → 25.531 s
, a
92.1% reduction / 12.66× speedup
.
C64 aggregate output: 877.01 → 2,534.61 token/s (+189.0%)
; per-request streaming decode:
15.69 → 49.10 token/s (+213.0%)
.
These are
whole-deployment improvements
, not the isolated effect of any one PR. We have contributed
#39306
,
#42922
, and
#42924
; their narrower validation and attribution are described below.
1. Setup and measurement scope
Hardware: 8× H20-3e, SM90, approximately 140 GiB visible memory per GPU, NVLink/NVSwitch (NV18 topology), 2 TiB host RAM, two NUMA nodes.
Baseline: v0.5.21 at
e00930c5489053f26d86b179cee0d087f846acbb
,
TP8/EP8, DSpark block size 5 already enabled
, no CP, no decoder bounded replay, GPU-resident Engram, no HiCache.
Final:
TP8/EP4, CP8 interleave, CP decode-attention TP, DSpark5, decoder SWA bounded replay
, FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE with FP8 precision; Engram host table in
per_rank
layout, NUMA binding, HiCache ratio 1.5 /
write_through
.
Both use a 524,288-token context limit, static memory fraction 0.8, chunk size 8192 and max-running-requests 64. Prefill CUDA graphs remain disabled; decode CUDA graphs are enabled.
Final local integration revision:
79b468a7435e1bd29ad0d377587ff10b3c214ba3
(
not an upstream release/commit
). Runtime: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, FlashInfer 0.6.18; the final DeepGEMM integration uses
sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.2
. This is a backported integration, not a claim that stock v0.5.21 supports this configuration.
The baseline and final integration use the same V4.1 model weights on the same hardware. No P/D disaggregation is used. All performance below is from a single eight-GPU server. These results describe the pinned October 5–7 snapshots, not the latest heads of every roadmap PR.
Comparison boundary:
the near-512K and C64 baseline measurements were supplemented using exactly the final workload construction, warmup and three measured rounds. Input hashes, token counts, output lengths and zero-cache-hit conditions match. Other baseline cells are historical references: cold-prefill nonces differ, and the early natural-generation prompts/warmup procedure differ from the final protocol. The tables explicitly mark the paired supplements with †. Runs were sequential, on different dates, not randomized interleaved A/B trials.
2. Optimization path and what we retained
Use vision-compatible CP as the foundation.
We chose
model: DeepSeek V4.1 vision CP and single-owner image encoding
#40219
for its merge-before-shard multimodal preparation and single-owner image encoding. We adapted the owner callback API and fixed physical request-pool row mapping in the Torch prefill indexer. We borrowed the replay-tail idea from
[DSV4.1] DeepSeek-V4.1 support prefill CP
#40161
later, rather than importing its entire P/D integration.
Integrate the Hopper paths and H20 configurations.
This included
[Perf] Optimize DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Hopper paths and Blackwell prefill selection
#41251
,
[DSV4.1] Add H20 block-FP8 tuned configs
#41098
and the relevant
[DSV4.1] Enable Hopper decode optimizations for TP8
#39114
path, plus scorer/Top-K, compression, RoPE, dispatch and preparation changes listed below. We checked actual dispatch and added tables for six further missing matrix shapes encountered in this integration; small tuning differences below 3% retained the default. These additional local tables are distinct from the original six tables in
[DSV4.1] Add tuned H20-3e block-FP8 GEMM configs
#39306
.
Enable Engram host storage and HiCache together, then tune EP.
The
per_rank
layout shards the host Engram table across ranks rather than replicating the entire table eight times. The combined memory configuration increased the engine-reported KV token-pool capacity by about 31.25% relative to our preceding GPU-Engram/HiCache-ratio-2/memory-fraction-0.88 configuration, with essentially unchanged near-512K TTFT. This is a combined memory-layout result, not a standalone offload speedup.
Add decoder bounded replay while preserving image requests and DSpark.
After the last KV-source layer, replay shortens the late-layer token rows. We added tail-aware CP gather, global token indices for logits/DSpark, original CP-owner mapping, and preservation of canonical image IDs. This became
[DSV4.1] Support decoder SWA bounded replay with vision CP and DSpark
#42924
, with
[DSV4.1] Fix Torch prefill indexer request-pool rows under CP
#42922
as a separate row-mapping fix.
Add fused prefill scoring and native SM90 block32 FP8 GEMM.
[DSV4.1] Fuse Hopper prefill indexer scoring into one Triton kernel
#42365
fuses indexer score/ReLU/weighting/head reduction;
[SM90] Use native block32 DeepGEMM for DeepSeek-V4.1
#42604
enables the supported native DeepGEMM linear paths. We retained the existing compact-candidate path and fallbacks. Routed MXFP4 experts still use FlashInfer.

Experiments not retained:
TP8/EP1 with Marlin W4A16:
C64 aggregate output 1,797.47 token/s, versus 2,362.80 for the then-current EP4 build. Both backend and parallelism changed, so this is not an isolated EP comparison.
TP8/EP1 with an adapted FlashInfer W4A8 path:
preserve logical shard boundaries, then pad the 288-wide expert intermediate dimension to 384 for the required 128 alignment, including gate/up halves, down columns and scale handling. It passed our operator/model checks, but C64 reached 2,139.99 token/s, still below EP4.
TP8/EP2:
slightly better TTFT, generally worse natural-generation aggregate throughput.
Chunk 8192 → 16384:
about 1.5% better long TTFT, about 4.6% worse C64 aggregate output; retained 8192.
CP local-projection deduplication:
approximately 21–33% faster in the projection+gather microbenchmark, only 0.4–1.1% TTFT improvement end to end with mixed throughput results; removed.

correctness checks passed, but none of the six tested shapes beat the existing scorer; not dispatched in production.
The medium-mHC path remained disabled pending further validation.

title: [DeepSeek-V4] Enable fused and overlapped mHC stats for small SM90 decode batches
body:
## Motivation

On SM90, DeepSeek-V4 previously used fused mHC stats only for `M=1`.
Small decode and target-verify graphs therefore ran:

```text
partial -> reduce -> split_sinkhorn
```

on the main stream for every layer. For small `M`, this work is independent
of the following attention or MoE computation and can be hidden on the
existing mHC stats stream.

## Modifications

- Add the opt-in JSON environment variable
  `SGLANG_OPT_MHC_STATS_OVERLAP_EXTRA_TOKEN_COUNTS`.
- For explicitly enabled SM90 decode/target-verify shapes with
  `1 < M <= 16`, use the existing fused stats path:

  ```text
  partial -> reduce_sinkhorn
  ```

- Submit attention stats before attention and FFN stats before MoE on the
  existing stats stream.
- Join the stats stream only immediately before `hc_post` consumes `post`
  and `comb`.

The default allowlist is empty, so existing SM90 behavior is unchanged unless
the optimization is explicitly enabled. `M=1`, prefill, Blackwell, and the
FP4 MoE operator are unchanged.

Suggested H20 setting:

```bash
export SGLANG_OPT_MHC_STATS_OVERLAP_EXTRA_TOKEN_COUNTS='[4,8,12,16]'
```

## Accuracy Tests

- Fused-vs-unfused stats numerics passed for `M=1/4/8/12/16` with
  `torch.testing.assert_close(rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)`.
- Maximum absolute error for every tested shape:
  `1.1920928955078125e-7`.
- Shape-policy checks passed:
  - Default: only the existing `M=1` path is enabled.
  - With `[4,8,12,16,20]`: `M=1/4/8/12/16` are enabled and `M=20`
    remains rejected by the hard cap.
- Existing mHC kernel test: 27 passed, 1 failed.
  - The failure is the existing BF16 tolerance boundary in
    `test_mhc_fused_post_pre_matches_unfused[False-17-7168]`.
  - One of 121,856 elements differs by `0.00390625` versus tolerance
    `0.002`; this test covers an unchanged operator.
- Full model accuracy evaluation was not run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment:

- Performance-tested base: `86cb4a0f97`
- 8x NVIDIA H20 (SM90, 97,871 MiB, 78 SMs/GPU)
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8/EP8
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, Triton 3.6.0, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1
- `dsv4` attention, `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE
- Full decode CUDA graphs; prefill CUDA graphs disabled

Method:

- Random token IDs, 100 input / 128 output tokens
- Concurrency `4/8/12/16`, `4 * concurrency` requests per case
- One warmup plus five measured runs per case and variant
- Order: baseline A1 -> optimized -> baseline A2, with a fresh server and
  graph capture for every variant
- Baseline is the median of 10 A1+A2 runs; optimized is the median of 5 runs

| Decode M | Baseline tok/s | Optimized tok/s | Throughput | Baseline TPOT ms | Optimized TPOT ms | TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 199.90 | 207.38 | +3.74% | 18.311 | 17.567 | -4.06% |
| 8 | 358.34 | 367.61 | +2.59% | 20.285 | 19.727 | -2.75% |
| 12 | 469.14 | 484.80 | +3.34% | 22.227 | 21.371 | -3.85% |
| 16 | 594.56 | 600.71 | +1.03% | 23.224 | 22.935 | -1.25% |

Baseline A1-to-A2 throughput drift was `+0.23%/+0.21%/+0.16%/+0.17%`.
Optimized throughput CV was at most `0.07%`.

TP0 trace at `M=8`:

| Path | Partial | Separate reduce | Separate Sinkhorn | Fused reduce+Sinkhorn |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 5,280 | 5,280 | 5,280 | 0 |
| Optimized | 5,280 | 160 | 160 | 5,120 |

- All 5,120 fused decode kernels overlapped work on another CUDA stream.
- Conservative interval overlap: 30.298 ms of 51.775 ms fused-kernel GPU
  time (58.5%).
- Frequent overlap partners include RMSNorm, FP8 quantization, W8A8 matmul,
  tiny-N GEMM, and router kernels.

The fused kernel is not faster in isolation. The E2E gain comes primarily
from moving dependency-independent stats ahead of attention/MoE and hiding
that work on the side stream, plus removing one launch and intermediate
handoff.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and static checks passed (`py_compile`, `git diff --check`, shell
  syntax check).
- [x] Existing relevant unit test was run; the one known BF16 boundary failure
  is documented above.
- [ ] Documentation update is not required for this opt-in experimental knob.
- [x] Kernel numerics, E2E speed benchmarks, and GPU traces are provided.
- [x] The change follows the existing model scheduling and environment-variable
  patterns.

title: Valid Per-Field Selective Risk Control for Document Extraction: Three Failure Modes, a Validity Ladder, and When Conditioning Pays
body: Per-field accept/review with selective risk at most alpha -- accept a field only if the error rate among accepted fields is controlled -- is the trust contract document-extraction systems need, and the natural procedure silently violates it on real documents. On 13,859 genuine claude-sonnet-5 fields from 800 CORD receipts (49.0% correct) we diagnose three failure modes: document clustering (design effect 1.84-2.45), score-refit leakage (coverage 0.416 at risk 0.127, violating alpha=0.10 in 95% of splits), and a tie-mass pathology (a degenerate score collapses the threshold grid, 0.030 to 0.001). We organize the fixes as a validity ladder, guarantee form stated per tier. A fit/val split protocol restores expected-selective-risk control for a learned fusion: coverage 0.318 at risk 0.096 at nominal alpha=0.10, no tolerance band (production variant 0.326) -- an on-average point whose realized risk exceeds alpha in 47.5% of resplits, not a certificate. Mondrian Learn-then-Test with exact binomial tails yields per-group PAC certificates: field-iid 0.171 at risk 0.068, cluster-corrected 0.140, doc-iid 0.060 -- the only tier matching documents, honestly near-vacuous today. Support-bin, the pre-specified provenance taxonomy, wins every rigor tier on the sonnet CORD capture (p<1e-4, Bonferroni-corrected) -- a win that does not replicate on the same documents under haiku or qwen -- while on higher-accuracy corpora pooled thresholds win: conditioning helps exactly where pooled cannot certify, subsumed by a learned score elsewhere. A frozen-configuration confirmation on selection-untouched claude-haiku-4-5 held at both risk levels, and a blind three-annotator human-gold audit verifies the practical tier's accepted-set risk at 1.3% against its 10% budget (Fleiss' kappa=0.83; labels err one-sidedly pessimistic). Released Apache-2.0 with seed-pinned, regression-gated procedures.

title: Scaffold Splits Overestimate Virtual Screening Performance
body: Virtual Screening (VS) of vast compound libraries guided by Artificial Intelligence (AI) models is a highly productive approach to early drug discovery. Data splitting is crucial for better benchmarking of such AI models. Traditional random data splits produce similar molecules between training and test sets, conflicting with the reality of VS libraries which mostly contain structurally distinct compounds. Scaffold split, grouping molecules by shared core structure, is widely considered to reflect this real-world scenario. However, here we show that the scaffold split also overestimates VS performance. The reason is that molecules with different chemical scaffolds are often similar, which hence introduces unrealistically high similarities between training molecules and test molecules following a scaffold split. Our study examined three representative AI models on 60 NCI-60 datasets, each with approximately 30,000 to 50,000 molecules tested on a different cancer cell line. Each dataset was split with three methods: scaffold, Butina clustering and the more accurate Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) clustering. Regardless of the model, model performance is much worse with UMAP splits from the results of the 2100 models trained and evaluated for each algorithm and split. These robust results demonstrate the need for more realistic data splits to tune, compare, and select models for VS. For the same reason, avoiding the scaffold split is also recommended for other molecular property prediction problems. The code to reproduce these results is available at https://github.com/ScaffoldSplitsOverestimateVS

title: Ablate and Rescue: A Causal Analysis of Residual Stream Hyper-Connections
body: Multi-stream transformer architectures have recently been proposed as a promising direction for managing representation collapse and the vanishing gradient problem for residual connections, yet their internal mechanisms remain unexplored. In particular, the recently introduced Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) architecture posits multiple residual streams with constrained interaction, but lacks in-depth mechanistic analysis. We present the first open-source mHC language model (https://huggingface.co/wgpeng/mhc-780m) and analyze the multiple-stream architecture with a suite of representation-level metrics and causal interventions to probe how parallel streams encode and utilize information. Specifically, we introduce a systematic stream ablation-and-rescue framework that enables direct causal comparison of residual streams during inference. Through targeted pairwise interventions and controlled recovery experiments, we distinguish functional redundancy from asymmetric utilization and reveal how information is distributed across streams beyond what is observable from representational similarity alone.

title: refactor(klaud): resolve target clusters in code / refactor(klaud): 在代码中解析目标集群
body:
Stacked on #4137.

Until now, the planner's overlap-review agent worked out each candidate's target clusters from `runners.yaml` and returned them as `clusters`, and `select` gated capacity on that list. Before review, `choose()` also pre-filtered candidates by guessing that a cluster belonged to a hardware type if its name started with that hardware (`cluster == hardware or cluster.startswith(hardware + "-")`). Both are now deterministic.

- **`target_clusters(entries, inventory)`:** every cluster any of the family's generated rows can run on. Each row's `runner` label is resolved to its nodes through `runners.yaml` labels, and each node to its cluster through the existing `RunnerInventory.cluster_for`. It is computed inside `live_families`, which already generates every family, so nothing is generated twice; this adds about 12 ms of a 7.5 s planner step. All 210 live families resolve today.
- **`choose` and `select`:** a candidate needs **all** of its target clusters eligible (same rule as before). The clusters are written onto each candidate in `candidates.json`.
- **Fail closed:** a family whose runner maps to no cluster is skipped with `::warning::Klaud live-family-clusters-unresolved: <family>`.
- **Review:** `clusters` is removed from `CandidateReview`, its validators, the review schema and the review prompt. `capacity.json` is no longer written for the agent, and the now-unused `capacity_context` is removed, so the review agent no longer sees any private scheduler data.

One behavior change: a family on the generic `h100` label now targets exactly the clusters that label's runners belong to (today only `h100-cw`). The old prefix guess would have treated free capacity on `h100-dsxe` as enough.

Tests: a `choose` test (generic label spanning two clusters, an exact `cluster:` label, an unmapped runner) and a two-case `select` test; existing `select` and `live_families` tests are updated to the new shapes. Each of 11 mutations fails at least one test.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

此前规划器的重叠审查 Agent 需要根据 `runners.yaml` 自行推断每个候选的目标集群并返回 `clusters`，`select` 再据此做容量检查；审查之前，`choose()` 还会按名称前缀猜测集群属于哪种硬件（`cluster == hardware or cluster.startswith(hardware + "-")`）来预筛候选。两者现在都改为确定性计算。

- **`target_clusters(entries, inventory)`：** 返回配置族生成的矩阵行可运行的全部集群。每行的 `runner` 标签通过 `runners.yaml` 标签解析为节点，再通过现有的 `RunnerInventory.cluster_for` 解析为集群。它在本就会生成所有配置族的 `live_families` 中计算，不会重复生成；在 7.5 秒的规划步骤中约增加 12 毫秒。目前全部 210 个配置族都能解析。
- **`choose` 与 `select`：** 候选需要其**全部**目标集群满足容量条件（规则与之前相同）。集群会写入 `candidates.json` 中的每个候选。
- **失败即关闭：** runner 无法映射到任何集群的配置族会被跳过，并输出 `::warning::Klaud live-family-clusters-unresolved: <family>`。
- **审查：** `clusters` 从 `CandidateReview`、其校验、审查 schema 和审查提示词中移除；不再为 Agent 写入 `capacity.json`，并删除不再使用的 `capacity_context`，审查 Agent 不再接触任何私有调度数据。

一个行为变化：使用通用 `h100` 标签的配置族，其目标现在恰好是该标签的 runner 所属的集群（目前只有 `h100-cw`）；旧的前缀猜测会把 `h100-dsxe` 的空闲容量也算作满足条件。

测试：新增一个 `choose` 测试（跨两个集群的通用标签、精确的 `cluster:` 标签、无法映射的 runner）和一个含两个用例的 `select` 测试，并更新了现有的 `select` 与 `live_families` 测试。11 种变异各自至少使一个测试失败。

</details>

<details>
<summary>AI model disclosure</summary>

Prepared with `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`. A delegated `worker` agent of the same model made the change and its tests; the main agent reviewed the diff and drafted this description.

</details>

title: perf: reuse compact dispatch sort permutations for cached handles
body:
Compact deterministic dispatch sorts the received rows by source index on every call. For a cached dispatch the handle already fixes that order: the same slots are refilled, the receive counts are the same, and `topk_idx` is asserted immutable. This stores the permutation on the handle next to `cached_recv_src_metadata_before_sort` at the first dispatch and reuses it, so cached compact dispatch no longer builds the sort keys, masks the unused capacity, or sorts.

The stored permutation follows the same stream and lifetime rules as the handle's existing cached metadata, so no per-call checks are needed and the reuse also holds under CUDA Graph capture and for deferred epilogues waited on another stream. Each handle keeps one extra int64 tensor of capacity rows (128 KiB at 16k rows). No API, default, native or test-file changes; `tests/ep/test_ep.py` already compares repeated cached dispatch against the reference, and the EP8 suite passes on this branch with CPU counts (direct and deferred epilogues) and in the sync-free mode.

Measured on 8×H200 (PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132), one cached dispatch per rank, 2048 tokens/rank, hidden 4096, top-2, BF16, deterministic, `do_cpu_sync=False`, under both `EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM` policies; outputs (payload, `topk_idx`, weights, source index) are bitwise identical to main across 608 fresh/cached/deferred/graph cases per policy:

| Per cached dispatch | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Device kernels and memsets | 24 | 6 |
| Host enqueue time | 328 µs | 129 µs |
| Synchronized wall time, 8-rank max | 439 µs | 280 µs |
| Kernels in a captured cached dispatch | 15 (incl. sort) | 6 |

The removed kernels (radix sort, `arange`, compare, `clone`, `masked_fill`, memsets) account for about 46 µs of device time per call; the wall-time reduction is mostly host overhead and is a component measurement, not a training-throughput claim. Independent of #786, which removes the unused sorts of the expanded layout; both touch `deterministic_sort` and the later one needs a trivial rebase.

Architecture: 4 TC WGs (512) + 1 Epi WG (128) + 1 TMA WG (128) = 768 threads.
TC does dual-bank WGMMA (N=64 split, warpgroup_wait<1> overlap) +
partial reduce → STS to epi_buf in SMEM. Epi does LDS → horizontal
sum → STG to global. TMA is unchanged.

- TC@104 regs (0 spill): full weights[32] preload with scale_kv
  deferred to between empty_epi wait and warpgroup_wait<1>
- kNumEpiStages=3 matching kNumKVStages to prevent inter-WG
  pipeline desynchronization
- epi_buf stride = BLOCK_Q*4+1 (17) for bank conflict reduction
- Bootstrap guard uses (num_total_kv_blocks | kv_block_idx) != 0
  instead of a persistent boolean to save 1 register

- 12-parameter template with kNumEpiStages=3
- SMEM includes epi_buf (3 stages × BLOCK_KV × stride × sizeof(float))
- Thread count: num_math_threads + num_epi_threads + num_tma_threads

  Speedup vs production: mean 1.065x, min 1.027x, max 1.111x
  Regressions: 0 out of 342
  Correctness: 295/295 full test configs pass

title: [Fix] Bound cuBLASLt descriptor lifetime on errors
body:
## Summary

Replaced the five cuBLASLt descriptor allocations in the shared GEMM path with caller-owned opaque descriptors initialized through the native `*Init` APIs. The layouts live in the calling scope, and the operation descriptor and preference live through heuristic selection and matmul enqueue.

The current `Create` sequence leaves its corresponding `Destroy` calls at the end of the function. A heuristic or matmul error throws through the existing error macros and exits before those calls. Stack-owned descriptors give the success and exception paths the same bounded lifetime.

The native matmul initializer also sets the scalar type, so the shared path now omits the duplicate `SCALE_TYPE` attribute call. The algorithm selection, per-stream workspace, matrix attributes, scaling pointers, and public interfaces retain their existing behavior. NVIDIA TransformerEngine uses the same native descriptor ownership pattern in its [grouped GEMM implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/9c33764bd9fd88cb4984ef2b60e9f0623055d3b2/transformer_engine/common/gemm/cublaslt_grouped_gemm.cu#L1067-L1118).

## Reproduction

A public `cublaslt_gemm_nt` call with two CUDA FP64 `[16, 16]` inputs and an FP32 `[16, 16]` output reaches heuristic selection and returns `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`. Repeating this rejected call retains the allocated descriptors on the current default branch.

Measured glibc `mallinfo2().uordblks` in separate baseline and candidate processes after 128 warmup rejections. Each checkpoint runs garbage collection and `malloc_trim(0)`; inputs remain allocated throughout. The baseline is `78b69000794d0937b47ae3387eff7663410264d1`.

| 20,000 rejected calls | Baseline native allocation growth | Candidate native allocation growth |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unsupported dtype at cuBLASLt heuristic selection | 11,840,144 bytes | 144 bytes |
| Invalid output shape at the public input boundary | 256 bytes | 256 bytes |

The unsupported-dtype candidate measurement was repeated at `7d53ec4`; the invalid-output-shape control was measured at `0677683`. The baseline grows by approximately 592 bytes per cuBLASLt rejection. The candidate at `7d53ec4` has a stable native allocation total from 1,000 through 20,000 rejected calls. Both versions preserve the rejection and complete a subsequent valid BF16 GEMM with zero maximum absolute error. At `ad60716`, a fresh candidate process again retained a constant native allocation total from 1,000 through 20,000 rejected calls (147,976,064 bytes), followed by a valid BF16 GEMM with zero maximum absolute error.

## Validation

Rechecked current main `057ca596` on October 8; head `ad60716` already includes that release and remains unchanged. The current diff retains the release's output dtype, alpha scaling, and accumulation handling. A fresh native build passed all six existing test functions with their complete internal shape matrices and original tolerances (6 passed, 1,523.68 seconds):

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/test_bf16.py::test_cublaslt_gemm \
  tests/test_bf16.py::test_cublaslt_batched_syrk \
  tests/test_bf16.py::test_cublaslt_batched_symm \
  tests/test_einsum.py::test_bhr_hdr_bhd \
  tests/test_einsum.py::test_bhd_hdr_bhr \
  tests/test_einsum.py::test_bhd_bhr_hdr
```

These exercise matrix orientations, padded and strided layouts, BF16 and FP32 outputs, alpha scaling, and accumulation. At `ad60716`, a separate two-stream check uses distinct BF16 inputs and FP32 accumulators with non-aliased outputs. It validates finite reference-matching results after 64 interleaved eager rounds and after 64 CUDA graph replays; both stages pass with `calc_diff` below `1.2e-13` on each stream.

At `0677683`, four paired baseline and candidate workloads passed numerical checks in eager execution and CUDA graph replay: padded-weight `bhr,hdr->bhd` at `B=4, H=128, R=512, D=128`, batched SYRK and SYMM at `batch=16, M=576, K=5120`, and an FP32-output BF16 GEMM at `M=4, N=64, K=7168`. The measurements use the library's default heuristic cache. Host-call wall times varied across rounds.

Hardware: H200 (driver reports NVIDIA L20X), PyTorch-reported compute capability 9.0, driver `570.172.08`. The separate driver capability query reports 8.9. PyTorch `2.12.0.dev20260408+cu128`, CUDA toolkit `12.9.86`, loaded cuBLASLt `12.8.4` (`cublasLtGetVersion() == 120804`). The baseline native extension and the current candidate native extension both built successfully. The shared NVFP4 cuBLASLt wrapper compiled with the extension.

A separate same-process host probe compared descriptor initialization with the repeated scalar-type setter and with the initializer alone. Sixteen alternating rounds of 100,000 initializations gave median thread CPU times of 60.25 ns and 47.45 ns for FAST_TF32, and 60.50 ns and 47.29 ns for FP32. Public descriptor attributes matched for both compute types and all four transpose combinations. These numbers measure host descriptor initialization. 

Both native builds use the same `CPPFLAGS='-include cuda_fp8.h'` setting for the header dependency reported in #439. This PR leaves that separate fix with its existing author.


The timing comparison isolates host descriptor initialization; complete API and model-level performance remain unmeasured. SM100 received compile coverage for the shared wrapper; its runtime behavior requires additional hardware.

### October 19 mainline integration

Merged `1fc9c66975ee` into `99a334336cb1` through a normal merge, retaining the complete contribution.

The descriptor implementation is unchanged from the previous PR head. Source checks covered all six shared wrappers, the current epilogue dispatch, per-stream workspace ownership, and exception propagation; the contribution diff check passed. The earlier native build, numerical matrices, two-stream replay, and failure/recovery measurements retain their recorded revision and hardware coverage. CUDA compilation and SM90/SM100 runtime validation were not rerun for this merge.

Project CI: Please run the descriptor failure/recovery cases on the project SM90 and SM100 runtime lanes. The SM100 compilation and host descriptor timing results above retain their stated coverage.

title: github:deepseek-ai/DeepSpec:48 fetched implementation patch
body:
From b87f730bb5448b89dfd225ce5d8e3dc027c9bd9a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: whycoming <alwaysxd666@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 20:42:00 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] Add distribution-exactness tests for speculative rejection
 sampling

Statistical and deterministic tests for the lossless guarantee of
verify_draft_tokens and the sampling helpers: per-position committed
tokens match the target distribution (chi-square, any-seed thresholds),
a negative control proves the thresholds can actually reject, and
seed-matched regression tests pin the draft-side sampling distribution
to the verification-side distribution (issue #31) and the latter to an
independent float64 reference.

Refs #31
---
 tests/conftest.py                            |   7 +
 tests/test_speculative_sampling_exactness.py | 426 +++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 433 insertions(+)
 create mode 100644 tests/conftest.py
 create mode 100644 tests/test_speculative_sampling_exactness.py

diff --git a/tests/conftest.py b/tests/conftest.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..5645053e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/conftest.py
@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+# The repo has no packaging (no pyproject.toml/setup.py), so put the repo
+# root on sys.path to keep ``deepspec`` importable under a bare ``pytest``
+# from any cwd. Remove once packaging or a root conftest lands.
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
diff --git a/tests/test_speculative_sampling_exactness.py b/tests/test_speculative_sampling_exactness.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..c1415e36
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_speculative_sampling_exactness.py
@@ -0,0 +1,426 @@
+"""Distribution-exactness tests for speculative rejection sampling.
+
+Covers the lossless guarantee of ``verify_draft_tokens`` and the sampling
+helpers: committed tokens must follow the target model's distribution at
+every position, for any declared draft distribution. A negative control
+proves the chi-square thresholds can actually reject (the bug class of
+issue #31), and deterministic regression tests pin the draft-side sampling
+distribution to the verification-side distribution and the latter to an
+independent float64 reference.
+
+All tests are CPU-only. Statistical thresholds are chosen so the suite
+passes for any RNG stream (per-assert false-fail rate ~1e-9, asymptotic
+chi-square tail); the fixed seed only makes failures reproducible. Tests
+that need ``deepspec.eval.base_evaluator`` skip cleanly in environments
+without transformers installed.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from deepspec.utils.sampling import (
+    logits_to_probs,
+    sample_from_probs,
+    sample_residual,
+    sample_tokens,
+)
+
+_SEED = 20260702
+_VOCAB = 4
+_DRAFT_LEN = 2
+_TRIALS = 20_000
+_CONTROL_TRIALS = 10_000
+_TEMPERATURE = 0.7
+
+# Chi-square critical values for df = _VOCAB - 1 = 3, from the closed-form
+# survival function S(x) = erfc(sqrt(x/2)) + sqrt(2x/pi) * exp(-x/2)
+# (no scipy dependency): S(44.8413) = 1.0e-9 and S(64.0) = 8.2e-14.
+# 44.8413 bounds each positive assert's false-fail rate at ~1e-9 for any
+# seed; 64.0 is the floor the negative control must clear (its analytic
+# non-centrality is ~356 at _CONTROL_TRIALS, so its expected chi-square is
+# ~359, more than 7 standard deviations above the floor).
+_CRIT_1E9 = 44.8413
+_NEGATIVE_FLOOR = 64.0
+
+# Target logits for three verification positions, and the draft
+# distributions the tests declare. Reference target distributions are
+# recomputed with float64 softmax, independent of deepspec code, so a bug
+# in logits_to_probs cannot move the reference the tests compare against.
+_TARGET_LOGITS = [
+    [1.2, 0.4, -0.3, -0.9],
+    [0.1, 1.0, -0.5, 0.3],
+    [-0.2, 0.6, 0.9, -0.4],
+]
+_DRAFT_PROBS = [
+    [0.40, 0.30, 0.20, 0.10],
+    [0.25, 0.35, 0.15, 0.25],
+]
+# Deliberately mismatched proposal distribution for the negative control.
+_MISMATCHED_PROBS = [0.55, 0.22, 0.13, 0.10]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def evaluator_mod():
+    """Import the evaluator module, skipping when transformers is absent.
+
+    ``deepspec/eval/__init__.py`` imports the full modeling stack, which
+    needs the pinned transformers from requirements.txt; environments
+    without it skip these tests instead of failing at collection time.
+    """
+    return pytest.importorskip(
+        "deepspec.eval.base_evaluator",
+        reason="needs the pinned transformers from requirements.txt",
+    )
+
+
+def _reference_target_probs() -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Float64 softmax of the target logits, independent of deepspec."""
+    logits = torch.tensor(_TARGET_LOGITS, dtype=torch.float64)
+    return torch.softmax(logits / _TEMPERATURE, dim=-1)
+
+
+def _chi_square(counts: torch.Tensor, probs: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    expected = probs.to(torch.float64) * counts.sum()
+    observed = counts.to(torch.float64)
+    return float(((observed - expected) ** 2 / expected).sum())
+
+
+def _mismatch_noncentrality() -> float:
+    """Analytic chi-square non-centrality of the negative control.
+
+    Closed form of the committed-token law when proposals come from ``r``
+    but ``q`` is declared: committed(x) = r(x) * min(1, p(x) / q(x)) +
+    P(reject) * residual(x). Guards the control's power against future
+    edits to the probability vectors; the control's pass criterion itself
+    never uses this model, so the two cannot be wrong together.
+    """
+    p = _reference_target_probs()[0]
+    q = torch.tensor(_DRAFT_PROBS, dtype=torch.float64)[0]
+    r = torch.tensor(_MISMATCHED_PROBS, dtype=torch.float64)
+    accept = torch.minimum(torch.ones_like(p), p / q)
+    reject_mass = 1.0 - (r * accept).sum()
+    residual = torch.clamp(p - q, min=0.0)
+    residual = residual / residual.sum()
+    committed = r * accept + reject_mass * residual
+    return float(_CONTROL_TRIALS * ((committed - p) ** 2 / p).sum())
+
+
+def _make_fake_target(logits_rows: list[list[float]]):
+    """A stand-in target model returning fixed rank-3 float32 logits.
+
+    ``seen`` records the keyword arguments of the most recent call so
+    tests can check what verification actually passed to the target.
+    """
+    full = torch.tensor(logits_rows, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(0)
+    seen: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
+
+    def fake_target(
+        input_ids=None,
+        position_ids=None,
+        past_key_values=None,
+        use_cache=True,
+        output_hidden_states=True,
+    ):
+        seen["input_ids"] = input_ids
+        seen["position_ids"] = position_ids
+        length = input_ids.shape[1]
+        return SimpleNamespace(logits=full[:, :length, :].clone())
+
+    return fake_target, seen
+
+
+def _run_verify_once(
+    evaluator_mod,
+    *,
+    fake_target,
+    verify_input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    draft_probs: torch.Tensor | None,
+    draft_token_count: int,
+    temperature: float = _TEMPERATURE,
+    stop_token_ids: list[int] | None = None,
+):
+    """Single verification round; the only verify_draft_tokens call site."""
+    proposal = evaluator_mod.DraftProposal(
+        draft_token_count=draft_token_count,
+        verify_input_ids=verify_input_ids,
+        draft_probs=draft_probs,
+    )
+    return evaluator_mod.verify_draft_tokens(
+        target_model=fake_target,
+        proposal=proposal,
+        position_ids=torch.arange(_DRAFT_LEN + 1).unsqueeze(0),
+        start=0,
+        past_key_values_target=evaluator_mod.DynamicCache(),
+        temperature=temperature,
+        max_proposal_tokens=_DRAFT_LEN,
+        current_token_ids=verify_input_ids[:, :1],
+        stop_token_ids=stop_token_ids,
+    )
+
+
+def _committed_histograms(
+    evaluator_mod,
+    *,
+    proposal_dist: torch.Tensor,
+    declared_dist: torch.Tensor,
+    trials: int,
+    seed: int,
+):
+    """Histogram committed tokens per position over ``trials`` rounds.
+
+    Proposals are drawn from ``proposal_dist`` while ``declared_dist`` is
+    passed as draft_probs; the two match in the honest tests and differ in
+    the negative control. stop_token_ids stays None here: after a
+    stop-token truncation, committed_tokens carries a trailing correction
+    token that is not distribution-guaranteed (the decode loop discards
+    it), so stop handling gets deterministic coverage instead.
+    """
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    fake_target, _ = _make_fake_target(_TARGET_LOGITS)
+    declared = declared_dist.to(torch.float32).unsqueeze(0)
+    proposals = torch.stack(
+        [
+            torch.multinomial(
+                proposal_dist[pos].to(torch.float32), trials, replacement=True
+            )
+            for pos in range(_DRAFT_LEN)
+        ],
+        dim=1,
+    )
+    counts = torch.zeros(_DRAFT_LEN + 1, _VOCAB)
+    reached = torch.zeros(_DRAFT_LEN + 1)
+    current = torch.tensor([[3]])
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        for i in range(trials):
+            result = _run_verify_once(
+                evaluator_mod,
+                fake_target=fake_target,
+                verify_input_ids=torch.cat([current, proposals[i : i + 1]], dim=1),
+                draft_probs=declared,
+                draft_token_count=_DRAFT_LEN,
+            )
+            committed = result.committed_tokens[0]
+            for pos in range(committed.shape[0]):
+                counts[pos, committed[pos]] += 1
+                reached[pos] += 1
+    return counts, reached
+
+
+def test_committed_tokens_match_target_distribution(evaluator_mod):
+    """Lossless guarantee: with proposals drawn from the declared
+    draft_probs, the committed token at every position follows the target
+    distribution even though the draft distribution is deliberately
+    different from the target's."""
+    declared = torch.tensor(_DRAFT_PROBS, dtype=torch.float32)
+    counts, reached = _committed_histograms(
+        evaluator_mod,
+        proposal_dist=declared,
+        declared_dist=declared,
+        trials=_TRIALS,
+        seed=_SEED,
+    )
+    reference = _reference_target_probs()
+    assert int(reached[1]) > 1_000 and int(reached[2]) > 1_000, (
+        f"acceptance collapsed: reached={reached.tolist()} out of {_TRIALS} "
+        f"trials (seed={_SEED})"
+    )
+    for pos in range(_DRAFT_LEN + 1):
+        stat = _chi_square(counts[pos], reference[pos])
+        expected = [round(x, 1) for x in (reference[pos] * reached[pos]).tolist()]
+        assert stat < _CRIT_1E9, (
+            f"position {pos}: chi2={stat:.2f} exceeds {_CRIT_1E9} "
+            f"(false-fail rate 1e-9), n={int(reached[pos])}, seed={_SEED}, "
+            f"observed={counts[pos].tolist()}, expected={expected}"
+        )
+
+
+def test_chi_square_rejects_mismatched_proposals(evaluator_mod):
+    """Negative control: proposals drawn from a distribution other than
+    the declared draft_probs must blow past the rejection floor. This is
+    the bug class of issue #31 and proves the positive thresholds have
+    power (a distribution test that has never rejected proves nothing)."""
+    noncentrality = _mismatch_noncentrality()
+    assert noncentrality > 300, (
+        f"mismatch too weak to prove power: non-centrality={noncentrality:.0f}"
+    )
+    declared = torch.tensor(_DRAFT_PROBS, dtype=torch.float32)
+    mismatched = declared.clone()
+    mismatched[0] = torch.tensor(_MISMATCHED_PROBS)
+    counts, _ = _committed_histograms(
+        evaluator_mod,
+        proposal_dist=mismatched,
+        declared_dist=declared,
+        trials=_CONTROL_TRIALS,
+        seed=_SEED,
+    )
+    stat = _chi_square(counts[0], _reference_target_probs()[0])
+    assert stat > _NEGATIVE_FLOOR, (
+        f"mismatched proposals not detected: chi2={stat:.2f} is below "
+        f"{_NEGATIVE_FLOOR} (expected ~{3 + noncentrality:.0f}, seed={_SEED})"
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.xfail(
+    strict=True,
+    reason="issue #31: sample_tokens samples from the native-dtype softmax "
+    "while verification uses the float32 distribution from logits_to_probs; "
+    "delete this marker when the fix lands",
+)
+def test_sample_tokens_matches_verification_distribution():
+    """Seed-matched equivalence: drawing tokens via sample_tokens must be
+    bitwise-indistinguishable from sampling the distribution rejection
+    sampling assumes (logits_to_probs). Both paths make exactly one
+    torch.multinomial call whose internal noise inherits the probs dtype,
+    so equality requires the same probability values in the same dtype:
+    the float32 verification pipeline. The current bug compounds the
+    softmax dtype gap with multinomial's dtype-dependent noise for a
+    ~1e-3 mismatch rate over 100k draws, so this xfail is deterministic
+    for any seed and strict=True is safe: fixing #31 turns this into a
+    hard reminder to remove the marker and arm the regression guard."""
+    draws = 100_000
+    logits = (
+        torch.tensor([2.5, 1.25, -0.6, 0.4], dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        .view(1, 1, _VOCAB)
+        .expand(1, draws, _VOCAB)
+    )
+    torch.manual_seed(_SEED)
+    via_sample_tokens = sample_tokens(logits, temperature=_TEMPERATURE)
+    torch.manual_seed(_SEED)
+    via_verify_dist = sample_from_probs(logits_to_probs(logits, _TEMPERATURE))
+    mismatches = int((via_sample_tokens != via_verify_dist).sum())
+    assert mismatches == 0, (
+        f"{mismatches}/{draws} draft tokens were drawn from a different "
+        f"distribution than rejection sampling assumes (seed={_SEED})"
+    )
+
+
+def test_logits_to_probs_matches_float64_reference():
+    """The verification-side distribution must be computed in full
+    precision from reduced-precision logits: softmax of bfloat16 logits
+    must match an independent float64 reference within 1e-5, far tighter
+    than bfloat16 arithmetic (~1e-3) could achieve."""
+    torch.manual_seed(_SEED)
+    for scale in (1.0, 8.0, 32.0):
+        logits = (torch.randn(2, 5, _VOCAB) * scale).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        got = logits_to_probs(logits, _TEMPERATURE)
+        want = torch.softmax(logits.to(torch.float64) / _TEMPERATURE, dim=-1)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(got.to(torch.float64), want, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5)
+
+
+def test_greedy_verification_commits_argmax_chain(evaluator_mod):
+    """temperature < 1e-5 turns verification deterministic: a draft that
+    matches the target argmax chain is fully accepted and extended with
+    the argmax bonus token; a mismatching first token is rejected and
+    corrected to the argmax."""
+    fake_target, seen = _make_fake_target(_TARGET_LOGITS)
+    argmax_chain = [int(torch.tensor(row).argmax()) for row in _TARGET_LOGITS]
+    uniform = torch.full((1, _DRAFT_LEN, _VOCAB), 1.0 / _VOCAB)
+    current = torch.tensor([[3]])
+
+    matched = torch.tensor([argmax_chain[:_DRAFT_LEN]])
+    result = _run_verify_once(
+        evaluator_mod,
+        fake_target=fake_target,
+        verify_input_ids=torch.cat([current, matched], dim=1),
+        draft_probs=uniform,
+        draft_token_count=_DRAFT_LEN,
+        temperature=0.0,
+    )
+    assert result.accepted_draft_tokens == _DRAFT_LEN
+    assert result.committed_tokens[0].tolist() == argmax_chain
+    assert seen["position_ids"].tolist() == [[0, 1, 2]]
+    expected_input = torch.cat([current, matched], dim=1)
+    assert seen["input_ids"].tolist() == expected_input.tolist()
+
+    wrong_first = matched.clone()
+    wrong_first[0, 0] = (argmax_chain[0] + 1) % _VOCAB
+    result = _run_verify_once(
+        evaluator_mod,
+        fake_target=fake_target,
+        verify_input_ids=torch.cat([current, wrong_first], dim=1),
+        draft_probs=uniform,
+        draft_token_count=_DRAFT_LEN,
+        temperature=0.0,
+    )
+    assert result.accepted_draft_tokens == 0
+    assert result.committed_tokens[0].tolist() == argmax_chain[:1]
+
+
+def test_greedy_stop_token_truncates_acceptance(evaluator_mod):
+    """A stop token inside the accepted prefix truncates acceptance to the
+    stop position and flags termination. Deterministic (greedy) coverage
+    only: the trailing correction token in committed_tokens after a stop
+    truncation is not distribution-guaranteed and the decode loop discards
+    it, so no distributional assert belongs here."""
+    fake_target, _ = _make_fake_target(_TARGET_LOGITS)
+    argmax_chain = [int(torch.tensor(row).argmax()) for row in _TARGET_LOGITS]
+    uniform = torch.full((1, _DRAFT_LEN, _VOCAB), 1.0 / _VOCAB)
+    current = torch.tensor([[3]])
+    matched = torch.tensor([argmax_chain[:_DRAFT_LEN]])
+    result = _run_verify_once(
+        evaluator_mod,
+        fake_target=fake_target,
+        verify_input_ids=torch.cat([current, matched], dim=1),
+        draft_probs=uniform,
+        draft_token_count=_DRAFT_LEN,
+        temperature=0.0,
+        stop_token_ids=[argmax_chain[0]],
+    )
+    assert result.terminated_by_stop_token is True
+    assert result.accepted_draft_tokens == 1
+    assert result.effective_proposal_length == 1
+    assert result.committed_tokens[0, 0].item() == argmax_chain[0]
+
+
+def test_sample_residual_near_zero_mass_falls_back():
+    """sample_residual must fall back to sampling the target distribution
+    when the residual mass is zero (target == draft) or positive but under
+    the 1e-8 threshold. A one-hot target makes the fallback deterministic;
+    seed-matching pins it to the target distribution rather than any
+    degenerate renormalization of the tiny residual."""
+    one_hot = torch.tensor([[1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
+    token = sample_residual(one_hot, one_hot.clone())
+    assert token.tolist() == [0]
+
+    target = torch.tensor([[0.5, 0.3, 0.15, 0.05]])
+    torch.manual_seed(_SEED)
+    expect = sample_from_probs(target.unsqueeze(1)).squeeze(1)
+    torch.manual_seed(_SEED)
+    got = sample_residual(target, target.clone())
+    assert torch.equal(got, expect)
+
+    # One float32 ulp on the 0.05 entry (~3.7e-9) keeps the residual mass
+    # positive but under the 1e-8 threshold; smaller perturbations (e.g.
+    # +5e-9 on 0.5) round away entirely in float32.
+    nearly = target.clone()
+    nearly[0, 3] = torch.nextafter(nearly[0, 3], torch.tensor(1.0))
+    assert not torch.equal(nearly, target)
+    torch.manual_seed(_SEED)
+    expect = sample_from_probs(nearly.unsqueeze(1)).squeeze(1)
+    torch.manual_seed(_SEED)
+    got = sample_residual(nearly, target)
+    assert torch.equal(got, expect)
+
+
+def test_zero_draft_proposal_commits_one_token(evaluator_mod):
+    """draft_token_count=0 (no speculation): verification must still
+    commit exactly one token without needing draft_probs; under greedy
+    decoding that token is deterministically the target argmax."""
+    fake_target, _ = _make_fake_target(_TARGET_LOGITS)
+    current = torch.tensor([[3]])
+    result = _run_verify_once(
+        evaluator_mod,
+        fake_target=fake_target,
+        verify_input_ids=current,
+        draft_probs=None,
+        draft_token_count=0,
+        temperature=0.0,
+    )
+    assert result.accepted_draft_tokens == 0
+    assert result.committed_tokens.shape == (1, 1)
+    argmax_first = int(torch.tensor(_TARGET_LOGITS[0]).argmax())
+    assert result.committed_tokens[0, 0].item() == argmax_first

title: V4.1 Flash: user-supplied special-token literals produce different token counts from the official API
body:
## Description

I found a discrepancy between `DeepseekV41Encoding` and the official V4.1 Flash API when user message content contains literal special-token strings such as `<｜User｜>` or `<think>`.

The recipe recognizes these literals as single AddedTokens. However, the official API reports a larger `prompt_tokens` increase, consistent with ordinary BPE encoding for the individual literals tested.

## Environment

- Test date: September 11, 2026
- Official endpoint: `https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions`
- Model: `deepseek-flash` (V4.1 Flash)
- Python package: `deepseek-recipe==0.1.1`
- Repository inspected at commit: `8cadfede7063c896b944e7bae05daa3549ae97ea`
- Bundled tokenizer: `static/tokenizers/v41/tokenizer.json`

## Observed results

Each request contains one user message, with:

```json
{
  "thinking": {"type": "disabled"},
  "max_tokens": 1,
  "temperature": 0,
  "stream": false
}
```

The counts below include the conversation template:

| User content | Recipe token count | Official API `prompt_tokens` | API increase over empty content |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Empty string | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| `x` | 5 | 5 | 1 |
| `<｜User｜>` | 5 | 9 | **5** |
| `<｜Assistant｜>` | 5 | 9 | **5** |
| `<｜System｜>` | 5 | 9 | **5** |
| `<think>` | 5 | 7 | **3** |
| `</think>` | 5 | 7 | **3** |
| `｜DSML｜` | 5 | 8 | **4** |
| `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` | 5 | 16 | **12** |
| `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` | 5 | 16 | **12** |

For example, the recipe encodes the user-supplied `<｜User｜>` as `[128803]`. Encoding the same text with the bundled tokenizer’s `added_tokens` table cleared produces `[30, 28217, 6756, 28217, 32]`, matching the API’s five-token increase.

The discrepancy also occurs with default thinking settings: empty content produces 30 prompt tokens, while `<｜User｜>` produces 35.

## Minimal reproduction

Run from the repository root with `deepseek-recipe==0.1.1` installed and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` set:

```python
import json
import os
import urllib.request

from deepseek_recipe import (
    ChatCompletionRequest,
    ConversionOptions,
    DeepseekV41Encoding,
    Tokenizer,
)

encoding = DeepseekV41Encoding().with_tokenizer(
    Tokenizer.from_file("static/tokenizers/v41/tokenizer.json")
)

for content in ["", "x", "<｜User｜>", "<think>", "｜DSML｜"]:
    body = {
        "model": "deepseek-flash",
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
        "thinking": {"type": "disabled"},
        "max_tokens": 1,
        "temperature": 0,
        "stream": False,
    }

    converted = ChatCompletionRequest(body).convert(ConversionOptions())
    local_count = len(encoding.encode(converted.conversation))

    request = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions",
        data=json.dumps(body, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={
            "Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"],
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
        result = json.load(response)

    print(repr(content), local_count, result["usage"]["prompt_tokens"])
```

Observed counts:

```text
Content          Recipe   Official API
''               4        4
'x'              5        5
'<｜User｜>'      5        9
'<think>'        5        7
'｜DSML｜'       5        8
```

## Possible explanation

The current [tokenizer implementation](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe/blob/8cadfede7063c896b944e7bae05daa3549ae97ea/deepseek-recipe-encoding/src/tokenizer.rs) calls `encode(text, false)` on the rendered prompt. This still recognizes AddedToken literals, without distinguishing user content from template-generated control tokens.

## Scope and an additional edge case

The API observations above are based on usage counts. The API does not expose input token IDs, so these observations do not establish the exact server-side encoding algorithm.

There is also an edge case with adjacent DSML literals:

| User content | Recipe token count | Official API `prompt_tokens` | Ordinary BPE content + template |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `｜DSML｜` repeated 8 times without separators | 12 | 21 | 36 |

The API result was reproduced. Therefore, simply clearing `added_tokens` is not yet established as a complete fix.

## Expected behavior / clarification

Could you clarify the intended handling of special-token literals in user content?

Should the recipe distinguish them from template-generated control tokens, or is an additional preprocessing step required to match the official API?

title: feat(gdn): accept_paths for tree commits; tracked commits on the tcgen05 fold
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds an optional `accept_paths: int32 [B, T]` argument to `gated_delta_rule_replayssm_commit`, so the ReplaySSM commit can fold a root-to-node path through a draft tree instead of only a contiguous prefix. This is the commit half of tree-structured speculative decoding for GDN; #6155 is the verify half. The two are independent kernels and merge in either order, but an engine needs both to run a tree.

Tree speculative decoding (EAGLE-2/3 with `topk > 1`) accepts a path through the draft that in general is not a prefix: with three draft tokens a request may accept `{0, 2}` and reject the sibling at row 1. `accept_lens` is a count and cannot express that, and the commit kernel replays rows `0..n-1` by loop counter, so the rejected row reaches the checkpoint. That is measured, not inferred: poisoning row 1 with NaN and asking for three accepted tokens NaNs 100% of the committed state on `main`.

The recurrence is path-agnostic. Both folds build the Gram matrix and the coefficient recurrence over staged positions, not cache rows, so an ordered path keeps the strictly-triangular structure and only the load index moves. The change is four load sites in the SIMT fold and three in the tcgen05 fold. `accept_paths=None` compiles a `HAS_PATHS=False` variant with no gather, which is bitwise identical to the kernel before this PR, so chain decoding pays nothing. `accept_lens` is retained as that chain fast path, and `row j` of request `i` is read only when `j < accept_lens[i]`.

Out-of-range rows are clamped into `[0, T)` rather than rejected, because checking values on the host would need a device synchronization. `track_steps` needs no change: it already counts positions along the accepted sequence, which is what a path replays. The fp64 reference in `flashinfer/trace/templates/gdn.py` gains the same argument.

Second commit: tracked commits run on the tcgen05 fold. Until now any commit with `track_state_indices` fell back to the FP32 SIMT fold, and SGLang's `extra_buffer` mamba radix strategy passes track tensors on every commit, so in practice every commit under that strategy took the slower kernel, 20 to 25 percent slower at the shapes the all-layer commit runs at. The SIMT fold gains a `TRACK_ONLY` constexpr: a row with a live track slot and an in-range step replays only up to that step and writes only the track slot, every other CTA exits at the top. When tracking is requested the dispatcher runs that pass first, against the untouched checkpoint, then the tcgen05 fold commits the live slots as before; the ordering is what makes it correct. Below B x HV of about 256 the extra launch costs more than it saves, so `backend="auto"` keeps SIMT for tracked commits there; explicit `tcgen05` always takes the new path.

All 36 layers in one launch on B200, CUDA-graph timed, in microseconds:

| B | HV | slots | old tracked commit (SIMT) | new tracked commit (snapshot pass + tcgen05 fold) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13 | 32 | 66 | 506 | 458 |
| 21 | 32 | 106 | 770 | 729 |
| 32 | 32 | 106 | 1281 | 1115 |
| 64 | 8 | 1036 | 613 | 569 |
| 32 | 8 | 1036 | 297 | 290 |
| 8 | 8 | 1036 | 68 | 80 |

Stacked on #6229, which touches the same validation block. The diff here is two commits on top of it. #6496 (Int64 slot offsets in the same fold files) is independent and should land first; whichever of the two merges second needs a trivial rebase.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Builds on #5314. Commit-side companion to #6155. Stacked on #6229. Touches the same files as #6496.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

All in `tests/gdn/test_replayssm_spec_fold.py`, run on a B200 (SM100):

- `test_replayssm_commit_non_prefix_path[simt|tcgen05]`: the headline case. Verify a 4-token draft, NaN-poison rows 1 and 3, commit path `[0, 2]` with two accepted tokens, and require a finite result that matches an independent fp64 replay of exactly those rows.
- `test_replayssm_commit_path_cycles`: every accepted length from 0 to T for T in 3..8, on random non-prefix paths with a descending path in row 0, null slots, zero-length rows, and two layers, with every unread window row poisoned. Both backends; tracking on the SIMT backend.
- `test_replayssm_commit_identity_path_is_bitwise_identical`: the no-gather fast path and an explicit identity path agree with zero tolerance, on both backends.
- `test_replayssm_commit_path_cuda_graph`: verify plus path commit captured and replayed under CUDA graph.
- `test_replayssm_commit_path_validation`: dtype, shape, row count, strides, device and alignment are rejected before launch on all three backend values.
- `test_replayssm_commit_path_clamps_out_of_range_rows`: a row of 99 reads row 3, on both backends.
- The tcgen05 plus tracking cases of `test_replayssm_verify_commit_cycles` and `test_replayssm_commit_path_cycles` were skipped before and now run: every accepted length with tracked snapshots at in-range, out-of-range and null track slots against an fp64 reference, on both the identity and non-prefix paths. The validation case that asserted tracked tcgen05 must raise is removed.

Whole file on B200 with both commits: 270 passed, 15 skipped. The 72 new path cases contribute 63 passes and the 9 skips, which are the tcgen05 rules (T in 4..8, no tracking). `tests/trace/test_fi_trace.py` and `test_fi_trace_template_consistency.py` for the GDN and ReplaySSM templates pass, and the checked-in `gdn_replayssm_commit_k2_v8_d128.json` golden is regenerated so it carries the new reference source and the optional input.

## 🔬 Experimental Track

<!-- Only for PRs submitted under the experimental policy (CONTRIBUTING.md → "Experimental APIs and Backends").
     Leave this section untouched for normal PRs. -->

- [ ] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: #
  - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release.
  - [ ] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff).
  - [ ] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included.
  - [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)
  - [ ] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows.

<!-- Required for experimental PRs. Replace the commented lines below with your test targets. -->
```experimental-tests
# One target per line: a directory or a file. (A pytest ::selector is not
# supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under
# tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g.
#
#   tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py
#   tests/experimental/my_backend/
#
# Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every
# experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell.
```

## Reviewer Notes

Opening as a draft alongside #6155: nothing in SGLang or vLLM passes a path yet, and the acceptance representation should be agreed with SGLang's `accept_index` before the contract is locked. The `[B, T]` padded layout with `accept_lens` as the valid count was chosen to match how SGLang's EAGLE verify already emits accepted positions.

Rows are documented as distinct within a request but not checked, for the same device-sync reason as the range check. A repeated row replays the same token twice, which is a semantic error on the caller's side rather than a memory-safety one; every load stays within `[0, T)` after the clamp.

The "bitwise identical" claim for `accept_paths=None` was checked directly rather than by inspection: the four touched source files were reverted to the parent commit in a scratch copy, `gated_delta_rule_mtp` plus commit was run on both backends at T in {4, 6, 8} and B in {1, 5} with mixed accept lengths, and all twelve committed checkpoints are `torch.equal` to the ones produced by this branch. `HAS_PATHS` is part of both compile-cache keys and of the on-disk kernel name, so a chain caller never loads a tree variant.

For unaccepted staged positions the tcgen05 kernel fills `s_decay` and `s_beta` from the clamped padding row rather than from the rejected row. The only consumer of those positions is the coefficient loop, which is guarded by `step < n_commit`, and the corresponding key rows are zero, so the values are never used. The existing NaN-poison tests already prove that on the chain path; the path tests poison row 0, which is the padding row, and still pass.

An independent review pass ran before opening; its two findings, a missing non-ascending path case and an unmatched validation test, are folded in.

On the second commit: the tracked snapshot pass reads the checkpoint, so it must run before the fold; both launch on the caller's stream in that order. Its full grid exits early on untracked rows, which is where its fixed 35 to 80 microseconds comes from; a compacted grid over tracked rows would need a device-to-host count or an indirect launch and was not worth it at these sizes. Most of the commit-kernel diff is the SIMT launch moving into a nested helper so it can be invoked twice with different constexprs; the kernel body changes are the `TRACK_ONLY` gate on `is_live`, the loop bound, and the final store.

title: [cake deslop] Round 2 tracking: 49 family audits of Cake-generated code on main (2026-10-17)
body:
Second audit pass over every Cake-generated family on `main` @ 3184bbea6e41290320237fbda2ed87b05661881e (2026-10-17), after the 74 first-round sub-issues of #5768 (#5769–#5844) were closed by their PRs. Each family issue below lists what is still dispatch-unreachable, duplicated, per-arch-copied, shape-baked or host-heavy, with the dispatch code that proves it, the tests that pin it and the mechanical-first steps to remove it.

This tracker exists because #5768 reached GitHub's limit of 100 sub-issues per parent; the round-2 family issues are attached here, and this issue is attached to #5768. Work proceeds in the order below (largest expected reduction first); each mechanical step ships as its own PR gated on per-symbol SASS equivalence of the surviving kernels and the existing tests on the target GPUs.

title: [WIP][DSv4.1] Opt in to mHC coefficient overlap on SM90
body:
## Overview

Draft: add an experimental, explicit opt-in for DeepSeek-V4.1 mHC coefficient overlap on Hopper (SM90), reusing the stream path introduced by #57603. Hopper remains disabled by default; GPU validation is pending.

## Claims

- `KernelConfig.enable_mhc_overlap=None` preserves SM100 automatic selection; `True` additionally permits SM90, and `False` disables overlap.
- Existing DeepGEMM, shape, ubatching, FULL CUDA graph and small-batch restrictions remain. SM90 uses the ordinary TP collective and cannot select the SM100-only fused all-reduce.
- No speedup, numerical equivalence, model quality or production-readiness claim is made in this draft.

## Validation

CPU only, using this branch's Python source on Linux, Python 3.12.3 and pytest 9.1.1, in an isolated container with no GPU devices (2 CPU cores / 4 GiB). Installed dependencies were inherited from a vLLM v0.28.0 image; this was not a fresh main wheel build.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=void VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
  PYTHONPATH=$PWD PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/kernels/mhc -o addopts= \
  -q tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_dispatch.py
```

**14 passed**, covering opt-in/default/off selection, unsupported architectures, missing DeepGEMM, shape/ubatching fallback and exclusion of the SM100 collective. These mock capability checks validate dispatch only. Source-only version metadata and torch deprecation warnings were emitted.

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/kernel.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/mhc.py \
  tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_dispatch.py tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py
git diff --check
```

All applicable hooks pass, including mypy, config validation and Buildkite test tethering. The new dispatch tests are in the existing mHC suite. The replay test now permits SM90 but **has not been run on GPU**; the existing dedicated NVIDIA mHC CI job uses B200.

Before marking ready:

- [ ] Verify that the tested DeepGEMM dependency contains the SM90 register-lifetime repair tracked by deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#448 / #59129; this draft does not implement that fix.
- [ ] Run the mHC replay test and independent numerical references on Hopper, including stream ordering and repeated graph replay.
- [ ] Verify eager/piecewise/large-batch fallback, TP modes and an SM100 regression run.
- [ ] Run DeepSeek-V4.1 end-to-end model evaluation and matched baseline/opt-in serving measurements, including `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.
- [ ] Reassess the existing 16-token threshold on Hopper and complete human line-by-line review. Human review is not asserted.

## Details

The existing eligibility gate excludes SM90. This change makes Hopper experimental and opt-in via `--kernel-config '{"enable_mhc_overlap": true}'`; omitting it preserves defaults. This is a proposed serving configuration, not a GPU-validated launch recipe. The existing configuration hash includes the new field.

This reuses vLLM's TF32 prenorm coefficient path. It does **not** port the compensated-BF16 projection from sgl-project/sglang#41251. Kernel arithmetic, the existing stream schedule and the GB200-derived 16-token threshold are unchanged. The all-reduce architecture guard is needed because its caller can now also create an mHC stream on SM90.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-10-09 covered issue #57448 and open/closed PRs matching mHC, overlap, SM90 and Hopper. No equivalent Hopper coefficient-overlap PR was found: #57603 targets SM100; #59802 targets ROCm; #59129 packages the separate DeepGEMM correctness repair. This draft depends on confirming that repair rather than duplicating it.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for investigation, implementation, tests and this description. This is WIP awaiting GPU resources; model evaluations and performance results are not yet available.
