title: fix(precompiled-cache-rubin): Include missing MoE and FP8 dependencies in the SM107 precompiled cache
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re needed. -->

The SM107 precompiled-cache provider omits fused_moe_100, fp8_gemm_cutlass, and trtllm_utils, although their existing generators support SM107. Consequently, FlashInfer compiles these modules at runtime even when flashinfer-jit-cache-sm107a is installed.

  This affected vLLM’s DeepSeek FP8 GSM8K evaluation on Rubin: compiling fused_moe_100 took approximately 789 seconds, and subsequent initialization exceeded the test’s unchanged 1,200-second startup deadline.

  This change adds the missing AOT registrations. It does not change kernel implementations, runtime dispatch, or compiler-target generation.

  Why each condition changes

  • fused_moe_100: use has_sm100 or has_sm107 or has_sm110.
    The existing generator supports SM107 by emitting compatible SM100f code. Moving its registration into one shared condition adds SM107, preserves SM100 and SM110 support, and avoids duplicate registration when multiple targets are enabled. SM103 retains its separate fused MoE module.

  • Keep the original if has_sm100: block restricted to SM100.
    Simply adding or has_sm107 to that block would also register gen_fp4_quantization_sm100_module(), which explicitly builds SM100a code. SM107 already has its own quantization generator and registration. Broadening the block would additionally enable the FP4 GEMM module, which supports SM107 targeting but is
    outside this FP8 failure’s requirements and validation.

  • fp8_gemm_cutlass: use has_sm100 or has_sm103 or has_sm107.
    Moving this registration out of the larger SM100/SM103 block adds the missing FP8 dependency without enabling every other module in that block. Existing SM100/SM103 coverage is preserved, and the generator already maps SM107 to SM100f.

  • trtllm_utils: add has_sm107 to its existing condition.
    This module is another dependency required by the same evaluation. Its omission otherwise causes an additional runtime compilation.

## Validation

- 44 AOT registration tests passed, covering SM107, existing architectures, mixed targets, disabled build categories, and duplicate prevention.

- Confirmed modules load with JIT disabled and are loaded from the provider by the actual evaluation engine.

- The original vLLM case passed on Rubin:

tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py::test_gsm8k_correctness[DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8]
Accuracy was 78.47% across 1,319 questions. Engine initialization took 433.32 seconds, with the original accuracy tolerance and startup deadline unchanged.


## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Expanded build support for fused mixture-of-experts modules across SM100, SM107, and SM110 targets.
  * Added SM107 support for FP8 GEMM modules and TensorRT-LLM utilities.
  * Updated module selection for SM100 and SM103 builds to match their supported capabilities.

title: [cake deslop] MegaMoE (round 2): dedupe SM120 part002, retire ep16 CuTe DSL arm, fold SM90 fc1_gated pair, replace 7.8K-line #error ladder
body:
**Background.** This issue covers four Cake-generated MegaMoE families, 92 files / 92,198 lines at main@3184bbea (including 5,420 lines of tests and 1,898 lines of benchmarks and examples):
(1) `flashinfer/experimental/cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16` (23,888 lines). This is the experimental `flashinfer.moe_ep.CakeMxfp8MegaMoeEp16(..., backend="cuda"|"cute_dsl")`, a fixed program for EP16, 512 experts, top-8, H3072, I5120 and 16/32/64 tokens on CC 10.0/10.3.
(2) `csrc/cake_megamoe_topk_reduce` (264 lines, plus a 219-line JIT module). This is the native top-k reducer of the sm100 nvfp4 `MoEEpLayer` backend.
(3) `flashinfer/moe_ep/kernel_src/sm120/cake_mxfp4_megamoe` (46,286 lines, added in #6346) plus a 4,503-line backend. It is the `MoEEpLayer` backend `sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_bf16_cake` and requires exactly CC 12.0.
(4) `flashinfer/moe_ep/kernel_src/sm90/cake_bf16_megamoe` (8,357 lines, from #5958, #6058 and #6116) plus a 759-line backend. It is the `MoEEpLayer` backend `sm90_bf16_bf16_bf16_push_cake`.

Round 1 covered only (1) and (2):
- #5789 (closed by #5911) reduced topk_reduce to one arch-neutral source.
- #5822 (closed by #5922) cut ep16 from 42,591 to 23,774 lines by folding the CTA-0 and all-CTA variants behind `CAKE_MEGAMOE_RETURN_ALL_CTA`. Its "keep one backend" question got no maintainer answer.
- #5904 dropped the smoke-shape programs, the SM-count override and the per-call preparation from the generated MegaMoE code.

Since then, #5958 (+10,122), #6058 (+2,450/−1,175), #6116 (+19) and #6346 (+53,894) grew the families from about 24K to 92K lines. Half of that is the SM120 package, and no deslop PR has touched the SM90 or SM120 families. There are no per-arch source copies. `csrc/megamoe` and `flashinfer/jit/megamoe.py` (974 + 347 lines) are the hand-written SM90 FP4 path, last changed by #6343, and are out of scope. The hand-written `backends/split/comm/cake` adapter (527 lines, rewritten by #6047) belongs with the comm kernels.

**Findings**
- **SM120 `part002.cuh` is a byte copy of `part001.cuh`.**
  - Both files have the same sha256 (`4b2c7226…`), 1,090 lines each, 0 code lines and 258 `#error` directives.
  - The only two include sites are mutually exclusive: `part003.cuh:20` (`MOE_SHARED_EXPERT == 0`, `MOE_INSTANCE == 0`) and `part005.cuh:136` (`MOE_SHARED_EXPERT == 1`, `MOE_INSTANCE == 0`). No part uses `#pragma once`, so pointing line 136 at part001 cannot include it twice.
  - `shim/cake_jit.py::read_manifest()` (152-173) SHA-checks the files the manifest lists, and the device-module URI hashes `manifest["device"]["sources"]` (321-326). The change therefore needs a manifest re-seal and changes every SM120 JIT URI. The only cost of the new URIs is a JIT cache miss.
- **SM120 `#error` ladder.**
  - `part001`, `part003` and `part005.cuh:133-3636` hold 7,832 lines (8,922 with part002) of nested `#if`/`#error` with 0 code lines: 2,072 `#error` directives with 6 distinct messages.
  - The host mirrors the same tree: `geometry.json` has a 17-entry `switch_ladder` and 320 buckets. `cake_geometry.py::resolve()` (306-350) evaluates them when called from `cake_backend.py::validate_init` (758-800).
  - All 320 host buckets reach an accepted leaf. One accepted-region predicate per switch, or a `static_assert` on the geometry formulas, would replace about 7,800 lines with about 50. Nobody has checked whether the ladder also accepts combinations the host never produces.
- **The SM120 device source is a preprocessor merge, and no arm is dead.**
  - The 12 generated `part*.cuh` (44,134 lines) contain 2,428 select `#if` and 858 `#elif` (10,209 directive lines, 23%) over 17 `MOE_SW_*` switches and 130 `MOE_X_` constants.
  - The `#if` conditions were evaluated as text for all 320 buckets; this is not yet cross-checked with `nvcc -E`. No bucket hits an `#error`. Each bucket keeps 6,221-8,405 of the 32,070 code lines (19.4-26.2%), and the union over all buckets covers 100% of them. No device arm can be deleted.
  - 2,080 lines are active only for ranks > 16 (`MOE_SW_WIDE_RANKS`). The README says this path is compile-checked at 32 ranks and GPU-validated at 4/8/16.
  - The repeated `MOE_X_` defines in part006 sit in mutually exclusive arms, so they are not duplicates.
- **SM120 phase timestamps are written but never read.**
  - They take 129 device lines across part006/008/009/011/012: 26 `atomicMax`, 5 `atomicMin`, 91 plain stores and 5 peer writes. They also take 2 of the 130 kernel args and 2 scratch buffers allocated at `cake_backend.py:349-350`.
  - Nothing in `flashinfer/`, `tests/`, `benchmarks/` or `docs/` reads them. It is unknown whether an external Cake profiler does.
  - The other ~480 `%globaltimer` reads implement the 600 s wait deadline and stay.
- **The ep16 CuTe DSL arm (~17,150 lines) duplicates the CUDA closure.**
  - `cute/cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16_fused.py` (16,444), `cute/cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16_topk_reduce.py` (194), `cute_dsl.py` (303) and the `cute_dsl` branches implement the same two-kernel EP16 forward as the CUDA closure: `fused_kernel.cu` (755), `fused_body.cuh` (3,572), the reducer (140) and the binding (1,226).
  - Only an explicit `backend="cute_dsl"` reaches it. The default is `"cuda"` in `__init__.py:44`, `moe_ep/cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16.py:58` and the example. No env var, AOT entry, doc or dispatcher selects it, and the only `cute_dsl` import is `backend.py:456`, under `if backend == "cute_dsl"`.
  - #5433 measured a CUDA/CuTe latency ratio of 1.053-1.077x on 16x GB300 (the CuTe arm has 5.0-7.2% lower latency). That is the only argument for keeping it.
- **SM90 `fc1_gated` vs `fc1_gated_clamp`.**
  - `cake_gemm.py` builds `fc1_gated` (1,225 lines) when `clamp_limit is None` and `fc1_gated_clamp` (1,489 lines) otherwise.
  - The normalized diff is 456 lines, all in the clamp epilogue. `fc1_gated` keeps an unused `float clamp_limit` parameter (`fc1_gated_kernel.cu:153`).
  - The three 228-line bindings differ in 5 content lines, and each stage has a 125-line manifest record.
  - Passing `clamp_limit=+inf` to the clamp kernel gives the same values except for NaN inputs, because PTX `max.f32` returns the non-NaN operand. It costs 2 extra ops per element.
- **Dead host code and a dev-only path.**
  - `CakeDeviceMultiprocessorCount` in `flashinfer/experimental/cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16/csrc/cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16/cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16_seq_b6463fb4cca601f89fce_binding.cu:75-94` is never called. Its `#include <atomic>` (:25) has no other use, and the ep16 manifest stores no sha256 for the binding.
  - The same helper is emitted in `csrc/kda/tf32/cake_kda_prefill_host_shim.cuh:74` and in 8 `csrc/fused_moe/cake_kimi_k3_situ/*_binding.cu`. Those files have not been checked for callers.
  - `FLASHINFER_SM90_CAKE_BF16_DEV_LAUNCHER` (`cake_gemm.py:244-274`) loads an out-of-tree generator launcher that "is never shipped". Only a test that skips by default and `CLAUDE.md:797` use it.
  - `.pre-commit-config.yaml:55` still excludes `experimental/cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16/kernels/fused_(?:cta0|all_ctas)\.py`, files that #5922 removed.
- **Two generated top-k reducers.**
  - The ep16 reducer (`cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16_2ce7cc644321f53ef127_kernel.cu`: 140 lines, 128 threads, H3072/k8) and `csrc/cake_megamoe_topk_reduce/cake_megamoe_topk_reduce_kernels.cu` (143 lines, 256 threads, H4096/k6) run the same ordered fp32x2-FMA reduce. A CuTe copy adds another 194 lines. #5822 proposed sharing them, and #5922 deferred it.
  - `_uses_native_topk_reduce` (`backends/mega/kernel/sm100/nvfp4_nvfp4_bf16_cutedsl/backend.py:188-204`) enables the Cake reducer only when `max_tokens_per_rank in (256, 4096)` (line 199). The binding itself accepts any `num_tokens <= capacity`. Every other capacity runs the slower CuTeDSL terminal reducer. It is unknown whether the gate, added with #5509, is a deliberate policy or an oversight.
- **Opt-in SM90 routes.**
  - The `prereduced_hilo` combine wire is never a default. `cake_runner.py::_combine_wire_default` returns `per_route` for capacity <= 8 and `prereduced` otherwise. Only an explicit `combine_wire` or `FLASHINFER_SM90_CAKE_BF16_COMBINE_WIRE` selects it, and #6058 describes it as "kept selectable (it is not faster)".
  - The wire is a `split_partials` ABI arg of both prereduced kernels. It is documented in `docs/design_docs/moe_ep_runbook.md:316`, `CLAUDE.md:798` and the benchmark choices.
  - The `FLASHINFER_SM90_CAKE_BF16_FUSED_TAIL=0` and `_FUSED_DISPATCH=0` routes (~40 lines in `cake_runner.py`) switch to the vendored `push_style_megamoe` kernels. Removing them would make nothing in these families unreachable.
- **Per-call host work.**
  - The ep16 binding (1,226 lines) defines its own `ScopedCudaDevice` (45-73) instead of using `ffi::CUDADeviceGuard`. It wraps two `cudaFuncSetAttribute` calls in a mutex and an `unordered_map` (902-934), and it does 34 `TensorView` push_backs and 172 tensor checks on every call.
  - SM120 `cake_backend.py::compute()` packs 130 ABI args through `_write_arg` (`struct.pack`) on every call. When `compile_tokens_per_rank is None`, `_gather_routing` adds an all-gather, a `.cpu()` and two `.tolist()` calls per call.
  - The SM90 GEMM bindings encode the A and W TMA descriptors on every launch, 4 encodes per forward.
- **Metadata and pinning tests.**
  - `cake_sm120_megamoe_geometry.json` is a single line of 288,845 bytes, and the host depends on it. The SM90 manifest has 476 lines, 377 of them in three stage records.
  - These tests pin the sealed sources and must change in the same PR as any removal: `tests/moe_ep/test_sm90_bf16_push_cake_frozen_sources.py`, `tests/moe_ep/test_sm120_w4a8_cake_host.py::test_manifest_seals_the_parametric_closure` and `::test_aot_device_parameters_match_the_default_deployment`, plus the backend and wire tests named in the steps.
  - The contiguity checks apply only to buffers the backend owns, so they cause no per-call copies.

**Proposed steps**
- [ ] Delete `flashinfer/moe_ep/kernel_src/sm120/cake_mxfp4_megamoe/src/cake_sm120_megamoe_kernel_part002.cuh` and point `part005.cuh:136` at part001 (−1,090).
  - In the same PR, re-seal `cake_sm120_megamoe_manifest.json` with the Cake export tool: drop the part002 record (:70) and update part005's sha256, `single_file_sha256` and `unrenamed_sha256`. Also fix `README.md:150` if it lists part002, and rebuild the AOT modules (`aot.py:977-978`).
  - Confirm with an `nvcc -E` diff at the AOT EP4/EP8 points and one shared=1/instance=0 point, which is the only path through part002. Also run a `cuobjdump -sass` diff of the m128/m64 nocopier cubins on sm_120a, `test_sm120_w4a8_cake_host.py`, and `run_tests.sh mega_sm120_cake` on 4 SM120 GPUs with NCCL 2.30.7.
- [ ] Remove `CakeDeviceMultiprocessorCount` (`binding.cu:75-94`) and `#include <atomic>` (:25) from the ep16 binding (−21; host-only, no re-seal). Remove the stale `kernels/fused_(?:cta0|all_ctas)\.py` branch from the `.pre-commit-config.yaml:55` exclude regex.
  - Confirm that the ep16 module rebuilds for sm_100a/sm_103a with unchanged per-symbol SASS. Then run `pre-commit run --all-files` and the CPU slice of `tests/experimental/test_cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16.py`, including `test_host_binding_argument_count`.
  - Ask for the Cake binding template to stop emitting the helper when nothing calls it.
- [ ] Remove the `FLASHINFER_SM90_CAKE_BF16_DEV_LAUNCHER` path (about −100).
  - Edit `flashinfer/moe_ep/kernel_src/sm90/cake_bf16_megamoe/shim/cake_gemm.py`: remove the `importlib`/`os` imports at :19-20, the `__all__` entry at :26 and the launcher code at :244-260, and change :267-274 so that `create_grouped_gemm` returns `ExportedGroupedGemm` directly.
  - Delete `test_ep1_exported_gemm_matches_in_process` (`tests/moe_ep/test_sm90_bf16_push_cake_backend.py:541-614`) and the `CLAUDE.md:797` row.
  - Before deleting, confirm that the Cake generator CI still runs an equivalent exported-vs-in-process check. Validate with `run_tests.sh sm90_bf16_push_cake` (ep1 + 2-GPU) on H100.
- [ ] Get a maintainer decision, then retire the ep16 CuTe DSL arm (−17,150).
  - Delete `cute/` (16,444 + 194 lines) and `cute_dsl.py` (303).
  - Remove the `cute_dsl` branches, the `_CUTE_DSL_*` constants and the host-peer-table path in `backend.py` (~60 lines), plus `jit.py:191-201` and the manifest `cute_dsl` key (:209-213).
  - Update the README backend-selection text, the example `--backend` option and the docstring at `moe_ep/cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16.py:60`.
  - `_validate_backend` then accepts only `"cuda"`, optionally with a warn-once alias for `"cute_dsl"`.
  - In the same PR, delete the 9 cute-only tests and update `test_backend_keyword_defaults_to_cuda`, the two `test_invalid_backend_is_rejected_*` tests, `test_generated_source_closure` and the `[cute_dsl]` case of `test_ep16_sparse_reference_and_repeated_result`.
  - The CUDA SASS is unchanged. Record the accepted cost from #5433. Run `[default_cuda]` on 16x GB200/GB300 only if an allocation appears; none exists today.
- [ ] SM90: route `clamp_limit=None` through `fc1_gated_clamp` with `+inf`, or have the generator emit one FC1 kernel with a runtime clamp (about −2,000 in total).
  - Drop `cake_sm90_bf16_megamoe_fc1_gated_kernel.cu` (1,225), its binding (228), its 125-line manifest record and its 2 file entries. Have the generator emit one binding TU for all three stages (3 × 228 → ~240).
  - First confirm on H100 that fc1 outputs are bit-exact with and without the clamp on the ep1/ep2 cases, including NaN/Inf inputs. Also run a SASS diff and `bench_moe_ep_sm90_bf16_mega.py` at the shipped shapes.
  - In the same PR, re-seal `test_sm90_bf16_push_cake_frozen_sources.py` (stage parametrization :106, `use_clamp` assertion :116).
- [ ] SM120: regenerate from Cake (about −7,900).
  - (a) Replace the 7,832-line ladder with one accepted-region predicate per switch, or with a `static_assert` on the geometry formulas (~50 lines). Keep the same 320 accepted buckets.
  - (b) Drop `phase_timestamps`/`peer_phase_timestamps`: the 2 ABI args, the buffers at `cake_backend.py:349-350`, the 129 device lines and the `PHASE_TIMESTAMP_COUNT`/`PEER_PHASE_TIMESTAMP_COUNT`/`DIAG_WORDS` constants. Do this only after the #6346 author or the Cake owners confirm that no external profiler reads the buffers.
  - (c) Optionally, emit per-switch includes or `if constexpr` arms so each module compiles only its 19-26% of the source. This saves compile time, not repo lines.
  - Confirm with `nvcc -E` for all 4 instances at the EP4/EP8 AOT points, EP16 and one shared=0 point. Check that SASS is identical at EP4/EP8/EP16 on sm_120a; for (b), only STG/`%globaltimer` instructions should disappear.

title: [Bugfix][DSV4] Early-fail when MegaMoE is used with NVFP4 artifacts
body:
## Purpose

Add an explicit guard in `map_nvfp4_backend` that converts the confusing late-binding `KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.w13_input_scale'` (which fires deep inside `params_dict[name_mapped]` during model weight load) into a clear early `ValueError` that tells the user what's actually wrong: `deep_gemm_mega_moe` is not currently wired up for NVFP4 expert layout dispatch.

Closes #43454.

## Context

Issue #43454 documents the failure mode: any NVFP4-quantized DSV4 artifact (e.g. our [`canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4-FP8-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4-FP8-MTP)) served with `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` raises:

```
ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:870] KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.w13_input_scale'
```

during model load, with no hint about the underlying incompatibility. Users see this and reasonably conclude something is broken with their artifact or their config.

## Root cause

The `deep_gemm_mega_moe` mega-kernel path (in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/deep_gemm_moe.py:DeepGemmFP4Experts`) expects FP8 activations + MXFP4 weights:

- `_ACT_BLOCK_K = 128` (FP8 activation group)
- `_WEIGHT_BLOCK_K = 32` (MXFP4 weight group)
- `_supports_quant_scheme` requires exactly `(kMxfp4Static, kFp8Dynamic128Sym)`
- The kernel binding is `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous` (FP8 × FP4 GEMM)

NVFP4 W4A4 uses a different scheme:

- group=16 (not 32)
- E4M3 block scales (not E8M0)
- per-tensor FP32 `weight_scale_2` global scale (no MXFP4 equivalent)
- FP4 activations (W4A4, not W4A8) — different kernel signature

There is no equivalent FP4×FP4 mega-MoE kernel in current DeepGEMM (the `sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe.cuh` header is FP8×FP4 only), so NVFP4 cannot dispatch through `deep_gemm_mega_moe` without significant kernel work.

The PR for the kernel-level fix is out of scope here; this PR only ensures users get a clear error explaining the gap.

## Behavior change

**Before**:
```
$ vllm serve <NVFP4-DSV4-artifact> --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe
# ... 5 min model load progress ...
ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:870] KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.w13_input_scale'
ERROR [core.py:1159] EngineCore failed to start.
RuntimeError: Executor failed.
```

**After**:
```
$ vllm serve <NVFP4-DSV4-artifact> --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe
# ... immediate config validation ...
ValueError: moe_backend='deep_gemm_mega_moe' does not currently dispatch NVFP4
expert layout. The deep_gemm mega-kernel is designed for FP8 activations + MXFP4
weights (group=32 E8M0 scales); NVFP4 uses group=16 E4M3 scales plus per-tensor
FP32 global scale and a different W4A4 activation path. Use 'flashinfer_trtllm'
for NVFP4 MoE artifacts on Blackwell, or use 'deep_gemm_mega_moe' on a native
MXFP4 source artifact.
```

The user gets the right next-action (switch to `flashinfer_trtllm`) without spending 5 minutes loading 852 GB of weights to discover the incompatibility.

## Testing

- Manual repro on 8× B300 SXM6 with [`canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4-FP8-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4-FP8-MTP):
  - Before: KeyError after ~5 min weight load.
  - After this PR: ValueError at config validation, immediate.
- Verified the existing valid backends path is unchanged:
  - `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm` continues to load and serve (Cell A of [our backend×format matrix](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-pro-nvfp4-fp8-mtp/blob/main/docs/findings/backend_format_matrix.md)).
  - `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass` continues to dispatch correctly.
  - The other six backends in the mapping are unaffected.

## Future work

The actual fix (adding NVFP4 dispatch to `deep_gemm_mega_moe`) requires:
1. A new DeepGEMM kernel for FP4-act × FP4-weight grouped GEMM (or an FP4-weight extension to the existing FP8×FP4 kernel that handles group=16 and a per-tensor global scale).
2. A new experts class `DeepGemmNvFp4Experts` mirroring `DeepGemmFP4Experts` for NVFP4 layout.
3. A new branch in `backend_to_kernel_cls` for `NvFp4MoeBackend.DEEP_GEMM_MEGA_MOE`.

That's a larger change with kernel implications; tracked separately and not blocking this PR.

title: [Model][DeepSeek-V4] Make MegaMoE shared-expert finalize independent of linear post-load order
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

MegaMoE fuses the DeepSeek-V4 shared expert using the shared linears' block-FP8 UE8M0 scales. Those linears' own DeepGEMM post-load hook repacks the same scales into int32, in place.

`_finalize_shared_expert_weights` only converted scales that were still in checkpoint layout, and passed packed scales straight to MegaMoE. So it was only correct when it ran **before** that hook:
- Real loads finalize inside `load_weights`, before the hook, so they are fine.
- A dummy load never calls `load_weights` and finalizes **after** the hook. With DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MegaMoE + EP, DeepGEMM then asserts at startup (`layout.hpp:114`).

The packed layout already stores one UE8M0 byte per (row, k-block), four k-blocks per int32. `_prepare_shared_expert_scale` now reads per-row exponents from either layout and builds the same 1x32 MegaMoE scale. The rest of the path is unchanged, including the existing shape check and the fallback to the serial shared MLP.

This removes the ordering constraint that keeps DeepSeek-V4 finalizing inside `load_weights`. #57733 builds on it.

## Test Plan / Results

`tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py::test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe_finalizes_native_shared_expert_weights` gains two `-packed` cases. Their scales are packed by the real linear-hook packer (`deepgemm_post_process_weight_scale_block`) before finalize runs. Results on GB200:
- With this PR: 7 passed.
- On `main`: both `-packed` cases fail at the check that the scale reaching MegaMoE equals the checkpoint scale.
- The rest of the file has 14 failures, identical on `main`. They are V4.1 / hash-routing tests that need a DeepGEMM build with `bf16_mega_gate`.

GPU checks with real DeepGEMM. Setup: the vLLM image `nightly-dev-arm64-cu130-ac9126e58aa7` plus this commit, overlaid file by file with SHA-256 gates.

| check | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Fused shared scale from checkpoint scales vs from hook-packed scales. Shapes (4096, 4096), (4096, 2048), (6144, 7168), (7168, 3072). | packed scales not converted | **bitwise identical** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4-layer config (FP4 experts), MegaMoE + EP, TP1, `load_format="dummy"` | startup crash, DeepGEMM `layout.hpp:114` | starts; shared expert **fused** on all 4 layers; finite logprobs |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, real weights, `vllm serve` DP4 / EP4, MegaMoE (shared expert fused); greedy decoding, top-5 logprobs | baseline | **bit-identical** tokens and logprobs, 4/4 prompts |

`pre-commit` passes.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `MegaMoE shared expert`, `_finalize_shared_expert_weights`, `transform_weights_for_mega_moe` and `deepseek v4 dummy load mega moe`. None of them changes how the shared-expert scales are read.

title: [DSV4][Kernel] Fuse shared experts into MegaMoE

## Summary

Part of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45861.

This PR fuses DeepSeek V4's replicated FP8 shared expert into DeepGEMM's persistent SM100 MegaMoE kernel in the NVIDIA-specific model path.

Before this change, every MoE layer launched the routed FP4 MegaMoE kernel and then ran the shared FP8 gate/up and down projections serially, followed by a separate add. title: [RFC]: support hopper FP8 MegaMoE backend for DeepSeek-V4
body: ### Motivation. DeepSeek-V4's fused MoE expert kernel ("MegaMoE") is wired into vLLM for Blackwell (sm_100) as `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts`, calling `deep_gemm.fp8_fp4_mega_moe`. On **Hopper (sm_90 — H20 / H100 / H800)** that path is unusable because Hopper has no FP4 tensor cores. [DeepGEMM PR #323](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/323)has just landed an SM90 sibling, `fp8_mega_moe`, that fuses the same five steps and accepts block-(128, 128) MN-major `float32` weight SF tensors **directly** This RFC proposes wiring `deep_gemm.fp8_mega_moe` into vLLM as a sibling of the existing FP4 MegaMoE class so DeepSeek-V4 served on Hopper (especially H20) gets the fused kernel benefit Blackwell already enjoys. ### Proposed Change. ### Adaptation points One file changed | Where | What | | -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4.py` | Add `DeepseekV4HopperMegaMoEExperts` (block-FP8 sibling of `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts`) + an SM90 input-staging Triton kernel + a custom op. | | `DeepseekV4MoE._init_mega_moe_experts` (same file) | Dispatch on `expert_dtype`: `"fp4"` → existing class (sm_100), `"fp8"` → new class (sm_90). | | `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py` | Extend with Hopper unit tests. | | `tests/models/run_hopper_mega_moe_ep8.py` + `scripts/run_megamoe_bench.sh` | Manual EP8 multi-GPU correctness + bench harness. | ```bash python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --kernel-config '{"moe_backend": "deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' ``` ### Code sketch `DeepseekV4MoE._init_mega_moe_experts` becomes (existing `if/else` shown for context, the `fp8` branch is new): ```python if self._mega_moe_expert_dtype == "fp4": self.experts = DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts(...) # sm_100, existing else: # "fp8" self.experts = DeepseekV4HopperMegaMoEExperts(...) # sm_90, NEW ``` `DeepseekV4HopperMegaMoEExperts.finalize_weights` (one-shot weight transform; idempotent): ```python import deep_gemm # DeepGEMM PR #323: SM90 weight transform = gate/up gran-8 N interleave # only; block-(128, 128) float32 SF flows through unchanged. l1, l2 = deep_gemm.transform_weights_for_mega_moe_sm90( (self.w13_weight.data, self.w13_weight_scale_inv.data), (self.w2_weight.data, self.w2_weight_scale_inv.data), ) self._transformed_l1_weights, self._transformed_l2_weights = l1, l2 ``` `DeepseekV4HopperMegaMoEExperts._run_hopper_mega_moe` (one fused launch per layer per forward): ```python import deep_gemm # Stage hidden -> FP8 + per-128-K float SF into the symmetric buffer. _stage_deepseek_v4_mega_moe_inputs_sm90( hidden_states, topk_weights, topk_ids, symm_buffer.x[:n], symm_buffer.x_sf[:n], symm_buffer.topk_idx[:n], symm_buffer.topk_weights[:n], ) deep_gemm.fp8_mega_moe( y, self._transformed_l1_weights, self._transformed_l2_weights, symm_buffer, recipe=(128, 128, 128), # required by the SM90 host-side check activation="swiglu", activation_clamp=activation_clamp, fast_math=fast_math, ) ``` ### Hard guards The new class fails loudly (`NotImplementedError` / `ValueError`) when: * device is not sm_90; * `--enable-expert-parallel` is missing; * `scoring_func != "sqrtsoftplus"`; * `hidden % 128 != 0` or `intermediate % 128 != 0`; * SF dtype != `float32` or shape != `(E, M//128, K//128)`. ##### This RFC depends on upstream [DeepGEMM PR #323](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/323) (HEAD `192a513a`), which adds the SM90 `fp8_mega_moe` kernel, `transform_weights_for_mega_moe_sm90`, and `get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe`. The corresponding vLLM implementation is **already written and locally verified** (10 unit tests passed, 1 skipped-by-design; full EP8 correctness + bench harness in place). However, **no further development on the vLLM side will happen until DeepGEMM #323 is merged**: * the implementation PR will not be opened (or will stay in `Draft`) while the upstream API can still change; * no request for review will be made of vLLM maintainers until 323 lands; ## Test Plan * **Unit (CI-friendly)** — `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py` ```bash pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py -v ``` * **vLLM EP benchmark (8×H20)** — ```bash bash scripts/run_megamoe_bench.sh small full ``` Spawns 8 ranks via `torch.multiprocessing.spawn`, then for each shape compares (a) direct DeepGEMM call vs (b)`DeepEP-LL + BatchedDeepGemmExperts` pipeline for a latency baseline. Numbers will be pasted into the implementation PR description. ### Feedback Period. two weeks ### CC List. @WoosukKwon ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Model] Add DeepGEMM MegaMoE support to GLM with compressed-tensors MXFP4
body:
## Purpose

Extend the `deep_gemm_mega_moe` backend to DeepSeek-derived GLM model
implementations without changing compressed-tensors NVFP4 weights into a
different FP4 encoding.

This change:

- adds MegaMoE adapters for DeepSeek V2/V3.2 and GLM-5-next, including their
  MTP paths;
- supports unquantized BF16 and checkpoint-native MXFP4 expert weights;
- rejects compressed-tensors NVFP4 expert checkpoints instead of performing a
  lossy NVFP4-to-E2M1/UE8M0 conversion;
- preserves grouped routing, deferred-reduction, and sequence-parallel
  semantics;
- puts the reusable expert implementation in a shared module; DSv4 and Kimi K3
  model files and the existing DSv4 tests are unchanged;
- covers the adapters, checkpoint-format selection, and explicit NVFP4
  rejection with focused tests.

## Duplicate-work check

This does not duplicate the open related work:

- #40833 introduces the general DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernel integration; it does
  not provide these GLM/DeepSeek model adapters.
- #42844 experiments with FP4 activation dispatch for DeepSeek V4 using an
  external DeepGEMM package; this PR uses the existing FP8-activation/FP4-weight
  MegaMoE path.
- #53527 targets FP8 DeepSeek V4 on SM90; this PR adds model integration for
  MegaMoE on SM100.

## Test plan and results

Local checks after splitting the shared implementation from DSv4:

```text
pre-commit run
# all hooks passed on the staged split

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py -q
# 11 passed, 29 skipped (CUDA/SM100 unavailable locally)
```

The CPU tests cover checkpoint-format selection, NVFP4 rejection, mocked
BF16/MXFP4 loading and finalization, expert mapping, and deferred-reduction
scaling. Non-compressed-tensors quantization configurations are not rejected
by the MXFP4 format predicate.

DSv4 migration is kept separately on
[feature/dsv4-shared-megamoe](https://github.com/tlrmchlsmth/vllm/tree/feature/dsv4-shared-megamoe),
stacked on this PR. No follow-up PR has been opened. Kimi K3 file changes are
omitted from both branches.

The following results predate this extraction; no new GPU or model-accuracy
evaluation was run for the split.

GB200 kernel validation performed earlier on the PR:

- Random FP8 x FP4 MegaMoE, four ranks: relative L2 0.0252-0.0276 and cosine
  similarity greater than 0.9996.
- Exact GLM topology (EP8 across two GB200 nodes, hidden size 6144,
  intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, top-k 8): all ranks produced finite
  outputs.

MXFP4 performance validation used `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-MXFP4xMXFP8` on two GB200
nodes with TP8/EP8. At concurrency 64, DeepGEMM MegaMoE reached 927.8 output
tokens/s, compared with 562.2 for TP8, 540.2 for EP8 with AGRS and CUTLASS
MXFP4, and 237.8 for EP8 with DeepEP-v2 and CUTLASS MXFP4. All 2,269 recorded
requests across the four runs completed successfully. These are single-run
client-side measurements, not repeated trials; Prometheus/DCGM series were not
exported.

No NVFP4 model evaluation is claimed: compressed-tensors NVFP4 is deliberately
unsupported by this PR because conversion into DeepGEMM's different FP4
representation showed unacceptable source-level error.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to implement, debug, test, and draft this change.
Human review of the latest split and relevant GPU/model validation are pending.

title: [Feature]: mega-MoE expert path for SM90 (H100/H20) DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1-Flash — Marlin weight-only is the only option today
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

A mega-MoE expert path for SM90 (H100/H20) DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1-Flash.

The RFC #42284 mega-MoE work landed, but both new paths are gated away from Hopper, so DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 on SM90 still falls back to weight-only Marlin — which dequantizes MXFP4 to bf16 and leaves the fp8 tensor cores idle. A SM90 mega-MoE (fp8-only) variant would directly address the main throughput bottleneck on the most common Hopper serving fleet.

What is gated away on SM90:

- `deep_gemm_mega_moe` (native): `DeepGEMM MegaMoE requires SM100 GPUs` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py`, `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts`) — the kernel consumes fp4 tensor cores.
- `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_*`: requires an NVFP4-quantized checkpoint (fp8-e4m3 per-16 block scales + per-tensor `weight_scale_2`); MXFP4 checkpoints are rejected with "deep_gemm consumes the MXFP4 checkpoint instead".

So on SM90 there is no fused/quantized-MMA MoE option at all for the V4 family: only the weight-only Marlin/MXFP4 fixed-block kernel.

### Alternatives

1. An SM90 mega-MoE variant (fp8 weights/MMA, no fp4 tensor cores — e.g. via DeepGEMM fp8 grouped GEMM with the same fused dispatch→Linear1→Act→Linear2→combine structure).
2. Extending the flashinfer moe_ep path to accept MXFP4 checkpoints on Hopper.
3. Status quo: stay on Marlin. Config-level tuning is a dead end — `VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER` triton MoE configs are ineffective for this model (it does not go through the triton fused_moe path), so Marlin is the ceiling unless a new kernel path exists.

### Additional context

Measured on 8×H20 (TP8, MXFP4 checkpoint, zero offload): conc64 / mt=256 **2434 tok/s**; conc256 short-output **~3300 tok/s**; 128K cold prefill 17.3 s (0 errors, unique-marker bench). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is 510 GB / 48 shards; 8×H20 fits it entirely in VRAM, so the fleet this targets is exactly Hopper.

Happy to benchmark any WIP branch on 8×H20 and share numbers.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] flashinfer_megamoe: SM120 prefill support with FlashInfer's cake MegaMoE backend (DeepSeek-V4-Flash)
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

Co-authors: @jychen21 @AichenF
Submitted by: @GnohzZ 

> **Draft / dependency scope:** this is opt-in, experimental SM120 support requiring a FlashInfer source build containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6346 (validated at `399b6c1d31a13f38dd827018f89c6a04c8487acb`). The default FlashInfer `0.7.1` pin and Docker/CI dependencies remain unchanged. An older build gives an explicit startup error only when SM120 MegaMoE is selected; the regular SM120 backend remains available. The cookbook includes a fixed-revision source-install recipe. We propose reviewing this guarded integration ahead of a dependency release; out-of-box support and validation against a released dependency will follow a coordinated version bump. The candidate is rebased onto main `2528cd2b91`, including CI maintenance base `ff8d964cf5b6`.

## Motivation

`--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` currently requires SM100. FlashInfer #6346 added `sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_bf16_cake`, a fused EP all-to-all + MXFP4 x MXFP8 expert-compute kernel for SM120 (RTX PRO Blackwell) that runs through the same `flashinfer.moe_ep.MoEEpMegaLayer` API this backend already uses. This PR wires it into the existing `flashinfer_megamoe` path for FP4-expert checkpoints, starting with DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

The kernel targets **prefill**. On 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (72 GB, PCIe) it roughly doubles prefill throughput over `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` at the same TP4 / attention-DP4 layout, while decode with a few requests per rank is slower (numbers below). The recommended use is the prefill server of a PD-disaggregated deployment, with decode on the existing SM120 recipe; the server logs this at startup when it is not a PD prefill server.

The PR also fixes a static-EPLB bug on DeepSeek's `forward_normal` path, which serves `flashinfer_megamoe` (SM100 included) and the plain TP MoE: it only mapped logical to physical expert ids with `--enable-eplb`, so `--init-expert-location` alone (which also selects a dispatch algorithm) left the router's logical ids pointing at the physical layout the weights were loaded in.

## Modifications

1. **[Fix] `models/deepseek_v2.py`**: `DeepseekV2MoE._normal_path_dispatch_info()` always builds `ExpertLocationDispatchInfo` on non-NextN layers, as the DeepEP path already does. `init_new` returns `None` without a dispatch algorithm, so the default path is unchanged.
2. **SM120 branch of `flashinfer_megamoe`** (`layers/moe/flashinfer_megamoe.py`, `arg_groups/moe_hook.py`, `environ.py`):
   - Platform gate: SM120 with compute capability exactly 12.0, FP4 experts, EP >= 2, and a FlashInfer build exporting `Sm120_Mxfp4_Mxfp8_Bf16_Cake_MegaMoeConfig` (clear error otherwise). `--enable-eplb` is rejected (the packed scales are not expert-major); speculative decoding without an explicit `--speculative-moe-runner-backend` is rejected (the default draft runner `flashinfer_trtllm` is SM100-only). Settings the SM120 kernel cannot honor fail at startup instead of after the model loads: an unknown transport table, `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0`, the SM100-only `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_COMBINE_DTYPE` / `..._IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE`, and a per-rank prefill chunk or CUDA-graph batch larger than the workspace (`validate_flashinfer_megamoe_sm120_token_budget`). SM100 behaviour is unchanged.
   - `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` by default on this path: the kernel joins the EP group's NCCL communicator through NCCL's Device API, which needs cuMem buffers (SGLang otherwise sets it to 0). Same pattern as the `deepep_v2` branch.
   - Weights: FlashInfer's own preprocessing (`preprocess_sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_cake_mega_weights`). FC1 is a gate/up row interleave of `w13` and is written back into `w13`; FC1/FC2 alias the layer weights, so the experts stay resident once. The float32 (E8M0-widened) checkpoint scales are converted exactly to UE8M0 bytes and replaced by the packed kernel scales.
   - Forward: one pooled workspace; each call stages `compile_tokens_per_rank = max(get_dp_global_num_tokens())`, identical on every EP rank, so there is no per-layer routing all-gather / host sync, and each decode CUDA-graph batch size captures its own bucket. `MegaMoeTunedForward` is not used on SM120 (it would build one compiled kernel + NCCL window set per profiled capacity). Router ids are widened to int64 for this kernel. The kernel's `protocol_error` flag (BF16 return-codec overflow) is not read on the hot path because that needs a host sync; the default codec reserve is 25 % of a row, real V4-Flash activations need about 0.3 %.
   - `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM120_TRANSPORT_TABLE` (default `lsa_where_reachable`) selects the peer transport.
3. **Tests** (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`): `test_flashinfer_megamoe.py` (bucket = max over DP ranks + int64 ids, cake config / no startup tuning, swiglu limit, exact UE8M0 conversion, single resident copy of the experts), `test_server_args.py` (SM120 accept / reject cases, cuMem default, token budget), new `test_deepseek_moe_dispatch_info.py` (both real normal-forward entrypoints exercise physical expert selection without `--enable-eplb`; both fail with the pre-fix bodies, while no-dispatch and NextN controls pass); `test/manual/dsv4/test_sm120_flash.py` runs the cookbook recipe on four SM120 GPUs (sgl-eval GSM8K smoke and AIME25).
4. **Docs**: DeepSeek-V4 cookbook, new "FlashInfer MegaMoE on SM120 for prefill (Experimental)" note.

**Local CPU validation** on the rebased candidate: server-args, FlashInfer MegaMoE, EPLB and normal-forward dispatch suites: 376 passed, 1 skipped; pre-commit passed for all changed files. A cake server smoke also passed on the rebased candidate using FlashInfer source `399b6c1d`; validation against the eventual released dependency remains pending.

**Test environment** (GPU numbers below, collected before the rebase): one host, 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB (SM120, PCIe, two CPU sockets), driver 580.95.05; image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` built 2026-10-13 (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130, NCCL 2.30.7, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0) with this branch on top of `27b68303d0` and FlashInfer main `399b6c1d` (#6346) from source; model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`; sgl-eval 0.1.2. Unless noted: `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4` on GPUs 0-3.

**Dependency compatibility (2026-10-16).** With the actual installed FlashInfer `0.7.1` wheel (module loaded from `site-packages`, no source override), server-args, MegaMoE adapter and expert-remapping CPU suites passed: 334 tests and 140 subtests. A separate CPU probe uses real FlashInfer imports and simulated SM120 platform facts: default/`flashinfer_mxfp4` argument processing succeeds, while explicit SM120 MegaMoE selection raises the expected missing-backend error. This probe does not claim GPU execution. The existing unit test also covers a missing cake API.

The fixed source revision was additionally installed as an editable package (`0.7.2+g399b6c1d`) in the pinned CUDA 13 image, without a `PYTHONPATH` overlay or disabled version checks. Runtime and distribution versions match, the recorded Git commit matches, and the same 334 tests / 140 subtests pass. Old cubin/JIT-cache distributions and their orphan namespace directories were removed; the source build validates its kernel manifest. This installation intentionally overrides SGLang's `0.7.1` pin (`pip check` reports that mismatch), and ordinary default-wheel CI does not exercise the new cake kernel.

The actual released-wheel GPU check also passed on 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, TP4/attention-DP4 and `flashinfer_mxfp4`: four HTTP chat requests completed with nonempty responses, including correct answers to 17 x 23 and 48 + 24. FlashInfer autotune logs identify version `0.7.1`; the container had an empty `PYTHONPATH` and no version-check bypass. This is a functional smoke, not an accuracy benchmark.

The source-installed cake GPU smoke also passed on the same GPUs/model/parallelism, using the separately built image and a fresh JIT workspace: all four requests completed, arithmetic checks returned 391 and 72, and server logs identify `0.7.2+g399b6c1d`. The smoke exercised eager prefill plus decode CUDA Graph capture/replay; generated cake binding/device artifacts are present under that version's cache. This validates the source-install recipe without changing the previously reported accuracy/performance measurements.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0731), 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB (PCIe), `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4`.

**GSM8K-1319** (`sgl-eval run gsm8k --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, sgl-eval 0.1.2: the model's preset, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max_tokens 200000, reasoning_effort=max):

| config | score | truncated | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` (baseline) | 96.59 % | 0 % | 0 % |
| `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` (this PR) | 96.13 % | 0 % | 0 % |

**GPQA-diamond** (`sgl-eval run gpqa --from-dataset <gpqa_diamond.jsonl> --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --n-repeats 4`, sgl-eval 0.1.2, 198 questions x 4 repeats). Both arms used the model preset: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max_tokens 200000, reasoning_effort=max, and `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": true}`.

| config | pass@1 (avg of 4) | repeat-level SEM | pass@4 | majority@4 | truncated | error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_mxfp4` | 90.28 % | 0.56 % | 93.94 % | 90.15 % | 0.00 % | 0.00 % |
| `flashinfer_megamoe` | 90.15 % | 0.44 % | 93.94 % | 90.66 % | 0.00 % | 0.00 % |

These results replace the earlier temperature-0 / 32k-cap run. Scores were independently recomputed from all 792 outputs per arm. The SEM is across four repeats of the same 198 questions; it is not a confidence interval over independently sampled questions or a formal equivalence test.

**AIME25** (`test/manual/dsv4/test_sm120_flash.py::TestSM120FlashFlashInferMegaMoE::test_aime25`, the fixture shared with the other DeepSeek-V4 cookbook tests: sgl-eval, 30 x 16 repeats, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, `--max-tokens 65536`): pass@1 = 98.1 % (SEM 0.5 %), pass@16 = 100 %, no truncation, threshold 0.93. `test_smoke_gsm8k` of the same file passes as well.

**Static EPLB** (a recording of V4-Flash routing, `--init-expert-location <file> --ep-dispatch-algorithm static`, no `--enable-eplb`) on this PR's backend; GSM8K-200 via the deprecated `sglang.test.run_eval` (5-shot), run before upstream moved to sgl-eval:

| config | GSM8K-200 | pf1k input tok/s | ShareGPT input tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, no EPLB | 0.990 | 26109 | 1561 |
| this PR, recorded placement, 0 redundant experts | 0.990 | 25013 | 1507 |
| this PR, recorded placement, 32 redundant experts | 0.990 | 25633 | 1453 |
| recorded placement, 0 redundant, **without the EPLB fix** (commit 1 reverted) | 0.005 (garbled output) | 25152 | 1587 |

(The no-EPLB reference is the median of three c1 rounds; the recorded-placement rows are single c3 rounds. They demonstrate functional correctness, but are not a controlled estimate of remapping overhead.)

The same bug on the plain TP MoE path (`--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4`, no a2a backend, `--init-expert-location <file>` only, which selects the `dynamic` dispatch algorithm): GSM8K-200 (sgl-eval preset) = 0.0 % on the base commit, 96.5 % with commit 1.

**PD-disaggregated functional check** (cake prefill server on GPUs 0-3 with `--disaggregation-mode prefill`, `flashinfer_mxfp4` decode server on GPUs 4-7, NIXL/UCX KV transfer over RoCE, `sglang_router --pd-disaggregation`): coherent smoke answers and GSM8K-200 = 0.990 (`run_eval`) in two separate runs. (In the second run one request hit the 300 s disaggregation bootstrap timeout before its prefill started.) PD throughput was not measured.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup; `--chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 4096` (4096 prefill tokens per rank), `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, decode CUDA graphs on (prefill CUDA graphs are disabled for DeepSeek-V4 by SGLang's own rule), `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random-ids`. Prefill: a dedicated rerun on 2026-10-15 with radix cache disabled, three rounds per point, all three backends on the same production tree. Decode: the earlier c7 session on the same production tree, one round per point; GSM8K-200 (sgl-eval preset) in that session: 96.5 % / 97.0 % / 97.0 %.

**Prefill** (OSL 1, `--max-concurrency 64`, `--disable-radix-cache`), input tokens/s (TTFT mean / median / P99, ms). Both baselines run W4A8 (MXFP4 weights x MXFP8 activations, FlashInfer CUTLASS fused MoE) with the tokens all-gathered over attention DP and reduce-scattered after the MoE; `--ep-size 4` places whole experts per rank like this PR:

| ISL | flashinfer_mxfp4, TP MoE | flashinfer_mxfp4, EP4 | flashinfer_megamoe | vs TP / vs EP4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 12125 (2669 / 2630 / 3670) | 13853 (2334 / 2279 / 3243) | 24174 (1336 / 1291 / 1982) | 1.99x / 1.75x |
| 1024 | 12332 (5126 / 5289 / 6301) | 14165 (4462 / 4603 / 5483) | 25106 (2518 / 2583 / 3121) | 2.04x / 1.77x |
| 2048 | 12101 (9861 / 10774 / 11961) | 13854 (8611 / 9411 / 10469) | 24085 (4950 / 5367 / 6086) | 1.99x / 1.74x |
| 4096 | 11935 (17502 / 21537 / 23239) | 13644 (15287 / 18821 / 20285) | 23400 (8923 / 10887 / 11918) | 1.96x / 1.72x |

In this serving configuration, EP4 improves the baseline by about 1.14-1.15x and the MegaMoE backend is 1.72-1.77x faster than that EP4 baseline (1.96-2.04x over TP MoE). This comparison measures the complete backend, including communication and integration; it does not isolate kernel fusion alone.

Each prefill round has 524288 requested input tokens (`num-prompts = 524288 / ISL`), request rate infinity, concurrency 64, temperature 0, and client seeds 101, 102 and 103; a separate cold run is excluded. The server uses `--disable-radix-cache` and each benchmark passes `--flush-cache`. All 36 measured runs completed every request without errors; all output lengths are one token. The table reports medians of three run-level metrics (including run-level P99s), not pooled request percentiles. The largest per-point throughput range `(max-min)/median` across the three rounds was 0.8% / 0.6% / 3.1% for TP / EP4 / MegaMoE respectively. The runs were sequential on one host, so these are synthetic serving measurements, not a PD throughput or kernel microbenchmark result.

Decode uses seed 42, concurrency 4/16/64/256 and 32/32/128/512 requests respectively; all measured output lengths are 1024 tokens. These earlier decode runs retained radix caching and did not explicitly flush between cases.

**Decode** (ISL 128 / OSL 1024, ignore_eos), median TPOT (ms):

| concurrency (req/rank) | flashinfer_mxfp4, TP MoE | flashinfer_mxfp4, `--ep-size 4` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 (1) | 15.4 | 16.0 | 21.6 |
| 16 (4) | 21.0 | 22.0 | 27.1 |
| 64 (16) | 33.4 | 33.4 | 37.0 |
| 256 (64) | 61.7 | 60.9 | 60.2 |

Hence the prefill positioning. Decode CUDA graphs capture one bucket per batch size: with `--disable-cuda-graph` the median TPOT of this PR is 65.1 / 62.6 / 62.9 ms at concurrency 4 / 16 / 64 (mxfp4: 66.3 / 65.4 / 66.6 ms).

**Topology (supplementary, historical cache-enabled runs).** The kernel picks a per-peer transport: NCCL LSA (CUDA peer access over PCIe/NVLink) where peers can reach each other and NCCL GIN (GPU-initiated RDMA over the NIC) elsewhere. `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM120_TRANSPORT_TABLE` selects the table. Prefill, OSL 1, `--max-concurrency 128`, input tokens/s for ISL 2048 / 4096:

| cake layout | GPUs | flashinfer_mxfp4 (TP MoE, EP=1) | this PR, `lsa_where_reachable` (default) | this PR, `all_gin` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 / attn-DP4 / EP4 | 0-3, one CPU socket | 12126 / 12130 | 24283 / 23629 (2.00x / 1.95x) | 24563 / 23967 (2.03x / 1.98x) |
| TP8 / attn-DP8 / EP8 | 0-7, two CPU sockets | 13578 / 14855 | 40690 / 42221 (3.00x / 2.84x) | 41629 / 44673 (3.07x / 3.01x) |

At EP8 the two sockets have no CUDA peer path between them, so the default table runs LSA for the 24 directed off-diagonal peer pairs inside the sockets and GIN for the 32 directed pairs across sockets (56 off-diagonal pairs in total); an all-LSA table is not possible on this host. At EP8 this PR needed `--mem-fraction-static 0.70` on these 72 GB GPUs (at 0.80 the first MegaMoE launch ran out of memory); the EP8 rows of both backends use 0.70. GSM8K-200 (`run_eval`) was 0.985-0.990 in every layout.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

title: HiFloat4 Format for Language Model Pre-training on Ascend NPUs
body: Large foundation models have become central to modern machine learning, with performance scaling predictably with model size and data. However, training and deploying such models incur substantial computational and memory costs, motivating the development of low-precision training techniques. Recent work has demonstrated that 4-bit floating-point (FP4) formats--such as MXFP4 and NVFP4--can be successfully applied to linear GEMM operations in large language models (LLMs), achieving up to 4x improvements in compute throughput and memory efficiency compared to higher-precision baselines. In this work, we investigate the recently proposed HiFloat4 FP4 format for Huawei Ascend NPUs and systematically compare it with MXFP4 in large-scale training settings. All experiments are conducted on Ascend NPU clusters, with linear and expert GEMM operations performed entirely in FP4 precision. We evaluate both dense architectures (e.g., Pangu and LLaMA-style models) and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, where both standard linear layers and expert-specific GEMMs operate in FP4. Furthermore, we explore stabilization techniques tailored to FP4 training that significantly reduce numerical degradation, maintaining relative error within 1% of full-precision baselines while preserving the efficiency benefits of 4-bit computation. Our results provide a comprehensive empirical study of FP4 training on NPUs and highlight the practical trade-offs between FP4 formats in large-scale dense and MoE models.

title: QUADS: Stabilizing NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning for MoE via QUantization-error Alignment across Dual Sides
body: Rollout generation is a major bottleneck in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models, motivating low-precision rollout acceleration such as FP8. As an emerging low-precision format, NVFP4 combines fine-grained scaling for accuracy preservation with native W4A4 FP4 GEMMs for higher throughput than FP8. However, we find that directly applying NVFP4 to MoE RL rollout is impractical. NVFP4 rollout with BF16 training collapses after roughly 150 steps, accompanied by rapidly growing rollout-trainer log-probability gaps. Through training-inference error analysis and controlled ablations, we identify activation error, rather than weight error, as the dominant source of FP4 RL instability: weights can be synchronized and aligned by a shared quantization-dequantization path, whereas activations are recomputed online and error is amplified by the coarse E2M1 grid. Therefore, to stabilize NVFP4 RL for MoE, we propose QUantization-error Alignment across Dual Sides (QUADS). On the trainer side, we introduce Asymmetric Quantization-Aware Training fake-quantizing weights while keeping activations unquantized for better alignment. On the rollout side, Residual Activation Compensation corrects high-error activation channels while preserving native W4A4 GEMMs. In our MoE RL experiments on several benchmarks, QUADS achieves BF16-level accuracy, improves average pass@1 by 21.49 points over naive NVFP4 RL, and delivers ~16% higher rollout throughput than FP8.

title:
Multi-modal Gated Mixture of Local-to-Global Experts for Dynamic Image
  Fusion
body:
Infrared and visible image fusion aims to integrate comprehensive information
from multiple sources to achieve superior performances on various practical
tasks, such as detection, over that of a single modality. However, most
existing methods directly combined the texture details and object contrast of
different modalities, ignoring the dynamic changes in reality, which diminishes
the visible texture in good lighting conditions and the infrared contrast in
low lighting conditions. To fill this gap, we propose a dynamic image fusion
framework with a multi-modal gated mixture of local-to-global experts, termed
MoE-Fusion, to dynamically extract effective and comprehensive information from
the respective modalities. Our model consists of a Mixture of Local Experts
(MoLE) and a Mixture of Global Experts (MoGE) guided by a multi-modal gate. The
MoLE performs specialized learning of multi-modal local features, prompting the
fused images to retain the local information in a sample-adaptive manner, while
the MoGE focuses on the global information that complements the fused image
with overall texture detail and contrast. Extensive experiments show that our
MoE-Fusion outperforms state-of-the-art methods in preserving multi-modal image
texture and contrast through the local-to-global dynamic learning paradigm, and
also achieves superior performance on detection tasks. Our code will be
available: https://github.com/SunYM2020/MoE-Fusion.
